## Arthur Jenkins
- age：43
- status：Deceased
- dob：2033
- dod：2076
- home：Night City
- gender：Male
- hair_color：Black
- eyes：Blue
- affiliation：Arasaka Corporation
- role：Senior member of Arasaka Counter Intelligence Division
- voiced_by：Alec Newman

Arthur Jenkins was a senior member of the Arasaka Corporation's Counterintelligence Division and head of Night City's department in . Jenkins is referred to as a "very capable psychopath" by an Arasaka subordinate which is what makes him an effective leader.

Biography

:Arthur Jenkins was V's direct superior at the Arasaka Corporation. It is not mentioned as to their relationship, only that Jenkins saved V from a life far less kind and has been indebted to him since. V's colleagues seem jealous of V's position, referring to V as "Jenkins' boy/girl".

:Arthur despises his superior and rival, Director Susan Abernathy of Special Operations. According to Jenkins' claims, Abernathy double-crossed him and worked her way up by slandering him in the process when the two of them were working together in Osaka. Before their transfer to Night City, Abernathy stole his promotion to the directorship by smearing him to the administrative board, something he has never forgiven and bitterly clings to.

:After a damaging leak about an incident in Frankfurt puts the company at risk of losing its license to bases on the Sea of Clouds on Luna, Jenkins orders a cyberattack against the European Space Council, delaying a vote on the revocation of the license. Abernathy calls to criticize Jenkins' tactic as too messy and says it will be costly to cover up. Jenkins, already brimming with hatred for Abernathy, then orders V to eliminate Abernathy by any means they see fit and gives them a datachip with a file on her personal life including her philandering, extortion and numerous other incriminating data files.

:Jenkins' scheme, however, was already relayed to Abernathy by Carter Smith long before she was ever in danger of being assassinated. Upon organizing and attempting to remove her, V is abruptly assaulted by Abernathy's Arasaka security contractors and interrogated at Lizzie's Bar whilst attempting to organize a contract with Jackie Welles.

Ultimately, Abernathy's agents retrieve the datashard with all incriminating information collected on her. Jenkins and the majority of the Counter Intelligence Division are executed at some point. V is spared only because of their Valentinos and Mox compatriots keeping the peace at Lizzie's Bar. Though fired and left virtually destitute, V used the €$10,000 given to them by Jenkins — originally meant for hiring hitmen against Abernathy — to start anew. Jenkins' memorial can be found at the Columbarium, regardless of V's lifepath.

Associated Quests
*The Corpo-Rat

## Ashlay
- status：Alive
- home：Night City
- gender：Male
- affiliation：Charon Exotics
- occupation：Security Contractor
- role：Netrunner

Ashlay is a character in .

Biography
Ashlay was a netrunner living in Night City. At some point he got contracted by Charon Exotics to set up their net security.

:In June of 2077, while Ashlay was working on a side gig, a breach of security in the company's network was noticed. He looked through the net and found that V, a local mercenary, was responsible for the intrusion. As fixing the situation would be easier without the stolen car still being a part of the network, he secretly reached out to V, offering to strike a deal. They were to wipe the company's software from the vehicle, and in exchange they could keep it. Ashlay directed them to an elevator near the main enterance to the EBM Petrochem Stadium.

:Once V arrived, Ashlay hacked the Stadium's security cameras to avoid detection and to keep an eye on the mercenary. He also asked V to keep a low profile and unlocked the elevator to the underground garage. Ashlay occasionally provided tips on how to avoid being seen and helped with erasing the data from the Quadra.

:
::V left the Stadium's garage with the car, which was now out of Charon Exotics' system and avoided detection by the BARGHEST security forces. Ashlay announced that their mission was a success, asked V to not put him in a situation like this again in the future and deleted the contact number.

:
::V was noticed, which ment that Ashlay's situation has gotten worse. Furious, he sent a notification in which he revealed V's intrusion to the entire BARGHEST security force present at the garage and cut contact with the mercenary. BARGHEST's prevention unit was sent after V when they left the garage with the car, which was now out of Charon Exotics' system.

Associated Quests
*Moving Heat

## Atlanta
location
population
- type：City
- country：NUSA
- region：South
- state：Georgia

Atlanta is the capital city of the NUSA state of Georgia.

History
1990s - 2020s
Though Atlanta remains the effective capital of Georgia, the real seat of political power lies in the modern city of Plantation. The Planetran Maglev Network line from Night City to Washington, D.C. had a stop in Atlanta.

2040s
In 2045, the Wright Hotel in the city was to be used as a staging ground for a SovOil operation against Petrochem-backed local rebels, who had been attacking SovOil holdings in the American South.

2070s
If V has taken the Streetkid lifepath, it is mentioned that in 2074 they left for Atlanta to find a better place to live than Night City, but unfortunately it didn't work out and they returned to NC two years later in 2076. V says they only got back a few weeks ago when talking to Padre, and depending on how V reacts during their confrontation with 6th Street thug Sam Carter, Padre may comment that Atlanta "broke" V. Later, when arrested by Inspector Stints from the NCPD, he explains he had heard news of V's exploration for a "slice of happiness" there.

## Atlantic City
- type：City
- owner：Diverse Media Systems
- country：NUSA
- state：New Jersey

Atlantic City is a city located in the NUSA state of New Jersey.

History
Diverse Media Systems purchased Atlantic City after the Collapse left the city completely in debt. DMS forced out the organized crime elements and rebuilt the city to appeal to modern European-style gentrification. The rising sea level forced the state to build dikes along the shores, but there are stairs and docks that offer viewpoints to visitors so as to still see the ocean.

By 2077, most of Atlantic City lies in ruins, but it is still partially inhabited. The rest of the city has been used as a 10,000-acre landfill, one of the world's largest, for toxic and biological waste. At one point, a large fire breaks out in the dump that lasts over a week with no signs of slowing down. The inferno claims the lives of seven firefighters and incapacitates dozens more through inhalation of the poisonous fumes.

Biography

A French netrunner, Aurore Cassel and her twin brother Aymeric have worked for various high-profile clients in France and Western Europe under their collective pseudonym "Skylight". At an indeterminate time they were hired by Militech to reactivate the secretive Project Cynosure, with the goal of capturing and harnessing powerful AIs from beyond the Blackwall. They also did various jobs for the criminal underworld of France and Western Europe as part of The Collective, although such work was not without consequences—Aurore ended up in a stint at Paris's high-security La Santé Prison for five years, and ultimately had a bounty placed on her head by a French crime syndicate.

In 2077, Aurore and her brother were invited by the mercenary warlord Kurt Hansen to help with activating the Neural Matrix, a piece of Militech/Project Cynosure technology unearthed beneath Night City's Combat Zone, Dogtown. Along the way they had their identities stolen by the mercenary V and the FIA sleeper agent Alena Xenakis. In the process, she is executed by Alena and her brother is executed by fellow FIA agent Solomon Reed.

Australia, officially the Federal Republic of Australia, is the largest country located within Oceania and occupied the entire Australian continent, up until the secession of West Australia.

History
1990s - 2020
In 1993, the Australian government attempted to recognize Aboriginal ownership of traditional land, but the corporations that wanted to own the land themselves pressured them into privatizing the land. When the Crash of '94 occurred, it was seen by Australia as just the same decline that the country had been going down since the mid-80s.

In the year 2000, Orbital Air and the European Space Agency teamed up to purchase most of Cape York in order to build a spaceport there, cutting down much of the rainforest. The same year, the Olympic Games in Sydney were boycotted due to the Aboriginal land rights situation.

The turning point for Australia came in 2001 when the Martial Law Authority deposed the monarchy of the United Kingdom. This eliminated the last opposition towards making Australia a full republic, and a new constitution was written. This constitution did nothing to remedy the Aboriginal land ownership situation, and several Aboriginal nationalist fronts started popping up over the next decade.

West Australia, on the other hand, seceded from the country, as they believed they were self-sufficient. The Federal Republic refused to acknowledge them as a sovereign nation and initiated a trade embargo. A battle between the Federal Australians, West Australians (now with Arasaka backing them), and Indonesians occurred the same year.

In 2002, a virus killed off the entire wheat supply in mainland Australia, with Tasmania being quarantined to prevent the virus from spreading. An entrepreneur named Angus Youngblood, predicting the development of disease-resistant crops, began buying up Australian farmland for cheap.

During the First Orbital War in 2008, the lunar city of Tycho launched several rocks at the earth to destroy the United States's space communication network. They attempted to destroy the relay at Pine Gap in Australia, but accidentally hit the town of Alice Springs, resulting in 25,000 deaths.

In 2009, Indonesia invaded the former Australian colony of Papua New Guinea. The Australians began diplomatic negotiations with the country, but positioned troops on their north coast in case war broke out.

In 2011, Militech's experimental nanotech designed to clean up radiation grew out of control in Maralinga. No ready solutions were come up with for the potentially dangerous growth in the desert.

In 2013, Angus Youngblood sold his farmland to Petrochem for CHOOH2 production in exchange for a seat on the board of directors. The company proceeded to buy up more farmland in New South Wales.

In 2016, riots occurred in Adelaide as drought and pollution destroyed their water supply. Arasaka was tasked with developing a desalination system.

By 2020, most of the Federal Republic of Australia was divided between foreign-owned corporations and violent ethnic groups.

2021 - 2077
During the Fourth Corporate War, Militech supplied Federal Australia with aircrafts to use to attack Arasaka-controlled ports in West Australia.

In 2043, Ziggurat opened offices in Melbourne with the intent of penetrating the Australian market but was met stiff resistance from local competitors.

In 2068, A major bushfire wiped out all but one of Australia's remaining wild koala population. The last surviving koala was found on Sydney's outskirts, and was appropriately named "Omega," meaning "last" or "the end" in the Greek alphabet. Authorities originally planned to euthanize Omega, but this was countermanded in response to citizen protests. Omega became a popular tourist draw, and was allowed to stay in the wild under careful supervision.

In 2073, Decker, Tanaka & Rogers tripled the amount of airship fuel consumption to satisfy Australia's growing need for plastic. Being an island nation, but just as wasteful as all First World nations in the 2070s necessitated this following all naval shipping being no longer considered safe.

In 2077, the koala named Omega died of natural causes, making species effectively extinct.

Government
The Federal Republic has a three-layer system based on the Westminster System. They’re led by a parliament which elect a Prime Minister based on their majority, with a president being elected by independently and having a mostly ceremonial role.

Its popularly speculated that companies such as Petrochem and Orbital Air had massive influence over the parliament, particularly when it came to foreign trade.

Law and Order
In Australia, it is illegal to own fully automatic weapons, grenades, combat Cyberware, and EMPs, though all of them are readily available on the black market. To legally purchase a gun, a license is needed, but the gun doesn’t have to be registered. A 20% import tax is placed on all weapons and cyberware, with smuggling them also being a big criminal industry.

Culture==
Australians love sports, particularly football. Unlike other countries, Cyberware is fully banned during these events, but they make up for it with their unabashed brutality on the field, and performance-enhancing Drugs are still legal. Particularly violent players are banned from future games, and since 2007 umpires have had to carry tasers. There is a growing interest in cyberleague football amongst the younger generations.

Beer is also incredibly popular in the country, with each territory having their own favorite brand, and with Smash being seen as pointless street-trash.

Australia was once a very ethnically diverse place, but the political unrest and food shortages in the 90s quickly sparked racial conflict. By 2020, these conflicts were thankfully rare, but there were still certain areas you shouldn’t go if you’re a certain race.

Automatic Love is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough
After meeting with Takemura, V must track down Evelyn Parker to find out if she knows anything about the Relic. After optionally calling Judy, V heads to Lizzie's Bar, and enters her workshop. After a brief conversation with Judy, V discovers that she doesn't know where Evelyn is, but she points them in the direction of a dollhouse called Clouds on the 12th floor of Megabuilding H8, where Evelyn used to work. The iconic Omaha can be found in the adjacent room from the workshop.

Clouds opens at 5pm, if V goes earlier then they will have the option to sit on a nearby bench and wait. After arriving, V must an appointment to see a doll there, either Angel or Skye, as well as temporarily giving up any weapons while in the facility, though a Liberty pistol can be found behind the counter. The appointment with Angel or Skye can be cut short by using a safe word, or followed through on a soul-search by the doll. Upon using the safe word, V questions them for information about Evelyn's location, and they suggest speaking to another doll named Tom in the VIP area. At this point, V has the option to examine booth 11, where the incident that resulted in Evelyn's absence occurred. V can examine a missing port on the wall next to the bed and blood on the wall opposite it. Finally, V can play a recording which shows that the customer did not harm Evelyn, instead, she bugged out in what looks like a remote hack by a netrunner. Some dialogue lines with Johnny are available here.

Entering the VIP area without an access card will cause the Tyger Claws to become hostile towards V, but if one waits outside for a while, a gang member will enter the nearby bathroom where they can stealthily taken out for his access card. Alternatively, a shutter in the hallway leading between the main ring of booths and the VIP door leads to an exterior walkway, which can be followed around to a backroom. This same backroom can also be accessed from the bathroom area via a door with a Body requirement to force open. Inside this backroom is a single Tyger Claw, who can be knocked out for an access card, along with an elevator to a backroom in the VIP area, permitting access even without an access card. Guards in the main room will spot V if they linger in front of the glass window too long, but will not comment or stop V if them walk out of the backroom into the VIP lounge.

Once in the VIP area, V must enter Tom's booth, Where he will reveal that Evelyn had an accident there and ended up in a special clinic in Oslo. He suggests speaking to the dolls' caretaker, Woodman, whose office is in a restricted part of the building. Several side-rooms off the path to Woodman can be explored, including a dressing/prep room for the dolls. On the counter in the first cubby by the door is the iconic katana , as well as Evelyn's jacket, which is only a scanable prop that will evoke a comment from Johnny. More information about the accident can be found on the computer in the server room near Woodman's office and on a shard there. V can also find Evelyn's Schedule shard and Evelyn's Handbag in the locker room nearby.

Woodman will not immediately be hostile when V enters his office, but certain dialogue chosen during the interrogation can cause him to become so. With enough Intelligence, one can offer information on how to better secure their system, or, if one chose the Corpo lifepath, on the real bosses of the Tyger Claws, in exchange for information about what happened to Evelyn. Alternatively, if Gig: Monster Hunt has been completed, Jotaro Shobo's fate can be mentioned and used to intimidate Woodman into giving information. Otherwise, to maintain a peaceful conclusion, V will need to choose the following:

*You don't understand what's at stake.
*Let's not make this harder than it has to be.
*One way or another, I'll find out...

If Woodman does become hostile, V will instead have to defeat him and learn the information by reading a message on his computer. Either way, V will be directed to see a ripperdoc called Fingers on Jig-Jig Street.

Journal Entry
: So you've decided to find the chick who put on this first-class shitshow. She had a job and you took it 'cause there was no one else to knock some sense into your gonk head. I'm here now, but so what? This search and rescue bullshit's a dead end, but that's not about to stop you. Maybe Evelyn will, who knows? Sure seems like she doesn't wanna be found.

Axel Mankievicz, also known as Axeman, is a character in the universe.

Biography
Axeman was born and raised on the street, spending his childhood living out of cardboard boxes and Coffins. He eventually became a private investigator, taking jobs the Night City Police Department were unwilling to, such as murders committed in the Combat Zone. He got through most cases non-violently.

Eventually, Axeman retired as a detective due to several near-death experiences, including time spent in a coma and a severe beating from Infocomp agents. After the Fourth Corporate War, he found work with John "The Professor" Freeman assisting war veterans, specialising in tracking down those that have disappeared.

Aymeric Cassel is a netrunner in .

Biography

A French netrunner, Aymeric Cassel and his twin sister Aurore have worked for various high-profile clients in France and Western Europe under their collective pseudonym "Skylight" and as part of The Collective. For Aymeric, this includes working for Petrochem during the years of 2072-2074. At an indeterminate time, they were hired by Militech to reactivate the secretive Project Cynosure, with the goal of capturing and harnessing powerful AIs from beyond the Blackwall.

Aymeric practices "spiritual hygiene" by avoiding substance abuse and regularly transfers his memories to external storage disks. However, the latter led to his memories of the years 2073-2075 being stolen, resulting in losing the memory of most of his time with Petrochem.

In 2077, Aymeric and his sister were invited by the mercenary warlord Kurt Hansen to help with activating the Neural Matrix, a piece of Militech/Project Cynosure technology unearthed beneath Night City's Combat Zone, Dogtown. Along the way, they had their identities stolen by the mercenary V and the FIA sleeper agent Alena Xenakis. In the process, he and his sister are killed by both Alena and fellow FIA agent Solomon Reed.

Notes
*If V is male, the player uses Aymeric's identity during the mission Birds with Broken Wings.
*While disguised as Aymeric, V can ask to inspect Kurt Hansen's knife during their meeting and claim he gained an interest in knives while travelling in the Philippines. This interest is not stated in Aymeric's dossier, though it does not make Hansen suspicious.
*Aymeric is a classic car collector. One possible dialogue option for V to select during their meeting with Kurt Hansen is that Aymeric came to Night City to buy Johnny's Porsche 911 from Jeremiah Grayson.
*Aymeric's dossier mentions that he is highly allergic to strawberries.
*When V offers to buy a drink for the twins, he mentions that he doesn't drink.

## B@d
- status：Active (2077)
- role：Netrunner

b@d is an enigmatic netrunner mentioned in .

Overview
b@d tasks fixer Regina Jones to hire a merc to infiltrate Megabuilding H11 in Watson. B@d needs their malware uploaded to the building's computer in order to use it as smokescreen to attack an Arasaka subnet.

On the top of the communications tower on Forbes Street in Kabuki, the corpse of a netrunner called Watcher can be found. He carries an archived conversation in which b@d asks him to use their "sweet little program [...] to jailbreak the system in Kabuki". b@d adds that they are not able to physically jack into the tower themselves. Although b@d is concerned for his safety and tells him to be careful, Watcher is a big fanboy and more than willing to assist.

b@d also had dealings with the Wraiths. They passed information about a Maelstrom drug stash in Northside on to the Wraiths, who then raided the place. b@d also provided the Wraiths with a virus that they used to disable drones passing by Union Railroad Station in the Rocky Ridge region so that their cargo can then be stolen. However, as b@d allegedly "took them on", the Wraiths would use another netrunner to locate b@d's hideout. The bunker the Wraiths located south-east of Edgewood Farm in the northern Badlands was a trap containing a taunting message left by b@d and plenty of mines that killed the attackers.

## Baby Let Me Take You
Baby Let Me Take You is a Side Job in .

This quest is only available after completing Just Another Story at least 7 times.

Walkthrough
Muamar will contact V about a gig, telling them to drop all other deliveries for now (despite this, players can still continue to do courier missions as normal if so desired), and will ask to meet at his hangout by the dam. Upon arrival Muamar will be seen arguing with Ayden Daniels, before the latter leaves. Muamar will tell V about a gig to steal an Arasaka truck full of medicine from the docks, with Daniels providing support, before walking off sullenly. Johnny Silverhand will appear telling V to follow Muamar to ask what's wrong. Speak to Muamar about what's troubling him, then after the conversation finishes go to the Arasaka Port by the City Center in Corpo Plaza.

At the docks, find and speak to Daniels first, who will tell V what to look for: a Behemoth truck aboard the ship docked there, with several guards within the compound on watch. Regardless of whether they got to the truck stealthily or not, once V enters the truck an alarm will be triggered with several Arasaka squads hitting the docks soon afterwards, with a firefight breaking out between Arasaka and Daniels. V then has the option of getting out of the truck to save Daniels at this point, or leaving him to his fate by driving off with the truck.

 - If V gets out to save Daniels, Arasaka will have more time to set up roadblocks along the escape route and some of the medical equipment in the truck will get damaged along the way. Muamar will comment on this later, and a few days after the quest Daniels will message V angrily about this.

 - If V leaves Daniels behind he will die but there will be no roadblocks or much organised Arasaka resistance on the drive back to the garage, and none of the medical equipment will get damaged.

Drive the truck to the marked garage by Santo Domingo in Arroyo, making sure to eliminate any pursuing Arasaka enemies on the road.

Once the truck has been delivered, talk to Muamar, who will be waiting for V.

 - Muamar will congratulate V on a job well done, saying that while they will have less supplies to work with when building the clinic he's thankful that Daniels survived.

 - Muamar will be much more sombre, thanking them for getting the supplies, but saying that celebrating feels hollow now that Daniels is dead.

He then tells them to take their reward, a Herrera Outlaw "Weiler" and a bottle of Champaradise in an ice bucket, before leaving the garage.

Journal Entry
:Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes wants to focus? On somethin' important? Shit, what could be more important than a criminal enterprise dedicated to the art of grand theft auto on a massive scale? So many questions, and so few answers.

Objectives
*Meet El Capitan by the dam.
*Talk to El Capitan.
*Go to the Arasaka docks.
*Read the message from Daniels. [Optional]
*Meet with Daniels at the docks.
*Talk to Daniels.
*Get onto the Arasaka cargo ship.
*Find the Arasaka Truck on the cargo ship.
*Get in Truck.
*Deliver the vehicle to the garage.
*Save Daniels. [Optional]
**Check on Daniels. [Optional]
*Deliver the vehicle to the garage.
*Talk to El Capitan.
*Get in the car.

Associated Shards

Notes
*Muamar mentions the factories poisoning Santo Domingo since 2061 were owned by Arasaka. This should not be possible as Arasaka was banned from North America until 2070.
*It is possible to completely fail the mission by letting the Arasaka truck be destroyed, either through taking enough damage, or by driving it into the water. Muamar will message V afterwards about the specific manner on how the truck was destroyed.
*While doing this mission, you can find a locked container that can be opened using the Technical Ability attribute. The container is removed when the mission has been completed.

## Badlands
- type：Arid desert
- country：NUSA
- state：North California
South California
- region：Central Californian Coast
- appears_books：

()

引文：Sparsely populated by nomads, the Badlands are the vast plains outside of the city proper. Unchecked resource extraction, burning oil fields, rampant pollution; this region makes Night City feel like a rich oasis. But it holds golden opportunities for those in the know.

The Badlands is a vast arid region that extends across the states of Northern and Southern California, on the West Coast of North America. This desert surrounds most of Night City.

Overview
These vast plains outside of Night City make the metropolis look more glamorous in comparison. However, there's still life and golden opportunities out there.

Unchecked resource extraction and derelict oil fields dominate in the north. Wastelands full of chemicals and landfills reign supreme in the east. Acid rains are a result of the massive pollution, this guarantees nothing will ever grow there anytime soon, perhaps ever, while the winds carry the unbearable stench that makes sure Night City doesn't forget this place exists. The south side is comprised of mostly desert. Due to Biotechnica's many protein farms, as well as the Jackson Plains power plant, this part of the Badlands is less apocalyptic than the rest. Some even think it's safe around here, but let your guard down for a second and it'll eat you up alive.

History
Beyond Night City and its surrounding suburbs, there is a wide-open space of endless dry Californian scrub, punctuated by the occasional abandoned town or dry lake bed. The Badlands, as it is often referred to, were formed at some point during the 2020s because of the persisting drought Northern California was suffering, turning much of the region beyond Night City into a desert.

The Badlands has been a place that few Night Citizens have ever willingly ventured out into, save for the hardy nomads who have always crossed the desert in their huge and well-protected caravans, as well as the plenty of dangerous gangs that plague its open roads. During the Time of the Red, the Aldecaldos set up a camp on the outskirts of Santo Domingo, from which they ran an expansive trade and transport network, often hiring themselves out to guide people across the desert and transport goods. It was during this time that many refugees from the Fourth Corporate War reclaimed abandoned towns and cities not far from the urban sprawl of Night City.

By 2077, nomads were not the only ones who called the Badlands their home. A gang made up mostly of exiles from local tribes and families known as the Wraiths resided here in great numbers, being the ones responsible for the corporate transport disappearances in the region. Anyone that crossed into their territory without armed transport wouldn't likely survive.

In 2077, Saul Bright's family of Aldecaldos camped on the outskirts of Night City in hopes of finding new employment.

Behind the Scenes

引文：Spend enough time in Night City and you start to wonder why anyone would want to live here. Beyond the city limits, you stop wondering real quick: things are a hell of a lot worse outside. Unchecked resource extraction, rampant pollution and a climate in crisis do not make for a happy weekend getaway. For all its flaws, at least Night City gives you moments of reprieve, in its flashing casinos and slick cocktail bars where you can forget your miserable life for an hour and pretend that everything is going to be fine and dandy. In the wasted badlands and burning oil fields outside the city, the smell of dystopia (or is it just the sulfur?) never leaves your nostrils. Beyond the city's borders we find Entropism at its ugliest, but also at its grandest in terms of scale. Looking down from an AV or an airplane approaching the city, you see endless rows of solar panels and windmills, acres and acres of greenhouses, huge open-pit oil fields... you can't help but be impressed. You see just what it cost to keep a resource-intensive economy going for another century. The natural world—California's great legacy—is dead. Or shall we say undead.

Notes
*The Badlands were first introduced in and , as such there is no mention of them in .

## Balls to the Wall
- quest_giver：Paco Torres
- district：Pacifica
- sub_district：Dogtown
- location：Black Sapphire
- enemies：Yuri Bychkov (dependent)
- previous_quest：Spider and the Fly
- reward_item：(dependent)
Skill Shard: Solo (dependent)
- reward_xp：1832
- reward_sc：167

Balls to the Wall is a Side Job in .

Walkthrough

The marker for this side job is found by a BARGHEST garrison in front of the Black Sapphire hotel in Dogtown.

V will be called out by a recruit named Paco Torres, who is currently drinking his problems away, alongside his companion Babs Okoye. V can hear him out, and after introductions Paco will share the story of an op lead by Kurt Hansen that went wrong.

At one point, Paco will offer to take V on a "Deep Dive", i.e. using drugs to make Paco's story more vivid. If V accepts, they will inhale the drugs, and the viewpoint will then shift from V into Kurt Hansen. As Kurt Hansen, talk to Yuri Bychkov, then go down into the lobby where Paco is standing. Talk to Paco to initiate a fist fight, with the goal being to defeat Paco. Once Paco is defeated, Hansen will assign Paco to convoy duty, and the game transitions back to V's viewpoint.

Paco will confess that he had been skimming cargo from the convoy. V is then asked to take another Deep Dive, which transitions them back to Hansen's viewpoint. This time, Hansen will be a passenger in a truck driven by Paco, moments before they are jumped by Scavengers in vehicles. A gunfight will ensue in which Hansen must defeat any pursuing vehicles using his revolver. The truck is stopped by Scavengers manning a barricade, and Hansen will then disembark to fight them. Hansen only has his revolver and his knife to defeat the Scavengers with, though they were accompanied by some Barghest soldiers that supported them. After defeating all of the Scavengers, Hansen approached one of the wounded Scavenger being tended to by Yuri.

The viewpoint will transition back to V, and Paco will reveal the gist of the story: the convoy was carrying generators, which Paco stole before selling them for cash, and now Paco and Babs want to ask V for advice on what to do. V can offer to tell them to either frame Yuri for the crime, leave Dogtown immediately, or have V call some friends for help (requires that certain Side jobs be completed beforehand).

:Paco and Babs will agree with V's plan and give V both of their contact info, after which V, Paco, and Babs will agree to meet by the underpass beneath The Needle the following day. Either go to the meeting site and sit on the marked location to fast forward 24 hours, or wait 24 hours and go to the location. V will be met by Yuri, who then proceeds to open fire. Defeating Yuri will allow his body to be looted for weapons, and a message shard between him and Hansen that tells Yuri to hang Paco's body under The Needle. Go to the designated point, where V can find Paco's body hanging from the ceiling, at which point V can message Babs to check on her. Messaging Babs will reveal that she had called in a favor and escaped Dogtown to fly to Kenya.

:Babs will offer to stay behind in Dogtown to reduce suspicion on them both. After adding Paco and Bab into the contact list, V must follow Paco to the latter's car, where V can then ask Paco to get in the trunk. Drive the car to the marked location by the Grand Imperial Mall, then open up the trunk to let Paco out, after which he will then ask V to wait for two days. After 48 hours, a message from Paco will ask for a meeting by the Afterlife. Paco will be waiting outside near the Afterlife Fast Travel point, and will then tell V that he's giving them his assault rifle as a gift, and that he has joined the Scavengers. After arguing with Paco about their choice, V can then loot the DA8 Umbra from the chair it's laying on.

:V will offer to contact one of their friends to either smuggle Paco and Babs out of Dogtown or find generators to replace the ones Paco sold.

The available contacts that can be called depends on the character-related Side jobs that V has completed beforehand, giving them the choice of calling in favors from River Ward, Panam Palmer, or Rogue Amendiares to help, and V can then message them about the situation. Panam can help smuggle the two out of Night City, while River can supply replacement generators for the two out of an NCPD evidence locker in Santo Domingo. Rogue can be messaged about sourcing generators, but considers it too small time for her to directly supply them, instead directing V to the generators seized by the NCPD, which they will need to go through River to collect. Depending on which combination of favors are called in, after waiting 24 hours Paco will message V that they've either been successfully smuggled out of Dogtown and plan to leave Night City, or have received enough generators to avert suspicion from their superiors and intend to be more cautious in their black market entrepreneurship. As a reward, they will leave a crate in their tent in the Barghest garrison, on the chair where Paco was sitting, containing the DA8 Umbra, a Skill Shard: Solo, and €$8000.

Journal Entry
:Two BARGHEST pups're in way over their heads and, of course, who else but V to the rescue? I always had a soft spot for tragedies and this one's already got me hooked. You're taking this gig - end of discussion. Think you can pull them outta this shitshow? Got my fingers half-crossed.

Objectives

*Talk to the strangers.
*Talk to Paco and Babs.
**Sit down with Paco and Babs.
*Take Deep Dive with Paco and Babs.
**Take the elevator to the lobby.
**Talk to Yuri.
**Talk to Paco.
**Defeat Paco in a fistfight.
**Talk to Paco.
*Talk to Paco and Babs.
*Take Deep Dive with Paco and Babs.
**Drive with Paco.
**Defeat the Scavengers.
**Approach the wounded scavenger.
**Talk to Paco and the BARGHEST soldiers.
*Talk to Paco and Babs.
*If you call in a favor:
*Message your contacts to find help for Paco and Babs.
**Message Rogue to ask for help. [Optional]
**Message Panam to ask for help. [Optional]
**Message River to ask for help. [Optional]
**Talk to Paco about the help you arranged.
*Wait to hear from Paco and Babs.
*Collect the package Paco left you.

Associated Shards

Notes
*The quest and its related characters become unavailable after finishing Firestarter, and will automatically fail if left uncompleted before the aforementioned quest.

Trivia
*This quest is named after the song Balls to the Wall from the album of the same name by the German metal band Accept.

## Barry Lewis

Barry Lewis is an officer of the NCPD residing in his apartment inside Megabuilding H10 in Little China, Watson.

Biography
2077 has been a tough year for Barry, dealing with the increased rate of crime following the mayor's death and colleagues that simply having no further depth than job efficacy. Sure, Barry wants to do the right thing and help the people of Night City, but that's somewhat difficult when every crazed gangoon or murderous corpo that gets into trouble with the law seems to be deep in the pockets of someone who can make their crimes go away with a simple transfer of eddies to the chief's wallet, or can close an investigation faster than the NCPD can open it. To make matters worse, his best friend Andrew recently passed away, leaving him feeling alone in an unforgiving world. In order to process his thoughts and deal with inner turmoil, Berry has taken an indefinite leave from work without providing a proper elaboration, which has incited worry among his colleagues. After an extended time of not responding to their holo calls or emails, Juan Mendez and Nadia Petrova, both fellow officers of the NCPD, have decided to pay Barry a personal visit. However, their voices were ignored, as Barry failed to feel sincerity in their intention and feared they would not understand him should he actually explain the nature of his troubles.

Passing through the megabuilding atrium, V can encounter the two officers standing in front of the apartment and desperately wanting Barry to open the door. Should V decide to interfere, they will make use of the neighbourly acquaintanceship and send V to try to get Barry to open up and finally explain what's truly going on.

How V approaches this task will be pivotal to Barry's fate. Being kind or using the Body attribute check will provide entrance to his rather unkempt apartment. Barry is willing to talk to a stranger, much more freely, in fact, than he could to his colleagues - ones he considered friends as well. He will soon realize that V thinks that his state is simply due to the loss of a close friend, as is what Mendez and Petrova had said, so he decides elaborate on the story. A lot of bad events have stricken poor Barry in recent months, from overlooked injustices to witnessing a murder of a child by a Maelstrom gangoon, only for the case to be thrown out with the paperwork and ruled a suicide because this particular gangoon had a friend in a high place. Through it all, his old pal Andrew has been with him; in fact, he's been with Barry since even before the world started losing sense, so his departure seems to have broken the only strand of hope Barry had of better days being remembered. He will also note that Andrew's remains now rest in a niche in the Columbarium, indicating that there might be something worth investigating.

:V has not learned enough information, only that Barry can no longer stand his job and wants understanding, something V relays to Mendez and Petrova. Mendez will think that Barry is just a "drama queen", ignoring Barry's real feelings, and believing Barry just needs to take some time alone to toughen up and pull himself together. Unfortunately, without anyone to talk to, Barry will commit suicide several hours later, leaving Mendez sobbing and regretting his words.

:After arriving at the Columbarium, V reads the description on Andrew's niche. Much to V's surprise, the so-called Andrew is actually a tortoise, instead of a human. With Johnny's help and explanations, V realizes that Barry is not well at all: he couldn't bring himself to talk about his issues with his human companions for fear of being ridiculed for having "pussy genes" (in Mendez's words), so Andrew was all Barry had to keep him from doing something stupid - and now Andrew is gone.
:V goes back to the megabuilding and tells the officers about Andrew and how serious Barry's situation is. Mendez initially refuses to believe it, but he and Petrova eventually realize what Barry has been going through. After the conversation, they decide to talk with Barry, with Mendez opening up about a similar incident with a murdered child he had, and Barry finally lets them into his apartment to help him start the long road to recovery.

Associated Quests
*Happy Together

Humans of Night City

Notes
*It is possible to read the messages and files on Barry's computer once V is in his apartment. He will dislike it but will not become hostile.
*The footnotes on the files in his computer show he's been spending a lot of time digging through old cases that seem to have omitting of evidence in common.

## Beat on the Brat: Arroyo
- quest_giver：Coach Fred
- district：Santo Domingo
- sub_district：Arroyo
- enemies：Buck Arnold
6th Street members (dependent)
- reward_item：(optional)
- previous_quest：Beat on the Brat

Beat on the Brat: Arroyo is a Side Job in .

Walkthrough
This is one of the more difficult fist fights, as Buck can deal a lot of damage in one punch to the point 2-3 hits on you will cause you to lose, so it's best to plan accordingly beforehand, like consuming boosters, food, etc.

When you approach to talk to him, he'll be talking about his unique rifle, O'Five. If you have at least 8 in Body you can comment on this which will then give you the option to have him also put it up for grabs, provided you have €$ 18,000 to spare to fight him for it. Otherwise, you just need €$6,000 to fight him.

Note that if you got him to put up his sniper rifle, once you win he and his buddies will turn hostile and start shooting at you. At this point you're free to also use your own guns and kill them if you wish. Once they're down, go collect the gun to complete the job. You won't automatically receive your eddies if you select this method, but you can loot the prize money from Buck's body.

The normal bet will end up with Buck telling you to leave if you win. You can just directly leave the area, or talk to him. You can decide whether to provoke him or to calm him down. If you decide to provoke him, Buck and his friends will proceed to attack you, and his rifle O'Five will be immediately be available for you to get.

Once they're down, go collect the gun to complete the job.

Journal Entry
:Heard somewhere the champ of Arroyo is a grade-A prick. Good news - should make beatin' his ass all the more fun.

Objectives

*Go to the fight in Arroyo.
*Talk to the champion of Arroyo.
*Defeat Buck.

Notes
* Buck does not need be killed to get his rifle, as long as he is hostile after the fistfight it can be acquired.
* If V leaves the area without killing Buck, he will despawn.

## Beat on the Brat: Pacifica
Beat on the Brat: Pacifica is a Side Job in .

Walkthrough
This one requires you to complete the main job Transmission first to then open up the side job Send in the Clowns which needs to be completed for this. As such, you can actually end up doing the championship fight in Beat on the Brat with Razor Hugh before you get this one based on how you completed other quests.

You'll be fighting in the large, dry pool area, so you'll have plenty of room to evade. That said, your major concern is Ozob's nose: it is a live grenade so if you hit it wrong too many times, you could set it off.

Ozob's grenade nose will detonate after accumulating about 75% of his health in damage to his head. This instantly kills Ozob and V wins by "technical knockout" and must talk to the referee standing on the side of the pool to get the reward money and complete the quest.

Journal Entry
:A throwdown in Pacifica, huh? Wonder who you're up again. I'd say a Haitian, though I guess that much is probably obvious. Careful, those Pacificans don't fight for first blood - they fight for last blood.

Objectives
*Go to the fight in Pacifica.

Beatrice Ellen Trieste, better known by her handle 8ug8ear, is a minor character in .

Biography
8ug8ear was a skilled Netrunner living in Japantown, Westbrook, Night City. She is an associate of Wakako Okada and the Tyger Claws. At some point before 2077, she wrote and published an opinion piece critiquing the after-effects of the DataKrash brought about by Rache Bartmoss.

2077
In 2077, she was working together with Norimasa, a Tyger Claw member, to try and steal tech from a Kiroshi Optics warehouse job. The gig had her remotely hack the Kiroshi van and cut the alarms for the Tyger Claws to get access to the gear. However, 8ug8ear remotely drove out the van packed with high-end gear and abandoned them inside. The gang members survived and next day they pulled up to her apartment wanting to know where she had stashed the tech. 8ug8ear was desperate, and escaped to the Net, shrouding herself within software that would flatline her if they tried to disconnect her. The Tyger Claws began waiting patiently as she couldn't stay like that for long. 8ug8ear was attempting to get help from Z3d, another Netrunner, who wasn't willing to help until she told him where the Kiroshi van was hidden, but their conversation was cut short when Z3d was killed by Tyger Claws who discovered his location. Wakako Okada then notified a merc named V to save her from gang before her time ran out.

:8ug8ear was carefully brought out of the Net by V, and then transported into a car secured by Wakako.

:8ug8ear's niche can be found at the Columbarium.

Overview
This implant allows you to reset your Bounty level, while under level 4, once every 25 minutes. The cooldown can be reduced to 20 minutes at and 15 minutes at .

When installed, this implant occupies its own dedicated Face cyberware slot, separate from the slot used for the player's Kiroshi implants. This second slot cannot be used for any other implant.

Storywise, this implant allows a person to use metanthropic cloaking technology to completely change their facial features to disguise them as another person. As its name implies, this faceplate synchronizes with any installed behavioral imprint to perfectly mimic another person's voice, facial expressions and mannerisms.

Ben DeBaillon, also known as SpaceBoy_66, is a Voodoo Boys netrunner who, in attempt to climb the gang ladder, tried to take the Grand Imperial Mall from the Animals and got discovered by NetWatch, leading him into cyberpsychosis.

Biography

Ben's plan seemed to be well-thought out although, in lack of proper connections and full gang support, he had to rely on recommendation by word. Prior to even approaching the topic of virtually taking over the mall, he followed a friend's endorsement of a company called Eagle Eye Inc. and hired them to perform reconnaissance and risk assessment of the area. Prior to doing the job, the company representative informed him that the going rate for a job as complex as the mall, would be double the regular, which is not something Ben could afford, although, reluctantly, he agreed. Upon meeting the next day, he attempted to follow the Voodoo Boys code and dispose of the man on the spot in order to avoid leaving any witnesses of the job being performed, however, he hadn't anticipated that the target had advanced defensive cybernetics and pulled out from the attack alive. In addition to this failure, the act had been detected by NetWatch as well, who added their own daemons to the equation and severely damaged Ben's operating processes right before he managed to disconnect.

With critical malfunctions of cyberware making his brain feel neural disturbances, he managed to drag himself back to his garage on the pier and request help from William S. Bradley. Having delusions of their own kind, he started experiencing fear-induced paranoia as well, he set up heavy automated security and started disposing of anyone that approached his place. Delusions made him see scavengers everywhere and, regardless of being aware that they potentially might not even be there, he defended his position. Most victims of this arrangement were homeless people, while the one surviving eyewitness described a horror done by a lone actor which attracted the attention of Watson fixer Regina Jones, who is always on the lookout for cyberpsychos in the city. She contracted local merc V to investigate the situation and pacify a potential subject for her trials.

Once dealt with, if kept in a living condition, Regina's people will come to pick him up.

## Benedict McAdams
status
dod
home
affiliation
appears_games
- gender：Male
- aka：Ben McAdams
- role：Solo
- voiced_by：Robert Vernon

Benedict McAdams is a reliable, professional merc, often relied upon by the Badlands fixer Dakota Smith, through whose contract he ended up in need of a rescue himself.

Biography
The job he had been hired to do was an easy one, although solely by execution. Namely, Councilman McLean, an individual of political perspective, was becoming increasingly problematic for the resident Badlands fixer due to his persistence in coercing her to lose a step in her footing. The only visible solution she could think of was simply removing him from the story altogether, and McAdams was happy to oblige. Due to the sensitivity of the job, he had installed a GPS tracker into his biomon, so the fixer had an eye on him at all times. The job had been finished within merely six hours of it being assigned, although not as low-profile as would allow his name to remain unnoticed, so it was necessary to get him across the border as soon as possible. Unfortunately, the driver he was working with, nomad of the Aldecaldos tribe, Jason Wildriver, had a different plan, and instead of transporting McAdams across the border, he drove him to a shack on Clements Street. The GPS tracker going off route was immediately noticed, so Dakota acted by hiring an additional merc, V, to check out what went wrong and extract McAdams.

Having done this in the past, Wilddriver already had a contact with Militech and knew they've put up a bounty on the head of McAdams as soon as the job was done. His demands were not immediately accepted, so McAdams needed to stay put for a little while longer. This time, he had spent sitting in the shack basement, contemplating his role in the matter and thinking up ways to address his captor and whoever agrees to pay the bounty. His demeanour and tough attitude, despite simply being an act of coping with the situation, instilled a form of admiration in his captor, so he was not restrained and provided with both drink and food while the negotiations went on. Once V arrived to meet him, McAdams expected all but a rescue, greeting them as if addressing Militech personnel. He will explain what his job was, briefly denote that the councilman he took out had been bought by Militech to pass bills benefitting their corporation, and that due to this, he became the most valid scapegoat for the mess which ensued. With some extra fault attached too, as it would derail NCPD from looking into other related matters. Due to the situation, he sarcastically exclaims how, due to all the desperation, he'll only be expected to take his own life in order to escape.

Once V explains that they are actually sent by his own fixer rather than Militech, McAdams drops the act entirely, admitting he does not enjoy playing tough in the face of death, although takes pleasure in it fooling his captor to the point of starting to behave like him to appear more tough. In spite of not being bound, McAdams has not moved since being sat on the floor upon arrival and he will complain of, among other things, the difficulty of using his legs. On the way to a more reliable driver, he surprises V with musings about melons. Sweet, honey melons that his fixer's people grow. The kind he direly needed in that basement but was not given among all the food and drink that he received. This appeared to have upset him quite a lot.

A bit further away from the Biotechnica flats, east into the Badlands, Dakota's vetted driver Starkey arrived to pick McAdams up. McAdams was glad to see a familiar face, even though it's been years since they've last met. Final word about him comes in form of a closure message from Dakota, stating that he is safe.

:As the Aldecaldos have a last night together before attacking Arasaka in order to help V and steal tech, Benedict can be encountered leaning by the stairs up the food truck in the Nomad Camp. He complains that he is getting itchy hands but Dakota told him to sit tight for a little longer as Militech is still sniffing around.

Database Entry

## Bes Isis
引文：Nobody ever leaves Night City. Except in a body bag.（Bes Isis）

Bes Isis, born Nancy Hartley, and known professionally as Nancy Rocastle, is the ex-keyboardist for the band Samurai. After the end of her musical career, she became an investigative journalist for Network News 54.

Biography
2000s - 2020
Nancy Hartley was a kicker for a local Boostergang before joining the band Samurai, for which she played the keyboard. She was a member of the band until 2008 when she spent seven months in jail for throwing her abusive husband out of their 83rd story apartment through the window. During her incarceration, the band was dissolved.

At some point after her release, she took on the name Bes Isis and became a major media presence on Network 54 due to her persistent pursuit of stories nobody else dared to cover.

Sometime in 2011, Bes Isis was in Mexico City, working on a story about the American nomad underground in the region, specifically about the 1990s band Justifiable Homicide. While having a drink in a local bar with the band, a 16-year-old soldier came to her, giving a story about 600,000 nomad workers marooned in South America, trying to get out by walking 3000 miles, in an event known as "The Long Walk". Bes Isis documented the story and was nominated for a Pulitzer Prize for it. Later, she participated in The Long Walk itself.

2045
By 2045, Isis continues to run a show on the Data Pool, having a mixed reputation compared to other Medias due to her rule-breaking investigations, as well as having replaced her leg and chest with chrome replacements to feign injury to obtain a "meat jumping" story.

2077
In 2077, she remains a Network 54 employee, proceeding to cover difficult events as an investigative journalist. She also had an adult son named Dan. Bes briefly went missing while investigating Maelstrom at the Totentanz club. Depending on who led the gang at the time (either Royce, Brick, or Patricia), the merc V helps her interview the leader or fight their way out of the building after being sent to pick her up by Kerry Eurodyne, who wanted to organize a one-night reunion of Samurai.

After the gig, V calls Nancy about an old request she had posted on an illegal netsite for information on Leonard Swedenborg-Riviera, an anti-establishment political philosopher who no one knew anything about yet who had reached a wide audience on the Net with his nearly incomprehensible ideology. Nancy had gotten no leads for her planned segment and forgot about the request, but V picks up the trail and discovers Leonard was actually "Leonora, the Savantron", a fortune-telling machine that someone had reprogrammed and linked to the Net as a prank. If Nancy is told, she is thrilled by the development, claiming it will make for an even better report than what she thought. She will later receive a Pulitzer Prize for this report.

Associated Quests
*Holdin' On
*Second Conflict
*Killing in the Name

Humans of Night City

Notes
*Nancy admits using Samurai and Silverhand as a common manner of riling the followers of her media once the news cannot provide more interesting content.
*After Nancy receives the Pulitzer Prize, she will message V to thank them for their assistance in her investigation. She will include a photo of the cover of Nightweek Magazine, on which she is cited as Nancy Rocastle.

Bill is the grieving widower of his deceased wife, Caroline Jablonsky, who was murdered by Joshua Stephenson. Through Wakako Okada, Bill hires V to assassinate Joshua during his transit across Arroyo, with V responsible for driving Bill's vehicle of choice. ## Biotechnica Building
- type：Regional HQ
- owner：Biotechnica
- city：Night City
- district：City Center
- sub_district：Corporate Center
- location：Corporate Plaza

The Biotechnica Building is a massive building located in the Corporate Plaza of Night City. It acts as the regional headquarters for Biotechnica.

Overview
This gigantic building is Biotechnica's regional headquarters in Night City. Like the other major office buildings in Corporate Plaza, it is accessed via a bridge from Memorial Park.

Biotechnica's building is almost as big as the nearby Militech Offices, expanding northwest from its main entrance until almost touching the nearby edifices. The most impressive structure, however, has to be the skybridge that connects the main tower in Corporate Plaza to another building in Wellsprings to the west, crossing over parts of the Glen until reaching the northeastern area of Wellsprings.

History
When reconstruction of Corporate Plaza begun in 2052, many megacorporations around Night City planned to move their new headquarters there.

At some point prior to 2075, netrunner Sasha Yakovleva got a gig to extract Biotechnica's secret financial records on CHOOH2 and information on a new immunosuppressant prototype 0.091. Helped by her crewmate Maine, Sasha managed to infiltrate the Biotechnica regional headquarters of Night City. After reaching an office, she connected to the building's database and once she found what she was looking for, she sent Maine the extracted data for the gig. While doing so, Sasha discovered confidential files on Securicine — the painkillers her mother used while she was sick and which eventually led to her death. The main side effect of the painkiller included gradual neurodegeneration and, despite this being known, Biotechnica decided that Securicine was too profitable and would not be pulled from the market. Sasha, determined to do right by her mother, started to upload the entire Securicine database file to the Network 54 News tipline. Sasha was discovered, but she trenched herself in the office to make sure the uploading was completed. Knowing she was not going make it out alive, she prepared a set of explosives and cut off the connection line with Maine. Sasha managed to fully send the information to N54, but was shot and sent through the office's window, prompting the explosives to activate and destroy the room she was in. Her body fell down onto the roof of a passing car and was soon found by Maine.

In 2077, the Biotechnica building in Corporate Plaza still stood as an imposing megastructure in Night City.

Notes
*The Biotechnica Campus of shares a similar location with some parts of the 2077 megastructure.

## Biotechnica Flats
- type：Protein farms
- owner：Biotechnica
- region：Badlands
- subregion：Southern Desert
- appears_books：

The Biotechnica Flats (also known as the Biotechnica Farms) is a large expanse of protein farms located on the southern Badlands of Night City.

Overview
The Flats are a vast expanse of protein farm greenhouses owned by Biotechnica. This facility is one of the many that the corporation operates worldwide, tasked with mass-producing synthetic protein derivates. The farms extend from the southern border of Night City, near Pacifica, all the way south until it reaches the border wall with South California. The Pacific Ocean lies to the west, while Highway 101 takes its eastern border alongside the Jackson Plains.

Biotechnica uses all this staggering amount of land to provide Night City with more than half of its demands for alternative protein, becoming the source of much of the meat and meat-substitute products in the metropolis. The most popular, yet expansive production is based on protein-rich crickets. An alternative and less costly production consists of mass-growing worms, which are later grounded down into a meat-like paste known as SCOP. This paste is then shipped off to facilities where it is molded, flavored, and dyed into a shape that vaguely resembles meat. This "meat" is later used as a primary ingredient for much of the produced food in Night City and can be found in many establishments around the metropolis including restaurants, marketplaces, etc. While crickets have become an acceptable type of food, consumers still bristle when being told they are eating worms.

History
The protein farms were built on a large area on the southern Badlands of Night City. There was at least one previous settlement which became completely surrounded and whose inhabitants were contracted to work in the farms. By 2077, not much of this community was left, though there were still some locals living in its premises.

## Biotechnica Hotel
- type：Corporate hotel

- city：Night City
- district：City Center
- sub_district：Downtown

The Biotechnica Hotel, also known as the Republic Way Hotel, is located in Downtown, in the City Center district of Night City.

Overview
This corporate hotel is owned and operated by Biotechnica, including security. Only employees of the corporation are able to get apartments in this hotel.

Layout
Lobby

Floor 19
The 19th floor can only be accessed by the elevator from the main lobby. There are several idle Robots, and one guard patrolling the room. There is a small security room with 2 guards in on the east side. Apartments 191 through 194 can be found on the south side, as well as a staircase that leads to the rooftop.

Director Joanne Koch resides in apartment 193. The door can only be opened using 19 Technical Ability. Directly upon entering the apartment, Joanne's computer can be found. On the left there is a bedroom and a bathroom. Inside the bedroom, a cache with a Crafting Spec: A-22B Chao can be found, as well as another cache with components and a Skill Shard: Crafting.

Straight ahead will lead to the living room and kitchen, where Joanne Koch herself can be found engaged in a braindance session.

Rooftop
The rooftop is patrolled by 4 guards. In the center, a landing pad can be found that is suitable for most AVs. On the east side an out of order elevator can be found. On the west side, a small storage room can be found where a cache with a Crafting Spec resides. It is also possible to find an open window that leads inside apartment 193. There is an Access Point near a satellite dish that requires 19 Intelligence.

*Gig: Guinea Pigs

Birds with Broken Wings is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough

After breaching the party at Black Sapphire and stealing the identities of the two netrunners who will attend a meeting with Kurt Hansen and Songbird, Alex and Reed tell V to meet them at the basement of The Moth to discuss what comes next. The plan is to intercept the netrunners assume their identity and meet Hansen and snatch both the matrix and Songbird also killing Hansen for attempting an assassination on the president.

The plan is to hack into Charon Exotics and take control of the netrunners vehicle. To do that Alex instructs V to go to a tracking station of Charon Exotics and install the encryption key. But as V leaves The Moth Songbird reaches out to V and asks them to meet her to talk in private.

:Songbird asks V to come to a spot that she likes and reminisces about old times. Then after V confronts her, she confesses that she was the one who told Hansen about when and where Space Force One would be. She tells V that her real plan was for her and V to run away with the matrix and save the president, but that her getting captured changed everything. Her plan is to escape from Hansen and to give the matrix to a ripper who can help both her and V.

If V has sufficiently high Intelligence, V only needs to visit one Charon Exotics tracking station by choosing to remote access the second tracking station. If not, the second transceiver is broken and V will have to restart the transceiver. To find where to do so a kid named Luka can be paid 1000 Eurodollars to play a hot or cold game to instruct V on where to go. If you refuse his offer he will reduce his price down to 10, however refusing again won't lower the price further. Alternatively you can just go to the end of the roof, to the left of V when facing away from the station, and press the button as it is always available to be pressed.

After receiving the data, V needs to wait a couple hours for Reed to contact them. While waiting Alex reaches out and invites V to The Moth to kick back a little.

At The Moth V and Alex talk about who they would want to be if they weren't who they are now. They bond and V can choose to dance if they choose to.

A few hours later Reed calls and tells V to see a specific ripperdoc to get an implant that will allow V to use the biometrics of the netrunners. Reed also plans on taking Songbird with him but thinks he needs to ICE her first so implants a module to ICE Songbird into V as well.

As V gets the implant they talk to Johnny about the predicament that they are in. One side is a woman trying to survive as a living nuke, potentially dragging you with them to the explosion, while the other side is a man that runs on principles trying to do good by them potentially ready to mess up the entire situation. Leaving the ripperdoc finishes the mission.

Journal Entry
:Always thought it was in showbiz you couldn't trust a soul. Turns out, in hindsight, met a few good eggs in my time. But, man... all these cloaks from Langley? Guaranteed dagger in the back... And probably stuck there by a friend. You're gettin' played here, no doubt about it, but not much choice with our survival on the table. Just do me a favor – ears perked, eyes peeled and mind always, always razor-fuckin'-sharp.

Black Lace is a consumable in .

Overview
Black Lace is a drug that increases adrenaline and endorphins levels up to the point that one is almost incapable of feeling pain. Black Lace is composed of 27% dextromethamphetamine, 15% cannabinoid, 40% water, and 8% chemical ingredients of unknown origin. Potential reactions that may occur consist of altered states of consciousness, panic attacks, elevated heart rates, dehydration, and sometimes heart attacks. The trip is so intense that it verges on cyberpsychosis. Corporations handed it out to their forces during the Corporate Wars. Cyberpsychos are heavy consumers of the drug. Vaporizing the drug instead of swallowing it lessens the aftereffects, without compromising the trip.

Effect(s)
When consumed, Black Lace changes the following stats for 300 seconds:
*Armor by -
*Stamina Regen Rate by -%
*Damage by -%
*Crit Chance by -%
*Crit Damage by -%
*Health by −-%

Acquisition
*The Pickup - Can be accepted from Dum Dum during the initial meet.
**Subsequently, if V has the Streetkid lifepath and the Maelstrom deal is concluded in favor of Maelstrom or peacefully, Dum Dum will offer one additional Black Lace for V to keep, as a gesture of goodwill.
* Dropped by cyberjunkies and regular junkies.

## Black Sapphire
appears_other
- type：Unfinished hotel
Headquarters
- city：Night City
- district：Pacifica
- sub_district：Dogtown
- location：Golden Pacific
- street：George Washington & Abraham Lincoln
- affiliation：BARGHEST

The Black Sapphire is a large skyscraper located in Dogtown, in the Pacifica district of southern Night City. It is the headquarters of BARGHEST.

History

Originally part of the resort project of Pacifica, Halsey, Ferris & Skiv began construction of the Black Sapphire in 2061 and despite its scheduled opening of 2065, by 2069 the building was still incomplete.

After the Unification War ended in 2070, Kurt Hansen laid claim to the unfinished hotel and transformed it into the new base of operations for BARGHEST.

Hansen used the club located at the top of the Sapphire to lure in elite individuals from all over the world in order to make all kinds of shady deals under his watchful eye.

Database Entry

Layout
The Black Sapphire are four independent towers connected by the ground and top floors through elevators, and to each tower via bridges. The unfinished hotel stands at a height of 415 m (1360 ft) and has 99 floors, with a total of 2792 rooms.

Underground Parking
Both the parking and the maintenance tunnels were partially demolished and flooded by the Barghest.

Floor 01
The ground floor contains the warehouses and barracks of the Barghest, as well as the mess hall.

Floor 67
Most of the unfinished floor is for maintenance. All towers are connected via scaffolding and improvised bridges.

Floor 99
The top of the building is divided between the four towers, all connected by a terrace. This area includes a restaurant and AV landing pads. The northern tower holds a club and a casino.

Notes
*During early development of , the Black Sapphire was known as Paradise Hotel, a name later reused for another location in Dogtown. The last mural picture below still shows this name at the hotel's entrance.

## Black Steel In The Hour of Chaos
Black Steel In The Hour of Chaos is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough

MaxTac has captured Songbird, so V and Solomon Reed need to break her out.

V will need to call in a favor from a netrunner contact to gain intel on the MaxTac convoy transporting Songbird. Depending on what missions have been previously completed, V can call the following netrunners:
*Nix - Delivers V data after 6 hours at the Arasaka Memorial; gives V a frontal cortex implant Self-ICE to aid in fighting MaxTac. Requires completing KOLD MIRAGE with Nix alive.
*Sandra Dorsett - Delivers V data after 8 hours at Reconciliation Park; requests V to install a Trojan virus into MaxTac in return. Requires completing Full Disclosure and picking the Intelligence/or congratulating her dialogue option.
*Chang-Hoon Nam - Delivers V data after 12 hours at his shop in Japantown; suffers from aphasia after hack and will leave Night City. Requires completing Gig: Wakako's Favorite.
*Carol Emeka - Refuses to provide V the data, but sends either a weapon or quick hack to aid in fighting MaxTac. Requires advancing on Panam Palmer's side quests.
*Alternatively, V can pay Mr. Hands €$15,000 to enlist his netrunner Yoko Tsuru, who completes the job in 10 hours, and provides an additional objective to send Mr. Hands coordinates of the ambush.

After retrieving the data, V will meet up with Reed and members of the 6th Street gang in an abandoned hotel in Pacifica overlooking a skybridge.

Before the MaxTac convoy arrives, a 6th Street soldier will overview the planned ambush. V can select placement of either turrets or mines, as well as review 3 possible starting positions. At the start of the ambush, V and Reed will need to first eliminate the NCPD escort, followed by a squad of four MaxTac officers.

Songbird will escape with the MaxTac truck. Following the path of the truck leads V to Songbird and directly into the quest Somewhat Damaged.

Journal Entry
:Not lookin' good, V. Alex is dead, Songbird's been nabbed by MaxTac and Reed... well, Reed still thinks he's got everything under control. But isn't this whole rescue op proof that he's lost the thread? I'll give him one thing - come hell or high water, he doesn't give up - keeps pushing forward till he gets his way. The key to success, you think? Guess we'll find out... long as we don't end up tossed into Los Padres first.

Objectives
*Call a netrunner to help breach MaxTac.

- column：4
- column1：Call Carol and convince her to help. *Call a different Netrunner contact. **Retrieve Carol's gift from the stash. [Optional]
- column2：Call Chang-Hoon Nam and convince him to help. *Meet with Chang-Hoon Nam in 12 hours. *Read Chang-Hoon's message. [Optional] *Talk to Chang-Hoon.
- column3：Talk to Nix and convince him to help. *Meet with Nix at the Arasaka Memorial in 6 hours. *Read Nix's message. [Optional] *Talk to Nix.
- column4：Talk to Sandra and convince her to help. *Meet Sandra at the park in 8 hours. *Read Sandra's message. [Optional] *Talk to Sandra.

*Call Mr. Hands. [Optional]
**Use the netrunner working for Mr. Hands.
**Meet the netrunner in Kabuki in 10 hours.
**Talk to Yoko.
**Listen to Yoko's proposal. [Optional]

*Send Reed a message with details.
*Wait for Reed to text you.
*Meet Reed at the abandoned hotel.
**Talk to Johnny. (Optional)
*Talk to Reed.
*Talk to the 6th Street gang.
*
**Take the shard.
*Talk to Reed.
*Talk to Johnny.
*Wait for the convoy.
*
**Send Mr. Hands coordinates of the ambush site. (Optional)
*Defeat the NCPD escort.
*Open the truck's rear doors.
*Defeat the MaxTac operators.
*Follow traces left by Songbird.
*Check on Reed. (Optional)
**Talk to Reed. (Optional)

Associated Shards

Notes
*Agreeing to Yoko's proposal allows V to obtain the MaxTac Mantis Blades as a reward.
*If Stadium Love is completed using a non-violent approach beforehand, the 6th Street Gang leader, Will Gunner, will recognize V and comment about their gun handling. If a violent approach was taken, he will have less kind things to say about them.
*V fights four named MaxTac officers, each matching a different roles: Faye Russo (Assault), Asher Peterson (Mantis Blades), Dallas Foster (Heavy), and Jasper Collins (Netrunner).

Trivia
*The quest's name is taken from the Public Enemy song of the same name.

## Blake Croyle
- status：Dependent
- dod：2077 (dependent)
- place_of_death：Kabuki (dependent)
- home：Night City
- gender：Male
- hair_color：Black
- equipment：Defender
- affiliation：Animals

Blake Croyle is a character in and member of the Animals gang.

Biography
Blake Croyle likes to give the impression of a polite, well-spoken man whose job is simply to collect the debts of those he so graciously lent some eurodollars to out of the kindness of his own heart. The truth of the matter, however, is that he is a predator, barely a step above the brutish thugs from the Animals that he himself pays to do his dirty work. And choom, he puts the "shark" in loanshark.

See, he uses a very simple system: first and foremost, don't let your mark realize what a gonk they are right away. Be their friend, offer your generosity...and then, when the time comes, snap the trap shut around their wallet just as they start to see your true colors. And if they don't pay? Well, no big deal—just give them a good scare, smash their things up a little, give them a few bruises or perhaps a harsh shove and a mild concussion to show you mean business, and throw in some threats to their family if they need some extra "encouragment." And, when they open that fat wallet of theirs to pay out the eddies owed, you know they're yours. This process has worked for Croyle countless times before, and with it, he rakes in a fat stack of eddies from across the city.

Nowadays, Mr. Croyle has recently set his ambitious sights on the store chain of one Roger Wang. Even though he never actually lent Wang any money, Blake believes he is owed simply for the privilege of giving Roger "business advice" regarding his money troubles. So, he takes a payout from Wang—along with one of Wang's shops in Kabuki, as "interest." And he has no intention of stopping there.

Unfortunately, it is here that Blake made an error: unlike his other clients who could be cowed and shaken down, Roger took his concerns to one Regina Jones, a local fixer who just so happens to have no love for Mr. Croyle, or his predatory actions against the people in her neighborhood. Soon enough, Regina gets a hold of V and explains Roger's plight to them, before instructing the Solo to put an end to Blake Croyle's business dealings—permanently.

Should V take the job, they find Blake set up in Roger's former shop, reclining and running his business out of a room in the back while occasionally chatting on the holo or to his Animals bodyguards, which V must either sneak or fight past to reach him. From here, V may offer some "business advice" of their own—the unspoken kind, which may be immediately lethal, ending the life of Mr. Croyle right there, or perhaps nonlethal, allowing the loanshark to be gathered up and stuffed into the trunk of a waiting Archer, for express delivery to the fixer to be dealt with as she sees fit.

And so, the career, and life, of Blake Croyle draws to a close, bringing with it a very valuable lesson: Some debts are paid with blood rather than eddies.
