## Gig: Spy in the Jungle
- quest_giver：Mr. Hands
- objective：Find Mark Bana
- district：Pacifica
- sub_district：Dogtown
- location：Longshore Stacks
Organitopia
- tier：3
- enemies：Boris Ribakov
Scavengers
- previous_quest：Get It Together
- next_quest：Money For Nothing (dependent)
The Show Must Go On (dependent)
- reward_item：(missable)
- reward_xp：1832
- reward_sc：167
- reward_eb：3000

Spy in the Jungle is a Gig in .

Walkthrough
After being given the gig, V will be directed to to meet the Brazilian Intelligence Agency agents Steven Santos and Ana Friedman at their room in the Paradise Hotel in the Longshore Stacks, where they provide further information on the gig. They reveal the biomonitor of their mentor and colleague Mark Bana has recently reactivated after he was presumed dead in Dogtown, and he is being hunted by Scavengers led by Boris Ribakov at Organitopia in Terra Cognita. The agents do not have official permission from the BIA to investigate and have hired V to find Bana under the radar.

Upon arriving at Organitopia, scavs will be found guarding the museum's locked-down entrance. After entering through a smashed gate, opening a shuttered window with a Body check of 3, and jacking into an access point to gain further entry, Bana will contact V and indicate that he is okay and hiding deeper inside the museum past a large indoor jungle exhibit. Scavs, including netrunning Spiders, will be found patrolling the area on the ground floor and overhead glass walkways, surrounded by several deactivated landmines and security turrets. If engaging in combat with the scavs, Bana will refuse to open the door into the next area before all enemies are defeated.

In the next area, a megafauna exhibit, Bana directs V to a room in the back where he is hiding. However, when attempting to enter the room, Ribakov will jump down from the ceiling, triggering a mandatory boss battle. Ribakov regularly uses Optical Camo, Sandevistan, and a combo of smoke and flashbang grenades to evade and relocate. He will initially jump up onto the elevated catwalks to snipe at V using a Nekomata, but after losing 30% of his health, he will disappear, summoning several hostile Griffin drones into the arena. After most of the drones have been destroyed, Ribakov will reappear, this time fighting on the ground level using his Smart SMG , and occasionally spawning several holographic decoys of himself. While distracting, his decoys have very little health, and cannot inflict damage. Throughout the fight, Ribakov may attempt to quickhack V from afar; at 5% health, he will spawn several additional decoys on both the upper and lower levels, and become capable of using the System Collapse quickhack. Once defeated, Pizdets and the shard Contract Objective: Terminate Katya Karelina can be looted from his body.

Ana will contact V again and listen in after entering a hidden room where "Bana" is hiding, revealed to actually be a woman named Katya Karelina using a voice changer implant to impersonate Bana. She reveals that she interrogated the real Bana for SovOil before he died, but claims that she wasn't responsible for his death. Ana orders V to kill Katya before hanging up. V will then have the option to kill Katya outright, or make a deal with her to let her live in exchange for the location of a secret stash, starting Money For Nothing. She can still be killed after revealing the location of a secret stash. Regardless, V must now take Bana's biomonitor from Katya back to the Brazilian agents. On the way, Steven will text you to ask that you leave the biomonitor at a drop point instead, fearing that Ana will leak the circumstances of Bana's death, causing Brazil to lose out on a multibillion-eurodollar contract with SovOil and anger those involved in the deal. V can deposit the biomonitor at a marked drop point to end the gig immediately, or go back to the agents instead.

:Steven and Ana will be found packing up and preparing to leave while arguing over the fate of the biomonitor. Steven reveals that Brazil is actively holding talks with SovOil as they speak and that the agency knew that Bana was killed by SovOil, but has chosen to ignore it so as to not jeopardize the deal. Ana will state she fully intends to leak the data on the biomonitor to the media and the rest of the agency. V has the option to hand over the biomonitor or personally destroy it. The agent with whom V sided with give V their thanks, while the other will storm out and lean against a railing outside. Mr. Hands will contact V shortly afterwards to close the gig and send their payment.

:Steven will text V after a few days, saying he is back in Night City, and asks to meet in Downtown, starting The Show Must Go On.

:After a few days, Steven can be found at EBM Petrochem Stadium by the Autofixer terminal, having joined BARGHEST as an analyst in order to lay low in Dogtown and is resentful of V for putting him in this situation. When asked, he reveals that Ana returned to Night City and was extradited back to Brazil where she is now imprisoned for treason, and that aside from ending the SovOil deal, the scandal resulted in a mid-level director at the agency being fired and Bana receiving a posthumous medal.

Journal Entry
:Powerful fingers like to poke this little pie called Dogtown. But let's be honest witth ourselves... Without the spygames, without the power struggles between forces we scarcely understand, this place would become a bore like any other. Wouldn't you agree?

:Two Brazilian intelligence agents recently reached out to me. One of their people has gone missing in Dogtown. The person in question is one Mark Bana.
:Naturally, as with all intelligence operations, there is a catch. Several, perhaps. I've identified one already. The agents seem to be acting without the approval of Brazilian Intelligence Agency. Might I advise inquiring as to their true motives.

:Have fun.

Objectives
*Go to the Paradise hotel.
*Go to room 203.
*Talk to the agents.
*Go to Organitopia.
*Find an entrance to Organitopia.
*Talk to Bana.
*Go to the main museum hall.
*Talk to Bana.
*Meet Bana in the room upstairs.
*Defeat Ribakov.
**Destroy the drones.
*Find Bana.
*Enter the secret room.
*Talk to the stranger.
*Talk to Katya.
*Confront Katya.
*Take the biomonitor.
*Leave the area.
*Deliver the biomonitor to the agents.
**Read the message from Steven Santos. [Optional]
**Deposit the biomonitor in the fixer's drop point. [Optional]

*Talk to the agents.
*Leave the room.

Associated Shards

Notes
*After completing this gig, the iconic smart pistol can be obtained in a hidden stash inside the abandoned diner behind the basketball court where V first met Reed.
*Even if Katya is spared, she will later be neutralized by Scavengers. Her body can be found southwest of the Luxor High Wellness Spa.
*Completing this gig will also alter one of the scripted Airdrops that lands at the Tranquil Terrace, changing the transcript of a shard and adding an additional shard.

See also
*Money For Nothing
*The Show Must Go On

## Gig: Sr. Ladrillo's Private Collection
Sr. Ladrillo's Private Collection is a Gig in .

Walkthrough
Padre will call V and task them to steal a set of recordings from Sr. Ladrillo, pimp and proprietor of Dicky Twister, with an optional objective to do so undetected. At the front door, one can bribe $100 or convince the guard using sufficient Technical Ability to let them through. V's target is in Ladrillo's office, which is the glass room that can be seen above the dance floor. To reach it, one will need to proceed through the club and reach the stairs in the hostile area in the back.

With very high Technical Ability, one can also open a locked door from the alley behind the establishment and reach a storage room past the main guards. With high Body, one can also open a double door in the alley, or jump to the roof and open a door leading directly to Sr. Ladrillo's office.

There are several guards and cameras on the top floor. When you reach the office, Saulo Capon, one of Ladrillo's lieutenants, will be standing near the computer. Neutralize him before stealing the data. V can also disable any remaining cameras from this terminal.

Leave the establishment via the nearby doors to complete this gig.

Journal Entry
:Saint Augustine once wrote: When one has a healthy sense of smell, he will immediately recognize the stench of sin. Well, even anyone with a sinus infection in this city can smell the fuckfests over at Dicky Twister. This gay strip club is full of chicos with glazed, dead eyes who will do anything you desire for an extra eddie tucked into their thongs.
:The stench coming from that place finally wafted into NCPD command. My little rats tell me they plan to kick down the door any day now. That's bad news. The owner of Dicky Twister, a pimp called Sr. Ladrillo, is no gonk - and a fanatic for recordkeeping. He has a computer full of data thanks to spying tech in his VIP rooms. We're talking politicians, suits, crime bosses, celebrities (maybe even the cops themselves)... If the boys in blue get their hands on these recordings, Ladrillo's geniusly built house of cards collapses, leaving the whole district in chaos. And chaos isn't in our best interest at the moment.
:Klep those recordings at the Dicky Twister before the cops do. Thankfully, the Lord has blessed us - Ladrillo is currently out of town. But better to make haste, for ignoring divine assistance is a sin in its own right.

Objectives
*Go to Dicky Twister.
*Get to Sr. Ladrillo's office.
*Steal the compromising material from within Dicky Twister.
*Get out of Dicky Twister.

Associated Shards
*Archived Conversation: Lena and Otis
*Archived Conversation: Maria Costa and Sebastian "Padre" Ibarra

See also
*Señor Ladrillo/Computers

Notes
*Unique dialogue can trigger in Dicky Twister during the gig, where Johnny Silverhand will mention being at the club before with Kerry. He says, "Huh, last time I was here with Kerry, this Latino hunk gave us a lap dance. Cheeks so smooth I could almost see my own reflection." When a surprised V says, "I thought you preferred girls," Johnny will respond with, "Mostly. Now and then I swung both ways. The more the merrier."

## Gig: Talent Academy
Talent Academy is a Gig in .

Walkthrough
V meets Mr. Hands' netrunner Baird near the entrance of the academy. Baird briefs V on his cover-up story and their main objective: reaching Fiona Vargas' office to steal all the tax-related data in their computer after pretending to be a recruiter for a San Diego sports team. V may ask for more details about their cover-up story: the netrunner declines to elaborate since V's fake identity is only supposed to get them into the facility and they shouldn't speak about themselves once inside.

:While chatting with the barman upon entering the Academy, V can tell him they work for a San Diego sports team. Another man then turns to V and starts asking inquisitive questions about specific people from the staff of their supposed club. Without any good answer from V, a suspicious guard is called to take V for another security check. After the check fails, every Academy member turns hostile to V.

:V can tell the Barman they don't want to chat. One of the kids on exhibition will crack the glass screen in front of him, and this will cause the bartender to leave. Nobody will be watching the nearby door marked Personnel only, and they can use it to sneak into the staff only areas.

:V can sneak into the underground facility by going directly to their right after exiting the elevator to the Exhibition Hall. A guard is monitoring an access to a technical back office where the Academy's netrunner works. There is a computer V can use to disconnect the surveillance system. A vent hole in the wall provides access to a technical shaft from which V can drop in a lab in the underground facility and meet Dr. Vargas. Double jump is required to go back in this tunnel through the ceiling.

Fiona's office is located one floor below the main floor, entering the office seems to cause the door to lock behind V. Upon entering the office, V will find Tommie Walker trying to find something in the drawers and spend some time talking to him. When trying to steal the data from Fiona's terminal, it will fail and Fiona will walk in. After some talking, Fiona will make V an offer to leak some data of low importance. One can ask about Tommie's chances of getting signed and accept Fiona's offer to leak the data and ensure that Tommie gets signed. Regardless of which option is chosen, the rewards are the same and Mr Hands is satisfied. Note that the elevator is disabled after the quest, and the exhibition hall will be inaccessable.

She will prompt V to leave, while they can decide to kill her right there. V can choose to kill Fiona Vargas after they decided what to do about her offer. If V kills her, Johnny will appear and express satisfaction about it, and V can grab Fiona's elevator key, which can shortcut to the ground floor.

Once the quest is completed, V can find Tommie Walker helping his dad David Walker at the EBM Petrochem Stadium. If V shut down the facility and let Tommie's father know, he'll resent them for shutting down their only chance at getting out of Dogtown.

Journal Entry
:Can you believe some people avoid paying their taxes? Shocking, I know. Someone needs to put a stop to it. Who is guilty of such heinous crimes, you might ask? Sports scouts who fly in from all across the globe to the center run by Fiona Vargas. They sign contracts with promising athletes, wire sizeable transfers and dodge taxes while they're at it. Our client isn't thrilled.
:You'll be acquiring any data linked to Fiona's clients and their contracts. Getting in won't be easy, which is why you'll have the help of my netrunner near the site. Best of luck, V.

## Gig: The Man Who Killed Jason Foreman
The Man Who Killed Jason Foreman is a Gig in .

Walkthrough
V witnesses local residents mourning of Jason Foreman in a dirty courtyard in Longshore Stacks. Mr. Hands instructed them to speak to Briana, the client. Briana explains that one the Stacks' younger residents, Jason Foreman, has recently been killed by a BARGHEST super killer, Leon Rinder.

V has to use their scanner to investigate the clues around the courtyard, mostly holes in the wall splashed with blood, massive footprints in the mud, a box of fired bullets and a fallen failsafe on the roof of a nearby container.

Then Briana gives V a encrypted shard to read. A hacking puzzle unlocks it. A conversation between Jason and Slava Makarov, a scavenger, leads V to a former motel in Pacifica, Los Osos. Jason was indeed an intermediary between a man supplying top-tier Militech chrome and the scavengers.

V can investigate new clues in the former motel - now a scavengers' hideout - to learn more about Rinder's actions. Rinder himself is locked in a room on third floor and is guarded by a heavily chromed scavenger. V finds out that most of Rinder's chrome has been sold to scavengers by Rinder himself. He reaches for a pistol when V enters, but in his convalescent state, he only manages to knock it out of his own reach.

:Completing the Investigate the area. [Optional] objective unlocks the dialog option "Whatever I did"? Let me enlighten you. when V confronts Rinder.
:It appears that one of Slava Makarov's suggestions pushed Jason into agressively demanding a bigger share to the supplier, Leon Rinder, which may have contributed to his death by leading the latter into cyberpsychosis.

:Take Rinder's dog tags from his body and bring them to Briana Dolson to complete the gig.

:Take Rinder's dog tags and bring them to Briana Dolson to complete the gig.

:Leon gives V the coordinates of his personal stash, a garage in Terra Cognita, starting the quest Addicted To Chaos. Take Rinder's dog tags and bring them to Briana Dolson to complete the gig.

:When questioning Rinder after completing the Investigate the area. [Optional] objective, choosing the dialogue option "Whatever I did"? Let me enlighten you. will make V realize that Rinder suffers from cyberpsychosis.
:One must also choose Put gun to Rinder's head | Choose your next words carefully dialog option, which will give V an option to force Rinder to contact Regina Jones for help.
:If one chooses to send Rinder to Regina, V will still get his dog tags to finish the gig. He will also send them the coordinates to his stash, starting the mission Addicted To Chaos. After a few days Rinder will contact V via text message and will thank them for making him contact Regina. Sometime after that, Rinder will text V again, this time saying he wants to take responsibility and compensate the community for his bad deeds. He intends to offer Briana some eddies, conceding that it "won't change much" and is "prolly[sic] gonk anyway." V can either encourage or discourage this idea. Allowing Rinder to contact Briana proves his intuition correct. Briana will pull V aside the next time V visits that area of the Longshore Stacks to berate V for not honoring the intent of the gig's contract. She says that she doesn't believe she will ever forgive Rinder, and revealing his true fate to the others would 'break' them due to lack of closure. At the end of her tirade, she declares that V is no longer welcome in her area of the Stacks.

Journal Entry
:The Stacks have seen better days. Leon Rinder, one of Hansen's former triggermen, killed eight civilians in cold blood. We don't know why he was there, or what caused him to snap, or why Hansen kicked him out of BARGHEST. Lots of questions, not many answers and only one one thing for certain - the victims' families want Rinder dead. But first, he'll need to be located. That's where you come in. Head to the Stacks, investigate the scene and talk to Briana Dolson, the Stacks' unofficial representative. Perhaps you'll uncover a lead there.

## Gig: The Union Strikes Back
The Union Strikes Back is a Gig in .

Walkthrough

This gig involves finding and neutralizing Vic Vega, the head of a private security company called C-Team that hires itself out to corporations to keep employees in line and break up unions. This sounds like a straight-forward assassination, but what Rogue Amendiares does not clearly communicate is that she would prefer that Vega be brought to her alive, and no other guards or workers in the office building that C-Team has rented out should be touched at all.

However, keeping Vega alive isn't a firm requirement to successfully complete the gig. Rogue will complain if anyone other than Vega is incapacitated or killed, and she's unenthusiastic if Vega is killed instead of being knocked out and delivered to her, but the gig's reward remains the same in all outcomes. For the optimal outcome where Rogue is satisfied, V must infiltrate the building's second floor, knock out Vega, and carry the unconscious Vega outside the building to a waiting vehicle. Otherwise, storm the building, kill Vega, and leave to finish the gig quickly.

The building has four points of entry: the front door (distract the receptionist to grab the access key on her desk), a garage with two doors that can be opened with Technical Ability or Body, and an open window on the second floor that can be reached from the roof of the garage. There is also an open window in Vega's office, but this is difficult to reach and Vega is facing it. On the upside, the building has no surveillance cameras or turrets to worry about.

V can enter via the second floor window, sneak into Vega's office and either kill him or take him down. If V takes him down, then the easiest way to get his body out of the building without alerting the guards is to drop out of the office's window while carrying him. The fixer's transport will be a few steps away. Another strategy is to carry him downstairs when the guard patrolling the staircase is out of the way. At the bottom of the stairs is a door on the right to a security office with one guard. It is possible to pass through the security office when the guard is looking away to reach the garage and then exit the building.

Once the gig is completed, Rogue calls to assess V's performance and send the reward. If V completes the mission without killing anyone else, Rogue comments about how the community has suffered enough, so she'll chalk it up as a "win."

Journal Entry
:At first I thought it was just rumors and the kind of drunken bullshit you hear at a bar at 3 AM, y'know? But when you hear the same story from three separate witnesses, you start taking an interest. Now that my informant confirmed the accounts, it's time to dive into the action.
:Look, I don't wanna sound like some naggy old crone, but back in my day workers knew how to stand up for themselves. Instead of fixers they had unions to fight for their rights. I know, I know. Anyway, now with the unions gone, these workers can't afford to hire fixers on starvation-level salaries. Lucky for them, I like to do some pro bono work from time to time. You know, a little something for the public good.
:Onto the fine detes. Vic Vega - the kind of scum who writes "cracking skulls" in the hobby section of his CV. Well, that's exactly what he's doing in Rancho Coronado. Cracking skulls. Not only that, but he's got the full backing of the corp execs, who'd rather give their workers brain damage instead of a 2% raise.
:Vega and his people've been terrorizing the whole neighborhood. Workers've had enough - who the fuck wouldn't agree? You're gonna find Vic Vega and end that psycho for good. Maybe then the corpos'll realize they crossed the line.

Objectives
*Get inside C-Team's building.
*Find Vic Vega.
*Neutralize Vic Vega.
*Take Vic Vega's body to the designated location.
*Put Vic Vega in the fixer's transport.

Trivia
*The gig's name is a reference to Star Wars: Episode V – The Empire Strikes Back.
*Both "Vincent" and "Vic" Vega are references to the Pulp Fiction and Reservoir Dogs characters Vincent Vega and Vic Vega.

Treating Symptoms is a Gig in .

Walkthrough

Indira Barazza has fallen victim to blackmail by Milko Alexis, a Netrunner affiliated with the Voodoo Boys. He's threatened to hack Indira's lungs if she refuses to comply with their demands. The victim reached out to Mr. Hands, who in turn hired V to travel to Milko's base of operations in Dogtown, the Luxor High Wellness Spa, in order to make direct contact with Milko and deal with those that stand in their way.

:While navigating through the base, V encounters their supplier, who has a deal with the Voodoo Boys and supplies them with implants used for research purposes. V then asks if he knows about Milko's whereabouts, to which he responds that he doesn't.

:
::The supplier argues back, claiming that he had the situation under control until V showed up.

:
::V pushes the supplier against the wall to coerce him into talking. He still refuses, prompting V to punch him in the face until he finally shares what he knows.
::The supplier explains that the Voodoo Boys take most of the implants and dismantle them in order to study their software and research new exploits. The leftover implants are installed in old combat robots. Of these robots, one in particular has proven useful to them.
::He then offers to patch into the server room where the robots are kept and sabotage the servers to render them explosive.

:
::V attempts to bribe the supplier into divulging information. He accepts the money, explains the purpose of the implants, and offers to sabotage the server room where the robots are stored.

:
::Instead of obtaining information from Kyle, V opted to take Kyle out.

V enters the server room, where a large group of Robot R Mk.2s is deployed to eliminate the intruder. After V neutralizes the boss, all of the other robots in the server room self-destruct and the emergency exit protocol is engaged. V follows the emergency exit hallway to find another man standing alongside a jacked-in Milko. He introduces himself as Alan Noël, an undercover NetWatch agent tasked with infiltrating the Voodoo Boys' ranks.
He explains that his mission was to dismantle their criminal network from within, and that he needs Milko alive so that he can piggyback off of his connection and glean as much information as possible. He asks for V to spare Milko in order to continue his mission.

:After V leaves the Voodoo Boys hideout, they receive a call from Mr. Hands. He informs V that Indira Barazza was just added to NetWatch's witness protection list, guarding her against virtually any potential attack.
:Mr. Hands pays V an extra €$8,000 for their efforts.
:Later on V gets a message from Alan Noël where he informs V about successful operation of uncovering a puppet master behind blackmail criminal network will send V an additional €$2,000. If V is a Corpo and used the associated dialogue option during their original conversation, the message will trigger the side job Corpo of the Month, and Noel will inform V of stash he left for them near the Voodoo Boys' base in Luxor Heights. The stash will include more money as well as Netrunner skill shard.

:V declines Alan's offer, instead neutralizing him and Milko in order to fulfill the contract as originally planned.

:Alan Noël chastises V for ruining an expensive Netwatch operation, but lets them leave without conflict.

Journal Entry
:Indira Barazza wouldn't be the first or the last to fall prey to the Voodoo Boys' blackmail. What's interesting is the gang seems to have only the technical employees of her corp in their sights. They made our client an offer she couldn't refuse – cooperate or die. Indira chose a third route: she called me. The Voodoo Boy threatening to hack her lungs is one Milko Alexis. See to it that he kindly leaves her the fuck alone.

Objectives
*Get inside the Voodoo Boys' base.
*Find Milko Alexis.
**Talk to the supplier. [Optional]
*Neutralize Milko Alexis.
**Talk to the Netrunner. [Optional]
*Leave the Voodoo Boy's base.

Associated Shards

See also
*Luxor High Wellness Spa/Computers
*Alan Noël/Computers

Notes

## Gig: Until Death Do Us Part
Until Death Do Us Part is a Gig in .

Walkthrough

Wakako will contact V (character) and request that infiltrate a Charter Hill penthouse in order to steal a shard containing the client's depository receipts. Wakako also offers a bonus if the gig is completed without setting off alarms.

The penthouse can be accessed by the main elevator. there are a number of security systems in place:
*Two Wyvern drones - one inside and one patrolling the perimeter.
*A robot in a room on the second floor.
*Three active security cameras across the area.
*Two couple turrets in the main room, which become active if the alarm is triggered.
*Red security gateways will set up the alarm if walked through while active.

The drones and robot can be destroyed without triggering the alarm, provided this is done while remaining undetected. The target shard is on the second floor, in the room immediately to the left at the top of the stairs. The computer in the same office as the target shard can be used to trigger an "emergency reset" of the security system, which will permanently disable the drones, turrets, and robot, as well as shut off the red security gateways for one minute. The exterior porch can also be accessed while the security gates are active via an open window in the dining room. A bathroom on the 2nd floor can be opened with a Tech attribute check and contains a loot box. Computers around the house contain details of Mrs. Gutierrez's underhanded attempts to destroy the life of her ex-husband.

Exit the building drop off the shard at a drop point to complete the gig.

Journal Entry
:Would you like to hear about my fourth husband? He was very lazy, gullible, and filthy rich. I divorced him as quickly as I could and never made so much money in such a short time. With that said, can I really blame Mrs. Gutierrez for stripping Mr. Gutierrez down to the last enny? Of course not. In fact, I'd like to meet her lawyers.
:But enough about Mrs. Gutierrez. Our client happens to be the injured party, Mr. Gutierrez. He lost his car and luxury penthouse, now the poor fool has barely anything to live in because he left his depository receipts in their old apartment (the locks are already changed). You'll have to retrieve them, because our new divorcee isn't going to give them back out of the kindness of her heart.
:The penthouse is on the last floor of the building. Don't worry, I'm providing you with elevator access.
:For obvious reasons, Mr. Gutierrez is counting on your utmost discretion. If things go quietly, he'll toss in extra.

Objectives

*Find Gutierrez's office.

*Steal the shard with the depository receipts.
*Escape the building.
*Deposit the shard in the Drop Point.

## Gig: Woman of La Mancha
Woman of La Mancha is a Gig in .

Walkthrough

Regina Jones contacts V with a new job, which is to find Anna Hamill in Kabuki market. A few people can be asked for information on her whereabouts. Imad can be seen arguing with a food vendor. While the vendor will say she is only there to sell food, Imad can be either bribed, intimidated by Streetkid V, or persuaded by Nomad V to reveal Anna's location. Alternatively, Eve can only be bribed and Robert Rainwater can give the information free of charge, provided V's Street Cred is 16 or higher.

:

:

:
::V threatens to tell the Tyger Claws that Imad is harboring Anna, which leads him to telling them that Anna Hamill is staying in Motel Kabuki.

:

Anna is staying in a nearby motel. The front door can be opened by paying for a room, the back door can be opened with enough Technical Ability, or V can go up the stairs of the building in front and find a way to cross over. Once inside, V may find Anna's room number on the terminal in the receptionist's office or look for it on their own.

After entering Anna's room, it is time to confront her. V will have to deal with three consecutive timed dialogue choices. In order to get a peaceful outcome, V has to say "Here to warn you." in the first and "Just wanna help you." in the second. For the third choice, if V says "It doesn't matter." and is a Nomad, they can then convince Anna to leave Night City. If the other option is selected, Anna will still stand down but will not leave town or join the Nomads.

Regardless of how V makes Anna drop her investigation, they can then leave the area and complete the Gig.

Journal Entry
:Anna Hamill is a blue-blooded cop, through and through. The kind you'd expect to see in some NCPD promo. Beautiful, smart, honest to a fault. In other words, a really bad fit for Night City.

:Her NCPD colleagues are another story. They all have back problems from sitting on fat wallets.

:This current case Hamill's working has them all breaking out in hives. She's digging into the smuggling racket in Kabuki market, which - if she makes any real headway - means bad biz for her cop buddies' finances. They want someone from outside the precinct to nip this thing in the bud.

:Normally that's where I'd leave it, but I wanna add one more thing. I kinda feel bad for the girl. Rather she not flatline if you can avoid it. Convince her to skip town, or drop the case and make a career change at least.

Gillean Jordan is a character in .

Biography
Gillean Jordan is a news reporter and presenter on Network News 54.

In 2077, she gives a live report of the assault that was made during the Arasaka dashi parade taking place in Japantown, Westbrook.

She can also be seen with Arif Iqbal in the Black Sapphire during You Know My Name. Afterwards, she can be found doing a news report just inside of Night City International and Translunar during The Killing Moon.

Notes
*While reporting live during the dashi parade, V can move in front of the camera to interrupt the recording, much to Gillean's annoyance.
*Gillean is a client of Zane Jagger, purchasing her clothes from him at Jinguji.
*Gillean's news broadcasts can be heard on every radio station in Night City, except 107.3 Morro Rock Radio.
*Gillean's news broadcasts reflect the events of all the main quests of the game.

## Gimme Danger
Gimme Danger is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough

Journal Entry
:Our crazed ronin shows no signs of slowing his roll. We barely get intel from Wakako about the parade and Takemura's already hatching some hairbraned scheme in Japantown. He wants to meet at the market? Fine, let's parley, but you already know where I stand. Don't let him strong-arm you into anything. Who knows how many loose screws are bouncing around that skull at this point...

Objectives
*Meet Takemura.
*Go over the plan with Takemura.
*Take the shard.
*Go over the plan with Takemura.
*Break into the security room.
*Infect the security system.
*Go over the plan with Takemura.
*Sit beside Takemura.
*Go to Arasaka Industrial Park.
*Follow Takemura.
*Get onto the roof.
*Follow Takemura.
*Go over the plan with Takemura.
*Scan the area.
*Keep scanning. [Optional]
*Talk to Takemura.
*Go over the plan with Takemura.
*Get up.
*Return to street level.
*Steal the truck. [Optional]
*Persuade Guard [Optional] [Corpo Life Path]
*Break into Arasaka Industrial Park.
*Get inside the warehouse.
*Hack the float.
*Talk to Takemura.
*Leave Arasaka Industrial Park.
*Talk to Takemura.

Gallery

Bakeneko Picture Takemura.png|Takemura's photo of the bakeneko

Notes

*The can be found in a shipping container with number "667", at the end of the exterior loading dock outside of the warehouse. Several notes on computers around the warehouse point to its presence in that specific shipping container. Inside the container is a mine you can disarm with 8 Intelligence. West of the main entrance to the warehouse in loading dock 4 is where you'll find the container.
*If V has the Corpo Lifepath, when scanning from the rooftop, they can overhear a guard near the front talk about an information leak, and can persuade the guard to let them enter and walk freely without turning guards hostile. Takemura is even amazed that their trick worked. Scanning the guard must immediately happen upon accepting the quest to unlock this avenue.
*If V begins shooting enemies while on the roof during the investigation and is spotted the quest will always turn loud, even if not currently spotted when approaching. Killing the Mech during this time will also play Takemura's voice line as if the heist has already started.

## Glitter
Glitter is an addictive psychedelic drug in .

Overview

Glitter is an inhaled drug that is highly addictive, and very easy to overdose on. It is made up of multiple substances: including a strong stimulant, a psychadelic similar to LSD, nitrous oxide, epinephrine, and lysergic acid. It also has a beta blocker (atenolol), likely to reduce the physical side effects of the stimulant. The stimulant may have some chemical similarity to cathinone.

It is made and produced by the Tyger Claws, and was possibly invented by James Reddington and Jin Araki, though their individual contributions to its creation are disputed between them.

Database Entry

- transcript：Glitter is a highly addictive psychedelic drug and recent arrival on Night City's streets. The new substance quickly drew Night City's full attention. First, it's truly strong stuff, even for the booster-and-braindance glutted residents of Night City. Second, glitter is illegal, immediately giving it the irresistible aura of "forbidden fruit." Finally: glitter kills. One off-dose or weak nervous system and glitter will have those neurons firing white-hot (hence the name, perhaps). Death is inevitable.

引文：Our marina is an exclusive place for relaxation and polite entertainment.（Macy Sherrier）

Gold Beach Marina is located in Downtown, in the City Center district of Night City.

Overview
Gold Beach Marina is an exclusive harbor, found on Gold Beach street in Downtown. It is privately owned, and has its own security detail. Some of Night City's most influential, wealthy and famous people have their yachts moored at the Gold Beach Marina, including Josh Kavorkin, Christian Cole and L. B. Kovachek. The marina is known for the loud, excessive parties taking place on the GEIshhhhA, a yacht owned by celebrity entertainer Bartolomeo Mordellini.

In 2077 the marina closed for some time, as it had contracted a new security company, which installed new security systems on the premises. At the same time fixer Dino Dinovic was hired by a corporate client to steal recordings of councilwoman Eva Cole from Mordellini's parties.

Gordon is a secondary character in .

Biography
Gordon was a Security Specialist in a Trauma Team extraction unit Squad Bravo, that also included Knapp, Stratter, Dean, Withers and Nadia.

Shortly after Nadia joined, the squad was tasked with a rescue mission after receiving an emergency call from Pacifica. They were were supposed to rescue a Platinum member known as Apex. Upon arriving in Pacifica, the medic group found Apex trapped in an unfinished skyscraper after he killed a boss of the Animals.

The squad's lead EMT, Knapp, proceeded to help the client and requested Nadia's immediate attention. Meanwhile, the Security Specialists, Gordon and Stratter, held the line against oncoming hostiles. Then, Gordon sustained a gunshot injury to the neck. Nadia, reluctant to help Knapp tend to Apex's wounds, attempted to save her colleague's life instead, but she did not manage to help him in time and Gordon died.

## Gorilla Arms
- caption：Classic and reliable replacements for natural limbs, suited for all kinds of hard labor.
- manufacturer：Arasaka
- type：Arms
- attribute：Body
- attribute_attunement：ArmsDamage
- attribute_value：0.5

- effects：Gorilla Arms are lightweight, efficient and hard-hitting arm replacement cyberware. +- to Body Attribute checks. Deal Physical damage.
-% Bleeding chance
- source：Ripperdocs

The Gorilla Arms are Cyberware for the Arms in .

Overview
This implant allows you to deal more Physical damage in melee combat, and have a -% chance to apply a Bleed effect.

During Attribute checks, your Body Attribute is increased by -.

Acquisition
*Can be purchased from any Ripperdoc after reaching level 10. Quality increases every 10 levels.

Behind the Scenes

引文：Some of the first widespread cyberware swapped manual laborer's arms for replacements powered by pistons and hydraulics so they could lift heavier loads. Strong Arms are the cutting-edge descendants of those primitive models. While the old tech used clumsy and slow cranial electrodes for control, Strong Arms, like most late generation cyberware, feature real-time 1:1 synaptic junctions that operate as fast as the user can think. Rather than mechanical actuators, their strength now comes from synthetic muscles made of electric-field activated shape-memory alloys that easily fit within the normal profile of your arm. Apply a layer of Realskinn on top, and no one needs to know you can rip open closed doors like they are made out of paper; though if you want, bright colors and trademark patterns can advertise what you're packing.

Notes
*Though previous versions of Cyberpunk 2077 show Arasaka models, alternate models include the Hausstok-W forearms by Moore Technologies. During an infomercial on the N54 channel, the host punches holes in a concrete pillar and then mentions for an extra premium, the manufacturer will supply thermal or stun modules, which is inline with the other available versions.

Unnamed father

引文：There are no clean hands. But it is important how they become dirty. [...] You dirty your hands for money. I - in the name of principles.（Takemura to V）

Goro Takemura (Japanese: 竹村 五郎, Hepburn: Takemura Goro) is the former personal bodyguard of Saburo Arasaka. He is a stoic man of honor and fiercely loyal to Arasaka, but finds himself betrayed and out of his element in Night City.

Biography
Early life
Goro Takemura was born in the slums of Chiba-11, the district with the highest murder rate in all of Japan. It's unknown what became of his mother; as his father worked full-time in a kitchen, Goro's grandmother used to tell him stories about yōkai.

Arasaka military transporters would occasionally pass through Chiba-11, picking children from the district to conscript into their army. As a kid, he and other young boys would go to wash their shirts in a polluted canal, because of a rumor that only the cleanest children would get chosen. Arasaka eventually chose him, a moment that lifted him out of poverty, and that he compared with having won the lottery. In the army, his basic needs were provided for more consistently and appropriately than before, and he would go on to join Arasaka's special forces division. Once his efforts were recognized, he was offered attendance at the Arasaka academy - an actual education - and graduated at the top of his class.

At some point Saburo Arasaka came to recruit a new personal bodyguard out of the one hundred soldiers the corporation deemed most skilled and loyal (a recruitment pool which may or may not be identical with the one for service at the Arasaka Family Compound). His loyalty to the family was beyond question, and he idolized his CEO.

As Saburo's personal protector, Takemura received one-of-a-kind cyberware, including an endoskeleton.

Takemura personally trained the cyberninja Sandayu Oda, who served as the bodyguard of Hanako Arasaka.

2077
In 2077, Takemura accompanied Saburo Arasaka to Konpeki Plaza, Night City, where the CEO intended to confront his son Yorinobu for stealing the Relic. Takemura was about to commence a full sweep of the penthouse, but was ordered out of the room by Saburo only moments before he would have uncovered V and Jackie Welles. After he and Adam Smasher had left, the hidden mercenaries were witness to a family argument, during the sad climax of which Yorinobu strangled his father in the heat of anger.

Immediately after the deed, the murderer alerted security, claiming that Saburo had been poisoned. He took advantage of Takemura's visible shock to assert his authority as the head of Arasaka family and corporation, ordering him to find the murderers before leaving the suite.

After V and Jackie had escaped Konpeki Plaza, Takemura tracked down Dexter DeShawn, who had set up the heist. As Jackie Welles had succumbed to his injuries and DeShawn had shot V and dumped their body into the landfill to cover his tracks, Takemura forced him to lead him to V. After he had dragged V out and attempted to bargain for his life, Takemura unceremoniously killed DeShawn with one single shot. Then Takemura called Yorinobu and told that the murderer had been found, and that he would deliver them in around an hour. Shortly after leaving the landfill, a group of assassins sent by Yorinobu approached them by motorcycle and attempted to kill Takemura and V. After beating the assassins, Takemura was injured, and V was in critical condition. Takemura told V to call someone who could save them, and V made every effort to call Delamain to deliver them to Viktor Vektor, and then passed out.

After V recovered, Takemura contacted V to discuss how to take revenge against Yorinobu, calling him to account for his crime. Takemura revealed that he initially attempted to contact Evelyn Parker, who had an intimate relationship with Yorinobu Arasaka, but failed. Then V told Takemura that Anders Hellman should be helpful, but Takemura said Hellman was just a pawn and had left Arasaka. He claimed the existence of powerful allies, who would be able to help clear their names and remove Yorinobu from power. But anyway, Takemura still advised V to find Parker and Hellman first.

After V found Anders Hellman, who escaped from the Kang Tao AV hit by EMP (and a rocket) and was stationed at a gas station, V called Takemura to come and ask Hellman some questions.

Later, Takemura tried to contact an old friend of his: Hanako Arasaka's bodyguard - Sandayu Oda. He arranged a personal meeting, giving V the opportunity to tell the truth about Saburo Arasaka's death. However, Oda refused to listen. While letting them go, he threatened that the next time he would not be as lenient. Whether by accident or on purpose, Oda let slip that Hanako was visiting Night City for the parade during Aratama-matsuri festival.

Deeming that this was the only chance to reveal the truth to Hanako Arasaka, Takemura sought help from V for approaching Hanako during the parade. They asked Wakako Okada the information about the parade.

Having formed the plan to jump on the dashi float from which Hanako Arasaka would be giving her speech, he invited V to help him test a virus he picked up in Kabuki on the parade ground's CCTV room, an attempt which was successful, and gave them full access to the cameras in the area. Afterwards, with or without V's help, he conducts a reconnaissance of the Arasaka Industrial Park, where the floats were in the process of being assembled. Once again, V helped Takemura upload the virus from before into Hanako's float.

During the parade, V took out the three snipers who would have prevented Takemura from getting on the float alive, only to hear that a netrunner had overridden the virus-granted access. While taking out the netrunner, V encountered Oda, who had been trying in vain to warn Adam Smasher about security concerns the entire time. He told V that they and Takemura should've left the city, like he told them last time they met. V finally defeated him with the help of Takemura's advice, having been Oda's teacher. After asking his ally to spare the defeated foe, he entered the float and tried to explain himself to Hanako Arasaka. However, Hanako tried to flee instead of listening, so Takemura shot her with a sedative administered via a tranquillizer gun that V didn't know about. He tells V to run before they unplug themself from the network, alarmed at what had just happened.

Having abducted the late CEO's daughter, Takemura took her to an abandoned apartment building he had been staying at, and called V to hurry over. After V came to the hideout, they tried to convince Hanako of what happened in Konpeki Plaza, telling Hanako about the Relic in the process. However, Hanako reactivated her tracker and Arasaka forces almost immediately stormed the building, shooting the wall down. V could see Takemura shielding Hanako from the gunfire with his own body, before they were hit by a stray EMP grenade. After they regained their vision, disoriented and staggered, V could see Hanako being carried away by Adam Smasher, who departed in the AV that had destroyed the wall. An Arasaka soldier ordered V to get on the ground, to which the floor collapsed under them both, and they fell.

When V regained consciousness after their fall, on top of a pile of rubble, Takemura yelling at them to run could be heard faintly from the third floor. The engram of Johnny Silverhand told them that Takemura was already dead and also advised them to run.

:V fled from Takemura's hideout, who fought the upcoming Arasaka forces until he was eventually killed.

:V ignored Johnny's advice and returned to the second floor to save Takemura, who was pinned down with poor cover in his bedroom, fighting off Arasaka soldiers with a Shingen. Scolding V for coming back only to die along with him, Takemura then proved himself wrong by helping them fight out of the apartment building.
After escaping the ambush Takemura urges V to split up, thinking they would both have a better chance of escaping Arasaka's notice on their own. Afterwards, he was contacted by Hanako, who had him brought to a secure location. In a text message to V after Hanako contacts them, he expresses gratitude for his life and concern for their wellbeing.

In the motel V escapes to after the ambush, Hanako Arasaka contacts them via proxy and reveals that Takemura had, at some point prior, placed a tracker on V.

:
::After witnessing the mercenary's attack on Arasaka Tower and the decline of the Arasaka Corporation, Takemura acknowledged that he had failed avenging Saburo's death. In his last message to V he talked about jisei: while he had found many of the ancient samurais' death poems to be very beautiful, he was not one of their number and so could not write one himself. Instead, he had decided to leave the mercenary a message, closing it with the heart-felt wish that they would burn in hell.

:
::Takemura and Anders Hellman rendezvoused with V at Misty's Esoterica, noting their deteriorating health. The three proceeded to the Arasaka Estate to extract Hanako from her brother's forces. After a successful rescue, the four of them took an AV to Arasaka Tower so that Saburo's daughter could confront the board of directors.
On the way, Hellman's comment about V's physical condition angered Takemura. He defended the mercenary so vehemently that Hanako interrupted the conversation to steer it back towards planning.

::At Arasaka Tower, he split from the rest of the group to meet with Oda (if V had not killed him) and those soldiers whose loyalty to Hanako he could guarantee. On the way to the Arasaka board meeting, Takemura heard from his ally that Saburo had survived as an engram. He expressed shock and disbelief, claiming that Saburo would have told him. It didn't take him long to regain his composure: when Saburo's engram berated the board of directors, he didn't bother to hide his amusement.

::The meeting was interrupted by Yorinobu attempting to destroy the Kiji and Hato factions by means of a violent coup. On Hanako's orders, Takemura and V fought their way through the Taka soldiers to take Yorinobu prisoner.

::Before reaching Yorinobu, Takemura and V had to overcome Adam Smasher. After defeating the cyborg, Takemura stops V in the hallway to Yorinobu's office to tell them that, as a last service, he would stay behind while V entered the CEO's office. He claimed that if he were to go in, he would kill Yorinobu, voiding V's agreement with Hanako - who ordered not a single hair on her brother's head be harmed.

::A month later, Takemura visited V on the Arasaka Orbital Station at the call of the clinic requesting someone talk to V. Depending on whether V fully trashed their room before his arrival, expressed disgust at the "barbaric" decision to confine V in a cell for "days," or if the room was messy, lamented on how awful a place the clinic is. He revealed that he had been reassigned to Takamatsu, Kagawa, no longer serving as Saburo's bodyguard. When asked about Saburo's revival in Yorinobu's body, he claimed that justice had been served. But V pressed Takemura, asking if he really got his revenge, to which he, biting his tongue, flatly stated he believes Hanako had made the best call.

::However, the reason for his visit was that the procedure had failed and the mercenary was still dying. He urges them not to lose hope, as there are alternatives. Takemura was genuinely shaken when V told him he let them down, betrayed their trust, as he had truly believed Arasaka could save them. On the behalf of Hanako Arasaka, he offered V a possibility of survival: a contract selling them to one Anders Hellman, that would allow them to join the Secure Your Soul program, entering Mikoshi as an engram until such a point where a compatible body could be provided.

::
:::V refused the deal and wished to return to Earth. When Takemura pleaded with them to reconsider, the mercenary replied that they liked him and wouldn't forget him, but they weren't willing to give up something that he never had: freedom. Picking up their things, they walked away from Takemura, who was visibly distraught. While there, he stayed in the chair he was sitting in, surveying the room. Every time his eyes scanned the bed V was just sitting on, he looks away in guilt.

::
:::V accepted the deal, stating that they wanted to live. Takemura replied that it was a good choice, advising them not to wait for their condition to worsen. When V inquired if they would meet again, he expressed his certainty that they would, inviting them to visit him in Kagawa, where he hoped to show them real food.

:
:V contacted FIA agent Solomon Reed for help in removing the Relic, but while the NUSA's surgeons were successful, the surgery left V in a coma. Meanwhile, Takemura and Hanako staged an attack on Arasaka Tower to depose Yorinobu, but their coup failed and Hanako was killed; Yorinobu framed Takemura for his sister's murder, leaving him a wanted fugitive once again, completely shattering his faith in the company he had dedicated his life to. Two years later, Takemura learned that V, who had awoken from their coma, had returned to Night City and successfully removing the Relic and sent them a message. He bitterly congratulated V and informed them of his situation. Reflecting a quotation of an old samurai, "good strong medicine is bitter to the mouth", Takemura remarked that V had been very strong medicine for him.

Development
Conception
CD Projekt RED wanted to tell a more corporate part of the main story, regarding Arasaka. Initially, they had a female character named Ayumi Gozen as a villain, but wanted to instead show a more human side of the corporation. Philipp Weber, Acting Lead Quest Designer at CD Projekt RED, wanted to create a character who was very close to Saburo, sharing his traditional values and believing that Arasaka's actions is morally right. Takemura came to life as a character who — in their own mind — was able to justify that everything they did for Arasaka was for the greater good. He believes in honour and traditional Japanese values. However, as the developers were concerned that players would be unable to empathize, they began to humanize him, wanting to display a character who had been forced to make terrible choices to guarantee his survival. This is the reason behind his likeable personality traits, such as being a foodie, the way he's not very good dealing with technology etc.

Overall, Takemura is supposed to be a character who genuinely believes that what he is doing for Arasaka is the right thing to do.

Developer Notes
*The selfie Takemura sends to V was Philipp Weber's idea, who came up with it after a picture of Takemura's face from a low angle reminded him of a 'dad selfie.' A cinematic designer he spoke to came up with a selection of possible selfies to use, including ones with him looking 'flirty' and 'awkward,' yet his initial favourite remained.
*Philip Weber came up with the idea of a little joke of the elderly man confusing Takemura as a famous celebrity. The idea was later developed by different members of the team, giving birth to the formerly-famous stand-up comedian Hideshi Hino. The team added more dialogue to the scene, scattering posters of Hideshi Hino across the city.
**The Hideshi story line can be further expanded during the Phantom Liberty main quest "You Know My Name" if V spends some time schmoozing with the party guests. V can approach a "Goro Look-alike" sitting at a bar, Johnny will appear with some dialog, and Hideshi will engage in a discussion with V about needing a body double.
*Takemura is a foodie. He has a strong belief in tradition and his belief that food should be prepared in a traditional way, and with care. CD Projekt RED's Paweł Sasko mentioned these traits are still an important reflection of his character.
*Takemura had been supposed to have very unique optics; however, due to time constraints, he had to share Hanako's. After patch 1.2, they changed to brown with a reflective ring around the pupil. According to Philip Weber during a Q&A, his one-of-a-kind optics are an important way to make the player aware of his unique cyberware (even if most of it had been removed or disabled), and a way to distinguish his skillset from Hanako's netrunning abilities. However, Patch 1.3 reverted this change.

Behind the Scenes
The information in was written during the development of the videogame and is outdated in some topics.

引文：Takemura's career peaked when Saburo Arasaka made him his personal bodyguard. That was the culmination of the long road he'd traveled from the gutters of Tokyo, one that took him through countless armed conflicts as an Arasaka soldier. Cyberware screwed into evey inch of the tall, thin frame draped with elegant black-and-white clothing, his face etched with unfazed expertise, he cut the figure of the perfect corporate samurai. Takemura's career tanked when Yorinobu Arasaka accused him failing to prevent his father's murder. Exiled from the organization he had made his life, stripped of titles and dignity, bounty hunters on his trail, he deactivated his implants and started, once more, on the streets. What remained was pure grit, determination and strength of character that allowed him to transform a tragic end into a turning-point.
citation

Notes
*When initially picking up V from the landfill, Takemura drives a red Mizutani Shion Targa MZT - gameplay-wise it is an MZ1, even when scanned.
*During Playing for Time, Takemura mentions to a Streetkid V that his father used to work in the kitchen all his life.
*During Gimme Danger, Takemua tells V that he despises take-out food. Given he has learned to cook, he mentioned that he could had cooked onigiri with cod or grilled salmon, but he doesn't have the ingredients handy.
*During Down on the Street, the elderly man in front of Wakako's Den can mistake Takemura for the former late-night comedian Hideshi Hino. This unlocks some humorous dialogues.
**This dialogue will trigger if V does not accompany Takemura upon his arrival and he has to wait for them. He should then be leaning against the wall next to the entrance.
*The cryptic text messages he sends V after their meeting in Tom's Diner are a reference to the kanji of his name: 竹 (bamboo), 村 (village), 五 (five). Since the game's subtitles render all names in katakana, he introduces himself to Wakako as タケムラゴロウ.
*During a developer stream, the designer who had been responsible for his development wrote in chat: "Takemura has never knew any better. He really believed he was lucky. Saburo could have been like a father to him. That would really distort the view of reality for him."
*After completing the Gimme Danger quest, an additional text exchange with Takemura can trigger under specific circumstances. It will start with him sending V a picture of the bakeneko taken on the rooftop.

Gottfrid Persson is the father of Fredrik Persson and a braindance editor in .

Biography
Gottfrid built up a lucrative infrastructure within Maelstrom to produce illegal braindances (XBDs) featuring real murder scenes. In that capacity he does not only produce and refine the "merchandise" together with his son Fredrik, but also seems to have extensive control over the selection and acquisition of the victims. These included the son of Bryce Stone, who tasked fixer Regina Jones to retrieve the XBD for clues on the murderers. Adam Ibrahimovic, co-owner of the Empathy club, also supplied Gottfrid with material to work on. Gottfrid's and Fredrik's work garnered enough reputation to have potential clients reach out to them, including one asking about an XBD on Evelyn Parker's murder. Gottfrid also has control over the distribution of the product, which appears to have involved XBD street dealer Lenny Nero.

Having many enemies, Gottfrid's database is well protected, which caused at least one netrunner hired by Regina Jones to be fried in an attempt to access it. Moreover, his power within Maelstrom seems to be substantial as he not only sends his "boys" to hardware acquisition raids, but also has a large detail of goons protecting him and his son.

In 2077, fixer Regina Jones sends merc V to Gottfrid's hideout to retrieve an XBD that might contain information on the murder of a client's son. V finds both Gottfrid and his son unaware while editing an XBD. As V gets their attention, they both plead for their lives, falsely claiming that they only refine the braindances based on dead drops provided by Maelstrom and therefore are not complicit in any murder. V can then retrieve the XBD themselves or force them to tell the merc where it is. During this conversation, V has the choice of killing either, both, or neither of them before leaving. Only killing Fredrik, who just calls Gottfrid "papa", causes him to collapse in agony and cry out "Freddy! No!".

Database Entry

- transcript：Gottfrid's work is the stuff of another person's nightmares. Nightmares often come true in Night City, and when they do, he takes them (or buys them) and edits them to turn a profit. As a matter of fact, he's fairly well-respected in the obscure circle of illegal braindance editors. He's a craftsman without a conscience - an advantage in his line of work. If the material is good, Gottfrid will take a raw BD from anyone and fine-tune the emotions, no questions asked. The closest person to him is his son, Fredrik, whom he taught and trained in his craft. When they're not editing together, they manage a deep net site.

The Grand Illusion is a club located in central Night City.

History
Early history - 2022
During the late 2000s and early 2010s, the Grand Illusion became one of the most popular rock clubs in Night City. A number of famous local music artists had started out here, and occasionally paid the Illusion an homage by appearing under assumed names. The establishment was well known for its three bars and hot dance floor.

Unbeknownst to many people, Johnny Silverhand and Kerry Eurodyne bought the club in 2012 and didn't make it public. At some point later, driven by memories and using their influence, both rockers begun an open mike night on Thursdays which was regularly attended by Universal Records executive Jack Masters, the label under which both rockerboys recorded.

During an afternoon of 2013, Eurodyne was assaulted while at the club by young female fans, prompting him to call Trauma Team for an extraction. In the end, the crowd was dispersed with teargas and nothing too serious happened to anyone, with the teenagers enjoying a bit of chaos, and Kerry billing TT's call cost and a new set of clothing to his music studio.

Around the late 2010s, the Grand Illusion contracted the Silver Slash gang to protect the building from any potential trouble in the surrounding neighborhood. By 2020, the club was considered one of the most popular places to party in the West Coast, with its only purpose being the same as always, music. Almost anybody was allowed to attend, from partying glitterfolk to biz-minded people or even booze-hunting streetscum. Although patrons were encouraged to go wild, security in this place was very strict. As such, all weapons had to be checked at the entrance, where everyone was scanned. When leaving, the confiscated items were returned, even if they were illegal. This was done as a way to show trust in order to get cyberpunks to part with their weaponry—ultimately, the ex-Samurai rock stars were aiming towards the dream of a nonviolent future. Around this time, an undercover NCPD agent known as Evie Lark started working as a waitress here while investigating on how to break the control Arasaka had over a local gang.

2023 - 2040s
Although the Grand Illusion survived the nuclear disaster of 2023, following the Fourth Corporate War, the club was shuttered and remained mostly abandoned for years. It wasn't until 2035 when Eurodyne hired a mercenary crew to flush out the squatters, then paid workers to remodel the place, and finally reopened it shortly thereafter. As an homage to Johnny and the old band, a massive mural depicting Samurai was adorned on the club's ceiling, done in scarps of plastic wreckage. In 2038, Kerry did an interview in which he talked about why he and Johnny bought the Illusion, stating the club was a place for "...fucking music, man!"

By the 2040s, the Grand Illusion's security policy of returning any weapon checked at the door, no matter if it was illegal or not, encouraged a diverse audience attending the events. On top of that, the club's Thursday "new discoveries" night had become the dream stage for local new rockers to play. The Illusion's manager at the time, Filomena Reyes, kept an eye open for real talent, sending any details back to Eurodyne.

2070s
By the 2070s, Lizzy Wizzy and other artists had performed at the Grand Illusion.

Notable Staff

The Grand Imperial Mall (GIM) is an abandoned shopping center located in Coastview, in the Pacifica district of southern Night City.

Overview
The Grand Imperial Mall was meant to be the largest and most luxurious shopping center within the Pacifica district during its redevelopment. It was aimed to contain six-floors with more than seventy stores, service outlets, restaurants, a gym, a cinema, its own amusement park — Eden Beach — as well as Hotel Tropique. The facilities would also offer napping pods available on-demand, and a lottery that would allow mall clients to participate for the chance of winning free park ride tickets after every purchase.

Although the shopping mall was almost complete by 2069, funding dried up during the Unification War and it was soon after abandoned. When the Voodoo Boys gang took control of western Pacifica, they preferred to keep away from the mall as they considered it reeked of corpo vanity. In 2077, the structure became a temporary base of operations for the Animals gang and NetWatch agent Bryce Mosley during his operations to stop the Voodoo Boys. When the Animals left, Scavengers scoured the place for valuables.

A boxing ring within the mall was momentarily used for the final match championship between V and Razor Hugh.

## Great Plains
The Great Plains (also known as the Great Plains States) is a region of the United States of America.

Overview
Formed after The Collapse, the Great Plains States are made up of the states of Iowa, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, North Dakota, South Dakota, and Wyoming.

History
The Great Plains States were, by and large, spared from the worst ravages of the past couple of decades. Of course, they didn't come through those dark years smelling like a rose - no one did. But the Great Plains states didn't have the volume of problems that others bore.

In the mid-to late-1990's, the Great Plains region was hit with several years of drought, which made life hard for everyone in the area. Water was strictly rationed, and food was scarce, yet most of the residents continued to be able to scrape out a living.

When the Collapse hit, the region was still parched. For that reason, most of the nomads and aimless wanderers avoided the area. No one particularly wanted to cross endless miles of dry, flat plains with no hope of water or a city where jobs might be found. They headed instead to the metropoli, and to places with better weather. This couldn't have pleased the residents more. They were happy to struggle on their own and let the rest of the nation deal with its problems elsewhere.

There were a few migrants passing through, o f course; generally the residents turned a cold shoulder to them, knowing that with towns so few and so small, the migrants would be unlikely to find help elsewhere, either. It is said that even today, abandoned cars can be found on back roads, some with the remains of Nomads still nearby.

During this time, agribusiness corporations began buying up the land of these states, which was being sold at pennies to the dollar. While it was not yet feasible or economic to farm the area on the scale they were envisioning, the agricorps were strengthening their position for the future. Some new agribusiness communities began construction around this time, scheduled to begin full-scale farming around the tum of the millennium. By that time it was projected that the lingering effects of the drought of '98 would be gone and there would be enough water to go around.

The Brushfire
Unfortunately for all, in the early summer of the year 2000, a major catastrophe occurred: The Brushfire. The simplicity of the name cannot convey the raw power it had and the terror it inspired. The Brushfire was a conflagration the like of which has never been seen. It burned huge portions of Montana and North Dakota, and visited other states as well.

Most people believe that The Brushfire was started by a careless Nomad pack somewhere on I-94 in eastern Montana. It is the most likely explanation, and if the Nomads weren't killed in the fire, they certainly aren't going to talk about it.

I-94 is a 250-mile stretch of road leading from Billings to North Dakota. According to the best estimates, the fire started here and fed itself rapidly on the dry brush in the area. Eventually, the smoke plume was spotted in Billings, and Leslie Sanstone, a low-ranking agribusiness corporate, drove out to investigate. She found the fire before she'd gone ninety miles, and it had already leapt across the interstate.

Sanstone's secretary had brought his camcorder and shot some of the most famous footage of the fire. By that time, it had become a firestorm, with thermal convection pulling in oxygen from around the flames and fueling them to blast furnace temperatures. For those with access to the film, note the steady breeze whipping Sanstone's dress as she narrates the video.

The breeze from the thermal convection kept the fire from spreading as fast as it perhaps could have. Since the fire was pulling in air from around itself, it was having to spread upwind in all directions. However, the fire had also burned away all the fuel in the center, taking on a ring shape, and was large enough that it was beginning to affect the weather conditions in the immediate vicinity. Eventually the fire calved, and, aided by a high-pressure zone which had moved in from the west end of the state, became several fire curtains which swept across the land.

A fire curtain is a terrifying thing. It's a long line of burning fuel, pushed in one direction by prevailing winds. The winds provide plenty of oxygen for the fire to consume, and then carry the heat downwind, where it preheats the brush for the fire to ignite next. The concept had been known for some time, and was even used in the firebombing of Japanese coastal cities, but a fire curtain the size of The Brushfire had never been seen.

The Brushfire found some of the agricorp land-gargantuan fields, untended and dry-awaiting next year's planting. Coaxed by the winds, it consumed countless thousands of acres. Normal fire-fighting tactics were useless before the fire, as its size outweighed anything the enfeebled states could pit against it, especially as they were hamstrung by water shortages.

The U.S. Army was finally called in to cut a dead area in North Dakota, where The Brushfire had finally spread. The Army efficiently destroyed an incredible amount of area, burning wood and grass in controlled fires, digging firebreaks, and sowing chemicals to further retard the fire.

Finally, the fire found itself trapped between this dead zone and the Missouri river in North Dakota, and, after a long, hard fight, burned itself out. Although the fire jumped the river in a few places, Army troops and Corporate workers managed to keep it in check.

There were also many other fires started by ashes (and entire bushes) carried aloft by The Brushfire, some as far away as Wyoming and South Dakota. All told, there were approximately fifty seven separate fires in this disaster.

Even once extinguished, The Brushfire still had an effect on Great Plains life. The incredible amounts of heat and smoke generated disrupted the local weather for the rest of the year, and falling ashes hampered the plant life and fouled mechanical devices. Asphalt roads had bubbled up under the heat and had to be rebuilt. The list goes on and on.

The most dramatic effect of The Brushfire, though, was on the attitude towards Nomads and the like. Nomads were blamed for igniting The Brushfire, perhaps with a cigarette butt or a campfire, and any homeless wandering the Great Plains roadways were all considered to share in the guilt. Vigilantes started attacking Nomad packs and homeless people on the 'ounce of prevention' philosophy, and most of the states passed very strict migrant laws. As word of this spread through the country, the various people roaming the nation's highways found better places to go, and the Great Plains were rarely bothered by Nomads again.

Modern Times
Since then, the Great Plains has rebuilt, and with the warming global climate, it had become the new breadbasket of the United States. Most of the area is dominated by gigantic agribusiness cooperatives, which farm vast open areas from their new city bases.

Of course, just because the countryside looks pastoral doesn't mean there's no fighting going on. The agricorps regularly field small hit teams for select sabotage, although each is careful not to ignite any fires. They also try to harvest each other's fields whenever possible. Similarly, there is constant friction between the agricorps who try to dominate the area and the small farms and city folk (i.e., the natives of the area). Finally, all along the northern border of the U.S., the agricorps have fields planted several miles inside Canada. Although they have no legal right to do this, and no recourse if some Canadians come and try to harvest, the amount of land they get to use and abuse for free is remarkable. Needless to say, the Canadians aren't too keen about this, and there has been some border friction in the area.

## Greece

- population：12 million
- language：Greek
- affiliation：European Economic Community

Greece is a member of the European Economic Community located along the Mediterranean Sea.

History
When the Mideast Meltdown occurred, thousands of immigrants from Turkey attempted to enter Greece and were killed or forced back by the Greek military. Additionally, Greece once again vetoed Turkey's attempt to join the European Economic Community. However, these immigration laws were relaxed in 2001 as Greece had fallen prey to the Wasting Plague and needed to rebuild its population.

As corporations began to buy out land across Europe, Greece pushed back and began nationalising much of their country instead. This resulted in the corporations backing the Greek military in overthrowing the government in 2006. President Ioannis Lacanos was assassinated and the remaining government fled to Rhodes.

In 2009, the military-controlled government then attempted to annex both Cyprus and Macedonia, but failed in both cases. To regain lost funds, and fight against internal partisan movements, they began increasing taxes. This ended up causing the corporations that had funded the initial military coup to abandon them.

In 2016, Rhodes was officially declared its own country by the EEC, despite the military governments protests. This emboldened the partisans, whom seized most of Tessaly. However, in 2018, Greece began receiving support from Albania which allowed them to successfully conquer Macedonia. Serbia reacted to this assistance by invading part of Albania, and the stalemate between them continued as of 2020.

Government
In 2006, Greece's government was overthrown by its military, which received corporate backing. The military government is very corrupt, and the black market flourishes in areas occupied by them. Army officers and policemen are very accepting of bribes.

Culture
Greeks are a very passionate people both in love and in war. The Greek's believe that anything has a price, and that anything can be bought for the right money. Greece is a very misogynistic country, though mostly subconsciously.

Greek cities are still popular tourist destinations, and though it’s a police state, the authorities are easily bribed. This has made Greece a hub for people secretly sneaking into Europe without the European Economic Community's knowledge.

The Greene Homestead is located on the eastern Badlands of Night City.

Overview
The home of Russell Greene, his wife and his son, the heavily fortified homestead is a testament to Greene's paranoia, being fenced in on all sides, landmines at the entrance, and two turrets on the roof of the house. The homestead, apart from the extensive defenses, is a modest single story dwelling with a detached garage and a computer inside.

When V encounters the house, Greene's wife and son had been accidently killed by the house's turrets, causing Greene to succumb to cyberpsychosis.

Biography
Mamá Welles married Raúl Welles, a member of the Valentinos. Living in Night City, they had a son, Jackie. However, Raúl was abusive and violent towards her and her son, until the boy grew up and stopped him physically. After beating Raúl almost to death, Jackie promised to finish what he started if Raúl ever returned.

After Jackie and V had their first job together, she allowed them to move with her and Jackie in their house, somewhere in Heywood. After six months, V found a place of their own.

During this time, Jackie had been dating Misty Olszewski, an old childhood friend. Guadalupe didn't approve of the relationship, instead preferring another girl from Heywood.
