Over the Edge is a Side Job in . It was added in Patch 1.6 as part of the Edgerunners Content DLC.

Walkthrough
As V approaches Megabuilding H4—in the south of Arroyo, Santo Domingo—they find a green tag next to the entrance and a braindance recording in a nearby trash can. As V puts on the Braindance Wreath and slots in the braindance, they experience the death of cyberpsycho Lt. Col. James Norris and receive a warning about the fate of David Martinez.

After the braindance ends, V finds themselves on the ground. They text Muamar Reyes to inquire about David Martinez. Muamar relates some of David's story, and promises to be in touch when he has found out more about the whereabouts of his companions.

After about 24 in-game hours, V receives a text message from Falco. In it, Falco will explain that he used to run with David, although they have fallen out of the spotlight. Mentioning that V and David have much in common, and that while their 15 minutes of fame may be over, it is not yet too late for V. Falco instructs V to visit Muamar, as he has left behind a gift.

When V arrives at Muamar Reyes's location at the Dam Viewpoint, they find a cache on the balustrade. Approaching the cache reveals that the package left for them was David's Jacket. Looting the jacket will conclude the quest.

Journal Entry
:Someone sprinklin' XBDs around the city with cyberpsychos in the leading roles? The fuck's that about? And that warning at the end... Strangest fuckin' PSA I've ever seen. Only thread to follow here is the name dropped at the end – David Martinez. Sounds like the headstrong type. I like him already.

Objectives
*Play the braindance.
*Text Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes and ask about David Martinez.
*Wait a day for Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes to respond about David Martinez.
*Reply to Falco's message.
*Collect the gift from Martinez's crew left with Muamar "El Capitan" Reyes.

Notes
*The text message exchange responses differ depending on V's lifepath.
*The braindance used to start the quest consists of the opening scene from Let You Down, the first episode of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners.

Ozob Bozo is a character in the universe.

Biography
Early life
Ozob was born in Brazil. At some point, Ozob's brother ripped off his nose during a fight using a pair of pliers. Instead of chroming a new nose, he decided that a grenade matched his style better. Later in his life he would become a mercenary.

2040s
In 2045, while Ozob was wandering around Night City, he happened to walk into the infamous Bozos' Hilaria event. After deciding to briefly join and blow something up, he disappeared amidst the crowd to the astonishment of the guests and prankster clowns present there.

2070s
In 2077, Ozob travelled to Night City, being surprised with how much the metropolis had changed since his last visit. There he employed a merc named V due to them being highly recommend as one of the best mercenaries in town. While driving to their destination, V asked Ozob about his grenade nose. He informed V that it was an active grenade to the latter's surprise, but that he would just need to be careful. Once in the Watson district, Ozob entered a building alone, and not long afterwards, an explosion blew out the establishment's windows. Ozob appeared running away from a bunch of Tyger Claws, and both him and V dealt with them. After paying V their fee, Bozo left the area.

Ozob later battled V in an illegal fist fight in the Combat Zone of Pacifica, with the winner being compensated with money. The grenade could be activated if hit enough times, signaled by red sparks. If the grenade got activated during the fight, it detonated, killing Ozob in the process, and V was declared the winner by "technical knockout." Otherwise, Ozob was satisfied with the fight and paid V for defeating him. After the event, V could mention to him that someday the nose grenade would explode. Bozo acknowledged that fact, but stated that everyone died at some point, and when he did, there would be some fireworks to celebrate.

Humans of Night City

- transcript：Before you start throwin' questions – yeah it's a grenade, and yeah, it's active. Veeeeery active. Seen crazier mods in NC, but this has gotta be top 10. Maybe even 5. But hey, who says it's a competition, right? Prob'ly wanna know how I got it. Yeah yeah, everyone does. Well, had a fight with my brother and the fucking genius decided it'd be cool to try out some pliers on my shncozz. So naturally I picked this as a fitting replacement. Suits me down to the ground, don't you think? Took some getting used to, sure, but lookin' on the bright side my bar game skyrocketed. 'Hey baby, pardon me for being nosy, but that drink looks like the bomb. What is it?' Never miss a shot with that one. Ozob's guarantee. It's a damn shame the hooch here is so bad though. Nothing's got any bite. Not enough for me, anyway. I need something that'll rattle my rain with just a sip. My biggest craving? Cachaça. And not any cachaça – talkin' 'bout the one and only No Regrets Cachaça from my hometown. Oh BOY. One shot in the morning and you'll be feeling the beat all day long... Or it'll waste ya there and then. Big diff. Too bad NC ain't got any. Whole place could use a kick up the ass.

Development
Ozob is a character originally created in the 1990s by Deive "Azaghal" Pazos, co-founder of the Brazilian geek site [https://jovemnerd.com.br/ Jovem Nerd], to be played in the tabletop RPG, Underground. However the character was never actually played until 2013 when it was featured in Nerdcast. The character became a fan favorite after being featured on three Cyberpunk RPG special episodes of "Nerdcast", the website's podcast and main attraction (see [https://jovemnerd.com.br/nerdcast/nerdcast-395-rpg-cyberpunk-1-o-grande-assalto/ NerdCast RPG Cyberpunk 1]). The character's backstory was furthered expanded in a novel written by Leonel Caldela and Deive Pazos.

Azaghal was the voice actor for Ozob in the Brazilian Portuguese version of where he ad-libbed most of his lines. Even though he was offered by CDPR to play Ozob in the English version, Azaghal declined the offer because he thought it would be better if a professional voice-actor did it due to his strong accent.

Notes
*Maximum Mike talks about Ozob in Morro Rock Radio, pondering if he is somehow related to the Bozos due to their similar attires.
*Should Ozob die, his niche can be found at the Columbarium and reads "We live in a society", a reference to the "[https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/gamer-joker-gamers-rise-up-we-live-in-a-society Gamer Joker/We live in a society]" meme.

Trivia
*Ozob's full-name is a palindrome, that is, it reads the same backwards and forwards.
*Ozob is an anadrome for Bozo "The World's Most Famous Clown".

## Pacific Northwest
The Pacific Northwest is a region of the USA.

Overview
Formed after The Collapse, the Pacific Northwest is made up of the states of Hawaii, Idaho, Oregon, and Washington.

History
Politically speaking, the Pacific Northwest region is as powerful as the Great Plains region, and these are the only two real competitors to the Appalachian dominance of national politics. Despite the fact that the region only has four states, it possesses the largest West Coast port (also the only Pacific port not in a Free State) and the Pacific Ocean Military Base. It also still has a large reserve of lumber, and produces a lot of real food, like apples, potatoes, hops,. wine grapes, and the few fish that are still safe to eat.

Added to these resources is the fact that these four states take their politics very seriously. The region's senators have the best attendance record in the national government. Furthermore, the Pacific Northwest region is the only region which has always voted as a bloc on every issue. These practices have added clout to what is a relatively small group of states.

Thanks to the port of Seattle, the Pacific Northwest has become somewhat of a thoroughfare for American society. Far from being a backwater relegated to a lonely corner o f the continent, the Northwest is towards the front of the American cultural wave, and it's slowly gaining ground on the leaders of the pack, Appalachia and the Free States. Many of the grunge rockers are making pilgrimages to the rebuilt ruins of the Northwest, hoping to find something of their roots in the new port and the abandoned skyscrapers. Or, as Kerry Eurodyne said, "We ll, the Northwest music scene used to be the pits. Now the only thing that stinks is Tacoma."

Despite years of severe ecological damage, the states of the Pacific Northwest region are trying to improve things, recognizing that natural resources are one of their biggest assets. The rugged beauty of the area, though, has been largely destroyed, and it may never return.

## Pacifica (2077)
- type：District
Combat Zone
- city：Night City
- appears_books：

引文：Pacifica could've been Night City's money-making vacation resort, but once the investment dried up it became a husk left to rot. Now, instead of tourists, the district is overrun by gangs and violence, with the Voodoo Boys protecting the community forsaken by NCPD.

Pacifica is one of the major districts of Night City, located in the southern portion of the metropolis.

Overview

Pacifica was originally envisioned as Night City's vacation resort for the ultra-wealthy. It was to be true paradise, catering to corporate employees and tourists alike and with Militech security contractors protecting its golden sandy beaches, luxurious hotels, and unmatched entertainment. By 2077 the district has become a lawless and anarchic Combat Zone, no longer considered part of Night City's administrative boundaries.

History
Resort Project (2050s - 2060s)
The slow rebuilding process of Pacifica was accelerated in the late 2050s and early 2060s, when investors, backed up by the Night City Council, tried to expand the region into a booming and wealthy touristic resort. Among these were Euro Business Machines, Petrochem, and other corporations, but of special note was Militech, who put major funding into this project.

Over the following years, the district became a massive construction project, importing hundreds upon hundreds of laborers (mostly from Haiti) and poured billions of eurodollars into building luxury hotels, casinos, shopping centers, spas and a newer and bolder amusement park, as well as an impressive sports arena. Militech spearheaded the construction effort, followed by major construction companies like HFS, Zhirafa, Corp-Bud, Aurochs, among others. Coastview and West Wind Estate became the western sub-districts, while the eastern section was to be called Serenisands. Old buildings were dilapidated to give space to modern structures, and a high-speed road network was connected to the rest of the metropolis. This investment was meant to show Night City's economic strength, but short into the project, a large explosion under a construction site put the whole thing on hold.

An extensive investigation did not provide any answers to the cause of the explosion, resulting in just doubling the local security detail. The truth was that in the 2020s Militech had built an extensive network of laboratories and bunkers hidden beneath Pacifica's infrastructure, only to be abandoned at some point prior to the Fourth Corporate War. Rumors said that the explosion had been caused after accidentally uncovering part of Cynosure's project. Due to this, the City Council decided to wall-off Serenisands, giving the excuse of a gas leak, and Militech constructed a large wall separating Serenisands from the rest of the city. But this didn't bother investors too much, and construction resumed.

Unfortunately, the dream of the new resort paradise ended in 2069 when the Unification War broke out.

Unification War & Aftermath (2069 - 2075)
The Unification War halted Pacifica's success in its tracks. Investors began to back out as completing the construction of a luxury resort dropped down the financial priority list. Around 2070, as fears mounted that the New United States would invade Night City from Southern California and Pacifica would become a battlefield, corporations and other investors raced to pull their funding from the ongoing projects. With Night City's economy already on a downturn, the effect on the district was disastrous. Pacifica was left unfinished and lawless. Construction work was put on permanent hold, leaving most buildings unfinished hulks of concrete and steel.

The techno-mystical group of netrunners known as the Voodoo Boys were part of the Haitian community that had settled in Night City after their country was ravaged by climate disaster. With so many dangers, they took it upon themselves to protect the local community, forsaken and left to fend for themselves by the NCPD. Soon after they begun to take control the district.

When war reached Night City, a Militech unit led by Kurt Hansen managed to take hold of parts of Serenisands. In the meantime, the Arasaka Corporation had been asked by Councilman Lucius Rhyne to return to Night City to aid them, and mere days later, a supercarrier was docked at Del Coronado Bay. The NUSA asked for their soldiers to retire, but Hansen decided to ignore the directive and remain in the area. Small fights between Arasaka, Militech and the armies of SoCal and NorCal reached the city, but not long after, the Arvin Accord was signed and the war was ended.

With Pacifica abandoned and in ruins, gangs and the homeless moved in. On the western side of the district, the Voodoo Boys led riots against the city officials and corporations that were trying to reclaim Pacifica. On the eastern side, the rogue Colonel Kurt Hansen, who viewed the Arvin Accord with disdain, decided to create his own fiefdom. Hansen tasked his unit with taking full control of Serenisands, a perfect location surrounded by thick walls, large edifices and hills, and set up a permanent base of operations. Soon after, Kurt and his unit established the BARGHEST militia, growing his forces by recruiting mercenaries and later any willing renegade and gangers. With all this chaos, Pacifica became a sanctuary for refugees, fugitives and criminals.

Over the following years, the city shut down all services in Pacifica, but both the Voodoo Boys and the BARGHEST found their ways around the official lack of water, power and CitiNet. Finally, in 2072 a series of violent protests led by the Voodoo Boys repealed a large NCPD task force. On October 17, the local NCPD Precinct was officially disbanded, resulting in the whole district being recognized as a Combat Zone. The Voodoo Boys emerged as the de facto authority in western Pacifica, while BARGHEST controlled their own area known as Dogtown.

2076 - 2077
By 2076, Pacifica was overrun by poverty and criminal activity. Buildings were occupied by the formerly homeless, and tourists — or merely visitors — to Pacifica were few. Scavengers and other criminal gangs plagued the district, leaving many who entered without valuable cybernetic implants or vital organs. The Voodoo Boys and BARGHEST still controlled vast swaths of the district. Other Night City officials still hold hope for Pacifica however, promoting the district to be capable of returning to the original vacation paradise it was on its way to becoming.

In 2077, Mayor Lucius Rhyne re-designated Pacifica an "independent district" of Night City, dropping it from the administrative boundaries of the city proper. This was a ploy that allowed Pacifica's crime statistics to be excluded from the city's official numbers. Rhyne and his deputy, Weldon Holt, took full credit for the resulting 3% "drop" in Night City's crime rate as he ran for re-election against challenger Jefferson Peralez.

That same year, Kang Tao began expressing an interest in buying property in Pacifica to build a new server facility. The Night City Council was debating whether or not to offer selling the lot to Kang Tao for a single eurodollar in exchange for a pledge to help quell the district's rampant crime.

Database Entry

Sub-districts

*Coastview
*Dogtown, formerly known as Serenisands.
*West Wind Estate

Behind the Scenes

引文：Squint, and Pacifica almost looks like the tantalizing vision that gave its initial investors stiffies: hotels with ocean views and private pools, an amusement park to bring in that family vacation eurodollar, a beach complete with a pier, umbrellas and, OK, garbage, but that's the price of being next to Night City. And that prime location is what would make this resort a money-making machine. Those investors didn't stay hard for Pacifica for long, however. Mid-construction, hotter opportunities came along and they pulled out, leaving the half-finished buildings to rot. Gangs moved in and the would-be beachfront paradise became a war zone. The city gave up on fixing or bulldozing it and just walled the whole place off. What was supposed to be every visitor's first stop is now a hostile hellhole you can't enter even if you're crazy enough to want to. As a result, Pacifica serves as 2077's version of a hallowed Cyberpunk tradition: the Combat Zone, a place where bullets can fly without any cops or civilians getting in the way. Making that zone an abandoned resort opened up room for our artists to play with sharp visual contrasts: funhouse signs riddled with bullet holes, luxury pools filled with chemical sludge. In terms of style, here Entropism has engulfed an aborted attempt at Kitsch.

Notes
*In 2077, the district security turrets can be seen to be damaged all around the area.
*Similarly, while ambient advertisement announcements can be heard, due to neglect these are greatly deteriorated and occasionally skip or barely play.

## Pacifica NCPD Precinct
- type：Police station
- owner：Govt. of Night City (formerly)
- city：Night City

- street：Pacific Boulevard
- affiliation：NCPD (formerly)

This NCPD Precinct was a division of the Night City Police Department located in Coastview, in the Pacifica district of southern Night City.

History
On October 17 of 2072, this NCPD precinct was officially disbanded by Deputy Commissioner Claudia Feldman — with the full support of Mayor Lucius Rhyne — after a series of violent protests around Pacifica, resulting in the district being recognized as a combat zone.

At some point afterwards, BARGHEST soldiers led by Dodger turned the abandoned building into their base of operations in the surrounding area.

In 2077, V was hired by Stella Ramos to infiltrate the precinct in order to rescue her husband Bill Mitchel and his friend Charles Wilson, two NCPD officers who were under the thumb of Dodger.

Database Entry

- transcript：The NCPD exists to serve and protect one thing - statistics. The fewer the murders and assaults, the higher their praise from the mayor. The higher the praise, the fatter their bonuses. NCPD officers like to close the book on most cases as quickly as possible. They come across a dead body in a dark alley with multiple gunshot wounds to the head and torso, they call it a suicide. People die violent deaths in Night City every day, but rarely will the police classify these as "murder". The statistics at the NCPD station in Pacifica painted too grim (read: realistic) a picture, so the city shuttered it overnight. Today, the station serves those who never made it into official police statistics, but who are certainly more than deserving.

Associated Quests
*Gig: Waiting for Dodger

## Pacifica Serenity Bible Church
- type：Church
- city：Night City
- district：Pacifica
- sub_district：Coastview
- gangs：Voodoo Boys

The Pacifica Serenity Bible Church is located in Coastview, in the Pacifica district of southern Night City.

Overview
The Serenity Bible Church is a simple brick-and-mortar place of worship that was originally intended to connect to a neighboring hotel complex funded by billionaire Rothman Castern. When the Unification War broke out, however, Castern pulled out his investments. As a result, the hotel was never completed, and the church survived only in its unfinished state. In time, the church became functional as a local community meeting place and hideout of the Voodoo Boys gang.

The chapel's unfinished basement connected to an old abandoned tunnel once used for the Maglev Network. The Voodoo Boys broke into this section to set up both their main netrunning center and a fallback shelter hidden to the eyes of the local population.

## Padania
military

Padania is a country that split off from Italy.

History
The country of Padania was formed from the northern part of Italy some time before 2077.

The Padanian government is attempting to prevent the illegal excavation and looting of priceless works of art from the sunken city of Venice. Strong demand for the art from collectors fed a robust black market trade that generated profits equivalent to one-third of Padania's GDP, and the government was unable to recover most of the stolen art because the owners usually lived in orbitals.

## Pan-African Alliance
- demonym：Africans
- aka：Pan African Confederation, PAC, Union of African Countries
- location：Africa
- appears_books：

The Pan-African Alliance, also known as New Africa is a confederation which appears in the universe.

History
From the Capetown bloodbath, New Africa emerged as a divided continent of warring countries under a bewildering array of dictators, democracies and socialist states. Eventually, as European countries negotiated with Tanzania to build the Kilimanjaro Mass driver, many African nations began to see their place in the 21st century. By negotiating for labour, raw materials and valuable land in the critical equatorial orbital belt, African states established themselves in space - almost a third of the space construction workforce is African. Technology has united Africa under one government, and the last of the petty dictators and warlords have fallen.

During the 2020s, the Pan-African Confederation seemed to some to be nothing more than a puppet of the European Economic Community. However, the PAA were more cunning than most people gave them credit for and planned to ditch the EEC once all of Africa had been united by the PAA using European money.

New Africa had been reborn by the Fourth Corporate War as a space-dominant nation, being unified by the European nations of the Eurotheatre. The Highrider nation had formed, declaring their sovereignty and space control from the rest of the world, due to most space workers, spaceports, and construction areas being on African soil or otherwise African-related. Major corporations such as the Kenyan megacorp Orbital Air serve as a testament to Africa's increasing focus on space exploration.

## Panam Palmer
- aka：Pan
- age：33 (2077)
- status：Alive

- residence：Nomad Camp (formerly, dependent)
- gender：Female

- partner：V (boyfriend, dependent)
- affiliation：Aldecaldos (Bright Family; formerly, dependent)
Afterlife Mercs (formerly, dependent)
- occupation：Mercenary (formerly, dependent)
Aldecaldos family leader (dependent)
- role：Nomad
Solo
Techie
- voiced_by：Emily Woo Zeller

引文：Because I truly care this time. Yet I fear I'll do or say something foolish - and be left alone in the desert.（Panam during With a Little Help from My Friends）

Panam Palmer is introduced as a former member of the Aldecaldos nomad clan, who, after a family dispute, decided to live a more independent life as a mercenary. She is also a possible romance option for V with a masculine body in .

Biography
Panam Palmer was part of the Aldecaldos nomad tribe. Her best friend was captured by the Raffen Shiv, a hostile Nomad group, when they were a child, only to be saved by fellow-Aldecaldo Cassidy Righter - an incident that deeply affected Panam into her adulthood, to the point of never telling anyone what happened in order to forget about it. Cassidy would remain a close friend of Panam and become somewhat protective of her. Panam also befriended several other clan members, including Mitch Anderson and Driss "Scorpion" Meriana. Panam idolized Saul Bright, a fellow Aldecaldo who used to pull off impressive as well as funny stunts in his earlier years.

At some time, Panam and Mitch were hauling cargo from San Francisco to Kansas for the owner of a syn-meat farm. The stench at the farm got Panam so sick that she puked on the owner's boots to which he simply replied "No need to bow, I'll just take a handshake." Another "long story with many twists and turns" involved the corpse of the Deputy Finance Director of Kaukaz riding in Panam's trunk.

At some point, Panam's clan set up camp in the Badlands outside Night City. She didn't see eye to eye with the clan's leader, Saul Bright, who was trying to strike a deal with Biotechnica in his attempt to keep the clan alive with consistent work. Panam disapproved, believing the clan should remain independent from corporations. Together with Scorpion, Panam kept joking about getting Mitch on board and heading off to Oregon on their own. Panam's conflict with Saul came to a head, however, when, due to her rebellious attitude, she eventually left the clan and moved to Night City, even though her friend Mitch tried to talk her out of it at first. Working as a mercenary under the fixer Rogue, Panam was often paired with nomad Nash on a few gigs, though she was unaware he was Raffen Shiv. Despite moving away, Panam maintained communication with members of the Aldecados, including her close friends Mitch Anderson and Scorpion.

2077
During an assignment to deliver "merchandise", Panam was betrayed by Nash, who stole both their cargo and her Thorton Mackinaw "Warhorse". Having messed up, she angrily confronted Rogue at the Afterlife, leaving without compensation or help to recover the stolen items. Some time later, Panam was contacted by local merc V, who had been directed to her by Rogue to help capture Anders Hellman. After V helps Panam recover her merchandise by ambushing the Raffen Shiv in Rocky Ridge, and optionally also to get back her car by attacking and killing Nash in his hideout, she agreed to help them capture Hellman from Kang Tao forces, whose AV was predicted to pass across the Badlands.

Planning to ground the airborne convoy, Panam and V stormed the Satwave Power Plant on Jackson Plains and modified the systems into an EMP. When it failed to stop them, she used a rocket launcher to ground the vehicle. However, Panam's friends Mitch and Scorpion underestimated the surviving Kang Tao guards at the crashed convoy and rushed in alone, which got Scorpion killed and MItch taken hostage by a surviving guard. Scorpion's death left Panam devastated.

:V and Panam wiped out the surviving Kang Tao forces around the downed AV and found Mitch inside, held at gunpoint by a guard. After V or Panam killed the guard, or convinced him to back off, they head to the gas station to the west, where Hellman and his bodyguards took shelter. After Hellman's capture, Aldecaldos reinforcements appear outside and Panam and V part ways. Panam's subsequent text messages to V reflect uncertainty about her life outside the clan and V can give her the advice to rejoin them.

:V left Panam and single-handedly retrieved Hellman from a nearby gas station that he and his bodyguards sought refuge in. Panam then showed up with Aldecaldos reinforcements, saying that she managed to rescue Mitch herself and that unlike V, she does not bail. Her subsequent text messages will be very frustrated about her life outside the clan and include a remark about Mitch, who gave Scorpion an Aldecaldos-style funeral by himself.

Some time later, Saul Bright disappeared with a small party of Aldecados. Learning of the attack, Panam returned to the Aldecados to help investigate. Eventually, they discovered the group had been ambushed by Wraiths, a Raffen Shiv gang, and Saul had been captured. As the interim-leader of the clan, Carol Emeka, was hesitant to take action and was worried about the Aldecaldos camp's vulnerability, Panam took it upon herself to act and contacted V to ask for assistance. As V agrees to help, Panam remarks "Do you know how good it is to hear that?" and asks to meet at the Aldecaldos camp, where the two along with Mitch go over some drone intel on the Wraith camp Saul is being kept at. As the plan is covert infiltration, only V and Panam set out, with the latter remaining at distance to provide the former with sniper cover fire if needed.

:Starting the job to rescue Saul but then leaving the area for too long will result in Panam sending a message saying that Saul is dead, and the job will be failed, precluding all follow-up missions involving Panam.

:After V rescued Saul, Panam drove the group away, escaping from pursuing Wraiths and using a sand storm to cover their tracks. Seeking shelter for the night in an abandoned farmhouse. A grateful Saul invites Panam to rejoin the Aldecaldos, but insists she will follow orders in the future. She responds by strongly objecting to Saul's planned cooperation with Biotechnica. As Saul turns in early, Panam sarcastically asks whether he needs "help"... to which Saul just responds "Fuck off" and remarks that sandstorms are called "haboobs" in north Africa - a word he is very fond of. As fellow Aldecaldos Cassidy Righter picks Saul up the next morning, V convinces Panam to rejoin the clan. Before Panam leaves she gives V her rifle Overwatch in return for their help. If V is male, the correct dialogue choice will result in Panam kissing him goodbye (see Romance - Optional Prelude).

:Despite his rescue, Panam and Saul remained at odds with each other. Panam would later identify a lightly guarded Militech convoy that is slated to transport a Basilisk tank through the Badlands, which her and Mitch want to steal. Deeming it to be too dangerous, Saul forbade Panam to pursue the matter. Behind Saul's back, she is determined to proceed anyway and gathers some like-minded fellow Aldecaldos including Mitch as well as Carol Emeka, and also contacts V to join her at the Nomad camp.
::
:::If V approaches Saul instead of Panam and tells him about her plan, the mission is aborted. A few hours later, a furious Panam contacts V, saying that her, Mitch, and Carol are now being treated like lepers by the others. She ends their friendship and severs all ties with V, precluding all follow-up missions involving Panam. Saul will subsequently contact V, saying that both he and Panam are grateful, although Panam might not realize it yet, and gifts V a unique car. The Aldecaldos then break camp and no further contact with any of them will be possible.
::
:::If V does not tell Saul about Panam's plan and instead immediately joins her and her group, the mission proceeds as planned with V's assistance. They decide to block the Militech convoy's path using an abandoned train system and camp near its control towers that night. Panam also begins to open up to V further, admitting them to her close circle. If V is male, he can also speak to Panam about their feelings for each other (see Romance - Optional Prelude). After an intense firefight against the Militech escort, the ambush on the convoy is successful and the group returns with both supplies and the Basilisk. Upon returning to the camp, Panam has another heated argument with Saul, who feared Militech could trace its stolen merchandise back to the Aldecaldos and told her they would have a "family council" soon to decide Panam's future in the clan. Cassidy then had the idea to, after unloading, leave the large, stolen convoy trucks in front of the Wraith camp Saul was held at previously in order to shift the blame for the heist. Panam and V then part ways as she and the others prepare to assemble the Basilisk.

:::The next day, an enthusiastic Panam calls V, asking to take the newly assembled Basilisk for a spin together. After returning to the camp, Cassidy, Mitch, and Panam tell V that they left the implicating loot from the raid on Militech near a Raffen Shiv camp to shift the blame. Panam and V then hop into the tank after Mitch makes some last minute adjustments. Panam instructs V to jack in to practice movement and target shooting with the tank's neural impulse interface outside of the camp. After that, Panam shows V the dual interface by joining them in the neural connection with the Basilisk, thereby linking their nervous systems and sharing their sensory awareness. If V is male, Panam will then use the interface to make sexual advances, which V can accept and thereby initiate the romance storyline (see Romancing Panam). In either case, Panam and V's experience is cut short by a Raffen Shiv ambush. After fighting them off with the tank, they head back to the camp, which is also under attack.

:::After the Raffen Shiv have been fought off, Saul wants to talk to Panam, who then expects to be kicked out of the clan for her foolhardiness. Instead, however, Saul makes Panam the new co-leader of the clan by his side, admitting he was wrong earlier, mistaking her willingness to risk everything for the family with recklessness. Saul and surprised Panam then decide to move the camp to a new location for safety reasons. To cool down, Panam shares a drink with V at the camp's bar and reiterates that they can always count on the Aldecaldos for help. She also asks V to join the clan, who has to decline in order to "finish some things first". After passing out from a Relic malfunction, V then wakes up in Panam's tent at the new camp location and has the choice to finally tell her about the worsening problem with the Relic and that Johnny Silverhand's engram is in their head. Panam will react concerned but understanding and then walks V to their ride. On the way, Saul, Mitch, and Cassidy will express their relief of seeing V back up on their feet. Before bidding goodbye, Panam repeats her and the entire family's willingness to help V at any cost. As their earlier joint kidnapping of Anders Hellman turned out to be a dead end, however, V does not know how the Nomads could help yet and is left with simply thanking Panam for being there for them. If V is male and initiated the romance earlier, he will give Panam a goodbye kiss.

:::After this, Panam can be found next to Saul in the Nomad camp's command truck. Despite their efforts to cover their tracks, Panam and Saul remained concerned by Militech retaliating against the clan, causing them to consider moving south across the border earlier than planned. V can also ask Panam how things are going with Rogue (to which she replies that they mostly stay out of each other's hair) or if she had any more trouble with the Kang Tao (which she declines, adding that they still believe it was the Raffen Shiv who attacked Hellman's transport). If she was not romanced and "The Sun" ending is chosen, this will be the last direct interaction between Panam and V. Panam's video message during the end credits will be the same as for the unromanced "Temperance" and "The Devil" endings (see below).

::::
:::::Contemplating their next move on the rooftop of Misty's Esoterica and realizing that they have only one last shot left to deal with the Relic issue, V can decide to call Panam and the Aldecaldos up on their offer to help. Johnny Silverhand does not like the idea as the lives of Panam and "her tarmac rats" will weigh heavy on their soul. Before V takes the omega blockers to be focused and alert for what could be their last ride, Johnny adds that he has a feeling that V will regret the decision and the "moment that dawns, he won't be there to help". Realizing that Johnny is shut out for the time being, V calls Panam. If Panam was romanced and called a few minutes earlier to say goodbye, she will already be waiting for V to call again (see Romance - Endings). If she was not romanced or V decided not to call her to say goodbye earlier, the phone is answered by a sleepy Panam, who V then reminds that she owes them a favor. Explaining that they immediately need a way into Arasaka Tower, Panam reacts surprised, but quickly agrees to help by simply saying "Ok." after V explains that Mikoshi in the tower's basement is their last chance to separate from Johnny's engram and survive. After V tells her where they are, Panam says "Don't go anywhere. I'm coming to get you." and hangs up. A short while later, Panam shows up at Misty's store and drives V to the Aldecaldos camp, who passes out again on the road. The next day, V wakes up at the camp. Saul and Panam, who are still bickering with each other, tapped into their Snake Nation sources that provided them with accurate plans of a Maglev Tunnel Construction Site outside Night City and the connected tunnels. Saul and Panam planned to commandeer a SERC inside the tunnel and infiltrate Arasaka Tower through its foundations. Saul and Panam then welcome V as a full member of the Aldecaldos, with Saul pointing out that V had been an informal member already. During their attack the following morning, the Aldecaldos encounter more resistance than anticipated, costing the lives of Bob and Teddy, but Saul, Panam, and V see the plan through and manage to fight their way into Arasaka Tower. However, upon reaching the entrance to Mikoshi, the three were intercepted by Adam Smasher. Saul was knocked to the ground but managed to shoot Smasher with his shotgun, destroying his chest plate. In retaliation, Smasher stomped on Saul's head, killing him instantly. The damage Saul did to Smasher then enabled Panam and V to defeat him. After V successfully reaches Mikoshi, Panam assumed full leadership of the Aldecaldos, leading her clan south across the border to Arizona.
:
::::
:::::If she was not romanced, V reaches Mikoshi alone or with the help of either Rogue or the Aldecaldos, and then decides to give their body to Johnny Silverhand, Panam's video message during the end credits will be an update from the Badlands and thanking V for all they have done for her. If she was romanced, Panam's video message will be very different (see Romance - Endings).
::::
:::::After having the relic surgically removed by Arasaka and seeking support from a friend, V can call Panam from the Arasaka Orbital Station. If she was not romanced, Panam will not grasp the distress V is in, simply telling them to come home, and then hangs up as Mitch demands her attention. She will not pick up again. Regardless of whether V then chooses to return to Earth or not, Panam's non-romanced video message during the end credits will be identical to the one for "The Sun" and "Temperance" endings (see above). If she was romanced, Panam's reaction to V's call from orbit as well as her end credits video message will be different (see Romance - Endings).

Database Entry

- transcript：Panam is a nomad - although, maybe "ex-nomad" rings truer these days. She locked horns with the family's leader, Saul, left Aldecaldo nation and moved to Night City to try her luck as a merc. Panam's life is at a crossroads - on one hand she knows her life needs a change, it's now or never. On the other hand, burning bridges with the nomad family where all her friends are might have been a bit drastic. On top of that, Night City doesn't take too kindly to nomads or have patience for people like Panam who are internally conflicted and dream of a brighter future.

Romancing Panam
If V has a masculine body (regardless of voice type and genitalia), they can pursue a romantic relationship with Panam. As such, Panam is unique as she is the only potential romantic partner for V, who can also be called for help during Nocturne Op55N1 towards the end of the game.

Optional Prelude
V can begin to flirt with Panam in the Sunset Motel bar at the end of Ghost Town, suggesting that they only get one room together. Although it will upset her initially, not completing the optional objectives earlier to assist Panam against the Raffen Shiv and Nash makes no difference. Panam agrees to sharing a room as that would save them money, pointing out that there are twin beds in every room. If V pursues the matter further, Panam first plays naive and then makes clear that they can "celebrate"... but not today. In their joint room, Panam will just immediately go to sleep in full clothes.

V can resume flirting in the abandoned farmhouse at the end of Riders on the Storm, after Saul went to bed. Although Panam will reject V touching her thigh, they can offer to fulfill her any wish, after which she replies "Careful, you can't know what I'd wish for..." and puts her legs on V's lap. Both fall asleep and Johnny Silverhand chimes in, wishing them sweet dreams. As Panam is about to depart the next morning, V has the option to ask her about last night, to which Panam replies that she is not that kind of girl. After V asks just what kind of girl she is, she responds by pulling him in for a kiss. Johnny then appears again, saying V should ride right after her if circumstances were different, but then and there they can just look. Johnny moves on saying "Damn hard to catch a girl like that. Only hope you've got is they feel a pang and stop to wait."

During With a Little Help from My Friends, V finds some time with Panam alone in the control tower and can choose to tell her that he missed her pretty bad. Panam immediately gets uncomfortable, as she is not used to talking about feelings. If V presses the issue, Panam admits that she also wants to talk about "it", but moves on by saying "My plan was to tiptoe around, test the waters, then retreat back into my shell." She adds that her hesitance is motivated by a fear to cock things up due to her volatile behavior and that, with V, she does not want to act on impulses but prefers to play it safe because - this time - she really cares. Later at the campfire with the other nomads, V can scooch closer to Panam and put his arm around her while looking at the stars together.

Not initiating any of the advances described above has no effect on the following romance option with Panam.

Endings
If V has romanced Panam, they can choose to call her to say goodbye at the end of the mission Nocturne Op55N1, which will unlock different endings with her. Before calling, V sighs that they only want to hear Panam's voice, but Johnny is wary that V might solicit the Aldecaldos' help against his advice and says, "Sure as hell hope it's that and only that." During the call, a sleepy Panam offers her help and, sensing V's serious distress, tells them to call back after taking a few deep breaths and rethinking everything. She then reminds V that she is there for them and hangs up. Following this, only one choice allows you to maintain the relationship, while the others remain ambiguous or end the relationship:

:Opting for "The Star" ending (asking Panam for help, which requires completing Queen of the Highway), will result in the Aldecaldos helping V to get to Mikoshi underneath Arasaka Tower. While the ensuing missions will play out the same regardless of whether Panam was romanced or not (see Biography), some additional interactions are added if her and V are lovers. At the end of We Gotta Live Together, the night before their raid on Arasaka, V will get the option to take Panam into his arms while they are sitting on the cliff edge by the Nomad camp. After V has been inside Mikoshi (and decided to keep their body), some dialogue between them and Panam will also be different. On the Dam at the beginning of All Along the Watchtower, Panam starts the conversation on a more personal note, saying that they will start everything anew once they are out of Night City. V can then ask Panam whether she would stay with them if they changed their mind and wanted to stay in the city. She replies that she could not leave her family and that she is glad she does not have to make that choice (hinting at the outcome if V chooses "The Sun" ending; see below). During the subsequent car ride to the temporary Nomad camp, V can remark that they are already bringing along everything they could possibly miss, prompting the following exchange: Panam: "Fuck V, you are a sweet-talker, aren't you." - V: "But it works, doesn't it? Say it, say it works." - Panam: "It works. All too well. You're with me now. We will figure out and take care of that piece of shit in your head." - V: "I know." While riding the Basilisk towards the border wall, Panam will confess to V that she once crossed the border from the other side, hoping for "some bright fucking future". V then points out that this crossing will be different, as she is different now. Panam agrees and adds that she now also has V and "the rest of these clowns [the Aldecaldos]". The final scene with Panam and V sitting on the tank will be identical to the unromanced version. During the end credits, Panam's video message will show her somewhere in the desert, telling V that she will not make it back home that night due to a sandstorm. As this is not the first time that she does not have time although they had "plans" together, she admits she never thought being chief would be that hard. She closes by saying "I'm so lucky to have you V. You can't even begin to imagine how much it means to me [...] I'll make it up to you, I promise".

:Opting for "The Sun" ending (choosing (Don't Fear) The Reaper or asking Rogue for help, which requires completing Blistering Love), will result in V waking up in bed in the penthouse at the beginning of Path of Glory, a few months after Nocturne Op55N1. In the shower, they will find Panam, who did not want to wake them. Panam is upset knowing that V's time is running out and confesses that she does not understand why V is not leaving the city after all that happened. She adds that her and the Aldecaldos are leaving tomorrow and just wants to run away with them, so that V can at least spend his last months among friends. V responds that they have to stay, to finish one last job - probably the most important one of their life - to show that, after all Night City took from them, it was for a reason. Panam thinks she understands, and with the Nomad lifepath, V can remark that there are no goodbyes, but simply roads that fork and re-converge. Moreover, V points out that Panam still owes him that story about the guy from Kaukaz, who rode in her trunk... V can then choose to hug her goodbye with the words "'til next time" to which Panam responds: "I will remember, V, always..." During the end credits, a video message from Panam plays, in which she reports that her and the Aldecaldos keep busy and all that she wishes for is a good night's sleep but that you cannot have it all... she then looks at the camera adding "you know what I mean." She moves on offering to take V for a "nice, looooong ride" if they should ever get bored of the city...

:Opting for "The Devil" ending (accepting Hanako Arasaka's offer to have the relic surgically removed), V can call Panam from the Arasaka Orbital Station during Where is My Mind?. Viktor Vektor told Panam what happened and she is furious that V did not ask her for help instead. She demands V to come home immediately before Arasaka hurts him. Her video message played during the end credits is identical to the one for "The Sun" ending (see above). This seems to imply that, even if V rejects Arasaka's offer and opts to return to Earth instead, they do not or cannot rejoin Panam immediately.

:Opting for the "Temperance" ending, i.e., reaching Mikoshi alone ((Don't Fear) The Reaper) or with the help of either Rogue or the Aldecaldos but then joining cyberspace with Alt and giving your body to Johnny Silverhand will prevent any further interaction with Panam during the epilogue. In her video message during the end credits, a furious Panam then threatens Johnny, vowing to find him and rip V out of their head.

:Opting for the "Tower" ending will see V unexpectedly enter a two-year coma after undergoing surgery. Upon waking up, V can attempt to call Panam to tell her about their recovery, discovering that Panam had left several messages to V that remained unanswered during their coma, with Panam's messages becoming more distressed over time. V will receive no answer and will only be able to leave a voice message. During the ending credits, Mitch will call V to ask for their understanding at Panam's anger over the situation, saying it took her a long time to pull herself together when they vanished, and advise V to not call Panam again.

Doctor Paradox is a character in .

Biography

One of the longest running underground screamsheets before the Fourth Corporate War, Doctor Paradox's Mysteries printed or displayed as a collection of barely coherent rantings, post-modern poetry, and purposefully disturbing images designed to "shake up the masses."

By 2020, Paradox began heavily promoting otherwise baseless conspiracy theories, including a government plot to utilize an Artificial intelligence to turn the population into zombies. Paradox believed President Elizabeth Kress to be an Artificial Intelligence herself, using a brainwashed actor to present a human face to the public when needed, later responding to questioning by raving about alien connections on the Net and similar occurrences.

## Paris
population
- type：Capital City
- country：France
- appears_books：

Paris is the capital of France.

Overview
Paris is a major European city and a center for art, fashion, food, and culture the world over. Artists flock to the city in droves every year, and some of them decide not to leave.

Paris's cityscape is a wonderful, sprawling mess of old and new, with grand old buildings haphazardly placed next to modern office blocks and factories. Things get more organized the further away they are from the city center.

The city is alive with a variety of subcultures, though thankfully the violence freaks and gross-outs prefer to stick to themselves. Groups of artists compete with each other in public spaces such as parks, putting on shows to display their work. Fashion Gangs compete to see who’s more fashionable and have been known to kill those whose taste they find appalling.

Almost every building in Paris is covered in graffiti and street-art. Only the best art is allowed to remain, however, and clean-up crews are each given a registered art critic to identify what art doesn’t come up to government standards.

## Path of Glory
Path of Glory is a Main Job in . It concludes "The Sun" ending and awards the associated achievement.

Walkthrough
V wakes up in their penthouse with the option to turn around, which will then bring any potential romantic partner into view who was called during Nocturne Op55N1 to say goodbye (Panam will already be in the shower; V will be alone if no one was called). After getting up, V will take a shower where they are optionally joined by Judy/Kerry/River. While having coffee in the kitchen, V's partner will voice concerns about the relationship. V will then have to join their partner on the balcony, where they bid farewell before V leaves to do a critical job. Dialogue choices cannot alter the basic outcomes of these dialogues: Kerry and River will promise to wait for V; the status with Panam will remain ambiguous but hopeful; Judy will end the relationship.

Before departing, one can check the room. There are messages about the upcoming job on V's computer. Johnny's Samurai jacket is hanging on the wall, which can be worn.

An AV operated by Delamain (depends on the choices made during Don't Lose Your Mind) will pick V and take them to the Afterlife. Upon arriving at the Afterlife, one has the option to approach bartender Claire, who will invite V to have a special drink for the coming operation. If one has taken the (Don't Fear) The Reaper path, Rogue will sit next to V, who suggests getting a tequila to oil the cogs before the important meet-up.

V will then meet with Mr. Blue Eyes in Rogue's old booth to discuss the upcoming job. The mission is to get data about clients of the Crystal Palace casino. At the end of the quest, V will be in a spaceship where they activate the auto-pilot, then leave the seat, put on a helmet, and pick up a pistol. V then enters the airlock and opens the door and floats into the space towards the Crystal Palace.

This final scene represents the tarot card "The Sun", thereby unlocking the associated achievement.

Journal Entry
:This quest does not have a journal entry.

Objectives
*Take a shower.
*Get dressed. (Optional)
*
**Talk to [Judy/Panam/River/Kerry].
*Take your jacket.
*Enter the AV.
*Enter the Afterlife.
*Talk to Claire. (Optional)
*Meet with the client.
*Sit.
*Talk to Mr. Blue Eyes.
*Leave the cockpit.
*Get armed.
*Put on the helmet.
*Listen to the client.
*Enter the airlock.
*Decompress the airlock.
*Wait for the airlock decompression.
*Exit the airlock and soar into the stars.

Notes
*If either River Ward or Judy Álvarez is the one to appear during this mission, V mentions to them that the job to infiltrate the Crystal Palace has been in the making for "a few months" now, implying this to be the amount of time that has passed since Nocturne Op55N1.

Trivia
*The title of the job comes from the Plasmatics song Path of Glory.

Pedro Aimar is a character in .

Biography

Pedro Aimar is a former algorithm coder for Zetatech. He was fired by his employer after developing health issues due to his ALS, and them not wanting to cover for his full body conversion.

Having found a Russian doctor by the name of Stanislav Federov, who was willing to perform the procedure in Russia, Aimar was desperate for money. Wanting to take revenge on Zetatech while also making enough eddies for the procedure, Aimar put out a contract for any mercs wanting to help him steal a truck full of Zetatech AV thrusters.

El Capitán reached out to V in order to help Pedro out. Using a Chinese ICE-breaker, V and Pedro plan to wait for the Zetatech truck outside Kenmore Diner and bring down it defenses in order to steal the tech.

Pepe Najarro is a bartender working in El Coyote Cojo bar in Heywood.

Biography
Pepe can be found working behind the bar, often double shifts without break at the most prominent local club, and he is fast to admit that he does it for his family. Despite putting all the extra hours in, he still has trouble paying off Kirk, a loan shark and aspiring fixer of the Heywood district.

Further down the road, V may revisit Pepe and provide their services for a taste of classical detective work regarding the private life of his wife, Cynthia. Due to her behaviour, lying about her whereabouts, followed by their child looking nothing like either of them, Pepe suspects a story as old as time - cheating. But, having no proof, he decides to hire someone he can rely on.

Depending on the decisions V makes through the concluding dialogue, they might affect the state of the Najarros' marriage, although this will solely reflect in individual holo calls received from the couple.

## Personal Link
The Personal Link is a piece of cyberware that is implanted into the palm of the user's non-dominant hand, and is part of the Neuroport package.

Overview

A Personal Link can be used to physically connect to various interfaces–usually part of a device or an Access Point–to perform simple hacking operations, such as the installation of simple malware programs that allow the user to gain control or access the device's data.

The Personal Link has a low bandwidth, making it unsuited for deep-dives into Cyberspace–for which a Personal Port is recommended–but due to its commonness and ease-of-use it is hard to detect once it has been connected to a local Net.

While the user is connected to an interface through Personal Link, they remain aware of their surroundings and have complete freedom of mobility.

A Personal Link can also be connected to another person's Neuroport, which is located in the neck.

Notes
*Henry, from Samurai, allegedly worked on the first Personal Link prototype.

See also
*Interface Plugs (2020)
*Interface Plugs (RED)

Peter Sampson is a character in .

Overview
Sampson is a Militech employee and an avid street racer. In 2076, during a race, he would be involved in a crash which took the life of Dean Russell, Claire Russell's husband. However, since the street races were not only illegal, but known to be violent with fatalities common to the sport, he suffered no legal consequences for the incident. Ever since, Claire has blamed Sampson for Dean's death, and wants revenge.

At the start of the final race, Claire can be seen talking with Sampson, and V can talk, though it does not affect the outcome. After the race has started, during some point Sampson's car will break down, causing him to forfeit the race, after which a choice can be made to either pursue him, or continuing on with the race.

:After crashing, Claire confronts him, and threatens death for the death of Dean. If V picks to let him go, V convinces Claire to give up killing Sampson, and gifts V her Beast, and Sampson gifts V his Type 66 "Cthulhu" for saving his life. Claire says that she wanted to kill him, but V says it wouldn't help, and Dean would prefer letting go of the past.

:Claire kills Sampson and proceed with the dialogue options, if V gets in, and drives to the garage. She will gift V her Beast as she no longer has an use for it.

This Petrochem Fuel Station is located alongside Interstate 9, on the eastern Badlands of Night City.

Overview
Established next to the freeway, this small CHOOH2 station was owned by Petrochem, and had an equally small Hundred Under Haven store attached to it. By 2045, the station was frequently refilled by a CHOOH2 tanker truck that drove from the Ebunike Docks in the Watson Development. Since the cargo was valuable and the distance long, an escort was needed to protect the vehicle from opportunistic gangs, marauder Raffen Shiv, or rival corporate agents (aka SovOil).

At some point, the Sunset Motel was built near the station. Around 2077, the small establishment included a vehicle workshop in its premises.

The Petrochem Nuclear Power Plant is located in Arroyo, in the Santo Domingo district of southeastern Night City.

Overview
The power plant compound is surrounded by a tall fence and has a security checkpoint entrance in Republic Way. It has a large parking area in front of two of the three main buildings.

It is in close proximity to Night City Prison to the northwest, Megabuilding H6 to the south, and the abandoned Electric Corporation Power Plant to the northeast. A TV interview near the gates has a reporter asking the manager about the safety of the power plant, as there are rumors it is poisoning the surrounding neighborhoods.

The game's Night City map from the physical edition, however, labels it instead as a nuclear power plant. Another location that has been described as using microwave tech is the Satwave Power Plant.

## Phant
Phant is a drug in .

Overview
Phant is a popular, highly addictive, hallucinogenic drug distributed by the Scavengers in Dogtown. The drug, consumed through an inhaler, stimulates the production of both serotonin and dopamine, affecting the central nervous system and causing irreversible changes to the brain. The delusions and hallucinations appear soon after the drug has been consumed and stimulate the user's sight, hearing and touch.

Research conducted by former biological engineer Maggie Isley indicates that 86% percent of those that have used Deep Dive–a less addictive and less effective drug–will later move on to Phant.

Asssociated Shards

Notes
*Phant is rumored to be better than even the best braindances.
*Phant is about 4 to 5 times more effective than Deep Dive.
*All of the eleven Cyberjunkies in Dogtown used Phant.

## Phantom Liberty
Phantom Liberty is an expansion for . It was announced on September 6, 2022, and released on September 26, 2023.

Pre-Release Description
Phantom Liberty is a new forthcoming addition to Cyberpunk 2077. It will feature a spy-thriller story set in a whole new area of Night City. As V, take on an impossible mission of espionage and survival. With new skills, new weapons and new tech, plunge deep into a web of broken loyalties and political power plays.

Coming some time in 2023, it will be available to PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Plot
V gets involved in the conflicts of Dogtown, which will somehow lead them to pledge allegiance to the New United States of America. In order to complete their mission, they will partner with FIA agent Solomon Reed.

## Philippe Oreste
- aka：Agwe
- status：Unknown
- place_of_birth：Haiti
- home：Pacifica, Night City
- gender：Male
- affiliation：Voodoo Boys
- occupation：Ship captain (formerly)
Gang leader

Philippe Oreste, also known as Agwe, is a character in the universe.

Biography
In 2062, a large tropical storm devastated what remained of Haiti, forcing its last residents to abandon the country in order to survive. Philippe Oreste, a captain of a ship, sailed through the waves, winds, and torrential rains of the storm to save 150 lives and guide them to safety atop pneumatic rafts. Over the following months, with their home lost, Philippe led the refugees in search of shelter and a new life, wandering around North America and eventually reaching Night City, where they were employed in the construction of a resort city in the Pacifica district.

Among the refugees was a gang of netrunners whom Philippe managed to organize to help the local Haitian community in Night City, including residents from other past diasporas. This gang would eventually gain the name of the Voodoo Boys among the city residents, since their real name was not revealed to outsiders. With how much Philippe had done for his people, the Haitians soon began to refer to him as "Agwe" in honor of the ancient loa deity of the same name, who was said to be the patron of sailors and captain of the ship Immamou that transported souls across the seas to Guinee. However, the Agwe of yore and other gods eventually faded from memory, for they couldn't look after the people as the nascent Voodoo Boys had come to do.

By the 2070s, the Voodoo Boys local Net network was named "Rezo Agwe" or "Agwe's Network" after Philippe.

Pisces is a Side Job in .

Walkthrough

Some time after receiving Judy Álvarez's message thanking them for being a good friend and agreeing to help her free Clouds, V receives a phone call from Judy, telling them that she finally heard back from Maiko Maeda, and that she is gathering with the others–Tom Caldera and Roxanne Sumner–at Megabuilding H8.

Once V joins them at the Megabuilding, the group reiterates the plan before taking the elevator to the maintenance level, where Judy and V disembark to take control over the level, while Tom and Roxanne continue on to level 8 where Clouds is located.

To gain control over the level, Judy tells V that she needs to gain access to the control panel located on this floor, but that the Tyger Claws resistance in the area may make it difficult for them, and tasks them with taking out the Tyger Claws. After V has dispatched of the enemies, they regroup with Judy at the control panel. Judy informs V that she will not be coming with them to the penthouse, and that from here on out they are on their own until they meet with Maiko. Judy stays behind on the maintenance level to observe both V's situation as well as the situation in Clouds, and V takes the freight elevator to go to the roof of the Megabuilding.

Once on the rooftop, Judy instructs V to jump down onto the balcony of Hiromi's penthouse. Inside the penthouse, there are four more Tyger Claws that make it more difficult for V to gain access to Hiromi's office. After V dispatches them and opens the door to the office, V is greeted by Maiko, who was waiting for their arrival. Inside the room, Hiromi Sato is accompanied by Jun Azegami and Marcus Ichida, two other high-ranking Tyger Claws bosses, and three dolls for pleasure. The three of them are engaged in a braindance, while V and Maiko talk.

When V questions Maiko about the unexpected presence of the two Tyger Claws, she reveals that she only went along with Judy's plan to arrange her own rise to power as Hiromi's replacement. The Tyger Claw bosses are there so Maiko can expose Hiromi's incompetence, gain their trust, and join the Tyger Claws herself. She is certain that without the protection of a gang, the dolls will be unable to hold onto Clouds by themselves and will be crushed. As Maiko prepares to jack the men out, V must decide what to do next: either side with Maiko in her negotiation with the bosses, or side with Judy and stick to the original plan to liberate the dolls.

:V decides to side with Maiko and accept her bribe. Angered by their decision, Judy severs ties with V over the betrayal and leaves the city. It is later revealed that although Clouds no longer has a constant Tyger Claw presence with Maiko in charge, working conditions are just as bad under Maiko as they were under Woodman. Tom and Roxanne are unhappy with the situation, but continue working at Clouds.

:Judy is disappointed with being played but comes to terms with it, admitting that Maiko knows more about how to protect Clouds than she does. It is later revealed that although Clouds no longer has a constant Tyger Claw presence with Maiko in charge, working conditions are just as bad under Maiko as they were under Woodman. Tom and Roxanne are unhappy with the situation but continue working at Clouds.

:Judy is shocked that Maiko is dead. V can argue that it was self-defense, and Maiko should have known better, but Judy insists that Maiko's death was unnecessary. Judy leaves, saying she needs time to process events. It is later revealed that the Tyger Claws retaliated against the dolls harshly and reclaimed Clouds. Tom is killed, Roxanne is forced into hiding, and Clouds is closed indefinitely.

:Judy is pleased that V stopped Maiko's power grab and Clouds is now managed by the dolls. Judy will mention that the Tyger Claws retaliated, resulting in Tom's death and Roxanne fleeing.

After the confrontation in Hiromi's office is settled, V must leave the apartment and take the elevator to the ground level to meet with Judy to discuss what happened.

Journal Entry
What's worse than a corpo? A wannabe corpo.

You know what? I'm not even surprised you let yourself get talked into this little uprising. Hey, back in my day I would've bum rushed the riot shields in the name of joytoys' freedom or whatever... But this Maiko chick? I've got a bad feeling about her.

Objectives
*Wait for Judy's call.
*Talk to Judy.
*Go to Megabuilding H8 in the afternoon.

citation

Placide is a high-ranking member of the Voodoo Boys gang in .

Biography
Early life
After Haiti was decimated by natural disasters, Placide, along with many other Haitians, moved into Pacifica, a run-down district of Night City. Placide became the second-in-command of the Voodoo Boys under Maman Brigitte. He radiated an aura of danger and threat – inspiring fear and respect in those around him. Placide cared little for the outsiders who came into Pacifica and would only help those in the Haitian community. Like most of the Voodoo Boys, he was a dedicated netrunner who was determined to uncover the secrets of the Old Net.

2077
In 2077, NetWatch had tasked an agent to map out the Voodoo Boys data fortress in Pacifica and shut it down. Ti Neptune discovered that NetWatch was in their system but was quickly hit with black ICE and frozen, along with Brigitte. The NetWatch agent kept her and Ti in stasis until they were finally awoken after Placide, another member of the Voodoo Boys, hired the mercenary V to infiltrate the Grand Imperial Mall to stop NetWatch and free Brigitte and Ti.

Placide was V's point of contact with the Voodoo Boys as the latter investigated who tried to kill Evelyn Parker with a virus, and in the hopes of finding a way to safely extract the Relic. Not knowing or caring what V wanted with Maman Brigitte, Placide intended to use V as a "ranyon", a "floor rag" or disposable merc, to infiltrate the Grand Imperial Mall and figure out what the Animals who had recently occupied the place were up to, and if they were connected to attempts to penetrate the Voodoo Boys' private Net, "Reza Agwe". V reluctantly agreed, unaware that Placide was acting independently and knew that Reza Agwe's attacker was a member of NetWatch. He installed a surveillance program in V's cyberware that would also act as a lethal virus that would kill the NetWatch agent, Bryce Mosley, every other agent connected to Mosley's network, and ultimately V.

When V discovered NetWatch's involvement, they were perturbed but continued hunting Mosley at Placide's urging.

:Placide was enraged at and suspicious of V's decision. And upon their return to the Voodoo Boys hideout, Placide confronted V as if to start a fight. However, Maman Brigitte interrupted the two, taking V with her. NetWatch agents then attacked Reza Agwe at the moment Alt appeared in the Net, causing her to conflate the Voodoo Boys with NetWatch and burn them. Brigitte and all Voodoo Boys connected to Reza Agwe died, and V was forced to deal with Placide as they left, since he held the access token needed to unlock the church's door.

:
::Placide would message V later on and threaten them.

:Once V hacked into Mosley, Placide ran a virus against the entire NetWatch network. Although, it's unclear if he intended to kill V as collateral-- V burned out but recovered thanks to the Relic. Once confronted, Placide chalked it up as an occupational hazard and blamed Mosely. The situation was deescalated by the awakened Brigitte, who led V to the group's secret mainframe and plugged into the Net, in order to retrieve one of Johnny Silverhand's memories to use as bait for the VDBs' main project: contacting Alt Cunningham beyond the Blackwall to negotiate an alliance with the rogue AIs there.

:
::V decided to kill the Voodoo Boys to avenge Evelyn Parker and/or because of the gang's continued mistreatment of them.

::
:::Placide later messaged V through the Net, telling them to watch their back.

:
::V ended business with Brigitte peacefully, and left the church under her protection, in which case Placide was somewhat disappointed that he was unable to kill them. Placide would later message V, telling them to watch their back.

Database Entry

- transcript：Placide – one of the top brass in the Voodoo Boys, a secretive and elusive gang of netrunners in Pacifica. The Voodoo Boys normally don't want anything to do with people from the "city," but Mr. Hands managed to arrange a meeting for V with Placide. He's not much of a talker and despises helping outsiders, but if V can use him to get access to Maman Brigitte, the chéfine of the Voodoo Boys, they'll be one step closer to solving their Relic problem.

Abilities

In addition to this, Placide is immune to the System Collapse quickhack.

Play It Safe is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough

V must travel through the parade in Japantown, eliminating three snipers who threaten Takemura. A can be found behind a closed door while en route to the second sniper, just after exiting the elevator and before climbing the ladder. The code is 2906. It is also possible to open the door with Technical Ability.

The bossfight against Sandayu Oda automatically triggers once V disconnects the netrunner. He will rapidly slash at V with blades, every so often running away and camoflaging himself to heal. Upon defeat, the katana can be obtained.
Takemura asks V to spare Oda. Incapacitating Oda will result in him appearing in Totalimmortal and helping V against Yorinobu Arasaka's forces, while killing Oda results in additional dialogue from Takemura being unhappy.

Journal Entry
:Since I obviously wasn't invited to Saburo Arasaka's funeral, I guess this sad little parade will have to do - I'm just missing confetti. But in all seriousness, Takemura must have a death wish. He's just gonna jump onto Hanako's platform? Be my fucking guest - we'll deal with the snipers. Meanwhile, keep an eye out for an escape route. This is gonna go all kinds of wrong - I can feel it.

Objectives

* Go to the bazaar in Japantown.
* Talk to Takemura.
* Neutralize the snipers. [0/3]
** Reach the first sniper.
** Reach the second sniper.
** Talk to Johnny. [Optional]
** Reach the third sniper.
* Talk to Takemura.
* Reach the netrunner.
* Disconnect the netrunner from the net.
* Defeat Oda.
* Talk to Takemura.
* Connect to the Access Point.
* Deactivate the security turret.
* Wait for Takemura to make his move.
* Escape the parade grounds.

Trivia
*The title of the job comes from the Iggy Pop song, Play It Safe.
*The parade procession is heavily inspired by the parade in Ghost in the Shell 2.

## Playing for Time
Playing for Time is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough

V appears in cyberspace and will sees a red figurem being prompted to follow. They will eventually be able to interact with him, which takes V out of cyberspace. They will wake up in a landfill and crawl out before Dexter DeShawn and Goro Takemura appear.

As V slips in and out of consciousness, Takemura ends up killing Dex and puts V in his vehicle to take them to Hanako Arasaka. However during the drive, Arasaka agents will appear and attack Takemura. at this point V will regain limited consciousness, and an injured Takemura will need their help fending off the attackers, providing V with an airhypo. V will then need to fight off the Arasaka assassins.

:V failed to use the airhypo in time and succumbed to their injuries.

Takemura will hand V a Kenshin to dispatch the assassins, the combat is largely scripted, with each enemy being taken out at a specific point, regardless of damage taken. Eventually an assassin armed with mantis blades will show up and jump on the car, eventually causing it to crash in a billboard. After dealing with the final enemy, Takemura asks V if they know a trustworthy ripperdoc so they can get the medical attention they require. After V names Viktor, the merc calls Delamain to pick the duo up. Takemura performs triage on V with Delamain's help, and narrowly manages to get to Viktor's Clinic in Little China, with Takemura almost succumbing to his own injuries upon arrival.

Several weeks will pass with sporadic moments of consciousness as Viktor tries to keep V alive. Eventually one day V will regain full consciousness, and is able to converse with Viktor.

Viktor explains that V's hallucinations are fragments of Johnny Silverhand's memories, triggered by Dex shooting the merc in the head. The Relic inside of their shard slot was consequently triggered, using nanites to revive their brain. However, these nanites also recognize V's mind as a foreign entity, which it is now destroying in an effort to clear the way for the Johnny's engram. Viktor will solemnly explain that V only has weeks to live, and that reversing the process is beyond his abilities.

Misty will then enter the room and take V back to their apartment before giving them medicine: Pseudoendotrizine that speeds up the process of the engram, and Omega blockers, which slow it down. V can speak with her a bit before she leaves. V will then go to sleep.

When V wakes up, Johnny will appear standing near them, reacting with hostility to his situation. V will then try to leave, but Johnny will push them backwards. At this point, Johnny and V will realize that their movements are connected, prompting the former to attempt disconnecting the Relic, knocking out the latter. When V comes to and attempts to take the Omega blockers, Johnny slaps them out of their hand and instead demands that they "stick an iron in your mouth and pull the trigger", before leaving them to crawl to their pills. V will eventually swallow one, resulting in them passing out again.

V will wake up in the shower, and after exiting and getting dressed, Takemura will call asking to meet in Tom's Diner to talk. V will then do as asked and head to the diner, where they will find Takemura drinking coffee. He will then explain to V about why he saved them and his plan prove that Yorinobu killed his father, with V as a witness. He also promises that Arasaka can help V with their biochip problem. V talks about alternative methods of possibly dealing with the biochip, but Takemura will dismiss them before leaving.

Once V is alone, Johnny will project himself in front of them. He will explain that he has done some thinking and that the two need to work together to deal with their predicament. He suggests they speak with Rogue, as the two knew each other a long time ago and that she can help.

Journal Entry
:Don't trust that Takemura. Meet with him, sure, check him out, but keep your eyes open. He's a corporat, meaning he's looking to use you.
:Well, chica/broder, looks like we got ourselves into a real fix. No chance in hell I'm wriggling myself out of this one, but you're still alive. And as Misty says, "As long as you're alive, there's hope." Fate's given you a second chance, so use it – get back on your feet. Do that, and consider your best friend's last wish fulfilled.

Objectives
*Approach the stranger.
*Crawl to safety.
*Neutralize the motorcyclists.
*Survive the attack.
*Call Delamain.
*Talk to the stranger.
*Leave the apartment.
*Crawl towards the pills.
*Take the pills.
*Stand.
*Leave the apartment.
**Find something to eat. [Optional]
**Open your inventory and put on some clothes. [Optional]
**Stock up on ammo. [Optional]
**Check your email. [Optional]
*Talk to Takemura.
*Read the message from the Megabuilding H10 Administration. [Optional]
*Meet with Takemura.
*Talk to Takemura.
*Talk to Johnny Silverhand.

Notes
*Although listed as the first job in Act 2, the part up until V standing up in the shower is still part of the interlude, and the in-game map, inventory, etc. are inaccessible until this point.
*The entire map and most activities like Gigs and scanner hustles are unlocked after leaving the apartment, but some content remains unavailable until the quest has been fully completed by talking to Takemura.
*When Johnny tells V they don't have to talk out loud with him, their voice projection changes slightly to indicate they are now talking mentally. This can be noticed anytime V talks to Johnny after this quest, even when they are completely alone.
