Poland, officially the Polish People's Republic, is a country located in East-Central Europe.

History
Due to the Crash of '94, foreign investors—who had kept the country afloat since the fall of Communism—decided to pull out, and martial law was declared. By 1999, Poland had managed to find its footing again due to its thriving criminal underground, despite the government trying to get rid of it.

In late 2018, Poland was invaded by the Czech Republic, which was spurred on in secret by the European Economic Community, who feared the Czech Republic's economic success, and hoped to vilify its government to the world and sew distrust within its people.

Government
In 1994, after the global stock-market crashed, the president of Poland declared martial law. They then instituted the Harbingers, a taskforce dedicated to taking down organised crime using brutal methods. This should make Poland a police state, but in actuality the Harbingers are too few in numbers to do much of anything.

Much of Polish society is also controlled by the Church of Poland, a radical sect that opposes the Neo-Catholic Reformation bringing modern societal values into the religion.

Culture
Poland is on paper a very poor country, but its black market keeps it afloat. Goods found in Poland include drug-making, operating shadow clinics, and trading in illegal software and Cyberware.

Major Cities
*Warsaw

Notes
*Misty Olszewski has family living in Warsaw.

Trivia
*The game development studio CD Projekt RED, the people behind the new , is based in Poland; more specifically in Warsaw - the capital city.

Poppy Farm is located on the southeastern Badlands of Night City.

History
Early history - 2040s
During the 2040s, this place was a farmstead that grew a breed of Papaver somniferum, also known as the opium poppy, hence the name. It was owned by Jack Boles, who had signed on Biotechnica's TradFarm Initiative, thus making his farm part of a franchise model where the megacorporation acted as both the exclusive provider of seeds and supplies, and as the primary distributor of the end product. It wasn't the best deal, but at least it prevented Continental Brands from sending out troops to raze his farm to the ground like they did with most competition.

The crops at Poppy Farm had been genetically modified by Biotechnica in order to withstand the virus that wiped out most of the species during the 1990s. This investment was of great importance to the megacorporation, and since it was located on the desolate Badlands, Biotechnica stationed guards around the place at all hours.

2070s
Around the mid-2070s, Poppy Farm was at first sight abandoned, though the Wraiths appeared to be storing equipment slated to be smuggled across the border with South California.

:In 2077, River Ward and V might have traveled to the farm in the hopes of finding River's kidnapped nephew, however they were met with a band of Wraiths. Once they were defeated, River and V made their way to Edgewood Farm.

Notes
*In , the closest dataterm labels the location as "Lake Farm."

引文：Took fifth place in the "Car of the Century" award in 1999.（911 Turbo (930)）

The 911 Turbo (930) is a vehicle manufactured by Porsche.

Overview
Originally intended to meet homologation requirements for Group 4, the 911 Turbo was Porsche's first turbocharged 911, featuring wider fenders and its signature "whale tail" design to aid engine cooling that differentiates it from standard 911s of the era.

By 2077, only a handful were left in the world, and each one of them was worth its weight in gold.

History
The Porsche 911 Turbo is the signature customized vehicle of legendary rockerboy Johnny Silverhand, lead singer of Samurai. This specific Porsche was manufactured in 1977. When Johnny got his hands on it many years later, he tuned the vehicle and customized it to represent his own tastes.

In the following years, Johnny would cruise through Night City with it. It was also the car Johnny drove while dating Rogue Amendiares when they were younger.

After Johnny's death in 2023, a former pararescue firefighter known as Samantha Stevens recovered Silverhand's car. She kept it hidden in her garage for more than a decade, preserving the vehicle in its pristine state by keeping it in cold storage. Unfortunately, Samantha died of cancer at some point after the events of Black Dog. This was due to her having accessed the Hot Zone shortly after the nuke went off.

At some point later, Adam Smasher acquired the rockerboy's possessions from Samantha's place, including the car, which ended locked up inside a cargo container on the Ebunike Docks of Night City. Aymeric Cassel, a classic car collector enthusiast, visited Night City in 2077 after Jeremiah Grayson — Smasher's right hand — offered the Porsche to him. Unfortunately for Aymeric, it was around that time when V and Rogue assaulted the docks to find information about Smasher, but instead they ended up finding Grayson. He had the keys to the car, and after obtaining them, V opened the container and got their hands on the 911 Turbo, to the surprise and enjoyment of Johnny's engram. Rogue was also surprised to see the car if V managed to convince her to have a date with Johnny.

Database Entry

- transcript：An all-time classic and king among 1% wannabes - the Porsche 911 Turbo (930) is one of the most iconic cars in automotive history. Not many are left in the world, but the ones that remain are each worth their weight in gold. Its sleek, compact appearance is unmistakable - who wouldn't want one? Sadly, none could ever hope to look as cool behind the wheel as Johnny Silverhand.

Acquisition
The 911 Turbo can be obtained during the Chippin' In quest, right after the fight against Jeremiah Grayson. You can either spare him so he gives you the keys to the car, or take them from his body if you decide to kill him. Afterwards, go to the ladder on the starboard of the ship and activate the button you'll find up there. One of the containers will be lifted down. Just go there, open the container doors and take the car.

Development
An unpublished story by Mike Pondsmith called "The Punk and the Parking Space" serves as a backstory to the car and its first appearance in the Never Fade Away adventure. The car was originally owned by Toshiro Harada, an Arasaka executive who Johnny had a dispute over a parking spot. In the end, Johnny shot out the tires of the executive's car. A few years afterwards, Johnny stole that same car, eventually deciding to keep it. Due to Toshiro being the one who captured Alt Cunningham, it ended up as being something personal for Johnny.

Before choosing the Porsche, Mike had considered the Sunbeam Tiger. He had owned four of them and was familiar with the vehicle. Ultimately though, Pondsmith decided not to do so after theorizing the car was not very recognizable by the 1980s.

Design
The developers of CD Projekt RED worked alongside with Porsche to accurately recreate the car in Cyberpunk 2077 as well as the changes made to fit the in-game world. The changes from the real-world model include LiDAR for self-driving capabilities, cameras instead of mirrors, self-changing transmission, various drive modes (almost directly lifted from current-day Porsche models), and the ability to run on biofuel.

Porsche themselves also made a one-off real-world recreation of the car that was on display at the Porsche Museum from October 15 to 22, 2020; while it did not feature any of the futuristic changes, it does have the livery that dons Silverhand's car in the game.

Notes
*Being manufactured in 1977, Silverhand's Porsche is 100 years old by the time the game is set, making it the oldest car in the game.
*Despite having four seats, the rear ones are inaccessible.
*In-game, its front wheels have a wider track width compared to the rear, going past the fenders. However, this is not true in pre-release screenshots and in its database photo.
*Alongside the cabriolet version, these are the only real-world automobiles included in Cyberpunk 2077.
*Prior to Patch 2.1 it was called Porsche 911 II (930) Turbo.

Trivia
*As depicted in the name, Johnny's Porsche is indented to be a 930, a variant of the 911.
*On the passenger side of the dashboard, there is a metal plaque that bears the signature of Jakub Przybolewski, the Senior Vehicle Artist at CD Projekt RED.
*In 2022, CD Projekt RED collaborated with Hot Wheels to manufacture a scale model car of the Porsche 911.
*In Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto Online, a livery that bears a resemblance to the 911 Turbo — named "[https://gta.fandom.com/wiki/File:CometS2-GTAO-front-RockN%27RollLegends.png Rock N' Roll Legends]" — is available for the Pfister Comet S2 (based on the Porsche 992) and its Cabrio variant.

## Portugal
type
- location：Iberian Peninsula, Europe
- capital：Lisbon
- population：10,000,000 (2020)
- demonym：Portuguese

English

French
Tamazight

- ethnic_groups：Caucasian, Arab, Amazigh, and others

- military：50,000 (Corporate Security; 2020)
- appears_books：

Portugal is a southern European country on the Iberian Peninsula, bordering Spain. It is a member of the European Economic Community, but is mostly controlled by corporations.

History
In 2002, in an alleged effort to decrease Spanish influence over the country, makes a deal to have Arasaka and Amazonian Service & Security replace its national police force. The European Economic Community, usually wary of corporate activity, allowed this as they saw Portugal as insignificant to Europe and its economy.

Leveraging this fact, AgriCorps successfully managed to make Portugal sell much of their land to them in 2008. By 2011, it was law that if a plot of land wasn’t producing enough equity, it had to be sold. Many small landowners were forced to sell to the AgriCorps because of it. In 2013, the Iberian Peninsula experienced a massive drought, forcing Portugal to sell itself completely to the corporations to prevent it from going bankrupt.

However, as of 2020 the corporate alliance controlling the company has split into two factions, each trying to elect their own president. The factions were primarily led by Arasaka and Amazonian Security respectively, and it was expected to evolve into a corporate war. It’s unlikely this happened, given that Arasaka ended up involved in the Fourth Corporate War against Militech before tensions could escalate.

Government
Portugal is a country completely controlled by the corporations, and represents their idea for the world in miniature.

However, in the year 2020 a schism has occurred and the corporate alliance controlling the company has split into two groups. The first group consisted of Amazonian Service & Security, Iberian AgroIndustrial, and World News Service, while the second group consisted of Arasaka, Metropolitan Merchant Finance, and Oliveira-Leisure.

Culture
Portugal is quiet and orderly, just how the corporations like it. Every adult citizen is assigned a job based on their specifications, and all they need to do to live their life is to work. Any rebels against this system are quickly taken away for "re-education".

Cities
*Lisbon
*Coimbra

## Practice Makes Perfect
Practice Makes Perfect is an optional Main Job in . It becomes available at the start of the main job The Rescue, and acts as a tutorial covering the basics for weapons, hacking, stealth, and melee combat.

Walkthrough
Narrated by T-Bug, it consists of four training modules, although only the first two are required to complete the job:
- Combat Basics
- Hacking
- Stealth
- Advanced Combat

Journal Entry
:Better to be prepared than dead. The street can be brutally unforgiving, so a quick brush-up on combat skills certainly couldn't hurt.

Objectives
*Talk to the drill sergeant.
*Complete all training modules.

;Module 1 - Combat Basics
*Pick up the weapon.
*Shoot all the targets.
*Wait for the next round of targets.
*Shoot all the targets.
*Pick up the weapon.
*Eliminate all enemies.
*Take the inhaler.
*Use the inhaler to regain Health.
*Enter the training area.
*Eliminate all enemies.
*Step onto the platform.

;Module 2 - Hacking
*Approach the window.
*Open your scanner.
*Scan two objects highlighted gold.
*Approach the window.
*Use the TV screen to distract your enemies.
*Sneak up to the guard.
*Eliminate the guard.
*Pick up the body.
*Hide the body.
*Sneak up to the guard.
*Take down the guard and hide the body.
*Enter the training area.
*Take control of the camera.
*Hack one of the guards and use the "Detonate Grenade" quickhack.
*Exit camera view.
*Connect to the Access Point.
*Step onto the platform.
*Use the door to exit the simulation. (optional)

;Module 3 - Stealth
*Go to the window.
*Tag all the guards.
*Enter the training area.
*Hide from the guards.
*Sneak to the exit.
*Enter the next training area.
*Tag the camera.
*Reach the exit without being detected by the camera.
*Step onto the platform.

;Module 4 - Advanced Combat
*Enter the arena.
*Hit the enemy 3 times with Fast Attacks.
*Hit the enemy with a combo attack.
*Hit the enemy with a Strong Attack.
*Hit the blocking enemy 3 times with Fast Attacks.
*Break the enemy's blocking stance with a Strong Attack.
*Block 3 enemy attacks.
*Block 2 Strong Attacks.
*Counter an enemy attack 2 times.
*Dodge 3 enemy attacks.
*Defeat the enemy.
*Take the katana.
*Defeat the enemy.
*Step into the training area to continue.
*Defeat all enemies.
*Step onto the platform.
*Use the door to exit the simulation.

Notes
*This job does not reward level experience or street cred.
*Patch 2.3 added the option to replay this job, available in Settings > Controls.
**This option can be used at anytime, as long as V is not in combat and nothing important is happening.
**If this job was skipped during The Rescue, completing the first two modules will be required before being allowed to exit.

One of Rogue Amendiares's signature weapons, alongside . Prejudice sports an orange paint job, with a number of small decals stuck all over it.

Prejudice has an iconic modifier that synergies with Pride. After an enemy has been neutralized using Pride, switching to Prejudice will cause it to not consume any ammunition in the magazine for 5 seconds. Pride is a variant of the Constitutional Arms Liberty in .

Characteristics
This iconic black and gold Liberty was the signature weapon of Rogue Amendiares.

If an enemy was recently neutralized with the , Pride will consume no ammunition for up to 5 seconds after swapping to it.

Pride has an iconic modifier that guarantees a Critical Hit on the first shot fired from a new magazine. While the user's Health is above 75%, headshots deal an additional 250% damage, for a total of 400% additional damage.

Pride additionally has 100% additional Crit Damage and 10% additional damage against Elite enemies at all times, though magazine size is reduced by 4 rounds.

Acquisition

Behind the Scenes

Notes
*If Johnny keeps V's body during the Sun Ending, he will have Rogue's gun and deposit it in her grave, despite Rogue being still alive and appearing in the calls in the credits.
*Pride was originally a Tsunami Nue. During For Whom the Bell Tolls, Rogue mentions a Tsunami weapon. She carries a Tsunami Nekomata for the rest of the following quests, but never uses it. Lastly, when scanning the pistol before leaving it in the niche during New Dawn Fades, the scans reads: "Pride; Rogue's Pistol; Rogue's custom Tsunami Nue." Moreover, in the interview featured in , Rogue mentions that she's using uniquely-modded Tsunami Nue as her personal weapon.

Trivia
*Alongside Rogue's assault rifle Prejudice, this handgun's name might be an allusion to the novel Pride and Prejudice.

## Protein Farms Trailer Park
- type：Community
- region：Badlands
- subregion：Biotechnica Flats

The Protein Farms Trailer Park is located inside the Biotechnica Flats, on the southern Badlands of Night City.

Overview
This semi-abandoned trailer park is completely surrounded by the Biotechnica protein farms. After the facility's construction, the inhabitants were contracted to work on the farms, with many having to take double shifts, hardly ever seeing their families. Pastor Sachs tried to uplift the community's spirit, but to no avail. Over the years, the settlement decreased in population, and even the church was abandoned. By 2077, only a handful of individuals still lived here. Noticeably, the location has a large cemetery surrounding much of the settlement.

The abandoned church was used by Polyhistor, where he installed some servers, computers and an Arasaka Tower 3D arcade.

## Pyramid Song
- type：Side Job
- quest_giver：Judy Álvarez
- district：Badlands
- sub_district：Laguna Bend Reservoir
- location：Abandoned Lake Dwelling
Laguna Bend ruins
- reward_item：Judy's Apartment as an apartment (dependent)
 (dependent)
MaxTac tactical helmet with multifunction infovisor (romance)
MaxTac multilayered armor-weave Jacket (romance)
Heavy-duty MaxTac cargo pants (romance)
Diving equipment box memorabilia
Laguna Bend wall photo memorabilia (dependent)
- previous_quest：Pisces

Pyramid Song is a Side Job in .

Walkthrough

Some time after the events at Clouds, Judy calls V to meet her at an abandoned shack near Laguna Bend Reservoir at sunrise.

Once V arrives, Judy explains what she wants to do here. She tells V that she wants to go diving in the lake where the shack is located, and record a braindance of them doing so. V agrees to do so, and puts on a diving suit. After V puts on a braindance scroller, which links their brains, they dive into the lake together. While in the water, V calibrates their suit by swimming around Judy, then swimming backwards, then finally letting her hum a song to check auditory responses.

Once calibrated, Judy and V use a pole to dive down to Laguna Bend, Judy's old hometown that has since been flooded. Judy will talk about the different locations they come across, while V has the opportunity to locate and scan a few objects, with memories of Judy's childhood playing in their head throughout. They first come across a restaurant and her home, in which V can scan and talk about the restaurant's sign, an old photo, and a hockey stick. V can also pick up and give Judy an old camera nearby. They then come across a gas station, in which V can scan and talk about an umbrella, a doll, and an abandoned car.

After moving on from the gas station, they come across a church. V must find a way into the church. After finding a way inside the church, Judy begins talking about her memories near the altar. While she is doing so, V's relic malfunctions, causing them to pass out.

V wakes up on the dock to Judy performing CPR on V, and Judy is relieved when V wakes up. She then offers for V to stay the night at the house. V goes into the house with Judy afterwards. Soon after, V must go outside to start the generator to power the house. While outside, V will hear Judy's memories of Evelyn Parker. When V returns, Judy will have gone to the bathroom. V enters to check in on her, and Judy talks about what happened as a result of the raid on Clouds.

:V gets affectionate with Judy. Judy takes V to the bedroom, and they have sex on the bed. V wakes up in the morning with Judy beside them, although she gets out of the bed before V wakes up.

:After V dresses, she meets Judy sitting on the dock. Judy asks V what they think their day prior meant to V.

:
::Judy becomes upset, and she will immediately leave not just the area, but Night City as a whole, and delete V from her contacts.

:
::Judy and V form a couple, causing Judy to stay in Night City. She gives V access to her apartment through personal link, allowing them to visit at any time.

:Judy goes to bed once they finish talking in the bathroom.

:
::V wakes up the next morning and meets Judy sitting on the dock. She will explain to them that she is leaving Night City, and gives V access to her now vacant apartment.

Journal Entry
:Everyone knows you can't just count on yourself in this goddamn city. You always gotta have a few chooms who owe you a favor. And a few you've got dirt on too. But when you've got the kind of choom who starts asking you for weirder and weirder shit? That's when problems start.

Objectives
*Meet Judy in the early evening.
*Talk to Judy.
*Go to the lake's edge with Judy.
*Take the wetsuit.
*Connect to the terminal.
*Wait for Judy to calibrate your gear.
*Dive into the water.
*Follow Judy.
*Calibrate your gear.
**Stand in position.
**Circle around Judy.
**Go back.
*Talk to Judy.
*Follow Judy.
**Search for clues near the diner and Judy's house. [4] [Optional]
*Follow Judy.
**Search for clues near the gas station. [3] [Optional]
*Follow Judy.
*Look for a path into the church.
*Talk to Judy.
**Stand up.
*Go to the cottage.
*Enter the cottage.
*Talk to Judy.
**Start the generator.
**Check on Judy.
*Grab your clothes.
*Find Judy.
*Talk to Judy.

Notes

*Completing this quest will award a box with diving equipment memorabilia for V's Apartment. Moreover, if she was romanced (female V only), Judy will text V some time after completing the mission, attaching a Laguna Bend-screenshot from the braindance she is working on, which then also becomes an apartment memorabilia.
*If a female V romances Judy, she will text V some time after the mission, saying that she left a gift on her kitchen counter - the Mox shotgun. If Judy is not romanced but the mission was completed amicably, Judy will simply leave the shotgun on the counter for V to find and take.
**There are a few gifts that are only rewarded when romancing Judy; the MaxTac multilayered armor-weave Jacket, MaxTac tactical helmet with multifunction infovisor, and Heavy-duty MaxTac cargo pants, which can be found in Judy's Apartment.
*The song Judy is humming can be identified by a Streetkid V as "Only You" by Etta Sorrentino. The melody is part of the Cyberpunk 2077 soundtrack song "Bells of Laguna Bend" by Paul Leonard-Morgan. If Judy is waiting for V when they arrive at the dive site, she is humming the same melody while she waits. If Judy is romanced, she will also hum the same song when in the shower in V's Apartment during I Really Want to Stay at Your House.
*In the underwater section you can find a unique item named the Heart of Laguna Bend. Before finding an access into the church, you can pick up the cross necklace found on top of garbage bags, in the stairs leading to the church's doors.
*Other items were supposed to be obtainable, though only the aforementioned necklace remains.
**Vintage camera - In front of Judy's old house. Though you can pick it up, it won't be added as an item. Still, you can give it to Judy.
**Doll - The doll found inside the barrel in the gas station was also supposed to be added to the inventory.
**Water-damaged record - An old record of Samurai also appeared.
**Waterlogged pistol - A rusted old Arasaka Tamayura could be found, though it wouldn't be usable.
*Not getting intimate with Judy during this mission (by choosing not to touch/kiss her or because of being male), will result in this mission being the last time she appears in game (not counting the video message during the end credits). Judy will have coffee by the lake with V in the morning to explain that she will leave Night City and then gives V access to her now vacant apartment. Some time later, she will send V a text message with a photo of Seattle, explaining that she is continuing her journey after having visited her grandparents in Oregon. If the player follows the advice by Johnny Silverhand, who got annoyed with Judy's illogical behavior, and already leaves while Judy is sleeping, she will not return to her apartment, simply disappear, and even remove V from her contacts. The same will happen if a female V has sex with Judy but then tells her it was nothing more than a "pleasant distraction" the next morning.

## Pyromania
Pyromania is a Perk in .

Overview
Pyromania can be unlocked at 15 Technical Ability after unlocking Health Freak.

Level 1 increases recharge speed of Health Items and grenades by 8%.

Level 2 increases explosion radius for grenades and the Projectile Launch System by 10%.

Level 3 grants a temporary buff that lasts 12 seconds that increases Movement Speed by 5% and explosion damage by 10% after hitting an enemy with an explosion in combat. This effect can stack up to 5 times. If you take damage from the explosion, the effect adds 2 stacks instead of 1.

Notes
Level 3 effect can be triggered by:
*CHAR Incendiary Grenade, EMP Grenade, F-GX Frag Grenade, MOLODETS BioHaz Grenade, Ozob's Nose
*Projectile Launch System
*Fully charged
*Vulnerability Analytics

Changelog
*Patch 2.0 - Added.

Péter Horváth is a character in .

Biography
At some point in his life Horváth spent time in jail, which caused such drastic change in his behaviour that people who knew him no longer recognized the man.

2077
Horváth is a former vendor who worked for Christine Markov at one of the stalls in the Cherry Blossom Market. He eventually left his work at the stall to make speeches about former mayor Lucius Rhyne and how corporations had controlled him. After a while, he showed back up at the stall with high-quality cyberware installed to the point where he was hardly recognizable. The cyberware was an anonymous gift from an unknown source that according to him, "finally saw what he was worth".

Horváth was hired to assassinate Mayor Rhyne at City Hall in The Glen, but was shot multiple times by River Ward before being able to do so.

The "Charon" is a custom variant of the Sport R-7 540, a vehicle manufactured by Quadra in .

Overview
The Sport R-7 "Charon" is a rental car owned by Charon Exotics. The Cassel twins rented it during their stay in Night City.

The Charon has a unique holographic paintjob which projects "hot rod"-style yellow and orange flames over the hood after reaching around 50 mph. Damaging the car will disable this projection.

Performance-wise, the Charon is a base model Quadra Sport R-7 540 and is therefore not as powerful as the 580-based "Sterling" or prototype "Vigilante" variants of the Sport R-7.

引文：The best-selling sports car of the last decade. As many as 300,000 units were produced by May 2075.（Turbo-R 740）

The Turbo-R 740 is a vehicle manufactured by Quadra in .

Overview
The Quadra Turbo-R was introduced as America's response to Japanese sports car manufactures. It was designed and built in Detroit. With its powerful turbo-charged V8 engine, it instantly became a star in the tuner scene when it was released in the mid 2050s, this was despite its universally criticized suspension. The next version introduced in 2058 was named the Turbo-R V-Tech, and featured an improved exhaust system and suspension, quickly earning it the status of cult muscle car. The most recent version, introduced in 2069, never surpassed the legendary Quadra Turbo-R '58 in the eyes of the many car enthusiast.

Upgrades
*CrystalCoat

Specifications
The vehicle is powered by CHOOH2, a standard synthetic alcohol fuel.

The Turbo-R 740's styling is reminiscent of 1980s exotic sports cars, particularly the Ferrari Testarossa and Lamborghini Countach, as it is wedge-shaped with bulging wheel arches. It has an aerodynamic rear spoiler, grey paint, and numerous light strips serving as brake lights.

The Turbo-R appears to have no rear bumper, leaving the car's exhaust visible. Two people can be seated in the car. Structural bracing protrudes from the door sills, and the dashboard features carbon fiber and several screens indicating the vehicle's status. Essential information like current speed and engine RPM are shown in a heads-up display (HUD). The gull-wing style steering 'wheel' has two handles for the driver to use.

The car is rear-wheel drive, with the rear tires larger and wider than its front ones. Additionally, the car's exhaust manifold and air intake are visible on the rear, and its mid-mounted engine can be seen by opening the hood. The vehicle's storage compartment is in the front, and can also be opened.

Database Entry

Acquisition
It can be acquired from the AUTOFIXER netpage for €$69,000.

Quadra Turbo-R 740 V Message CP2077.png

Notes
*Prior to Patch 1.5 it cost €$129,000.
*Prior to the introduction of AUTOFIXER, Wakako Okada sold the car via a text message: "I have a Quadra Turbo for sale, parked at the attached coordinates. I suspect it will not stay available for long, since it is a good machine and there is no shortage of buyers. If life has taught me anything, it is to size an opportunity as soon as it appears, for it might only appear once. You can think about that while you gather the money to pay."

引文：Appears in the iconic car chase on a factory roof in Jakarta in the blockbuster movie Bushidō 7: Revenge Never Sleeps.（Turbo-R V-Tech）

The Turbo-R V-Tech is a vehicle manufactured by Quadra in .

Overview
The Quadra Turbo-R was introduced as America's response to Japanese sports car manufactures. It was designed and built in Detroit, instantly becoming a star in the tuner scene when it was released in the mid 2050s.

The next version introduced in 2058 was named the Turbo-R V-Tech, and featured an improved exhaust system and suspension, quickly earning it the status of cult muscle car. The most recent version, introduced in 2069, never surpassed the legendary Quadra Turbo-R '58 in the eyes of the many car enthusiast.

Upgrades
*CrystalCoat

Specifications
The vehicle is powered by CHOOH2, a standard synthetic alcohol fuel.

The V-Tech is rear-wheel drive, with the rear tires larger and wider than its front ones. Additionally, the car's exhaust manifold and air intake are visible on the rear, and its mid-mounted engine can be seen by opening the hood. The vehicle's storage compartment is in the front, and can also be opened initially evidenced by Jackie placing a Militech bot inside of it in the [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vjF9GgrY9c0 2018 gameplay reveal].

Database Entry

- transcript：What's the difference between the V-Tech and the classic Turbo-R? Well... What's the difference between a diamond and a chunk of coal? The building blocks are the same, but end results couldn't be more different. Quadra's Turbo-R V-Tech is the queen of the road, a car that turns heads even when you're not burning rubber.

Acquisition
It is rewarded at the end of Sex On Wheels, a quest which is accessible after completing Gig: Life's Work.

Message

引文："Hey! Got your umber from El Capitan. Thanks for all your help with the car :) Listen, there's just one last thing... I won't be coming back to NC anytime soo, and there's this sweet ride I had to leave behind. It'd be a damn shame for her to sit alone gathering dust and rust. It's a Quadra Turbo-R. It's yours now :) Go wild, have fun, show off. Sending you [COORDINATES], Check your map, it's near the train tacks out in Rancho. Car's in a garage near the loading station. Adiós, V!"（Jake Estevez）

Known owners
*V (dependent)
*Jake Estevez (formerly)

Development
The V-Tech was first featured in the 2018 Cyberpunk 2077 E3 trailer, where it was driven by V, and again in the Cyberpunk 2077 48-minute gameplay reveal, where it was owned by Jackie Welles. The game files still mention a V-Tech owned by Jackie.

The car was originally named the "Quadra V-Tech", before it was changed to its current name during the first Night City Wire event. With the name change, a badge reading "Turbo-R" is seen on the right side above the taillights where the car's company name is.

At the end of the E3 2018 trailer, an IP address was briefly shown. Users who entered the IP address in a web browser were brought to a Quadra-themed website, which was the start of the Cyberpunk 2077 ARG.

Notes
*The V-Tech is one of the few vehicles in Cyberpunk 2077 (the others being V's Hella EC-D i360 and the Galena "Rattler") that has a sticker of a horse on the rear right side of the car, and a bulldog bobblehead on the dashboard.
*A parked V-Tech can be seen during The Heist. After exiting the elevator to the parking in the last stage of Konpeki Plaza, it can be found to the player's right.
*In the Nomad lifepath, V obtains a V-Tech car model memorabilia.
*As a rear-engine, rear-wheel drive car with narrower front tires, the V-Tech has a strong tendency to understeer when cornering hard. It can however be induced into a drift through the use of handbrakes.

Trivia
*The horse decal is a reference to Roach, Geralt of Rivia's horse in The Witcher series.
*As part of a cross-promotional event with Microsoft, Turn 10 Studios, and Playground Games, the Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech is available in Forza Horizon 4 starting December 11, 2020. To obtain it, one needs to win the "_:NIGHTCITY.exe:_" street race event, which is a one-on-one race against the car itself.
**In this game, the V-Tech is depicted to have a mid-mounted 4.4L twin-turbocharged V10, developing 607 hp and 560 ft-lb of torque. It is said to weigh 2756 lb (1250 kg). Additionally, it is equipped with a rear-biased all-wheel drive system.
*The Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech appears as a car decal in Fortnite Chapter 6, Season 1 alongside V, Johnny Silverhand and several other cosmetic items as part of the Night City Denizens Set.
*The distinctive engine note from the Quadra Turbo-R and its V-Tech variant was created using recordings of a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamborghini_Huracán Lamborghini Huracan] / [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audi_R8 Audi R8] [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamborghini_V10 5.2L V10 engine].

Bugs
*The V-Tech that V drives during Sex On Wheels is not the same which spawns when calling the vehicle. As such, the former will stay where it was left, even if destroyed.

The "Cthulhu" is a modified version of the Type-66, a vehicle manufactured by Quadra in .

Overview
The Cthulhu is a customized Type-66 that was owned by the corporate and street racer Peter Sampson.

Sampson used the car during the Night City annual death races in which his rival Dean Russell - and Claire's husband - died. The following year, Peter raced with Cthulhu as the champion in the final race. Depending on the choices made during the event, he will either finish the race safely or crash the car, which will be then engulfed in flames. Nevertheless, the Cthulhu is eventually repaired and it's either given to V for free, or is sold by AUTOFIXER.

Upgrades
*CrystalCoat

Database Entry

Acquisition
The Cthulhu can be obtained by two different ways depending on the choices made during The Beast In Me quest chain.

:After a few days, Muamar Reyes will send V a message saying he is selling the car. It then can be acquired from the AUTOFIXER netpage for €$67,000.

Quadra Type-66 "Cthulhu" V Message CP2077.png

:It is obtained for free after receiving a message from Sampson a few days later. Sampson thanks V for convincing Claire to spare his life. See "The Beast in Me" below for more details.

The Beast in Me
To obtain the Cthulhu for free, V has to proceed carefully at certain moments in The Beast in Me: Santo Domingo and The Beast in Me: The Big Race. After qualifying for the final race at the end of the former job, Claire will ask to speak to V about her husband Dean. Make sure to select the following dialogue options when they appear:

- "You sure it was murder?"
- "Sorry, Claire, but I can't help."
- "Okay, I'll still drive. But only to win."

During the final race, keep pace with Sampson's car. Note that choosing to race with Claire's car instead of one V owns is sufficient for this route. At a specific point along the highway, Sampson's car will become too damaged and he will pull off the course. Follow him (this will forfeit the race) until he crashes, then get out of the car with Claire to confront him. Make sure to trigger each of the limited-time dialogue choices that appear:

- "What's he mean?"
- "Wait, wanna hear this."
- "Claire, that true?"
- "Yeah. Let him go."

If all requirements were met, Claire will be persuaded to spare Sampson and drive back to her garage. She will also give her car - Beast - to V since she no longer wants to race. After the quest is completed, Claire will send V a follow up text within a day, and this will be followed by a separate text from Sampson 7–10 days later informing V that they now own the fully-repaired Cthulhu.

Notes
*The trunk does not open, but the Stash can be accessed.
*Prior to Patch 2.0 it cost €$76,000.
*Prior to the introduction of AUTOFIXER, Regina Jones sold the car via a text message: "Hey, so the "Cthulhu" has just emerged from the abyss. Sounds scary, right? Seriously though - car's out of this fucking world. Barely even touch the gas and the next thing you know you're burning rubber and your eyes are tearing up. But something tells me if anyone can handle this beast, it's you. Buy it and don't look back."

Trivia
*The car is named after the fictional entity Cthulhu, created by H.P. Lovecraft.
*One of the file names for this car is "dominic_truck." Considering this name, the type of car, its color, and bodywork; it is likely the "Cthulhu" is inspired by the black muscle cars driven by Dominic Toretto of the Fast & Furious franchise.

The "Hoon" is a unique version of the Type-66, a vehicle manufactured by Quadra in .

Overview
The Type-66 Hoon has an exceptionally high top speed, acceleration, and maneuverability befitting a racing car, but it suffers from low traction at the rear wheels, and can easily cause the car to spin out of control during a turn. However, if the latter is mastered, the driver will be able drift during sharp turns to compensate.

The Hoon is equipped with two machine guns that are both located in the front bumper, requiring the driver to turn the car towards its target in order to hit it. The machine guns are capable of destroying civilian vehicles within seconds. Small targets are a little harder to hit, but landing even a few hits can prove devastating. They have a limited ammo capacity of around 50 rounds per gun before needing to be reloaded.

The Hoon's CrystalDome allows it to withstand more damage than a non-combat vehicle and fully protects the driver from small arms fire, but not from larger caliber weapons or explosives.

Acquisition
*I'm in Love with My Car

Trivia
*This vehicle and its associated quest are an homage to Ken Block, a rally driver and YouTube star, who passed away on January 2, 2023.
**The vehicle uses his signature number 43.
**The name "Hoon" is a reference to the Hoonigan Racing Division, a motor racing team founded by Ken, as well as the act of hooning.
**The vehicle's livery resembles that of Ken's [https://www.hooniganracing.com/pages/garage 1965 Ford Mustang "Hoonicorn" RTR], a car specially built for Gymkhana.
**A sticker by the racing number reads "K.B. 67-23", referencing his initials and his years of birth and death.

The Javelina is also armed with a pair of fixed forward-mounted machine guns. While the guns cannot be aimed independently, the vehicle's high torque can be used to steer in-place in order to keep them pointed on a target.

## Quake
Quake is a Perk in .

Overview
Quake can be unlocked at 15 Body and unlocking Painkiller. Quake has three levels.

This perk only affects Blunt Weapons.

Level 1 reduces Stamina cost for Blunt Weapon attacks by 15%.

Level 2 increases Blunt Weapon attack speed by 20%.

Level 3 unlocks the ability to perform a Quake; a violent ground slam, which damages and staggers nearby enemies with a chance to Knockdown. Quake can also be performed from midair (Superhero Landing). This ability has a 10 second cooldown.

Superhero Landings can be achieved by jumping from an elevated area down to the ground. When landing, a shockwave will be released that damages nearby enemies based on falling distance.

Changelog
*Patch 2.0 - Added.

Queen of the Highway is a Side Job in .

Walkthrough
A day after helping Panam Palmer and the veteran Aldecaldos seize the Basilisk from Militech, V is contacted by Panam, telling them that they have completed the assembly of the panzer vehicle, and ask V if they want to drive it.

After accepting Panam's invite, V heads back to the Mobile Camp in Rocky Ridge to meet with her and the other Aldecaldos. Upon approaching them, they tell V that they're still finalizing a few little things, such as the panzer's Intrusion Countermeasures Electronics. Cassidy tells V that they left the Militech trucks at a nearby Raffen Shiv camp so that the corporation would start looking at them instead of the Aldecaldos. Upon telling them that they always dreamed of driving one of them, Panam tells V that they can climb inside the panzer.

As V climbs inside the panzer, Panam joins them in the other seat and starts up the Basilisk, which does not go smoothly. After starting the machine, Panam ask V what they think about the machine, and explains that while connected to the vehicle's systems, it in essence becomes an extension of the body. As Panam pilots the vehicle out of the camp for a test run, she explains V that a co-pilot is needed to handle the sensory overload, which is why the pilot takes care of the vehicles movement and the co-pilot takes care of the vehicle weapon systems.

Once far enough away from the camp, Panam disconnects from the vehicle, and instructs V to jack-in themselves and pilot for a short distance before asking them to maneuver through the Wind Farms. After piloting past several wind turbines, Panam tells V that it is time for some target practice, and asks that they take the five targets in the area.

After the target practice, Panam tells V that she will also be connecting to the vehicle. After she connects, V experiences strange feelings and asks Panam what happens. She explains that, while both jacked-in, the pilot and co-pilot's systems become intertwined.

:Panam asks V if they want to "try it out," which they accept, and a romantic scene will engage.

Suddenly, Panam and V are attacked and surrounded by the Raffen Shiv, and have to defeat them. Saul Bright contacts them over the radio, informing them that the Raffen Shiv have also started assaulting the camp, and instructs them to return to help.

After defeating the Raffen Shiv, Panam and V park and exit the Basilisk, and proceed to meet with Saul. Saul tells Panam that she's been making the right decisions for the Aldecaldos family, and asks her that she leads them alongside him. He admits to Panam that he was wrong about her actions before, and proceeds to hug her. After hugging, Panam exclaims that things have to change in order for her to accept her new position, to which Saul responds that the first thing they have to do is find a new location for their camp before Militech and more Wraiths find them. The rest of the Aldecaldos congratulate Panam, before she asks that V follows her.

While walking, Panam and V reflect back on their adventure so far, and Panam tells V that it is mostly because of them that they've made it this far, and that if they were ever in the need of the Aldecaldos's help, they would have it. Upon arriving at the camp's bar, she will ask V what type of drink they'd like, and talk more with each other. While talking, Panam asks that V stay with the Aldecaldos, which V isn't sure about because of the situation they are in. As V turns away from the bar, they suffer from another Relic malfunction and drop to the floor.

Some time passes, and V is woken up by Panam inside a tent. Panam explains to V that while they were passed out, the Aldecaldos moved camp to a safer place. Panam proceeds to ask V what is happening to them, to which V will explain the unique situation they are in. After talking, V gets up and is met by Mitch and Saul, also asking V what happened.

After talking with them, Panam escorts V out of the camp back to their vehicle. While following Panam, she will tell V that the camp's new location is outside Militech's usual patrol areas and that they have a better tactical advantage due to the layout, but that despite that, they will soon have to move again.

## Rache Bartmoss
- status：Unknown
- dob：1992
- dod：2020 (physical)
May 6, 2022 (consciousness)

- home：The Net

 (mentioned)

- appears_other：(mentioned)

Rache Bartmoss is a legendary netrunner in the -series who in the early 21st century became notorious as the man who caused the DataKrash and killed the old Net. He invented the Demon and Bloodhound series of programs. He also co-authored the Rache Bartmoss' Guide to the Net and Brainware Blowout books alongside Spider Murphy.

Biography
1990s
Rache Bartmoss was born in 1992 to unnamed parents.

At just four years old, Rache Bartmoss started netrunning for the first time. Because of his inexperience with the Net, he used his real identity, oblivious to the potential risks. By the time he had realized his mistake, he was good enough that it no longer mattered. Throughout the years, he experimented with everything and tried every interface that Spider Murphy had heard of.

2000s
For some time, Bartmoss tried working for companies, writing software for them, though he would always end up double-crossing them and running away before getting caught. He would then clean his record and move to other companies. In 2004, however, he worked for CCI Development for a year, since they did not deal with any wrongdoings.

During this time, he created the Demon programs for them. He was later fired for dropping a political movie into the database's code. Within a week, he fried their computer system and the company went bankrupt. Bartmoss later sold the source code to the Demon programs to several software houses and made enough money that he did not need to work anymore.

At the age of seventeen, he met Spider Murphy for the first time when she came to warn him about her Corporate father wiping his SIN from the system. He trained her from that moment on and they became close friends. Rache Bartmoss, along with Spider Murphy, Dog, and Edger, would run the Net for fun, lynch NetWatch hacks without profit, because they could and it was the right thing to do, and do things others thought impossible.

Shortly after the Pacifica region of the Net was formed, Rache Bartmoss would run the region with Alt Cunningham, who later called these times her best netrunning memories.

2010s
By the early 2010s, Bartmoss moved into a conapt building in South Night City (on the edge of the Combat Zone) where he arranged for everyone who did not have a neural implant to leave the building, and instead arranged to have corporate workers with neural processors installed move into the building, whereupon he installed within them a hidden subconscious personality program to control them. He would use everyone in the building for surveillance and protection. After working on this secret project for a decade, it finally became operational in 2019.

In September 2014, when the Ihara-Grubb Transformation Algorithms were released to reform the Net in order to provide a uniformed interface look and feel, Bartmoss stayed in to plant the R.A.B.I.D.S. viruses into the newly reformed Net, while the rest unplugged to watch it redesign himself. During this time his heart stopped for 10 seconds.

In 2015, Rache Bartmoss met Kimi Tara on the Net and took her out on a date. They slept together, which Bartmoss ended up regretting. She left him after with the intention of moving to the next media personality. Bartmoss denounced physical relationships after his encounter with Kimi.

2020s
In 2020, his heart stopped and physical body died for unknown reasons, though his life-support machines sensed it and super-cooled his body. Because he was connected to the Net at the time, his consciousness continued to live on. After his physical death, he tried to contact Spider Murphy for ten months, sending her an email to inform her of his death, and told her his life memories so that they could finish compiling Rache Barmoss' Guide to the Net. Around this time, Bartmoss released the "Succubus III" program, and made it look like Spider Murphy's Net ICON as a last "big brother" prank, so that she would be the lust object to "hormonally challenged losers" on the Net. He intentionally waited until he was dead so that Spider would not be able to take revenge.

In 2021, Militech contacted Bartmoss for his help against Arasaka in the Fourth Corporate War. Being convinced by Alt Cunningham's digital ghost, he attacked Arasaka from the Net and located the master program of Soulkiller.

Bartmoss died in 2022 after getting his signal tracked, which resulted in a corporate raid on his conapt building. Right before his death, Bartmoss contacted Spider Murphy and urgently invited her to a chat room, where he confessed his love to her before releasing the R.A.B.I.D.S. to the Net and causing the DataKrash.

2070s
Bartmoss was still widely regarded as one of the greatest Netrunners to have ever lived and was accepted to be the mastermind behind the DataKrash, though his fate still remained a mystery to most.

In the year 2075, a contract that was made with the cryogenic freezer's owners expired. The freezer, and Bartmoss's corpse within it, were discarded at the Municipal Landfill in the Red Peaks region of the Badlands by the Revere Courier Services per the contract's agreement.

Around two years later, in 2077, the mercenary V received an odd signal directing them to a set of coordinates in the Badlands, where the mercenary found the freezer, "confirming" Bartmoss's physical death and potentially putting decades of urban legends and conspiracy theories to rest. The digitized psyche of Johnny Silverhand—contained on the experimental biochip installed in the mercenaries neuroport—immediately recognized the person in the freezer as Bartmoss.

The mercenary took Bartmoss's Elysia cyberdeck, which was still accompanying his corpse in the freezer, to the netrunner Nix at the Afterlife for analysis. Having jacked-in to the cyberdeck, but unaware of all the security measures in place, the netrunner sprung one of the various traps that were laid by Bartmoss and would have died as a result if it weren't for the mercenary's quick thinking.

Cyberpunk 2027
In the CyberGeneration timeline Rache's body was recovered by the Eden Cabal. They couldn't revive him, but upgraded his hardware so he could communicate through the Virtual Net. He serves as a tutor and mentor to young hackers, teaching them how to use the Virtual Net as their combination playground and abattoir.

Cyberpunk 203X
In the alternative timeline, Rache left behind boobytrap and attack programs all over the Net. When his body was vaporized, his life-support stopped sending the delay codes. The programs went off, crashing systems and frying any netrunners jacked-in at the time.

Notes

*Rache Bartmoss considers himself a big brother to Spider Murphy.
*Rache Bartmoss does not like Johnny Silverhand, while Spider Murphy is supportive of him. Spider, on the other hand, does not like Kerry Eurodyne.
*Rache Bartmoss had a hairless cat named Deathwish.
*According to , it is not certain the corpse found in the junkyard fridge belongs to Bartmoss, considering Johnny's unreliable memories.
*Mike Pondsmith has said the inspiration for Rache Bartmoss was a combination of several hackers he knew in his youth, but the closest real person to Rache was Harlan Ellison.

## Rachel Casich
- status：Dependent
- dod：2077 (dependent)
- home：Night City
- gender：Female
- hair_color：Pink
- eyes：Pale Blue
- affiliation：Fourth Wall Studios
- occupation：Braindance Producer
- role：Corpo
- voiced_by：Rebecca Yeo

Rachel Casich is a braindance producer at Fourth Wall Studios in .

Biography
In 2077, Rachel had heard Joshua Stephenson's story being told in the media and saw an opportunity to exploit it to make a new braindance of his experiences. Rachel approached Stephenson in prison and offered him a deal: Stephenson would be released from prison under close NCPD supervision and permitted to visit the families of the victims he murdered so that he may try to seek forgiveness. In exchange, Rachel would be permitted to record all of his experiences, including his death by crucifixion and sell it as a high production braindance.

Rachel believed that Stephenson was crazy for deciding to end his life in such a brutal way, but that was irrelevant to her, she saw that Stephenson genuinely believed in what he was doing, which made it a truly unique experience for a braindance compared to actors. She titled the braindance "The Passion" and made arrangements for Stephenson's final days.

While traveling with Stephenson and NCPD officer Vasquez to visit Stephenson's victim's families, Rachel encounters Bill Jablonsky and V, chasing their vehicle. After Vasquez collides their vehicle into a truck, he confronts the pursuers. If V does not intervene in the altercation between Vasquez and Jablonsky, Stephenson asks V to accompany them on his mission, to which Rachel loudly objects as she does not want anything to distract or interfere with Stephenson's emotions while they are working on the braindance. Stephenson insists that V joins and Rachel reluctantly accepts in order to keep on schedule.

Rachel listens in on the conversations between V and Stephenson in the car rides to and from the El-Ahmar residence and becomes increasingly concerned about the nature of the conversation as she feels it is changing Stephenson's emotions. When the group stops at Pie-Z for lunch, Rachel ushers Stephenson and Vasquez inside so that she may talk to V privately in the car. She explains her concerns about V's conversations with Stephenson and offers to bribe V with money if they simply walk away and stop interfering with Rachel's project. If V refuses, Rachel becomes annoyed and enters Pie-Z to join Stephenson and Vasquez. Rachel tries to control her temper while V continues talking to her and Stephenson but ultimately snaps. She ends V's involvement in the project and abruptly leaves with Stephenson and Vasquez.

Some time later, Rachel organizes the crucifixion event for Stephenson in Stage 11 at Fourth Wall Studios. However, shortly before Stephenson is due to lay himself upon the cross, he begins to become very nervous and refuses to do it until he has spoken to V. Rachel, concerned about completing the project, agrees to call V and summon them to the studio. When V arrives, Rachel is clearly very stressed about the whole situation, concerned about the fate of her project rather than Stephenson's well being. Rachel shows V to Stephenson's dressing room and gives them a moment before interrupting to inform them it is time for Stephenson to go through with the crucifixion. If V agreed to Stephenson's request to have V nail him to the cross, Rachel will initially object, but quickly complies just to finish the project. Rachel explains to V what to do and that their lines will be on a teleprompter for them. After V or an actor has nailed Stephenson to the cross and the scripted lines have been performed, Rachel watches on and waits for Stephenson to die. She then thanks V for their help in getting the project finished and says she will contact them and wire their payment once the braindance has been released.

Depending on V's conversations with Stephenson, Rachel later calls V and sends their share of the sales from "The Passion". If V had been supportive of Stephenson, Rachel will call V ecstatically happy that the braindance was a huge success and thank them. If V was pessimistic during their conversations with Stephenson and sowed doubt in his mind, Rachel will call V absolutely furious that they ruined the project.

Associated Quests

## Rainbow Cadenza
- type：Bar & club
- city：Night City Area
- appears_books：
 (mentioned)

The Rainbow Cadenza was a club located in the Greater Night City Area.

History
Early history
Established somewhere in the Greater Night City Area, the Rainbow Cadenza was a small backstreet bar in which rookie rock bands gave it a shot at the club's stage. Such was the case for Samurai, a chromantic rock band that in 2003 had played some of their earliest gigs there. Of note, during Samurai's third gig at the Cadenza, a small fire broke out and some people in the public tried to put it out with beer, causing the situation to worsen. Samurai's drummer Denny got her hair slightly burned and had to wear a wig for a few weeks. It was never figured out who caused it, though rumors pointed to a lit cigarrete thrown by either Kerry Eurodyne or Johnny Silverhand, both members of Samurai.

One night of 2003, after finishing their performance, Samurai was approached by Jack Masters, the head executive at Universal Records at the time. He had been impressed by their music, and after the show, had decided to sign them into the label, something that would eventually lead Samurai towards stardom.

Legacy
At some point during the Time of the Red, the Rainbow Cadenza was demolished, with the surrounding area becoming the Crystal Park Market. Soon afterwards, the club's former location became the home of a small restaurant, replacing the space where rock legends once sang their hearts out with a kitchen in which tofunomiyaki was prepared.

By the 2070s, Rainbow Cadenza was still fondly remembered by diehard fans of Samurai, who kept visiting the restaurant in hopes of finding the bygone club. This happened frequently enough that the owner at the time was considering putting a sign at the entrance explaining the misunderstanding.

## Rancho Coronado (2077)
- type：Sub-district
- city：Night City
- district：Santo Domingo
- gangs：See Gangs
- appears_books：

Rancho Coronado is one of the sub-districts of Santo Domingo, located in southeastern Night City.

Overview
Rancho Coronado appears as a self-sufficient town within Night City. The corporations who own the Arroyo factories planned and advertised it as a place for their workers to live out the real American dream. Rancho Coronado consists almost solely of identical houses, reminiscent of the ones seen in mid twentieth century American suburbs.

The district has its own bars, shops, school, park, restaurants, and even a metro station. Security is overseen by the 6th Street gang, since the NCPD is spread too thin to effectively police the suburbs. Residents of Rancho Coronado are primarily mid to high-ranking factory workers, and some corpos who were tired of Night City's lights and noise. Most of the people here work in Arroyo and don't need to leave Santo Domingo for their entire lives. Despite its Utopian concept, the neglect and disrepair can be clearly seen.

Database Entry

- transcript：Some insist that Rancho Coronado is not a district of Night City, but in fact a little town situated at its edge. It could seem that way at first sight, with its identical townhouses reminiscent of the classic 20th century inner-city suburb, quaint stores, bars, a park, school and subway station. Sounds like the American dream, right? Well, that's exactly what the land and factory owners of Arroyo thought when they designed the neighborhood. Every building was intended for workers living near their respective plants. Corporations even made sure that Rancho Coronado had its own law enforcement, since the NCPD couldn't be relied on. Rancho Coronado now mostly houses middle and higher-ranking corporate employees from nearby factories and offices who wanted to get away from the city. Residents from other districts like to joke that it resembles more of a hamster cage - everyone in Rancho Coronado has everything they need in one place. You've got your wheel, your water, your food - what more could you ask for?

Behind the Scenes

引文：Tree-lined cul de sacs, backyard pools, red-tile roofs and a rocking chair on every porch: Rancho Coronado was supposed to have it all, the twentieth-century suburban dream recreated in a dried-up riverbed by the old Petrochem dam-cum-landfill on the edge of town. The glossy brochures wrote themselves: leave the meat-grinder of the city behind and live in a self-contained slice of paradise. You'll have shops, services and entertainment right in the neighborhood, and good jobs in the Arroyo factories next door. You'll never have to return to Night City proper again. The funding and will to actually achieve this vision never materialized. Rancho Coronado is a half-assed simulacrum of a suburb, a glorified shanty town slapped down on toxic soil next to a dump. Still, many are happy to live there. Its corporate owners pay for a private security force, so it's fairly safe. Tiny, cookie-cutter houses are no North Oak villas, but they sure beat the ratholes in Arroyo megabuildings. And while garbage AVs constantly spill trash on you, some of it you can fix up or sell.

The Container Freight Station (CFS) is located in Rancho Coronado, in the Santo Domingo district of southeastern Night City.

Overview
Located on San Amaro street in Rancho Coronado, during the 2070s, this CFS was one of the largest in Night City.

In 2075, Maine's crew can be seen using the location as a testing grounds for David Martinez and making use of Aldo's garage as a hideout. It is also where the crew ends up being chased by the Tyger Claws whom were hired by Maxim Kuznetsov to chase down the stolen Villefort Alvarado V4F 570 Delegate.

In 2077, V meets Panam Palmer here for the first time in person. She can be seen here working on the engine of a borrowed Thorton Colby C210 Camper. Jake Estevez also used one of the storage buildings in the area to keep his Turbo-R V-Tech.

Associated Quests

Notes

The Rancho Coronado Public High School is located in Rancho Coronado, in the Santo Domingo district of southeastern Night City.

Overview
This educational institution functioned as good as anyone would think.

The high school takes up a block with the school buildings in an L shape and has two basketball courts and a shabby baseball field. The grounds are secured by fences topped by barbed wire, and the main entrance has concrete pedestrian turnstiles and vehicle gates.

2077
There is a 6th Street presence with a trio of members and three vehicles in the parking lot and two Valentinos gang members loiter outside of the main gates. There are also two unique conversations held by NPCs: one by the parking lot where three students talk about using drugs as study aids and another by the basketball court where a man quickly changes the subject from drugs to education prior to BDs.

## Randy Kutcher
- aka：bRandy
- status：Dependent
- place_of_death：Edgewood Farm, Rocky Ridge (dependent)
- home：Kutcher's home, Trailer Park, Red Peaks

Randy Kutcher is a character in .

Biography
Randy Kutcher is the oldest son of Joss Kutcher and an unnamed father who was an Aldecaldo Nomad. He has two younger siblings, Monique and Dorian. When Randy was young he was close to his uncle, NCPD detective River Ward, who used to send him a record of his favorite band Tainted Overlord every year for his birthday.

Randy's mental health and family life deteriorated severely following the death of his father. He began using drugs and developed a deep depression, and no longer saw his uncle.

At some point in 2077 Randy chanced upon a Net site ran by Anthony Harris. Harris, a serial killer known as Peter Pan, took advantage of Randy's depression and built trust with the boy by talking to him about his experiences as well as sending him gifts. Randy eventually agreed to meet Harris in person, and was subsequently abducted by him and taken to Edgewood Farm, where Randy was hooked up to Harris's machinery which pumped various chemicals into his body.

Although Harris was later shot and rendered comatose by the NCPD following a routine road stop, the whereabouts of Randy and Peter Pan's other victims remained unknown. However Randy's uncle River decided to take matters into his own hands and, with the help of the mercenary V tracked Randy down to free him.

:Randy was later taken to the NC hospital where he spent a substantial amount of time recovering from his ordeal. Despite all this the future looked optimistic for Randy, as his uncle believed that his experience with Harris might serve as a clean break for him as well as an opportunity to repair his relationship with his mother and River.

:V and River did not manage to reach the farm in time, resulting in Randy's death.

Biography
Razor Hugh used to be a poor street kid like most Night Citizens who eventually joined the Animals and became a star athlete and professional boxer. Razor has elite corpo sponsors and prototype implants such as carbon fibers, Titanium Bones, nanofiber RealSkinn, shock absorbers and hydraulic joints, all optimized by Night City's best bioengineers.

He is Night City's three-time heavyweight champion and holds a record of forty-seven consecutive victories with twenty knockouts.

Razor is told by his manager he must go to Night City to fight in the bush leagues in order to promote himself. Razor claims it is to prove to people he is not a sellout and that he is still a street kid. His manager is willing to bribe V to take a dive and in exchange will receive a better payment than if they win.

He is the final fighter V must face in Beat on the Brat. Viktor Vektor tells V that Razor is near undefeatable due to his augmentations but has one weakness, Razor had his abdominal muscles swapped out and they have not completely settled in.

 Razor showed there could be sore winners, and teased V about their loss.

## Rebel! Rebel!
Rebel! Rebel! is a Side Job in .

Walkthrough
Some time after the Samurai reunion, Kerry will call V with a request to meet him in the early morning at the Foodscape bar on the corner of Manzanita and Mallagra street in Rancho Coronado, Santo Domingo.

:V waits on a chair at the Foodscape until Kerry arrives.

Kerry arrives in a Galena that he borrowed, and asks V to get in. After V gets in the car, he explains that the J-Pop group Us Cracks signed a deal for touring in the New United States, and they want to promote it using a cover of one of his songs. Kerry was tipped off about a van transporting the group's gear to Night City, and he wants to blow it up before it gets there.

Kerry and V drive to the Red Peaks in the Badlands, on the edge of the city, and stop at a bus stop. Kerry instructs V to get equipment out of the trunk and follow him to lay out the stinger for the van. After they hide at the bus stop, the van runs over the stinger and stops, and Kerry and V force the occupants out of the van. They cooperate and give them the access card to the van, and after V opens the van's rear doors, they let the occupants go.

Once the occupants are set free, V blows up the van using a grenade. After they and Kerry talk more, NCPD sirens are heard in the distance. Kerry and V get into their car and try to escape from the police.

:After losing the NCPD tail, Kerry instructs V to drop him off on Montenegro street, and offers V coffee at the nearby Capitán Caliente.

:

::V accepts Kerry's invitation, and they have a coffee at the restaurant. Kerry tells V that he used to have little money left after buying equipment, but that he and Johnny always had something left to visit the place. After the waitress takes their order, Kerry says that the last time he felt like the way he does now was during his last tour and concert, and wonders if their scheme will pay off. After some more talking, Kerry leaves.

:After a few minutes, Kerry will text V that he sent them a payment of €$21,470 for their help.

:
::V declines Kerry's invitation, and they part ways. Kerry tells V that he will send the payment later and says goodbye.

:Kerry and V escape the NCPD tail, but V leaves afterwards. Kerry will text V that he'll make it back home on his own, and that he will call if something comes up.

:Kerry and V are caught by the NCPD, resulting in V's death after a firefight.

:If V escapes the area without getting into the vehicle with Kerry, Kerry will angrily text V, telling them that he doesn't have time for their shenanigans. Kerry will not contact V again for any further jobs.

Journal Entry
:Look, I don't know if Kerry's just having a real late-life crisis, or whether his shrink's got him some on some sweet new meds, but I do know one thing: this gon' be good. Just meet with the guy. A friend in need is a friend indeed, and I've never been jealous of that second fiddle in my life.

Reboot Optics is a Control Quickhack in .

Overview
A control quickhack that resets the detection progress of the enemies it has been uploaded to outside of combat. When used during combat, it reduces enemy accuracy for 8 seconds.

The variant extends the base duration from 8 to 15 seconds.

The variant increases headshot and weakspot damage against the affected enemy by 15%.

The variant upgrades the base effect by blinding enemies for 15 seconds outside of combat, or greatly reducing enemy accuracy while in combat.

The variant causes the user to replenish 3 RAM units when neutralizing the affected enemy with a headshot or through a weakspot, and spreads the quickhack to the nearest enemy.

The variant doubles Reboot Optics headshot and weakspot bonus damage against against the affected enemy from 15% to 30%.

Acquisition
*All variants can be obtained through Breach Protocol.
*Quickhack and Crafting Spec can be purchased from Netrunners.

## Reconciliation Park
- type：Park
- city：Night City
- district：Heywood
- sub_district：The Glen
- gangs：Valentinos
- appears_books：

Reconciliation Park is located on the northern area of the Glen, in the Heywood district of central Night City. It borders with Corporate Plaza to the northeast.

Overview
Reconciliation Park is a large, tranquil park with lots of vegetation and recreational areas for the residents of Night City. Many citizens and workers from nearby offices go here to relax after a day of work, and is described as a place of repose amidst the bustling city. It is notably surrounded by gorgeous and elegant architecture.

The westernmost section has a small terrace with trees and a few shop stands. A large forest occupies the rest of the park, with multiple paths allowing for a relative peaceful stroll. A small but sizeable lake takes up the northeastern portion, while what appears to be a segmented fountain area is found southwest of the lake. In the northern corner, right at the edge of the lake, there is a small outdoor restaurant. The southeastern section of the forest is stylized after East Asian plant life and architecture, contrasting with the rest of the park. This area contains a Japanese-style gazebo, a torii gate, and a pond. The northeastern border with Corporate Plaza has staircase entrances to the View, an exterior shopping mall named after its views to the park.

The homeless live in lots of places around Reconciliation Park, while the Valentinos gang can usually be found in it as well. Many areas are kept untidy and filled with garbage. The park's view of the sky is partially blocked by a couple of road bridges and the Lincoln Boulevard.

Reconciliation Park was built at some point in the 2050s to celebrate and commemorate the rebuilding of the city — more specifically, the cleaning of the radioactive ruins and start of the reconstruction of the new Corporate Plaza in 2052, said to be inaugurating a new era of corporate harmony.

Associated Quests
*Black Steel In The Hour of Chaos (dependent)

Notes
*Its location and shape is reminiscent of the the old Lake Park, though there is no mention if both are one and the same.
**The southeastern section of Reconciliation Park is stylized after East Asian plant life and architecture. This may be a nod to Lake Park, as its southeastern section in 2020 was part of the Japantown neighborhood.
* describes City Hall as standing behind the elegant architecture that surrounds Reconciliation Park.

It borders Night City to the west, Laguna Bend Reservoir to the south, and the vast Rocky Ridge Plains to the east.

It is cut off in two sections by the Interstate 9. The northern half is mostly devoid, with hills rising tall. The few points of interest would be the near to Rancho Coronado, a small settlement known as the Trailer Park, and Sunset Motel along Interstate 9.

Regina Jones is a Fixer in .

Biography
Regina is a former Media that worked for the World News Service and later for FTF Radio. As a journalist, she also became a mentor to Max Jones. At some point during her muckraking days, Regina needed "help, and fast, too..." and indebted herself to some Chinese officials. It would take her quite some time to pay that debt off. After the radio station was acquired by N54 News, she struck out on her own. Using her extensive network of contacts, Regina quickly made a name for herself as a Fixer.

At some point, Regina won a unique AI-enhanced gun called "Skippy" in a poker game, but it was later stolen from her.

Operating out of Yaiba Tower in Kabuki, Watson, her main fixation is trying to help find a cure for cyberpsychosis, a disease caused by malfunctioning cyberware. In order to do so, she will reach out to V, a mercenary, to engage and neutralize cyberpsychos around Night City in order to help aid the research. In her search for the causes and potential remedies for the condition, Regina is interested in each cyberpsycho biography and will put strong emphasis on V dealing with the cyberpsychos without killing them.

## Relic
The Relic is a series of Arasaka biochips allowing the storage and manifested reading of digitized human psyches known as engrams.

Overview

At least two separate versions of the biochip prototype were developed by 2077, according to the summarized internal report assembled by the former director of the Relic project, Anders Hellman, upon turning coat for the benefit of Arasaka's rival corporation, Kang Tao.

The first version was intended for the commercial market and advertised as a means for wealthy elites to store their psyche in form of an engram capable of basic communication with their loved ones. The form itself would have consciousness but lack true self-awareness. In spite of its limitations, Relic 1.0 has managed to enter the market and the lives of Night City residents, giving hope by providing a notion of immortality truly approaching human reach. Arasaka logs on the other hand reveal that the Relic's initial purpose was of a more capitalist nature - using Soulkiller on celebrities, important cultural icons, and artists in order to create engrams for commercialisation purposes.

The second version of the biochip was a top secret project, personally commissioned and supervised by Saburo Arasaka. It was intended for internal use within the corporation only, never to be sold. Unlike the original biochip, which was only used to communicate with pre-saved engrams with artificially integrated limitations, Relic 2.0 contains a system which was meant to install and activate the engram in a new organic body. The core idea of the project was to implant a digitized psyche into a new host, although only after the body had all neural and cardiac functions terminated, at which point it would automatically expand into the host's brain using nanotechnology. In short, a person who copied their mind onto Relic 2.0 and then died could be restored to life in a new body using the chip, effectively granting them immortality. Internal testing of Relic 2.0 showed promising results, but Arasaka scientists had difficulty preventing the personality construct from becoming emotionally unstable after re-implantation, and the biochip eventually failed in every trial. The Arasaka Corporation also confirmed that Relic 2.0 would not activate if implanted in living individuals who were on the verge of death. The project had not progressed past the trial phase until an unplanned undertaking of the process by a living individual. Examination of the Relic's advancement proved that, despite keeping the subject alive, it was continuing its functional expansion and taking over the motor and psychological functions of the host.

Technical Details of Transport and Storage
The Relic biochip must be stored and transported in stable thermal conditions and in an appropriate neural environment. Even momentary exposure to temperatures falling outside the recommended range could result in permanent damage to the technology. The state of the art of research on the technology in 2077 recommended to store the Relic device in Arasaka laboratory-certified isothermal containers to ensure a stable storage temperature within 2-8 degrees Celsius (35.6-46.4 degrees Fahrenheit).

Ideology
It is easy to discern that a great majority of people, regardless of closeness to the Secure Your Soul program, treat the Relic as a device that grants immortality. Hanako Arasaka treats the engram of her father as a real human being and the Relic as a vessel of his consciousness. Yorinobu Arasaka potentially believed that interrupting the Relic project might prevent his father's resurrection. Liam Northom, the manager and lover of Lizzy Wizzy, had plans for making a backup of her own engram and editing it in order to modify her behaviour.

While Anders Hellman himself never treated the biochip as a device that can actually host consciousness, the contract for the repossession of a human "soul" for the Secure Your Soul program signed under his name promises not to make copies of the created engram due to ethical concerns.

Alt Cunningham, explains that, while she exists as an engram, uploaded to the Net, she has no consciousness, effectively functioning as a Rogue AI. She adds that, once Johnny Silverhand severed the connection between her engram and her consciousness during the 2013 Arasaka raid, the real Alt died along with her organic body. As an untethered AI, Alt is able to read other engrams in their most basic form, so regardless of them potentially experiencing a very human thought process, the raw data that is written this way leaves nothing concealed. On the other hand, the Mikoshi environment allows engrams themselves to interact with one another on a more human level, without the implications of reading each other's thoughts, hence emulating proper conversations.

Similar to all other types of data, engrams can be overwritten with another digitized psyche, which is something Alt offers V as a final solution for their troubles.

Database Entry

- transcript：Relic is an interface and component of Arasaka's experimental, flagship project publicly known as "Secure Your Soul." It uses the concept of personality transferal by converting the data in the human nervous system into a digitized engram and stored as a construct on the Relic biochip. The purpose of "Secure Your Soul" is the ability – currently only available to the wealthiest clients – to communicate with deceased loved ones. Their personality constructs, which are preserved on the Relic biochip mean that in practice, death is no longer the ultimate barrier. However, it doesn't take a genius to realize that the potential for the Relic technology is much higher – Arasaka currently is not sharing any information on its further plans for the program.
