Rhino is a character in and a minor character in .

Biography
In the early to mid 2070s, Rhino used to work together with the netrunner T-Bug, with whom she would do gigs in Coastview, until one of their gigs involved a client under the protection of the Animals. Their Fixer ghosted them shortly before Animals showed up at their doorstep, demanding to speak with T-Bug and challenge her. In her stead, Rhino volunteered to fight, and won.

Now a member of the Animals herself, Rhino is the fist fighting champion of Rancho Coronado and trains at a former paint factory, where she helps her compatriot Animals, such as Kyle, train. V is instructed to fight her in order to become the champion. Rhino boasts that she has never lost a fight and is the only opponent to fight V for free as she only wishes to fight for fun and make a name for herself. She is a very powerful opponent who can take V down in about three or four punches. After being defeated, she is shocked but congratulates V for winning.

In the comic, Cyberpunk 2077: You Have My Word, she briefly appears in the issue, helping another member of the Animals, Kyle, train.

Rhino later appears at the Grand Imperial Mall to watch V's title match against a fellow Animal, Razor Hugh. She will wish them luck before the fight.

## Richard Night
- age：44
- status：Deceased
- dob：1954
- place_of_birth：Pasadena, USA
- dod：September 20th 1998
- place_of_death：Parkview Tower
- home：Coronado City
- residence：Parkview Tower penthouse

Night International

Richard Alix Night was a businessman and founder of the eponymous Night City.

Biography
Early life
Richard Night was born in Pasadena, California, and was the second of five children. His parents were both researchers at Caltech — specializing in materials science. Night showed an aptitude for engineering at a relatively young age, but when a joint venture with his college roommate — Romney Zukarian — turned sour, an angry Night shifted his major from engineering to business financial investment. Armed with his new knowledge of the ins and outs of business, Night soon regained his company from his old rival.

Applying his backgrounds in engineering and investment, Richard soon founded — along with his new colleagues — Halsey, Ferris and Night, a development company that specialized in using advanced construction techniques to build massive mega-projects such as office complexes, airports, and even small cities, in record time. HFN was wildly successful in the years before the Collapse, contributing to the construction of many large model communities around the world, and making all three partners very wealthy men.

At some point he married Miriam Night.

Life-Dream Project
By the 1990s however, Night was concerned by the violence and disruption of the impending Collapse. Additionally, working mainly on corporate-funded projects was swiftly becoming tedious and boring to him. Seeing himself in a unique position to deal with the problem, Richard started a side company known as Night International, and began to draw up plans for a new, ideal city — an environment that would be controlled and managed by corporations, and would be ultimately safe from the economic and social disasters tearing the world apart. His new city would be completely self-sufficient, and capable of holding off even the most determined marauders. It would boast planned neighborhoods dedicated to preserving the feel of different types of nationalities and cultures, as well as a super-modern corporate center that would stand as a shining beacon of enlightened capitalism. It was ambitious, far-reaching, and visionary in its approach. A city so grand that all other cities built before or after it would pale in comparison.

His next move was to secure the unheard of amount of capital needed to finance the gargantuan project. Luckily for him, history and the forces of a collapsing society worked in his favor. With the Collapse, many corporations were looking to establish their own urban areas — controlled zones free of crime, poverty or debt. A place where governments would be corporate-run, allowing optimum zoning and no anti-business elements to interfere with corporate growth. Ideally, it would be a capitalist mecca of opportunity. Night's dream city was tailor-made for that purpose, and the corporations eagerly lent him the raw cash required to begin the project. By 1992, Arasaka, EBM and Petrochem had all signed on with Night, and all that was left was to find the ideal location to build his utopian city.

Richard was going to need a lot of land for his new infrastructure development, as well as access to both ocean ports and modern highways to deliver the huge amount of materials that he would need to construct it. He sent scouting teams to scour the East and West Coasts of the besieged United States, but in the end it was a small article in the San Francisco Chronicle that caught his eye — an article describing an incident of post-holocaust horror that had taken place in a small town called Morro Bay, along the Central Californian coast. Now a ghost town, Night was able to buy the remnants of Morro Bay for pennies on the dollar. He was also aided by Petrochem, who had taken over the now-abandoned Dynergy power plant in the town and was already planning to set up an offshore port and oil terminal site. A leveraged 132 million dollar purchase secured the remaining parcels.

Bankrolled by Merrill, Asukaga & Finch - who wanted to make the new city a financial hub — Night and Petrochem hired Arasaka to clean out the gangs and make the area "safe" again. Further funds came from external (and somewhat shady) investors lured to the project by the promise of lucrative building contracts and possible sources of extralegal income. To avoid the stigma of the Morro Bay Massacre, the partnership renamed the area Del Coronado Bay, the site of their new utopia of Coronado City. However, thanks to the rather out-sized personality of its founder, Coronado City soon became colloquially known by locals as "Night's City."

Coronado City
By 1993, Coronado City needed more space than what the original geology of the bay could accommodate, so Night leveled the surrounding hills and dumped them into the ocean as fill, reshaping the bay, and also re-dredging the harbor to make it capable of porting the large ships needed to build the city. Moreover, the region was an ideal location for a station of the Planetran intercontinental maglev.

Coronado City truly reflected its creator's eclectic vision. Instead of a huge construction of steel and glass, Night's urban plan broke the new city into a series of neighborhoods, each with a different architectural style and theme, much like the original Disneyland park's various "lands." In addition, Night also paid homage to the late and lamented small hamlet of Morro Bay by recreating much of the original layout of the area in an open-air environment reminiscent of a seaside village called Old Downtown. The city and corporate centers were the glittering zones of high-rises and corporate parks. It was here that Richard Night showed off his personal architectural skills in the designs of the many corporate "starscrapers" that were the most visible sign of Coronado City's rising affluence. Night's vision was indeed expansive and truly visionary. The only catch came when he started to build it in May 1994.

Although Petrochem and MA&F were the major bankrollers for the Coronado Partnership, they had one disadvantage: they weren't construction companies. For a job like Coronado City, the Partnership was going to need someone who could bring in the machines and workforce to actually dig the holes and put up the steel. They eventually ended up with the mob.

Night Falls
The West Coast Mobs (the Mafia, the Yakuza, etc.) had maintained a stranglehold on heavy construction on the "left coast" for decades. They controlled the construction unions, the transport unions, and most of the governmental agencies in charge of construction licenses, environmental impacts, and other building necessities. By investing a not inconsiderable sum in the Partnership (through a series of shell corporations), the Mobs hoped to not only make a staggering amount of return on lucrative construction work, but also have the inside track on future gambling, prostitution, and drug franchises in the new city. However, Night's visionary plan required using his own advanced building techniques and materials, which excluded a number of established unions and construction firms controlled by his organized crime partners, including his old associates — now called Halsey, Ferris and Skiv — who were short on money and had unwisely joined with the local mob. This didn't make any of them happy, and Night's further insistence that his new city would be safe and crime free angered them even more.

During the first four years of construction, there were daily threats against Night's life. A proud and self-reliant man, Richard typically ignored them. When the threats escalated to the level of sabotage and intimidation, he called in his corporate partners, who dealt with the issue swiftly and ruthlessly. Eventually, Night's luck ran out. On September 20, 1998, he was shot and killed in his penthouse suite at the top of the newly constructed Parkview Tower. Night's killer was never apprehended, and in his memory, the newly appointed City Council officially renamed Coronado City as "Night City" in his honor.

Legacy
The mob bosses who killed Richard Night ruled over Night City during the following years. Eventually, though, the corporations took the city back after business between both groups soured.

Miriam Night used the money of her late husband to build what would become Night Corp — former Night International — from the ground up and structure it around Night's ideals and principles.

By 2045, a photographic history of Night City had been assembled by Sachiko Evans, and due to an embarrassing piece of content contained in the manuscript, Night Corp would seek to hire a crew of edgerunners to ensure the book was never published to preserve Richard Night's legacy.

Notes
*The Gazebo in Lake Park was rumored to have been built by Richard Night himself as the place where he would propose to his lover, Miriam Night, after the completion of Coronado City. This tale was never confirmed, and Richard died before he ever got the chance to do so if true.

Riders on the Storm is a Side Job in .

Walkthrough
Some time after nabbing Anders Hellman from Kang Tao, a distressed Panam Palmer calls V with a request to come meet with her at the Aldecaldo Camp in Rocky Ridge.

Upon asking her what happened, she tells V that Saul Bright was taken by a group of Wraiths while he and some others were out on patrol, and that they've been observing their camp in Sierra Sonora ever since. Panam asks for V's help in this matter, and promises to give them Mitch's in turn.

After agreeing to help, Panam and V make their way to Mitch to get briefed, but instead only find Carol, Cassidy, Teddy, and Bob. Carol tells Panam that Mitch will be back shortly. As V leans on the car, Panam proposes a stealth plan where V sneaks into the Wraiths Camp, while she provides cover from a vantage point. They finish wrapping up the plan as Mitch returns, interrupting the bickering going on between the Aldecaldos.

Mitch proposes that V takes a look at the Wraiths Camp themselves using the drone that Mitch sent flying overhead. Using the drone, V observes the camps gate and perimeter, identifying the camps defenses. While observing, Panam asks V to inspect the tire tracks and the truck, before asking them to inspect the main building where Saul is most likely being kept. Having gathered enough intel, V disconnects from the drone.

Mitch, Panam, and V walk towards Villefort Columbus, in which they plan to approach the camp, but before setting off, Mitch advises that V take a SuperJet with them for when they find Saul. It should help with leading him out of the compound safely.

Upon closing up to the camp, Panam will mention an incoming dust storm, indicating that they have to move quickly if their plan is to succeed. After arriving at the camp and parking the van in a safe spot, V infiltrates the main camp and is able to find Saul in the basement if the main building.

:Upon exiting the camp with Saul safely, the trio rode off in the van to safety at the Ingalls Farm, where they spend the night to recover and avoid the dust storm.

:Upon exiting the camp with Saul, the trio rode off in the van chased by Wraiths, which they had to fend off. Due to the dust storm, they managed to reach the Ingalls' Farm safely, where they spend the night to recover.

In the morning, Panam thanks V for their help and gives them the promised .

:Before riding off, Panam pulls V close, giving them a kiss as a thank you for their help.

Journal Entry
:OK, this must actually be pretty serious. Tough chick like Panam wouldn't call you up for some chump chore. Must be something important. Wouldn't waste any time on this one if I were you. To the Aldecaldos' camp we go.

Riot is a nightclub located in Little China, in the Watson district of northern Night City.

Overview
A club in southern Watson known for being one of most important stages in Night City. Its solid sound system means that stars such as Lizzy Wizzy, Rubicones or the Cartesian Duelists have played here. The beer is good and the bathroom floor looks like a Pollock painting under an UV light.

Layout
Riot can be entered through the main entrance, where an Animals bouncer is stationed, as well as entered from either the backstage entrance, or from a fire escape on the east side of the building. There is a staircase leading to a secondary floor where the bar and toilets, and staff rooms are located. The west door can be opened with 9 Intelligence, while the east door can be opened with 11 Technical Ability, leading to the alternative side entrance and a Employee Badge.

The backstage area has a an elevator leading to the ground floor security room, and a garage door that can be opened with 10 Body which leads to the vehicle docking area, and the artist preparation rooms.

The ground floor security room has an elevator that leads to the VIP room located on the third floor, and a door that leads to Palm View.

River Ward is an NCPD detective in Night City. He is also a possible romance option for V in .

Biography
Early life
Growing up, River and his sister Joss' parents ran a small farm. Eventually it went out of business as larger corporations took over the agriculture industry. His parents took to running a grocery store and the family of four lived in the apartment area above it.

One day, some drugged up thugs broke in looking for cash and, when they didn't find any in the store, went into the living quarters and demanded money from the father, who swore they had nothing else. Not satisfied with that response, one of the thugs killed River and Joss' father and then put a gun in River's hand and had him point it at his own mother's head, demanding he shoot and kill her. River stalled, terrified, to the point the thug gave up trying to bait the child and took the gun and killed their mom himself before the thugs ran off, leaving River and Joss alive but now parentless. The siblings were then sent off to an orphanage to be cared for but the NCPD never caught the thugs who killed their parents. With this lack of justice, River saw this as complete incompetency regarding the NCPD and made it his goal to become a detective to solve cases like what happened to his family.

Adult Years
Sometime prior to 2077, River had become an NCPD detective and was first partnered with Jamie Sheen, but Jamie later committed suicide over his frustration with how the top brass cared more about bribes rather than upholding the law. River continued serving as a detective though and sometime later was partnered with another detective, Harold Han, and even worked with well-established people like Jefferson Peralez.

Meanwhile his sister, Joss, had married an Aldecaldo with whom she had three children with: Randy, Dorian, and Monique. With his brother-in-law not being much of a father figure, River would step in and help take care of the children, particularly when he once caught his brother-in-law with one of his young sons, Dorian, at a dive bar in the middle of the night, so the detective took his nephew home much to his brother-in-law's ire. When Joss' husband later died, River continued to try and help support her and her children by buying them a new trailer to live in, which resulted in Randy taking over the old one as his own place. However, River and Joss eventually had a falling out sometime before 2077 over River's driven desire to bring justice for his victims' cases to the point it was all he could talk and think about, with little regard for his own family issues.

At one point in 2077, he got a solid tip that Mayor Lucius Rhyne's life was in danger and had set out to speak with the mayor's security when a cyberpscyho, Péter Horváth, attacked right after River got there. River managed to incapacitate the would-be attacker before they could find and kill the mayor and the deputy mayor, Weldon Holt. River was subsequently celebrated by the press as "super cop" and received the Medal of Merit. However, Rhyne ended up dying anyways later that day from a separate heart problem. This odd coincidence didn't go unnoticed to River, but he had no way to really link the two incidents, especially as his superior ordered him to drop the case and even his partner, Harold, warned him to not re-open it.

:River got a call soon after from V, who was being tasked by the Peralezes to find out what really happened to Rhyne as they had their own suspicions about his untimely death. Together, River and V tracked down the Red Queen's Race, an invitation-only sex club that Rhyne had visited on the night of his death. They learned that Rhyne had died in the club from a virus-spiked braindance, and Deputy Mayor Weldon Holt had ordered Detective Han to cover it up. While V reported the findings to the Peralezes, River decided to try to re-open the inquest into Rhyne's death. However, when he confronted Han about his own actions in the coverup, he was told once more to drop it. Undeterred, he decided to take it up with his superiors but ultimately got suspended from the force instead.
:While still suspended, he came to believe that his missing nephew, Randy Kutcher, had been abducted by Anthony Harris, the man behind the "Peter Pan" child abductions, after seeing a video where Anthony was being chased by NCPD before being shot while one of his newer victims in the video had Randy's shoes on. However, while Anthony was still alive, he was comatose, preventing the NCPD from determining where his other victims were kept. Dismayed that the Peter Pan case was assigned to Detective Gonaghal, who was unlikely to pursue it seriously, River asked V to help him so that he could rescue Randy, conveniently leaving out that he'd been suspended from the force.
:
::Together, they infiltrated a NCPD-contracted medical lab in The Glen which had been experimenting with scrolling braindances of dreams for therapeutic and investigative purposes, hoping to examine any braindances of Anthony's dreams. They were confronted by Dr. Yawen Packard, an old girlfriend of River's, who revealed that Anthony was not dreaming due to his condition. With no other leads, River decided to break the news that Randy had been abducted to Joss and search Randy's room for clues to his whereabouts leading up to his disappearance, as well as any sensory stimulus that could be used to make Anthony dream. They found Randy had a new laptop and had come into contact with Anthony through a secret website hidden on a false website for people looking to kick their drug abuse habits. Thanks to a cartoon that Randy had downloaded from the site, Yawen was able to trigger Anthony's dreams.
::
:::River and V will drive to Poppy Farm where they defeat some Wraiths and quickly see that it is the wrong one. Finally arriving at Edgewood Farm, both find out that they came too late and that Randy is dead. River collapses and later gets angry with V, regretting that he did not hire a professional instead. River vows to kill Anthony Harris with or without V's help. Some time later he will send a text message to V, notifying them that the deed is done and bidding final goodbye. River later gets into a bar fight with someone who was talking badly about Anthony's victims, which lands him in the precinct prison in Little China. From there he leaves a video message played during the end credits and asks V to bail him out.
::
:::With V's help, River was able to deduce that Anthony must have been using Edgewood Farm to hold his victims, but V chose to not go any further in assisting River. In turn, River headed out on his own to rescue Randy but, ill-prepared for the defenses Anthony had set up around the farm, he was summarily killed and wasn't able to save Randy.
::
::: With V's help at analyzing the braindances, River was able to deduce that Anthony must have been using Edgewood Farm to hold his victims. The two set out to the farm, which was now heavily armed, but managed to get through the defenses and rescue Randy and several other victims that Anthony had been force-feeding and injecting with hormones via equipment designed for livestock.
:::While they had managed to rescue his nephew, River still felt that Anthony should die for what he did to all his victims. With this in mind, he went to the hospital where the comatose murderer was being kept and put his gun against the man's head, intent on killing him. As he stood there though, he had flashbacks to his childhood when the thug tried to make him shoot his mother and realized he'd be no better than that thug if he went through with the execution. With that, he left the hospital, letting Anthony live. A short time later, River invited V over for a dinner with his family.

:::As they hung out together before their jambalaya cookout, River eventually revealed to V how he decided to not kill Anthony, explaining what happened to his parents caused him to not go through with it. The two enjoyed the rest of the night having dinner with his family and playing games. As Joss and the kids started to make comments regarding V's romantic life (Joss being curious about a male V herself or pointing out River's affection for a female V), River decided to rescue V from that "ambush", taking them up on the adjacent water tower to enjoy the view. There River gifted V his revolver, , noting it carried too many bad memories for him.

:::
:::: V can accept River's advances by kissing him, initiating the romance story path with him (see Romancing River).

:::
:::: If V is male and tried to kiss him, River will react startled, causing V to say "Look, no need to explain. I get it. And it's fine." Alternatively, V can simply do nothing flirtatious or simply reject River's advances (as female V); in any case the two will have some drinks, either lemonade or something stronger, and V will wake up in the Kutcher's home the next morning while River is already up. He will depart promptly to see Randy in the hospital, but tells V to take their time.

::::Following their night together (with or without romance), River can be called or visited at the Kutcher's home and tells V that, knowing his time with the NCPD was at an end, he decided to become a private investigator instead. Although he still was not sure how to market himself, he decided he would like to specialize in kidnapping to help other families that experienced what happened to his.

::::
:::::After having the relic surgically removed and seeking support from a friend, V can call River from the Arasaka Orbital Station. However, River cuts V short, saying that it is a bad time and asks if he can call back. He then hangs up and will not pick up again.

::::If he was not romanced and either "The Devil", "The Sun", or "The Star" endings were chosen, a video message from River is played during the end credits, in which he says to use confiscated goods including weapons to equip "more people like V", which the city needs.

Database Entry

Romance
If V has a feminine body (regardless of voice type and genitalia), they can pursue a romantic relationship with River. With only three missions, none of which are part of the main story, River is the romantic option with the shortest storyline.

Romancing River
No romantic advances are made by either side during I Fought the Law or The Hunt. The first indication of affection is actually given by Joss in the kitchen during Following the River, when she mentions to V that River "can't seem to stop gushing about you". Later during dinner, Joss repeats her observation, noting that her brother likes V, slightly embarrassing a shy River. V can ask whether River actually put his sister up to saying that, which she admits to be true. River's nephews, Dorian and Monique, then make the situation even more awkward as they both raise hands asking "Who thinks V and Uncle River make a good couple?". V can choose to also raise her hand after which River gets up from the table, saying that he pulls V out of this "ambush". If V does not raise her hand, River will simply remark "Now that that's decided...". In any case, River then takes V on top of the adjacent water tower, a great spot for the views, as River puts it. After gifting V his gun, , River asks whether she knows why they are there together, adding "Say you do. Please don't string me along." V can choose to tell River about previous, horrible pickup lines guys tried on her. Eventually, he asks whether he stands a chance, to which V can either react positively, but adding that he better not fall in love with her (to which he responds "Too late."), or negatively, adding that they can stay friends. In the former case, V will then get the option to kiss River or a last chance to back down and abort the flirt. Friend-zoning River or aborting the flirt at the last minute will result in the evening playing out as if V was male without romance (see Biography). Kissing River, on the other hand, will initiate a cut-scene of both passionately kissing, making their way back to the house, sneaking by the sleeping kids, and having sex in River's room while staying as quiet as possible.

The next morning, Johnny appears and comments "Christ, V. Can't believe you're making me fuck a cop. Gonna go plug my ears, gouge my eyes.". Over some coffee, River asks whether their relationship is going anywhere longer term. V can choose to tell River about the relic and her impending death. Eventually, V can choose to kiss River and accept a relationship (to which both comment with "Let's give it a try.") or reject him, either claiming that it was just a one-night-stand (to which River reacts calmly but disappointed) or that V's condition simply keeps her from making such a commitment (to which River reacts understanding). Joss then comes in and cuts their conversation short, reminding River to get the power generator fixed so everything is ready for when Randy gets out of the hospital.

After this, River can be found at the Kutcher's home. If V agreed to a relationship with River, she can ask him if he is upset that V is busy (to which he responds "We'll make up for it.") or tell him that things are not working out between the two. The latter option will prompt V to quickly move on by saying "[...] Rambling. Just forget I said anything." to which River replies "Already forgotten.". River will also send a couple of romantic text messages to V, one ending with "I've got a good feeling about this, And well.. I'm just happy, like, dumb happy, you know? You're really amazing, V".

Endings
If V has romanced River and chooses to contact him to say goodbye at the end of the mission Nocturne Op55N1, she will refer to him as "that one stubborn badge" toward Johnny, to which he only replies: "Mhm". Different endings with River as romantic partner are then possible, but not all allow you to maintain the relationship:

:Opting for "The Sun" ending (choosing (Don't Fear) The Reaper or asking Rogue for help, which requires completing Blistering Love), will result in V waking up in bed in the penthouse together with River at the beginning of Path of Glory, a few months after Nocturne Op55N1. V can choose to give him a wake-up kiss before hopping in the shower, where he subsequently joins V. However, while having coffee River points out that something has been wrong since V's encounter with Mikoshi. V insists that there is one last job she needs to do and that she has to do it without River's help. He then wishes her good luck and promises to wait for her. In a video message during the end credits, River invites V to dinner the following week to celebrate Randy's birthday. Joss and Dorian can be heard in the background and River points out that it would mean a lot to them if V could come.

:Opting for "The Devil" ending (accepting Hanako Arasaka's offer to help), V can call River from the orbital facility during Where is My Mind?. River keeps being distracted by his nephew but asks V to give him the name of the orbital station so he can fly up to get them. V does not know anything about the station and River warns V not to trust Arasaka. He ends the call with "Gonna find you. Hear me?". Regardless of whether V then chooses to accept Arasaka's offer or to return to Earth, the video message during the end credits is identical to the one played for "The Sun" ending (see above).

:Opting for "The Star" ending (asking Panam for help, which requires completing Queen of the Highway), will result in V and River being briefly reunited at the temporary Aldecaldos camp during All Along the Watchtower. River came to the camp to talk to V before she heads for the border and leaves the area. Not wishing to abandon Night City's citizens including his sister Joss and the kids, whom he still felt the need to protect and support, River remarks that what V actually needs is a family. V can choose to ask whether he really wants to sacrifice everything for the sake of Night City, to which River replies that V might have found their family with the Aldecaldos and he likewise needs to be with his own. V can then hug River goodbye, after which he comments "Think we knew we wouldn't get a happily-ever-after. Think we both knew." In a video message during the end credits, River mentions pictures V sent him of the Badlands and says he will visit once Joss gets back on her feet.

:Opting for the "Temperance" ending, i.e., reaching Mikoshi alone ((Don't Fear) The Reaper) or with the help of either Rogue or the Aldecaldos but then joining cyberspace with Alt and giving your body to Johnny Silverhand will prevent any further interaction with River during the epilogue. In his video message during the end credits, River says he has been searching everywhere but cannot find V. Adding that "it's like you're a ghost", River ends with a plea for her to call him.

:Opting for the "Tower" ending will see V enter a two-year coma after undergoing surgery to remove the relic. Upon waking up, V will have the option to call River. At first River will be angry, believing it to be some kind of joke, but after V has a chance to explain their situation River will calm down and apologize. When V suggests meeting up, River will tell V he is a wanted man, revealing he sold classified NCPD information to Trauma Team to pay for Randy's rehab. Too ashamed to face V in person, River will hang up shortly after.

## Roach Race
Roach Race is a mini-game in . It was added in Patch 1.6 as part of the Arcade Minigame Cyberpunk 2077 DLC.

Description
:Embark on an epic adventure atop legendary and loyal Roach! Rank among the Top 5 best players to earn awesome rewards such as money and unique items!

Gameplay

The game's scenario is set in the Witcher universe. Geralt's mount - Roach, runs away. You control Roach to evade various obstacles, such as fences, wells, griffins (a species of monsters), crows etc.

In the game, Roach can:

*Jump (Press Ⓐ/X/d-pad up (console) or ↑/w/space (PC) once)
*Double jump (Press again when Roach is jumping)
*Glitch (Press again when Roach is double-jumping, the invincible mode needs 5 seconds to cool down after glitching)

There are two pickups:

*Apple - Worth 20 points.

* Carrot - Worth 50 extra points of passive score over its duration. Also temporarily increases gallop speed with Roach galloping with only her front hooves.

There are five stages, referencing The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings:

- Kaer Morhen
- Novigrad
- Flotsam forests
- Ard Skellig
- Isle of Mists

A small container with rewards will be sent to V's Apartment after getting top 3 score.

High scores
- 3354 – Z1R343L
- 3019 – B4RBOSA
- 2529 – NCALGOD
- 2110 – SCHEMA
- 1780 – NWONG
- 1433 – KEPLER
- 965 – NETMAN
- 798 – J4CKI3W
- 565 – PNEUMO
- 128 – SILVERHAND

Most players are a reference to other notable characters. Once V has enough points, they will enter the high score ranking, replacing SILVERHAND.

Rewards
*5th place: €$300
*4th place: €$500
*3rd place: €$1000 and mod inside the Roach Race chest in V's Apartment.
*2nd place: €$1700 and quickhack inside the Roach Race chest in V's Apartment.
*1st place: €$2500, Roach Whisperer outfit and Roach Race, based on true events shard inside the Roach Race chest in V's Apartment.
:Simply playing the game and then reaching all the places from 10 to 1 also results in receiving a unique message from CDP Arcades (which then later is remembered as a contact on V's phone), however there's no actual reward for the places 6-10. Reaching a higher place won't result in getting old messages retroactively.

Associated Shards
*Roach Race, a quick review
*Roach Race, based on true events

Notes
*A Roach Race arcade can be found in three of the four purchasable apartments.
*Despite the animation showing a coin being tossed, playing the minigame is free.

Trivia
* The scene in the main menu is inspired by the Gwent card Roach, where Roach appears on the roof of a house after Geralt whistled, with Geralt scratching his head. This in turn was inspired by a bug in The Witcher 3 where Roach would appear on top of a roof after calling him.
*The Japanese words displayed when Roach gets a carrot are "にんじんゲット！" (Romaji: ninjin getto). "にんじん" (Kanji: 人参, common form: ニンジン) means "carrot". "ゲット" is a borrowed word from "get".

See also

*Trauma Drama

## Robert Rainwater
引文：Replace even a single hand and you'll notice a dip in concentration and overall well-being. Cyberware's more harm than help.（Robert Rainwater）
citation

Robert Rainwater is a Ripperdoc operating his business on the corner edge of an open space in Kabuki Market in Kabuki, Watson.

Biography
Unlike most Night City residents, and rather ironic to his profession, Robert is an avid speaker against cyberware.

He has no implants and is quick to explain how they, no matter how insignificant, lead to a deterioration of the owner's body state of mind. He instead compensates for the harsh demands of the current reality by taking care of his body naturally, which is visible from the first glance, which V will not hesitate to make a comment on.

Inquiring on the purpose of this strange business counter advertisement, Robert is quick to respond on the current visitor's example - no matter what he says about the downsides of chrome, it will not waver the confidence of his customers.

Associated Quests

## Robert Wilson
- status：Alive
- gender：Male
- occupation：Weapon Vendor
- voiced_by：Dave B. Mitchell

引文：Gun's somethin' you gotta respect! You don't know how to shoot, don't do it!（Robert Wilson）

Robert Wilson, usually just referred to as Wilson, is a weapons vendor in . He's a 2nd Amendment franchise holder, and his shop is located in Megabuilding H10, Watson.

Biography
Wilson seems to be the tinkering kind, paying more mind to the quality of his merchandise than the efficiency of sales. This is why he will not sell a weapon which hasn't first passed through his skilled hands, although just as well the reason of his continuous complaints regarding the waning business. His attempts at advertisement also fall short, as the activities he organizes appear to be more shooting classes with a strict mentor than customer enticement.

Unlike many other Night City gun store owners who would gleefully sell someone a piece of iron to shoot up their enemies (and friends) with, Wilson has a respect for his deadly merchandise—not only does he prioritize his aforementioned tinkering to perfect every piece that comes through his door, but he is deeply irritated by those who don't show the proper care and respect that their guns deserve, and will throw customers out of his shop without hesitation if he sees them mishandling their iron or using it improperly. Unfortunately, however, most other Night City citizens do not share his sentiments, and his strictness typically only serves to drive away customers.

## Rocky Ridge
- type：Ghost town
- state：North California (formerly)
- county：San Luis Obispo (formerly)
- region：Badlands
- subregion：Rocky Ridge Plains
- population：6,014 (originally)
- gangs：Wraiths

引文：ROCKY RIDGE - A TRUE PARADISE FAR FROM THE BIG CITY BUSTLE（Build Your Future in Rocky Ridge!）

Rocky Ridge is an abandoned town located on the eastern Badlands of Night City.

History
Early history - 2076
Prior to the area's redevelopment, this place was the home of a container community known as Pol-Bud Miasto, a company town for the workers of the limestone mine to the northwest, and the cement factory to the far south.

After the closure of the facilites owned by Corp-Bud on the eastern Badlands of Night City, this settlement struggled for some time until a group of investors poured money into it, promising to construct a self-contained residential area similar to Rancho Coronado and just a stone's throw away from Night City, but far enough to guarantee peace and quiet. While using the planned freeway extension as a reason to breath new life into the town and give locals employment, investors advertised Rocky Ridge as a place developed to be self-sufficient, cozy, practical, and aiming to be a choice for people looking for a new home to live while having easy access to everything the neighboring metropolis had to offer.

After convincing the current and newly signed residents, construction began as streets were plotted out and more houses were built for the workers employed by the businesses located just next door, with the locals being excited for the future. However, like most investments in California at the time, it didn't end well. The nearby businesses went bankrupt shortly thereafter, with the freeway extension being put on an indefinite hiatus, and with the town's construction becoming too expensive as well. Soon, Rocky Ridge was no longer economically viable; from one day to the next, the construction workers had disappeared, and contractors had lost their jobs while the houses became vacant as the town was rapidly abandoned.

2077
By 2077, Rocky Ridge was ghost town on the outskirts of Night City, being completely abandoned, and almost forgotten by the city residents. The only thing it was notorious for was its landmark status, which broke up the otherwise monotonous drive out of metropolis. However, it was advised not to stop for long, as Rocky Ridge had become a hotspot for looters and the occasional Raffen Shiv band. Moreover, the decrepit houses were prone to collapse without warning.

One of the Raffen Shiv gangs who occasionally visited the area were a group of Wraiths led by Nash, who had established a small presence around the fuel station and bar. That same year, Panam Palmer lost her truck after Nash cheated her by stealing it and all the cargo they were supposed to deliver. With the help of V, Panam recovered her vehicle from Nash's Wraiths.

## Rocky Ridge Bar

Rocky Ridge

This Bar is located in the ghost town of Rocky Ridge, on the eastern Badlands of Night City.

History
This bar was built during the mid-late 2030s as part of Pol-Bud Miasto, a company town owned by the Pol-Bud corporation.

During the redevelopment of Rocky Ridge, this bar was renovated by Jax, who had been convinced — as many others — to own a building in the town with a low-rate mortgage. Jax hired his friend Bosey as a bartender, someone who had prior experience by working in Night City. When Rocky Ridge went down and customers were not visiting the bar, Bosey decided to finish the renovation work before returning back to NC, advising Jax to sell the establishment and do the same.

Around 2077, this bar was occasionally visited by the Wraiths.

Layout
Around 2077, the ground floor contained a bar, a pool table, and several arcade machines, while the upper floor had three private booths and some vending machines.

This Fuel Station is located in the ghost town of Rocky Ridge, on the eastern Badlands of Night City.

History
This CHOOH2 station was built during the mid-late 2030s as part of Pol-Bud Miasto, a company town owned by the Pol-Bud corporation.

During the 2070s, this fuel station in the abandoned Rocky Ridge town contained a workshop and a small store in its premises. Around 2077, the neighboring bar was occasionally visited by the Wraiths, with some gang members positioning on the fuel station's rooftop to watch over the surrounding area.

## Rocky Ridge Plains
- type：Arid plains
- region：Badlands
- subregion：Eastern Wastelands

The Rocky Ridge Plains are a vast arid expanse on the eastern Badlands of Night City. It has plenty of plains, a few hills, and a sizable gorge to the northeast. The secluded areas in the north are mostly surrounded by steep hills.

Overview
Rocky Ridge borders the Red Peaks hills to the west, the mountainous region of Sierra Sonora to the south, and along the Interstate 9 to the east, Vasquez Pass. Its most secluded areas to the north - only accessed by a narrow road northwest from the town of Rocky Ridge - are bordered by Night City's Watson and Westbrook districts.

This region is mostly controlled by the nomads, being from either the Aldecaldos or the Raffen Shiv Wraiths. Militech is also strengthening its position, making controls on the roads, and having recently converted an old motel into a base of operations. Dakota Smith is the most prominent fixer in the area, currently residing in her own garage along the I-9.

The abandoned town of Rocky Ridge can be found along the only pavemented road that goes northeast from the highway. A swamp occupies a sizable area in the southwest, while most of the eastern plains are dotted by the Wind Farms.

Roger Wang is a Meds Vendor located at Wang's Clinic in Kabuki in .

Biography
During his lifetime, Wang managed to set up his own supply network for chemicals.

Wang's friend suggested he should go into business with the Animals member Blake Croyle. After meeting with Croyle and simply by listening to some of the advice he was given by him, he got indebted. Roger tried to pay the debt in full, but was unable to do so after the accumulated "interest". In turn, after Blake made threats to his family, he granted Croyle access to his clinic in Kabuki.

Instead of trying to pay off his debt, he first turned towards the NCPD, who basically told him to do it himself, and so he approached Regina Jones, Watson's own local Fixer. Regina, who is possesed of no love for Mr. Croyle or his predatory actions towards people in her neighborhood, then opened up a contract to take out Blake Croyle and his Animals huscle.

After Croyle has been removed from his property by V, Wang will return to his clinic and start selling chems again. If asked about a possible discount as a reward for completing the gig, depending on the given response, he will reluctantly give a ten percent discount on items in his store.

## Rogue Amendiares
- aka：Queen of the Solos

Rogue Amendiares was a well-known solo during the 2010s in Night City, who became owner of the famous Afterlife nightclub, and was widely considered the city's best fixer by 2077.

Biography
Early life
Rogue was a rebellious teen, knew stiff hierarchy of gang life was not for her and set out on her own, to become a solo. She was a new and successful mercenary in Night City. Rogue also began a relationship with hit rockerboy sensation Johnny Silverhand. Rogue on occasion asked Johnny if they could visit a drive-in theatre on a date, which went largely ignored.

Her relationship with Johnny ended at some point in 2011, after Rogue found out about Johnny cheating on her.

2010s - 2023
In 2013, Rogue and her partner, Nomad Santiago were mercs, being reputed to be the best at the time. During a meeting between the two of them in the Atlantis Club, Johnny Silverhand interrupted them by entering the room to ask for their help in raiding Arasaka to save his girlfriend Alt Cunningham. While Rogue was still held a sour spot for Johnny, she ended up agreeing along with Santiago for nothing more than to give it to the corporations. The two participated in Silverhand's raid on Arasaka Tower to recover Alt and the Soulkiller program alongside a media known as Thompson, but the raid ended in failure as Alt was separated from her body, trapped in the Arasaka mainframe.

At some point after 2013, Rogue had a brief romantic relationship with Morgan Blackhand, though it was not known by many.

During the Fourth Corporate War, Rogue participated in another Arasaka raid that would end up with the Night City Holocaust. She, alongside Spider Murphy, Lyle Thompson, Shaitan, Johnny Silverhand, Morgan Blackhand, among others, raided the Arasaka Towers. Johnny's team was attacked by Adam Smasher and a group of Arasaka troopers. Thompson was injured and Johnny was killed. After getting a chance to escape, Spider tried to reach Silverhand's body, but Rogue stopped her, telling the netrunner he was gone. Spider helped Rogue and the surviving soldiers to drag the wounded Thompson into the elevator. Afterwards they escaped by using an AV on the Towers' rooftop. Soon after a nuclear device went off.

2023 - 2040s

At some point prior to 2045 Rogue got so badly injured in a car crash that even cyberware could not fix all of the internal damage. As such, she largely retired from the Solo lifestyle and became a Fixer; holding court with local solos and acting as a middleman with potential contacts, providing them with valuable information and the intelligence they needed. Rogue also started operating the Afterlife in downtown Night City, though she would later have to relocate the bar in Watson.

2077
By 2077, Rogue's reputation as a solo continued to inspire and influence others. As the "Queen of the Afterlife", she was regarded as Night City's top fixer. She continued to manage the Afterlife surrounding herself with experts in their fields to follow through with her plans; Nix was hired as the Afterlife's top netrunner, Crispin Weyland was her pick as the top solo and bodyguard to accompany during big gigs, Emmerick Bronson was hired as the bouncer of the club, and finally Claire Russell became the bartender who kept track of the customers. During this time she was contacted by a corporate bodyguard named Goro Takemura, who had been searching for information on an ex-Arasaka employee, Anders Hellman. Rogue recognized Takemura as the man accused of the murder of Saburo Arasaka and because of this she turned him away before any trouble could be traced to the Afterlife.

At some point, Rogue met with a lone nomad, Panam Palmer, who left her clan to work in Night City. She paired Panam with another nomad named Nash on a few gigs, but during an assignment to deliver "merchandise", Panam was betrayed by Nash, who stole both their cargo for the Raffen Shiv, and Panam's customized Thorton Mackinaw "Warhorse". Having messed up, Panam angrily confronted Rogue, however due to her mistake she refused to give compensation or help to recover the stolen items. After some time she was contacted by a local mercenary, V, who had been searching for information on Anders Hellman similar to Takemura before. Despite recognizing V as the sole survivor of the failed heist at Konpeki Plaza, which marked them as a merc with a body count behind them, she offered to give them the information they needed if they paid €$15,000. After receiving the payment she debriefed V with the information of a Kang Tao AV that was transporting a VIP to secure location, V voiced concerns of working in the Badlands and was paired with Panam, whom Rogue believed could help them retrieve what they needed. After giving V Panam's contact information, she went back to dealing with her business.

After successfully retrieving the stolen cargo from Nash, Panam called Rogue to gloat of her success. However, Rogue was not impressed and mocked Panam for having a high-temper and that fixing her own mistake was not an achievement, which only caused Panam to become angrier, disconnecting the call.

:Rogue discovered V had made an assault on Arasaka Tower and was impressed. Despite their unsuccessful heist with Dexter Deshawn, she was willing to give them a chance with a new gig she had been planning and later called them to contact her if they were interested.

:Later, Rogue was contacted again by V, who was acting very differently from how they were before, with manners and personality did not fit the mercenary she had met earlier. In fact, the mercenary seemed to acting more like an old acquaintance of hers, long-deceased rockerboy and her former boyfriend Johnny Silverhand himself. Johnny, in V's body, convinced her that it was him and that he needed information to find Adam Smasher. Having already done some investigating, along with a copious amount of partying and debauchery, in V's body, he informed Rogue that he had managed to track down a word that could lead them to Grayson, Smasher's second-in-command: "Ebunike." After V eventually woke up as themselves, Rogue explained that she knew everything and was willing to work with them. She later called and revealed that Ebunike was an old container ship docked in Night City and to meet her back at the Afterlife to discuss it further. After V arrived she gave them a Replica of Johnny's Samurai jacket he used to wear and they proceeded to the docs to infiltrate the Ebunike. Upon arriving they made in onto the ship and discovered information on Smasher, as well as Grayson himself. As Rogue and V questioned him, he revealed that Smasher had been promoted to head of Arasaka's security and was unlikely to return, and insinuated Rogue was on his side and there was a reason Arasaka had never hunted her after the Arasaka Towers bombing. Rogue, upset, shut him up before he revealed anymore information with a prompt pistol-whip to his head. Stating that she believed the plan was pointless and that they should forget about Smasher, Rogue then left the docks and went back to the Afterlife.

:
::Rogue was later contacted by V again, only this time they were inviting her on a date on Johnny's behalf. She believed there was something more thinking Johnny never called unless he wanted something. However, V reassured her that there were no strings attached and quickly provided where to have the date: the Silver Pixel Cloud drive-in theatre. The drive-in theatre was the same one she wanted Johnny to take her back when they were young. They both agreed and she told V to meet her at the Afterlife to pick her up. She got ready and waited in front, finally V arrived with Johnny's Porsche much to her surprise. Rogue noted that Johnny wasn't here and asked when he would show up, V informed her that they were only the driver, she commented on V keeping him on a "short leash." They proceeded to drive to the drive-in and upon arriving discovered it had been closed, V opened the entrance and began to set things up as Rogue sat and waited to see the movie.
::V fixed the projector and the movie was Bushidō X: Fade to Black, they then gave control to Johnny as he took over their body. Johnny joined Rogue as they watched the movie, during this they discussed the past and were talking about the differences that could have been made. Johnny started to kiss her and the two began a more intimate experience. However, Rogue stopped and told Johnny she could not go through with it, that too much had changed and she couldn't pretend everything was still the same. She left the drive-in to head back to the Afterlife.

::
:::After Johnny left a message for Rogue explaining everything that happened at Arasaka Tower and that he was leaving Night City for good, she was furious at him. She never imagined that Johnny would ever be so cruel to takeover someone else's body. Rogue left a message for Johnny asking how he felt having another person give up their life for him. She finally told Johnny to never return to Night City, insinuating she would hunt him down if he dared to ever show his face in the city again.

::
:::Rogue contacted V at some point after they last saw each other. She wanted them to tell Johnny that he was an arrogant, egotistical son of a bitch and that it was nice to talk with him again. Finally she wished for them to take care of themselves.

::
:::After V accomplished the suicide run on Arasaka Tower, Rogue gave up control over the Afterlife to them believing they had earned it. Rogue met up with V before they went to discuss a gig with Mr. Blue Eyes, giving them words of advice and how they should honor Afterlife tradition by having a special drink before the gig.

::
:::While taking a call, Rogue was visited by V, who revealed that they were actually Johnny and V was in the back seat. Johnny pressured her to talk about her past and the fifty years he had been gone, Rogue eventually clear the Afterlife and gave in. She discussed how she worked with Adam Smasher and regretted it. However, she also knew that Johnny never came to her unless he needed something, he proceeded to explain that he needed to get to Mikoshi in Arasaka Tower before V and him disappeared. Johnny also insinuated that Rogue would also be joining, which she did though reluctantly. Rogue agreed to come up with a plan of assault that also included Crispin Weyland, and using "Strix", a Militech heavy-duty AV, and special Arasaka feet equipment to descend from the tower shaft to the bottom floor.
:::Rogue left the Afterlife and called her son, telling him to stay safe as the assault was about to start. As the diversion was created to light up the sky of Night City from following debris from space, Arasaka Tower got a lock on the AV they were using. As the AV crashed inside Arasaka Tower, Rogue, Johnny, and Weyland fought through to the shaft and began descending floor by floor to the group level of the tower. The Hayabusa protocol was in effect as many Arasaka troops fought them going down. Rogue and Johnny finally made it to the level where Alt Cunningham was able to gain control of the tower and where Mikoshi could be accessed. Before getting to the access point they were ambushed by Adam Smasher, who picked up Rogue as he was about to kill her, she placed a grenade before in him before he could. Sacrificing herself for Johnny, Rogue was killed in the blast used against Smasher as Johnny fought him on her behalf. After the battle, Johnny searched the debris and found only Rogue's pistol, Pride, her body having been obliterated by the grenade's explosion.
:::
:::Johnny, now permanently in V's body, stopped at the Columbarium to pay respects to both V and Rogue. With Rogue's body having been destroyed in the battle, Johnny left her pistol in her niche, then departed Night City for good to start a new life elsewhere.

Behind the Scenes

引文：Rogue is one of the OG cyberpunks, kicking ass since before 2020, still doing it in 2077. She first made her name as a solo and it shows: she's tall, strong octogenarian that's a better shot than you and, yes, even a better lover than you. As a rebellious teen, she knew stiff hierarchy of gang life wasn't for her and set out on her own, pioneering the role of the do-it-all and do-it-alone merc. Than she ran into Johnny Silverhand, the milieu's rising star. Their intense romance endured twists and turns before ripping apart in a violent and spectacular fashion. After Johnny's death, Rogue hung up her weapons and moved out of the direct line of fire, using her contacts to became a fixer, the role in which V comes to know her. V can't help but be impressed and a little awed by this star cyberpunk, even though others from her era smirk that she sold out and became a glorified corporate matchmaker. One way or the other, for V to achieve her goals, winning Rogue over (with Johnny's help, of course) is a top priority.

Notes
*In the Never Fade Away adventure, Rogue is called Rache by Johnny; a name she doesn't like him calling her. It could most likely be an abbreviation for Rachel.
*Rogue Amendiares was a Buddhist.
*Scanning Rogue's niche during New Dawn Fades reveals it has been leased until July 21, 2177.
*In The Tower ending, it is revealed that Nibbles and the iguana (if present) were adopted by Rogue after V disappeared. They can be seen sitting on the counter behind Rogue in the message she leaves for V.

Mike's Trivia
*As per Mike Pondsmith words, it is very likely Rogue is the mother of Trace Santiago, but this is something he hasn't work out to add to the story yet. Pondsmith states when Rogue saw Johnny during Never Fade Away and how much he cared about Alt Cunningham, she finally gave up on getting him back. This left Nomad Santiago as the rebound guy, who had been trying to get with Rogue for some time already.
*Mike Pondsmith, in character as Maximum Mike, claimed that he used to date Rogue Amendiares on and off while she was still hurting for Johnny Silverhand, before the two drifted apart because of their work.
*Mike has mentioned that one of the reasons Johnny ended his relationship with Rogue was because she was pregnant of his child.
*Mike said that Rogue and Johnny's relationship was based on a couple he knew during college.

Ronald Malone, also known as the The Dogtown Prodigy, Pacifica Typhoon, or just Typhoon, is a Junk Vendor in .

Appearance
Malone is an African-American man of average age. He has brown eyes and black hair styled in a sculpted afro. Around his forehead a black and yellow bandana is tied to keep his hair in place. He wears a blue jacket with an orange text that says "NoControl" on each sleeve on top of a white and gold trimmed ballistic vest. His outfit is completed with a pair of green slacks and grayish-green dress shoes. On his right index finger he wears an NCU Signet Ring.

Biography
Malone is a resident of Dogtown, Pacifica.

When he was younger, he used to be a successful sprinter, and was able to do the 100 meters sprint in 6 seconds while under the effects of boosters. However, his rise to fame came to a standstill when he had to run against–and lost against–new, upcoming talents from Fiona Vargas's Center for Neuromotor Development, which were all implanted with top-of-the-line cyberware on top of using boosters.

Nowadays, he barely walks a hundred meters before calling it a day, and tries to make a living by selling his goods.

:Ronald is approached by the mercenary V, and talked with them. He explains to V that the Space Force One crash has everyone riled up, and that everyone is going crazy in the search for President Rosalind Myers. He is skeptical of the crash being real and is sure that his regulars will show up again once things have settled down.

:When asked by V about if he has any information about Dogtown, he explains the various neighborhoods of Dogtown to them, and offers to give them even more information later on. In exchange for a small sum of eurodollars, they would also help V gain access to the Capitán Caliente.

## Rosalind Myers
- dob：March 28
- aka：Mittens
- status：Dependent
- home：Washington, D.C., NUSA
- gender：Female
- hair_color：Blond with grey hair roots
- eyes：Grey/blue

Militech (formerly)
Federalist Party, NUSA
- occupation：Marine (former)
Militech CEO (former)
NUSA President
- relative：Unnamed mother
- role：Corporate/Lawman
- voiced_by：Kay Bess

Rosalind Myers is the third and current president of the New United States of America, the former CEO of Militech, and a former marine. Currently serving her third term, Myers is the second woman serving as president in the short history of the NUSA, continuing her gospel of unification.

Characteristics

Despite coming from corporate and political backgrounds, Rosalind shows a "commoner" attitude while carrying herself. Thus, as the politician she is, it may be part of the play, as she will do anything to get your vote. However, Myers also reveals her cold-blooded side, not particularly when it's necessary. To her, ends justify the means.

Appearance
Rosalind expresses her status as a high politician as well as an ex-marine in the choice of wardrobe. Her ivory collarless jacket with gold accents resembles the iconic formal wear of women coming from generational wealth, while the golden plate on her shoulder looks like an epaulette - a decoration used as insignia of rank by armed forces.

Myers also shows herself in disguise where she wears a black outfit consisting of a turtleneck, denim vest, jeans, and a cap with "I <3 NC" that she found in the hideout. Despite V mentioning the awful smell of the clothes she did what's necessary to hide her identity from the citizens of Dogtown.

After V cuts out the subdermal tracking device, this leaves a scar on Myers' neck.

Biography
After the death of Militech's CEO Donald Lundee, Rosalind Myers became his successor in leading the corporation. She was described as a proponent of peace and a distinguished politician that oversaw the NUSA's rapid economy recovery, while also having an interventionist and protectionist stance. Myers was CEO of Militech for almost a decade.

2065 - 2070
In 2065, after leaving her former position at Militech to Lucas Harford, Rosalind Myers was elected as the third President of the New United States of America. During her next campaign for reelection, President Myers presented a unification program to extend federal rule over the Free States under the pretense of strengthening the Union, though most of them opposed this unification. In January 2069, once Myers had been reelected, the NUSA and Militech instigated the conflict that became known as the Unification War to annex the remaining Free States that opposed Myers' program.

In 2070, after capturing most of the Free States, the NUSA moved in to take over Night City, but failed due to Arasaka's intervention. FIA agents Solomon Reed and Song So Mi were in the city, but were called off by the President herself. Not wanting the war to escalate into a global conflict, Myers had little choice but to sign the Arvin Accord with the Free States to bring the war to an early conclusion in June 2070, not succeeding in fully annexing them under the NUSA's banner, but forcing the Free States to get more involved with the Union — with the exception the Republic of Texas.

2077
By 2077, Rosalind Myers was serving her third term as president. Opinion of Myers in Night City was divided. Many people viewed her as a corrupt, corporate-backed fascist with imperialist delusions, while others pointed to Night City's crime rate being double than that of anywhere in the NUSA and argued in favor of accepting Myers' control. During this time, President Myers ordered the bombing of Texan airbases in Wellington and El Paso in retaliation for suicide bombings at the NUSA bases in New Mexico and Oklahoma, raising the odds of a border war with the Republic of Texas. Myers also issued a public statement — the contents of which were not specified — about the flow of refugees into the NUSA from the flooding Netherlands in Europe.

After Saburo Arasaka's passing, Myers stated that all accusations Arasaka had claimed against Militech and the NUSA of being the ones that orchestrated his death were all unfounded and irresponsible. She warned that in the past they had reminded the former CEO that he was not omnipotent, and that if necessary, she would not hesitate to teach his successor, Yorinobu Arasaka, the same lesson. She went on to say that despite having respected the Arvin Accord so far, both the NUSA and Militech would respond in full force if provoked.

At the 2077 Federalist Party convention, Myers announced that she would seek a fourth term in office. Her campaign slogan was unveiled to be "A Return to Unity", emphasizing her commitment to unification across all fronts.

Phantom Liberty
President Myers, Song So Mi, and nine other crew and staff, were traveling above the Californian coast on the Space Force One. While Myers and So Mi were talking, a missile struck right into the spaceplane's wing, forcing it to go down. Additionally, communications had been jammed and the spacecraft was being hacked, with its trajectory directly towards Night City's Dogtown. So Mi managed to contact a merc in Night City named V thanks to the Relic they possessed. After convincing the merc to help them, Songbrid guided V onto a vantage point from where they would get a good view of the situation. Shortly after getting on the top of the EBM Petrochem Stadium, another missile struck into the plane, cutting all communications. So Mi got President Myers into the spaceplane's saferoom, knowing she would survive the crash. So Mi herself barely managed to get into the emergency lifepod, and after passing right above the stadium, the lifepod got ejected, falling on the eastern side of Dogtown, while the Space Force One crashed-landed on the western side, an event that triggered a power struggle with significant consequences.

:After surviving the crash, Myers is surrounded and presumably killed by Hansen's Barghest forces. So Mi later angrily phones V to inform them of her death. So Mi would also sever connections with V and reactivate Johnny. The main story of Phantom Liberty would be locked out.

:After surviving the landing, So Mi guided V to rescue Myers from the crash site. Initially attacking the mercenary, she agreed to work with them after learning they'd been dispatched by So Mi to help her. Fighting off Barghest forces sent after them, the two fled through the district with So Mi's help. During the escape, Myers ordered V to remove a tracker hidden in her neck, believing that someone on her team had betrayed her. Eventually surrounded at the Founding Our Future Expo, Myers and V lost contact with So Mi after she took control of a Chimera stationed. With the machine taken over by a rogue AI whilst attacked them, they initially fled before working together to destroy it.

:V and Myers eventually made their way to abandoned apartment. To escape Dogtown and locate So Mi, Myers told V to contact sleeper agent Solomon Reed, who'd been stationed in the district following the Unification War. After they made contact, Myers tasks them both to locate and recover So Mi. If V attempts to back out, Myers and Reed will attempt to strongarm them into cooperating.
:
::So Mi later calls V to report that Myers and Reed are were discovered and killed by Barghest soldiers. Their bodies are presented to Kurt Hansen after their deaths.
:
::After two days, Reed and Myers are able to arrange for her extraction from Dogtown. She is returned to Washington whilst he remains behind to locate and extract So Mi.

Epilogue

:Shortly after the incident in Night City's Arasaka Tower, President Myers denounced Saburo Arasaka's "resurrection" and stated his seizure of power was against international law. Despite these declarations and months of escalated tensions between Arasaka and Militech, several weeks after the incident both Myers and Saburo agreed to meet in person to lay the foundations for a lasting peace between all parties.

Rose Horrigan is a cyberpsycho in .

Biography
Rose lives with her sister Juliet at their family home on Gibson Street, Rancho Coronado, Santo Domingo.

Rose frequented the ripperdoc Charles Bucks, with work including extensive procedures on both arms.

By 2077, Rose started suffering from cyberpsychosis as a result of her body rejecting her implants. Juliet reached out to Viktor Vektor to see what treatments could be done for Rose, but Viktor broke the news to her that Rose's "condition" had progressed too far to recover from, and advised Juliet to call MaxTac before Rose became violent. Juliet disregarded Viktor's advice, and attempted to treat Rose herself through the use of medication and "basement procedures", but this only exacerbated Rose's declining condition until she fully succumbed to cyberpsychosis, and killed Julliet.

The DB-2 Satara is a Tech Double-Barrel Shotgun manufactured by Rostović in .

Characteristics
The Satara is a modified version of the DB-4 Igla equipped with an electromagnetic barrel that can charge shots, which then can penetrate objects and walls. Like the Igla and DB-2 Testera, the Satara can hold two shells at a time, one for each barrel. Each shell contains 14 projectiles.

The Satara can be charged while fired from the hip.

The weapon cannot be equipped with a Scope or Muzzle attachment.

Database Entry

- transcript：The Satara is an unusual breed both because of its bizarre appearance and its unconventional technological foundation. Instead of firing ordinary buckshot, this electromag shotgun launches small, razor-sharp steel spikes. Critics argue the Satara heaviness and bulkiness make it unreasonably inconvenient for practical use. Its advocates, however, point out that the Serbian shotgun is undeterred by walls. MaxTac officers belong to the latter group. After many trials in the field, the Satara has proved consistently effective at bringing down even the most heavily chromed cyberpsychos.

The Igla is a double-barrel shotgun that can hold two 8-gauge shells, each containing 6 ball bearing pellets. Most other Rostović shotguns were based on the Igla, mostly adjusting the weapon to better adapt to other technologies, such as the Tech variant DB-2 Satara or the Smart variant DB-4 Palica. A modernized, sawed-off variant of the weapon exists in the form of the DB-2 Testera.

The weapon cannot be equipped with a Scope or Muzzle attachment.

Database Entry

- transcript：Fun fact: the Igla was conceived at the beginning of the 21st century as a hunting weapon. Specifically, it was engineered to hunt ducks (medium-sized waterfowl, somewhat similar to seagulls, now considered extinct). The Igla may have fared well against the ducks of Serbia's swamplands, but in 2077's Night City, this shotgun is considered an antique that not even the city's poor and desperate are willing to resort to. Many complain that it produces more noise than damage.

The Kolac (English: Stake) is a Power Precision Rifle manufactured by Rostović in . It was added in Patch 1.6 as part of the New Weapons: Firearms DLC.

Characteristics
The Kolac is a large caliber, semi-automatic, bullpup precision rifle. Like many products manufactured by Rostović, the rifle packs a punch, though is bulky and requires Body augments to be fully utilized. Kolac rifles will likely get damaged if used underwater.

It is not possible to install a Scope or Muzzle attachment.

Database Entry

- transcript：Rostović may not be considered a top-tier arms manufacturer, but their Kolac rifle is nothing to sneeze at. If you're shopping for reliable accuracy and dependable durability, look no further. And with such an affordable price tag, the Kolac feels like a steal. Unfortunately, ergonomics were not a top priority during development. While undeniably precise, this rifle feels heavy and unbalanced. From a quality of life standpoint, this is where Rostović falls behind competitors such as Arasaka, Kang Tao, Tsunami and Militech. Still, if the Kolac has earned a spot with Serbia's armed forces, there's no reason to doubt its effectiveness on the streets of Night City.

Roxxi was part of a mercenary duo with Kimiko Sanchez, with her being the more experienced of the two. Most of their gigs resulted in a massive amount of collateral damages, and while Roxxi pretended to be the more responsible one, usually just as much of the destruction was her fault. Both were regulars at the Forlorn Hope and regularly had to be rescued from sticky situations by its patrons.

During the Fourth Corporate War, Kissy and Roxxie were involved in a battle against Adam Smasher in a neighbourhood in Rancho Coronado. The two of them managed to survive while most of the neighbourhood were killed, giving them a new lease on life. The two of them got married and became more selective with what they chose to destroy.

Ruby Collins is a character in .

Biography
Ruby knew Jeremiah Grayson, an operator working for Adam Smasher. After acquiring this knowledge from Cassius Ryder, Johnny Silverhand — controlling V's body — went to Empathy where she worked. Once he found Ruby, Johnny bought her a couple of drinks. As the night went on, he managed to get close to her, convincing her to go with him.

Outside, Johnny smashed the window of a car and let Ruby drive it. During the drive, Johnny began to fondle her, distracting them both and causing a car accident. The pair survived, and Johnny asked her for Grayson's whereabouts. Still confused, she took a pack of cigars and wrote "Ebunike" on it. After giving Johnny what he had been looking for, she got up and left, still disoriented.

If Grayson survived V's encounter, Ruby was later killed for revealing the Ebunike's location.

Associated Quests

Notes
*Her niche in the Columbarium can appear after the quest Chippin' In with the name and epitaph: "Ruby Barrett. She lived life to the fullest." V reacts to it after scanning the niche: "Ruby... Wait, THAT Ruby?" Quest Director Paweł Sasko stated that Collins is likely her stage name.

引文：There's so much goin' on in NC on any given day it's easy to ignore what's happening across the globe.（Ruth Dzeng）

Ruth Dzeng is the host of the satirical TV talk show Info Flash.

Biography
If there's one thing to know about Ruth it's that she speaks freely. According to her commissioned autobiography, it is revealed that she stepped into the media as a crew assistant through her father's colleague who was a N54 News showrunner at the time. Her untied tongue and sense of comedy amused the higher ups, very quickly moving her from behind the camera into the spotlight. Speaking of the current events of Night City as well as the world in a way that is easily agreed with by the public suffering its effects has quickly earned her views and raised her ratings, making her one of the top celebrities of Night City. She claims that the jokes being made on air are not her own but in fact written by N54's interns, making it difficult to distinguish whether what she says is indeed something she stands for herself. It could also be the reason why the show, regardless of being openly critical of corporations as well as the running government, keeps being aired. In addition to this, her off-screen personality has been described as, while glamorous, still much softer than what her character appears to be on the show.
Phantom Liberty
In 2077, she attended one of Kurt Hansen's parties at the Black Sapphire where V could briefly interact with her.

Night City Media
