## The Ripperdoc
The Ripperdoc is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough

Since the last gig, V's cyberware has started to malfunction. So, after a holo-call with Jackie, they decide to pay a visit to their ripperdoc friend Viktor at his clinic to find out what the problem might be.

V leaves their apartment and heads down to meet Jackie outside Megabuilding H10. While V waits for Jackie to finish his noodles, they talk about a new gig, fronted by the fixer Dexter DeShawn, that Jackie managed to get them involved in.

The duo arrives at Misty's Esoterica in V's repaired car. After a brief chat with Misty, V heads into the clinic and talks to Viktor, bringing up the need for new upgrades for the upcoming gigs. They take a seat in the operating chair, have their new cyberware installed and become acquainted with the scan feature linked to the NCPD database.

Journal Entry
:If you're on the hunt for chrome, you won't find a better ripper than Viktor. Well, all right, maybe you could, but you sure as hell can't afford them, chica/ése. Not like Vik can afford you, either, but you're lucky he's got a soft spot - says you've got a good heart, like him. But before we pay ol' Vik a visit, we gotta decide what comes next.

The Scraper (originally known as the Breeze Hotel) is an unfinished hotel located in Dogtown, in the Pacifica district of southern Night City.

Overview

The Scraper was a planned 4-star hotel complex known as Breeze Hotel that was left unfinished due to the start of the Unification War.

In 2077—several years after its abandonment and Kurt Hansen's BARGHEST taking control of the district—the Scavengers were using the location as one of their hideouts for their illicit activities.

After raiding a Zetatech convoy, the Scraper Scavengers acquired a valuable Arasaka prototype optical implant in the possession of Hasan Demir.

There is a keycode-locked door to an armory on the ground floor near the elevator. The code is 2045.

The Serpent is a road found on the hills located on the southeastern Badlands of Night City.

Overview
The Serpent is a winding road located on the arid hills southeast of Night City. It is a popular place for drifting due to its stepped descent and serpentine layout. ## The Space in Between
The Space in Between is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough

After receiving more information from Oswald Forrest as to Evelyn Parker's location, head to Fingers' clinic on Jig-Jig Street. Before going there, V has the option to let Judy know. She will be waiting for V in front of Fingers' office whether V calls her or not.

V must find a way to get inside Fingers' office. Once inside, V and Judy will talk to Fingers. Moving further in Fingers' office, V can interrogate him to get more information about Evelyn's whereabouts. There are several methods to get the information, but in the end, V and Judy gets all the necessary information.

Journal Entry
:If I've learned one thing from joyhouses, it's to quit while the going's good. Stare at those fake smiles too long, and all you'll see is misery. As far as clubs go they're all pretty pathetic, but at least it's in their own way. You know the chances of finding Evelyn are close to zilch, right? Like that's gonna change your mind... Anyway, let's go pay a visit to this so-called Fingers. But if we don't find Parker, you owe me a drink.

## The Streetkid
The Streetkid is a Main Job in . It is one of the three possible starting jobs, and is only available to players who chose the Streetkid Lifepath. V grew up in the streets of Heywood, Night City before looking for greener pastures in Atlanta. Several years later and no better off, V returns to their hometown and fatefully decides to help out a friend.

Walkthrough
V starts out by fixing their broken nose at the El Coyote Cojo bar located in The Glen. Pepe, the bartender, tells V that he took out a loan from Kirk Sawyer, a new small-time Fixer in town, and Kirk is threatening to break his legs if he doesn't pay soon. Pepe requests that V either talks to Kirk into either forgetting about the debt or finding another way to settle it.

V approaches Kirk and, while he refuses to forgive Pepe's debt, a deal is settled. Kirk tasks V with stealing a Rayfield Aerondight owned by a corporate from Arasaka; If V is able to steal the car, then Kirk will forget about the debt Pepe owes him, and Kirk will even pay V some extra eddies for the job. After agreeing to the deal, V drives to Westbrook where the car is located, hitching a ride with Padre, a friend and local Fixer. Despite a brief confrontation with 6th Street gangoon Sam Carter, Padre delivers V to their destination and hands V his card.

Using the service key given to V by Kirk, V unlocks the car and turns it on, bypassing the alarm systems on the car that prevents the Night City Police Department from being alerted. Things seem to be going smoothly until someone suddenly opens the door from the outside, and V finds themselves staring down the barrel of a gun wielded by Jackie Welles, who intends to take the car for himself. V is then interrupted by the sudden arrival of the NCPD and Inspector Stints, who capture both of V and Jackie and has his officers pin them to the ground. Stints criticizes the two of them on their life choices and how little has changed, but before he can take them into custody, an Arasaka corporate, Kaoru Fujioka, who owns the car, comes to see the commotion. He uses his corporate reputation to order Stints to break V's legs and dump both V and Jackie in the river to drown. The officers knocks them unconscious, but instead of following what the Araskaka corporate said, Stints instead decides to just leave both V and Jackie in a alley since he dislikes corpos as much as everyone else.

V wakes up in the alley. V and Jackie talk as V takes a moment to recover. After getting to know V and the reason why they were stealing the Aerondight he had his eyes on, Jackie says that Kirk isn't as powerful as he seems to be, and his threats against Pepe are hollow at best. Jackie then invites V to breakfast, ending the questline leading into an introduction montage of Night City.

Journal Entry
:Hows it feel bein' back home, V? C'mon, admit it - you missed Heywood. What, between all the dealers, hookers and total lack of opportunities, it's got its charm, don't it? You're born in Heywood, you die in Heywood. Unless you're one of the lucky ones, that is. What about you, chica/mano? That include you?
:If there were an ad for Night City, it'd have Kirk's dumb, grinning face on it. He's slick, thinks he's smarter than he really is and is kind of an asshole, but whenever you call him, he's got the next Big Job that'll rake in millions - like stealing a car from a secure parking garage. 'Cause obviously the millionaires of the future are sitting in the Coyote Cojo scarfing down chili burgers... right?

Objectives

*Find Kirk on the second floor.
*Talk to Kirk.
*Leave the bar.
*Go to Embers.
*Talk to Padre.
*Get in Padre's car.
*Ride with Padre to Embers.
*Get out of the car.
*Take the elevator to the garage.
*Find the Rayfield.
*Find Rick. [Optional]
*Disable the lock using Kirk's device.
*Get in the car.
*Steal the Rayfield.
*Talk to the thief.
*Talk to the police officers.
*Talk to Jackie.

Notes
*A cat is seen right above the outer ventilation system of El Coyote Cojo, on the back alley.
*Contrary to what the Cyberpunk 2077 - The Complete Official Guide states, completing this quest will award the player with a Night City diorama memorabilia for V's Apartment, instead of the Arasaka clock, which is given in The Corpo-Rat.

The View is a shopping mall located in the Corporate Plaza of Night City.

Overview
The View is an open shopping mall found in the boundary of Corporate Plaza, offering a beautiful view to Reconciliation Park to the southwest, from where it takes its namesake. This multilevel facility offers an arrange of upscales establishments, being considered a premiere destination for dining and luxury shopping. For these reasons, the View is frequented by Night City's rich and famous.

A few staircases lead directly to Reconciliation Park to the southwest, while the northeastern portion adjacent to plaza drive acts as a small park with greenery and benches. Lincoln Boulevard goes through the mall's upper levels.

## Theo Price
- status：Alive
- home：Megabuilding H8, Night City
- gender：Female
- hair_color：Brown
- eyes：Green
- partner：Unnamed ex-boyfriend
- voiced_by：Amelia Rose Blaire

引文：Told them he was my best friend... they looked at me like I was crazy...（Theo Price）

Theo Price is a young woman living in Megabuilding H8, Japantown. She found an unexpected friend in the local S.C.S.M. Brendan.

Biography
Theo can be encountered having friendly exchanges with the AI-like S.C.S.M. next to the staircase of the Megabuilding H8. Their conversations will carry topic from light-hearted chatting, friendly advice, leading all the way to proper therapy sessions, which is something Theo desperately needed as she passed through a dire time in her relationship. Brendan will manage to open her eyes to the situation and encourage her to believe in herself and her own strength more. She freely refers to him as a person and plans her moves around his advice.

Once Brendan is taken for code reevaluation, Theo can be found crying in the garbage nook he was previously positioned in. She explains that the maintenance people didn't understand her grief, but did leave a contact due to purely feeling sorry for her. As she can no longer imagine living a life without him, she will beg V to retrieve him before it's too late. Once they return with unfortunate news, in spite of the conversation had with Brendan in the maintenance point, Theo will understand and realize precisely what he has been telling her all along - the strength is within her. With the conclusion of these events, she will accept being the one to blow things out of proportion, although she will admit that Brendan was the best thing to happen to her in months. He got her out of a bad, emotionally insecure situation and regardless of the manner of doing it, regardless of who or what he was, she will remain thankful to him.

Associated Quests
*Spray Paint
*Coin Operated Boy

Trivia
*The voices actors of Theo Price and Brendan, Amelia Rose Blaire and Bryan Dechart, are a real-life couple.

Ted Collins was a resident of Night City and a friend of netrunner Mike Galleck.

## There Is A Light That Never Goes Out
There Is A Light That Never Goes Out is a Side Job in .

Walkthrough
After getting in the NCPD SUV, Vasquez will drive Joshua Stephenson, Rachel Casich and V to their destination. While riding along, Joshua tells V that he was sentenced to prison twelve years ago for armed robbery amongst other things. He continues that he shot and killed several people in cold blood, but that it didn't do anything to him on the emotional level at the time. During his time in prison, he had the time to think about his actions, and thought of ways on how to correct them. Joshua asks that V sticks with him for the day, promising them payment equal to that they would have been paid for killing him. As they near their destination, Joshua will ask for a moment of time to think.

Arriving at the El-Ahmar House, Joshua and V get out of the vehicle. As Joshua approaches the house, a woman named Zuleikha El-Ahmar greets and invites him and V in to talk. While speaking with Zuleikha, V learns that her brother, Ruben El-Ahmar, was killed by Joshua. But instead of despising Joshua for it, she began to write to him while he was in prison, forgiving him for what he did as her Christian faith told her to not judge others. Because of her letters, Joshua became a Christian himself.

Joshua will then reveal what's going on: Rachel is with a braindance recording studio that plans to record Joshua's crucifixion. Joshua hopes that this will inspire people to convert to Christianity by showing them how Jesus suffered for them. Before more can be said though, Zuleikha's mother Gloria arrives, and unlike her daughter, she hasn't forgiven Joshua and demands he and V leave.

:Joshua and V return to the vehicle, and the group will decide to go for a meal, but Rachel would like a word in private with V first. She'll say that she thinks Joshua is nuts, but the fact that he genuinely believes what he says is valuable since it makes for better braindances. Rachel fears that V is jeopardizing this by asking "probing questions" which cause Joshua to doubt himself.

:Arriving at the PieZ restaurant in Rancho Coronado, Santo Domingo, Rachel instructs Vasquez to take Stephenson inside and grab a table, so that she is able to talk with V. She offers V double Joshua's payment to walk away.

:
::V heads into the restaurant and takes place at the table to talk more with Joshua and Rachel about the braindance and other topics, until Rachel gets fed up and tells V off before storming out. Joshua says goodbye to V before also leaving with Vasquez. Johnny will reappear and have some thought-provoking comments. This concludes the job, and pay is transferred shortly. A day later, Rachel will call V to attend Joshua's crucifixion.

:
::After accepting Rachel's bribe, Rachel heads inside, telling V that they'll say goodbye to Stephenson on their behalf. Some time after completing, Rachel reaches out to V about their payment, and transfers them 4600 eurodollars.
:
::V demands a bigger cut, as they're familiar with how high the budget for producing braindances can be. Rachel begrudgingly agrees before heading inside, telling V that they'll say goodbye to Stephenson on their behalf. Some time after completing, Rachel reaches out to V about their payment, and transfers them 9300 eurodollars.

:After talking with Zuleikha, V decided to leave, concluding the job.

Journal Entry
:I love these WTF situations. A guy hires you to off some other guy, and then that first guy dies, but then the second guy hires you to go somewhere with him for who the fuck knows what. But hey, it's not like you're short on work. Just don't fuck this one up, OK? I know you wanna know how this all plays out.

Objectives
*Talk to Joshua Stephenson.
*Ride along with Joshua.
*Follow Joshua Stephenson.
*Follow Zuleikha.
*Talk to Zuleikha.

*Return to the car.
*Get in the NCPD vehicle.

*Sit down at the table in PieZ.
*Talk to Joshua.

Notes

Trivia

## These Boots Are Made for Walkin'
These Boots Are Made for Walkin' is a Side Job in . It is only available to players who chose the Nomad Lifepath, and features V regaining their car from the prologue.

Walkthrough
After visiting Rogue Amendiares at the Afterlife during Ghost Town, V will get a message from their old car Thorton Galena 80845, revealing its geolocation in the Badlands, due south of the Medeski Fuel Station, within the landfill.

V heads out there and checks under the hood to see if someone has been tinkering with it, and they realize the engine is still warm - someone clearly drove the vehicle recently. As they finish checking it over though they'll be approached by a woman, Lana Prince, who's both surprised and annoyed V's messing with "her" car.

Upon asking, Lana reveals that she is desperate to leave the city and has had enough of the wastelands and sees the car as her only hope to start a new life.

:V told Lana that she can keep the car and gives Lana some suggestions of what she should be doing in order to repair the car before leaving Night City.

:V offered Lana a large sum of eurodollars in order to buy the car out of sentimental value, so that she can buy something different instead and leave NC. This decision allowed V to reclaim the vehicle as their own.

:V threatened Lana to leave, even willing to put her under gunpoint. This decision allowed V to reclaim the vehicle as their own.

Journal Entry
:Here you thought your old ride was totaled for good - yet here you are now. Like a phoenix from the ashes, it lives again. But how? Why now? You'd already closed that chapter of kickin' up sand with nomads out in the desert... But I mean, it'd be stupid if you didn't check it out... right? You never can underestimate the past. Because it sure as shit likes to take revenge.

Objectives
*Go to the indicated location.
*Scan your old car. [Optional]
*Look under the hood.
*Check the engine.
*Talk to the stranger.
*Get in your old car.
*Talk to Johnny.

Notes

## They Won't Go When I Go
They Won't Go When I Go is a Side Job in .

Walkthrough
Some time after leaving the PieZ restaurant after talking with Joshua Stephenson and Rachel Casich, Rachel will call V to say that Joshua has requested their presence while he prepares for his crucifixion braindance.

:V says they currently don't have time to come, which will cause Joshua to plead with V over the phone, claiming that they need V to be present during recording. Rachel tells V that they'll receive extra compensation for their time.

:
::V apologizes and tells them that they are on their own.

:V agrees to help out and heads to Fourth Wall Studios, where there's a group of people protesting against "The Passion of Joshua"'s filming. As V approaches the gate, they are hailed by Vasquez, who tells V that Rachel has been waiting for them, and instructs V to go to the building down the street with the NCPD Officer out front. After the Officer lets V inside, they talk to Rachel, who instructs them to talk to Joshua in the dressing room.

V approaches Joshua, and sits down on the stool in front of him. Joshua tells V that he is having second thoughts about recording the braindance and asks for V's opinion. Eventually, Joshua will ask V to join him in prayer.

:V and Joshua clasp their hands, and Joshua will recite Saint Augustine's Prayer to the Holy Spirit.
::"Breathe in me O Holy Spirit, that my thoughts may all be holy."
::"Act in me O Holy Spirit, that my work, too, may be holy."
::"Draw my heart O Holy Spirit, that I love but what is holy."
::"Strengthen me O Holy Spirit, to defend all that is holy."
::"Guard me, then, O Holy Spirit, that I always may be holy. Amen."

:V and Joshua clasp their hands, and V recites a prayer.

:V refuses to join Joshua in prayer, making Joshua pray silently on his own.

A moment later, Rachel enters backstage and interrupts Joshua and V, stating that the time has come to record the braindance. Joshua asks V if they want to perform his crucifixion.

:V accepts to crucify Joshua. After picking up the hammer, and waiting for everyone to be in position, V nails Joshua's wrists and feet to the cross while reciting the lines from the teleprompter.

:
::V presses the button to raise the cross, and waits for Joshua to pass.

:
::V says that they are unable to continue with nailing Joshua to the cross, and another actor continues to fulfill the role instead. The actor presses the button and raises the cross, as V waits for Joshua to pass.

:Afterwards, V talks with Rachel, who will tell V that they'll reach out to V at a later point for their payment.

:V refuses to perform Joshua's crucifixion, and witnesses another actor fulfill the role instead. After the crucifixion is finished and the cross is raised, V waits until Joshua has passed. Before leaving, V talks with Rachel, who will tell V that they'll reach out to V at a later point for their payment.

:V refuses to partake in Joshua's crucifixion and leaves Fourth Wall Studios.

V is contacted by Rachel again two days later, and she tells V that the braindance has been published.

:Rachel exclaims that the braindance was a hit and thanks V for their help, and promises a bonus for them. After the call finishes, she will transfer V a moderate sum of eurodollars.

:Rachel tells V that the braindance was of poor quality, and is angry with them. Despite this, she will transfer V a small sum of eurodollars.

Journal Entry
:Well, whaddaya know. This corpo-slut from the crucifixion BD wants you to come back to give her star a pep talk, massage his fucking shoulders and whatnot. Normally I'd tell you to drop it, find something more fun to do, but... I dunno, seems like this Jesus freak could really use your help.

Objectives
*Talk to Rachel.

*Talk to Vasquez.
*Go inside the braindance studio.
*Talk to Rachel.
*Talk to Joshua Stephenson.
*
**Help Joshua record the BD.
**Take the hammer and nails.
**Wait by the cross.
**Nail Joshua to the cross.
**Raise the cross.
**
***Sit on the chair
**Stay with Joshua until he dies.
**Talk to Rachel.
*
**Help Joshua record the BD.
**Sit on the chair.
**Stay with Joshua until he dies.
**Talk to Rachel.
*
**Leave the braindance studio.

## Things Done Changed
Things Done Changed is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough
Two years after accepting Solomon Reed's offer, in 2079, V wakes up from a medically induced coma in Edward Kernaghan Military Medical Center with Reed at their side. Reed explains to V that the operation to remove the relic was successful, but that due to the procedure V's brain became permanently damaged and unable to handle cyberware.

Solomon Reed proceeds to give V a job offer from the NUSA goverment, so that they can at least continue living, and allows V to reach out to their friends.

:Viktor Vektor is happy to hear from V, and V shares their diagnosis with the ripper. Vik will say the doctors are wrong, and the merc should pay him a visit.

:Judy Álvarez is surprised to hear from V but will admit her relief to know they're alive, also stating she won't be part of their next adventure as she is now living in Pittsburgh and married to a woman named Bianca.
:
::Judy will also apologize to V and ask her not to try and ruin their marriage, effectively ending their relationship.

:Panam won't answer the call, and V leaves her a phone message. Mitch Anderson sends V a video message during the epilogue saying she doesn't want to talk to them, and that it would be best if V does not try to call her again. If V romanced her, the relationship is ended.

:River Ward is angry at first, but gives V a chance to explain that they just woke up from two years of coma, after which River apologizes. After suggesting meeting up, River reveals that he sold everything he knew about the NCPD to Trauma Team to earn some money to pay for Randy's rehab, and as a consequence, he is now a wanted man. Ashamed of himself, he's unable to face V in person and ends the call. If romanced, the relationship is ended.

:Kerry Eurodyne is happy to hear from V but is also busy and constantly interrupted during his call as he's at the Crystal Palace on a concert tour, admitting that he doesn't have time for V at the moment. If romanced, he promises to reunite with V once the tour is over in a few months.

Afterwards, V returns to Night City and takes a Delamain Cab to Viktor's clinic (which is now a Zetatech franchise), having opportunities to talk with those two about what has changed in Night City. Viktor will also concur with the NUSA doctors, stating that V's motor cortex appears to have "turned deaf to implant signals".

After leaving Viktor's, V is accosted and beaten by a single street thug, a sad reminder of how weak they've become. Misty Olszewski arrives and helps V up. She shares that she is moving to Poland, and gives V advice on living as an average citizen. V can express various outlooks on their life and goals. In a cutscene, Misty leaves, and V fades into a crowd.

Journal Entry
:Know what you're thinkin' — all is lost, right? Could be true in some way, I guess. But it's just as true that you get to live on.
:Dunno, somebody out there might be lookin' out for you to come back. Start callin' — friends, acquaintances, associates, even. Then get back to NC. You'll build a new life for yourself, one with new meaning, I know you will. Or you'll find some traces of your old life and purpose.
:And if none of that pans out, set out and see what's beyond the horizon. 'Cause there's always somethin' there, V. Always.

Objectives
*Talk to Reed.
**Go to the window.
*Call your friends and decide who to visit.
*Use the intercom to leave the clinic.
**Call other friends. [Optional]
*Wait for the medical orderly.
*Talk to Delamain.
**Exit the cab.
*Meet with Viktor.
**Talk to the receptionist.
*Talk to Viktor.
**Sit in the ripper's chair.
*Leave Viktor's clinic.
*Return to Delamain.
*Deal with the back-alley thugs.
*Wait for help.
*Talk to Misty.
*Walk with Misty.

Associated Shards

Trivia
*The job is named after the The Notorious B.I.G. song "Things Done Changed" from the album Ready to Die.

## This Corrosion
- type：Side Job
- quest_giver：Unknown Number
- district：Watson
- sub_district：Kabuki
- previous_quest：Leave in Silence
- reward_item：(dependent)
 (dependent)

This Corrosion is a Side Job in .

Walkthrough

Prerequisites: For this quest to appear, one needs to have obtained one or both of the crafting specs for the or , and have looted the from the Cerberus during Somewhat Damaged.

About 24 hours after completing Somewhat Damaged, V will receive a message from an unknown number and party interested in the aforementioned items retrieved from the Cynosure Facility. V will be directed to meet with Yoko Tsuru at Kabuki Market, who will take a few hours to decrypt the algorithm on the behavioral system component. She will give V the Cerberus' decoded behavioral system component with a word of warning. The player can craft a single item: either the Erebus or the Canto Mk.6, after which this job will be completed.

Journal Entry
: You got out of that hellish bunker alive and brought a little souvenir with you. Only it's more than just that, isn't it? It's some kind of fucking mystery that you'll want to solve and that'll take us fuck knows where. Be careful, V. Some secrets are better left as they are - secrets.

Objectives
*Meet with the netrunner.
*Talk to Yoko.
*Wait for Yoko to decrypt the component.
*Retrieve the decrypted component from Yoko.
*Use the decrypted component to craft a single item: Erebus or Militech Canto Mk.6.

Notes
Sometime after completing the quest, V will randomly be attacked by team of NetWatch agents attempting to confiscate the crafted item.

Trivia
*This job is named after the song "This Corrosion" by the English goth band The Sisters of Mercy from their 1987 album Floodland.

## Thomas Hays
- status：Dependent
- home：Night City
- equipment：Tsunami Nue
- gender：Male
- affiliation：Valentino

Thomas Hays is a Valentino in Cyberpunk 2077.
Biography
Hays worked with fixer Kirk Sawyer, but suspected that the fixer was double crossing him. To confirm his suspicions, Hays sets up a trap, feeding Sawyer with false information about Militech cyberware being transported in a van parked at the Tirempire Auto Shop located in Arroyo, Santo Domingo.

After Sawyer sends V to retrieve the "cyberware", Hays and two other Valentinos ambushed Sawyer and his bodyguard Big Joe while they waited outside Tire Empire, killing them both.

After V returns, Hays will taunt the mercenary, claiming anyone who works with Sawyer is a "gonk little bitch", and demand that V say it.

:Hays lets V go without a fight.

:Hays and the two Valentinos will become hostile and V neutralizes them.

Abilities

The "Little Mule" is a nomad version of the pickup truck Colby CX410, a vehicle manufactured by Thorton in .

Overview
The Colby Little Mule is a small and inexpensive but reasonably well equipped nomad truck. Quite fast (including across open desert), very tough, with extra reinforced armor and a CrystalDome holoprojection system. It drives well by comparison to many other cars, having an impressive handling.

Upgrades
*CrystalDome
*Mounted Machine Guns

Database Entry

- transcript：Nomads, as the name suggests, don't linger too long in any one place. They're constantly on the move and that means bringing that belongings with them. It comes as no wonder the truck-bed variant of the Colby has become so popular with them. Little Mule - that's what they call this Thorton Colby model. But beyond the name they also swap out the standard engines for strongers ones, add light armor to the body and install an environment projection system based on CrystalDome tech in the cabin.

Acquisition
It can be acquired from the AUTOFIXER netpage for €$41,000.

Thorton Colby "Little Mule" V Message CP2077.png

Notes
*Game files indicate a version called Colby "Coyote" was supposed to appear and was owned by Mitch Anderson. Instead, in the game Mitch's Colby is simply called "Little Mule."
*Prior to Patch 1.5 it cost €$49,000. And before Patch 2.0 it cost €$35,000.
*Prior to the introduction of AUTOFIXER, Dakota Smith sold the car via a text message: "Hello, V. I have a "Little Mule" for sale - in other words a custom-tuned Thorton Colby. A techie friend of mine found it in a ditch outside of town - thought it was beyond repair. Nothing but rust, dust and a communal bathroom for rats, by the looks of it. But once he gave it a wash-down, banged it back into shape, swapped out the suspension and cranked up the engine... well, for riding around in the desert, you can't go wrong."

Trivia
*"Little Mule" is likely a reference to the 1982 Ford Bronco XLT that appears in the 1984 film Romancing the Stone - a black pickup nicknamed "Little Mule."

The "Gecko" is a variant of the Thorton Galena that has been customized by nomads to increase off-road performance for travel in the Badlands. Featuring a tuned engine, raised suspension, and many other modifications, it is a more capable version of the Galena. It has all-wheel drive in place of the base model's front-wheel drive, and CrystalDome in place of the standard glass windows.

The Gecko is also armed with a pair of fixed forward-mounted machine guns.

V's obtainable version is painted green with a red rear section and rollcage, green wheels and suspension, and has the number "23" printed on the doors.

Folks in the wasteland used to laugh at the sight of a Galena, but no one's laughing now.

The Galena G240 is a vehicle manufactured by Thorton in .

Overview

Database Entry

- transcript：It used to be people only desired bread and circuses. By the 21st century, however, automobiles were added to the list. Without a car, you can't get to work, drop off the kids at kindergarten or escape spontaneous turf wars. The Thorton Galena first hit roads in 2031 following a government stimulus to pump out affordable cars and give Americans a boost following the recession. As Thorton didn't have much experience producing small cars at the time, the company bought engines for the Galena from India's Mahir Motors. Unfortunately, the collaboration was not considered a success, with the Galena yielding unremarkable performance and even less remarkable sales. Still, it drives - and that's the most important thing.

Acquisition
It can be acquired from the AUTOFIXER netpage for €$13,000.

引文：With its unusually high mileage and relatively small frame, this car is a perennial favorite among taxi and delivery drivers.（Galena "Rattler"）

The "Rattler" is a nomad version of the Galena model, a vehicle manufactured by Thorton in .

History
The Rattler was a Galena GA40xt, which was heavily customized by the Bakkers Nomad clan. It is V's personal car if they have chosen the Nomad lifepath. V used it to escape the Arasaka convoy during a smuggling run into Night City, but the car was wrecked and they had to abandon it.

The Rattler was eventually found by a young woman called Lana Prince. She transported it to the city's landfill, where she managed to fix some of its major problems, including getting its computer functioning again. The reactivated vehicle sent a signal to its last registered owner, V, who followed the signal and was reunited with their old ride.

V inspected the Rattler, noting the repairs to the engine, but also that it still required a lot more work. Lana discovered him with the car and claimed it was hers now; after some small talk, she explained to V she needed it to leave Night City for good. V then chose to either give the car to Lana, in which case she eventually left with it; or to keep it, either by buying it from Lana or threatening her.

Database Entry

Acquisition
Only available for the Nomad lifepath. After the prologue, V will lose the Rattler. During Act II, V will receive a call with the location of the vehicle, starting the quest These Boots Are Made for Walkin'. Depending on the dialogue choices, the "Rattler" can be recovered at the end of said quest.

Associated Quests
*The Nomad
*These Boots Are Made for Walkin'

Notes
*It is not possible to listen to the radio while driving the car during the prologue.
*The Rattler is one of the few vehicles in Cyberpunk 2077 (the others being V's Hella EC-D i360 and the Turbo-R V-Tech) that have a horse decal on the rear right side of the car and a bulldog bobblehead on the dashboard.
*In the Call Vehicle Menu and while Scanning it is referred to as the Thorton Galena "Rattler".

Trivia
*The horse decal is a reference to Roach, Geralt of Rivia's horse in The Witcher series.

引文：With a souped-up suspension and performance-tuned engine, this car is ready for a wild ride.（Mackinaw "Beast"）

"Beast" is a modified version of the Mackinaw, a vehicle manufactured by Thorton in .

Overview
Beast is a heavily modified pickup truck used as a street racing vehicle by Claire Russell. She does the maintenance and upkeep on the it, and it sports several modifications, including additional bulletproof armor used to protect its occupants from gunfire.

Claire used to race Beast with her husband, Dean Russell, who died while participating in one of Night City's death races in 2076. In 2077, V drove Beast while helping Claire win the annual death races.

Database Entry

Specifications
The "Beast" is a dually truck, meaning that there are two tires placed at each side of the truck's rear. Bolt-on fender flares cover the wheels and Rotoria OOF3 tires. It is a heavily armored vehicle, with ballistic armor covering both the grill and hood. The front fenders and front headlights remain unprotected. There is a large tow hook under each headlight. The front fenders are not armored, and the driver's side fender contains the CHOOH2 gas cap.

A skid plate protects the engine, and mounted next to the plate on each side are four LED lamps for off-roading (with covers on). Front suspension includes two shock absorbers per wheel, one being a coil-over and the other being a hydraulic piston and cylinder assembly.

At the rear, it has its pickup bed, which has been modified with a roll bar. Inside the bed is a spare wheel and tire assembly. There is also a locking storage chest placed at the back of the bed to be used as a trunk, with two more tow hooks placed below the lower lip of the rear.

Its doors are protected with bolted-on armor plates. The rear passenger side door is fully covered with armor and the door latches are covered. Inside the "Beast", there are several carbon fiber features, including carbon fiber seats. The interior features a roll cage and an escape hatch that leads out of the vehicle from its roof. The rear passenger side seat has been replaced with an apparatus that is covered in diamond plate.

Acquisition
Beast is rewarded at the end of The Beast In Me if you follow Peter Sampson outside of the race.

Notes
*On its front end there is a pink bunny backpack, which has an orange Hawaiian shirt over it.
*On the tailgate on the back there is a painted transgender pride flag. Another one is painted in the middle of the vehicle's center console.

Acquisition

Given to V by Polyhistor after solving the FF:06:B5 mystery. The coordinates for the mattress are obtained by going to the Protein Farm church in the middle of Biotechnica Flats and at 4AM in-game time, access each email and file on the computer, then accessing the Arasaka Tower 3D arcade game. The arcade game does not need to be played past killing the first enemy. After completing the game, V can head near the Corp-Bud Cement Factory and find the mattress nearby in the middle of the desert. Standing still on the mattress for ±50–60 minutes (7–8 minutes real time) will trigger a cutscene after which V is woken up by Polyhistor, who will disappear afterwards, leaving the vehicle.

It is possible to bypass all these steps and just venture to the mattress after 04:00 AM in-game time.

Notes
*It was originally added in Patch 1.3, but wasn't made available until Patch 2.0.

The "Warhorse" is a heavily modified nomad pickup truck that belongs to Panam Palmer. It has a four-wheel drive with reinforced tires, a heavy turret on its top, advanced electronics, and a reinforced body, trunk and windows.

The only thing this car has in common with your basic Thorton Mackinaw is its steel body. A masterpiece of automotive tinkering, this baby was made for the wide, open desert.

Panam lost the truck after Nash cheated her by stealing it and all the cargo they were supposed to deliver. With the help of V, Panam recovered the "Warhorse" from a group of Wraiths in Rocky Ridge. She later used it to help them reach the AV transporting Anders Hellman.

## Through Pain to Heaven
Through Pain to Heaven is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough

Journal Entry
:Silence... Finally. Every time I think back to that first meeting with Songbird, I feel like I'm gonna blow chunks. The moment she made me fade out... A feeling worse than death. Believe me, I'm an expert on the subject. But now? Nothing. Not a peep. Not even an echo. As if she's far, far away, or... I dunno. Looks like it's just the two of us again. But for how long now, I wonder.

Objectives
* Find something to do until Reed contacts you.
* Talk to Reed.
* Meet Reed at the CHOOH2 station.
* Talk to Reed.
* Talk to Johnny.

 Trivia

*The name of the mission is from a song by [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popol_Vuh_(band) Popol Vuh], from their 1978 album [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nosferatu_(Popol_Vuh_album) Nosfetaru].

## Ti Neptune
- status：Dependent
- home：Night City
- gender：Male
- affiliation：Voodoo Boys
- role：Netrunner

Ti Neptune is a Voodoo Boys Netrunner in .

Biography
Ti was a netrunner who along alongside Brigitte was attempting to contact Alt Cunningham from beyond the Blackwall. The Voodoo Boys made a deal with Evelyn Parker to steal the Relic biochip from Yorinobu Arasaka, which contained the digitized personality construct, also known as engram, of Johnny Silverhand. They believed the only way Cunningham would come to them was if they used Johnny's engram as bait.

Upon discovering that NetWatch was attempting to penetrate their independent data fort, Rezo Agwe, Neptune investigated, but was quickly stopped by the Black ICE deployed by the NetWatch agent and was placed in stasis. Upon discovering Neptune, Brigitte pursued, using Neptune as a shield, and managed to take down parts of the NetWatch infrastructure with her before also being struck by the Black ICE.

The Netwatch agent kept Neptune in stasis until he was finally awoken after Placide had a mercenary by the name of V infiltrate the Grand Imperial Mall. He later joined Brigitte as they entered their BBS and used the mercenary to lure Alt out.

:Ti was flatlined upon seeing Alt as she had seen NetWatch had been tracing them to her.

:Ti along with Brigitte saw Alt and awaited V as they came back from the BBS. The mercenary spoke with Brigitte and was upset for being used by them.

## Ticking Time Bomb
Ticking Time Bomb is a Perk in .

Overview
Ticking Time Bomb can be unlocked at 20 Technical Ability after unlocking Pyromania and License To Chrome.

Unlocking this perk allows you to charge an EMP that hits nearby enemies after 3 seconds whenever you activate a Operating System cyberware (Berserk or Sandevistan) or Overclock. This EMP applies a Stun and deals damage proportionate to the quantity and tier of cyberware implants you have installed.

While charging an EMP, incoming damage is reduced by 50%.

## Tiff
- status：Deceased
- home：Watson, Night City
- gender：Female
- hair_color：Blonde
- eyes：Cyan
- cyberware：See Cyberware
- equipment：See Equipment
- partner：Mint (girlfriend)
- occupation：Mechanic
- role：Techie

Tiff is a character in .

Biography
At some point Tiff met fellow techie Mint. They spent two years rebuilding a Yaiba sports coupe, replacing many of its pieces by new ones. This process was put on hold after Mint disappeared.

Six months later, Mint returned to Tiff's home in Watson and broke into the building after finding out she was not there, deciding the spend the night in a bed. The next morning, Tiff was returning to her home with two Matapang Coffees, stopping along the way to give one to Mike, a homeless man who lived not far from her home and who she usually bought a cup coffee. After reaching her house, Tiff found the electronic lock broken. Expecting thieves, she grabbed her handgun, but lowered the guard when she found Mint sleeping in a bed. Tiff was angry at her for trespassing and disappearing for six months. After Mint mentioned she needed the Yaiba car, Tiff asked her where she had been for all that time, with Mint saying she didn't want to drag her in, but that she was involved with the NCPD, and with Gorilla and Caliber. Tiff was worried about her, warning that someone like Caliber was dangerous and unpredictable. She also mentioned Mint's bad reputation in the city, but that she didn't want to believe any of that. For Mint it wasn't that simple, as she was playing both sides trying to come out on top. After both finished installing the new engine to the car, Tiff gave Mint her handgun and asked her to not get killed.

Mint was tasked by Gorilla in capturing a boxer known as Riot, but failed at her original plan. She eventually had to ask for Tiff's help about a garage in Watson where Riot was heading. To stop him from getting there, Tiff left her workshop and crashed her Herrera Riptide into Riot's car, allowing Mint to capture him after checking up on Tiff first, who not long after managed to return to her home. Later that night, Mint returned to Tiff's place only to find out a Tyger Claw car parked in front of her building. Mint panicked, grabbed her gun and went to the car only to find Green Dragon — who Mint had wronged in the past — and another gangster dead. Suddenly, her NCPD contacts appeared, commenting that was a gift from them, as the NCPD always took care of their people as long as they showed results. Their cold-blooded behavior shocked Mint, who was left without any words as they both left. While all this was happening, Tiff was watching from her home's window.

Time Machine is a notorious music store located in the Glen, in the Heywood district of central Night City.

Overview
Time Machine is one of the most famous music stores in all of Night City, patronized by various famous artists and with the likes of Kerry Eurodyne visiting it from time to time.

The shop is primarily dedicated to rock and pop music, though it sells a range of items, including memorabilia and a variety of musical instruments; the most notable ones being a sizable selection of electric guitars. It also sells a large number of rock albums such as Samurai, Eurodyne, or Cutthroat; but its catalogue extends to include other musical genres, adding to the list artists like Lizzy Wizzy, Us Cracks or Tainted Overlord. The list of songs includes recent releases as well as old vintage music.

Time Machine's back room is reserved for true musical connoisseurs, with the owner, Journey Ruiz, inviting clients in to allow them to see and maybe purchase items from her priceless collection.

引文：Timmy won’t tell you he’ll fix you the Moon, he won’t tell you he knows everyone in this town and they know him. But. But. He has two traits on any other fixer in this town: he always answers my pings, and I like the guy.（Frank）

Timmy G is a character in .

Biography
Early life
Timmy G was a netrunner for most of his life. He started working as a fixer in Night City sometime in the 2060s. At one point he got pulled over by NCPD officer Frank, who discovered that Timmy was transporting neuroreactors stolen from a Petrochem lab. Frank let him walk for 20% of the profit from the cargo and the two became friends.

2070s
In the 2070s, Timmy G had a hideout in a postindustrial area of Watson. He was considered quite paranoid, as he installed cameras on the stairs to his floor, which he reserved all for himself.

In 2071, he was contacted by Frank and asked to look for any information about the weapons that were about to be unleashed on the street, particularly the ones which were tied to the death of Ora Dominguez. During his search he was detected by the cops headed by detective Brian Lee, and was subsequently killed. Frank found Timmy's body and wanted to check what he discovered, but was stopped by Brian.

## Tokyo
- motto："Tokyo Tokyo Old meets New"
- aka：Tokyo City
Tokyo Metropolis
- type：City
- country：Japan
- prefecture：Tokyo
- region：Kanto, Honshu
- location：Tokyo Bay
- population：14 million - City
57 million - Metropolis
- demonym：Tokyoite
- map1：Tokyo Subyway Lines Cyberpunk 2022.png
- map2：Cyberpunk Tokyo 2020.png
- map3：Tokyo Map 2020.png

引文：Tokyo - The Modern Babylon.（Araki Kae）

Tokyo (東京), a part of Tokyo Prefecture and officially Tokyo Metropolis (東京都), is the capital city of Japan. It has served as the Japanese capital since 1869, its urban area housing the Emperor of Japan and the Japanese government.

Overview
Tokyo City's population is around 14 million, however greater metropolitan area of the Tokyo Prefecture is around 57 million, with around 34 million being in the city on a daily for work. The trains at their peak periods of the day run at 300% to 400% capacity.

Tokyo is both one of the safest and one of the most dangerous cities in the world. It's kept safe by the hordes of corporate police controlled by the Zaibatsus. However the corporations only interfere when their profits are hurt. This is where the national police or local yakuza come in to keep the streets clean of crime. The city is kept clean and safe in high density areas.

Tokyo has only been the capital since the mid 1800s, during the time of the Meiji Restoration of the Emperor. For 1,000 years before that however, the capital of Japan was Kyoto. Since becoming the capital, Tokyo has expanded non-stop, decaying, and rebuilding in a strange cycle of progression.

History
1990s
Arasaka during the 1990s quickly was becoming the largest and most influential megacorporation in the world.

2000s
In 2010, the Tokyo Bay Crossway an Auto Defense System was installed to prevent a terrorist attack that could appear in the Bridge. However in 2018, the Ministry of Science and Technology lost communication with the Bridge. No definitive answer was ever found, Tokyo police were call in along side Chiba police and even Arasaka riot control groups, but nothing was effective in taking back the bridge. The bridge became inhabited with unemployed Nomad-types, bosozoku, refugees, and other criminals.

In 2023, conflict during the Fourth Corporate War also found its way to Tokyo. However fights did not last long as the government cracked down on Arasaka, preventing any further conflict within the city.

2077
In 2077, the Arasaka Corporation put 27 billion New Yen towards fixing the housing crisis in the city. The Japanese government also put forth the idea of draining part of Tokyo Bay in order to make room for more megabuildings.

Bioengineers celebrated the first successful cloning of a cave lion. Scientists from Tokyo, Seoul, and Yakutsk used genetic material from the remains of an ancient female lion discovered in a bog near Kolyma river in Northern Siberia.

The Nippon Daily Corporation reported on the Relic biochip a new premium line developed by Arasaka, which they later confirmed to be accurate and revealed afterwards.

Famous braindance producer, Hideyoshi Oshima, had strived to create real emotionally touching human experiences within his braindance studio in Tokyo. For inspiration Hideyoshi traveled to Night City staying at Konpeki Plaza where he met with braindance talent.

Economy & Shopping

Tokyo has the largest metropolitan economy in the world. According to a study conducted, the Greater Tokyo Area (Tokyo-Yokohama) of 57 million people had a total GDP of $8 trillion in 2045 (at purchasing power parity), which topped that list. The Tokyo region is Japan's leading industrial center, with a highly diversified manufacturing base. Heavy industries are concentrated in Chiba, Kawasaki, and Yokohama, while Tokyo proper is strongly inclined toward light industry, including book printing and the production of electronic equipment.

More significantly, perhaps, Tokyo is Japan's management and finance center. Corporations, or Zaibatsus, with headquarters or branches or production sites in other parts of the country often have large offices in Tokyo, Marunouchi being the location of many of these. The close relationship between government and business in Japan makes a Tokyo location advantageous if not necessary.

To the north of Marunouchi is Otemachi, where Japan's leading financial institutions and insurance companies are located. Otemachi is also home to NTT, the communications giant. Tokyo is also the site of the Tokyo Stock Exchange, located in Kabutocho. Arasaka the world's most influential Megacorporation and largest Japanese conglomerate is located in Chuo, each division of Arasaka is controlled through Tokyo.

Tokyo holds the most corporate headquarters and regional offices compared to any other major city. So many of which either were founded and came here in the hopes of finding big business and plenty of opportunity. Kendachi, SegAtari, Fujiwara Bank, and Mitsubishi are some of the many corporations that were founded within the city.

Tokyo is the heart of industry and consumption finding something inexpensive, unusual, or not exactly legal; are all found in different well-known shopping centers. These shopping centers are found all over the city.

Areas
Tokyo Bay Crossway

The Tokyo Bay Crossway was built at the turn of the century. It largely consists of 10 km of underwater tunnels, and 5 km of bridge crossing the bay. By the year 2010, law and order had declined fast and an Auto Defense System was installed to prevent a terrorist attack that could appear in the Bridge. Guard robots moving in and out of the small maintenance ducks were considered powerful enough to take on any head on attack by a terrorist group.

However in 2018, the Ministry of Science and Technology lost communication with the Bridge, which then took matters into it's own hands. Many different theories have surfaced over the years, one of the more popular ones is a virus took over the central AI and caused it to go rogue, but there still is no definitive answer.

First, the traffic lights all went down. Afterwards a small Security Office was attacked by their own drones, and then people were forced out. The Tokyo Police from Keishi-cho, Chiba Prefecture Police, and Arasaka Riot team upon request from the S&T Ministry attempted to take back the central computer, but they couldn't seem to reach it. Control from the Net to this day hasn't been established. The Bridge went rogue.

Not too long after, homeless started to migrate to the Bridge. These "Bridge People" aren't seen as enemies from the defense system, that is if they stay 200 meters away from the Control Room. Most of them live in the underwater sections of the bridge. Also, there are many who live on the artificial islands that support the above-ground portion of the bridge, and the girders of the bridge. The Tokyo Police have put it on record that around 8,000 people live in the Bridge.

As stated the people who live here are usually unemployed Nomad-types who aren't able to afford living in the big cities of Tokyo or Chiba. There's also a small portion of gaijin and Nambei-jin who are the first to go in a job crunch. There's also quite a few criminals who have also taken refuge. Since Arasaka is the law in Kanagawa, and Chiba Prefectural Police rule in Chiba, the bridge was always a jurisdiction gray zone; now a days it's just a sovereign territory.

As long as there's no skirmishes above a certain level, the bridge doesn't really interfere with the rest of the public. On rare occasions, a small riot team will go in to arrest a criminal who escaped to this location. However not all crimes will be cashed down here, big ones like Nov. 6, 2018, will be squashed with extreme force.

In the present day, the defenses appear to be invincible. There is plenty of ammo, as the auto-factories around the bridge legs keep making more from construction material stockpiles intended for the bridge itself. The government an local policing forces do not see the situation changing anytime soon.

Tokyo Disney City
Tokyo Disney City is located in Chiba, and operated by a Japanese corporation that handles the Disney licenses. Everyone is scanned for weapons on entrance by the companies own trained security team. The New VR BBS is at the corporate mainframe in central Tokyo. Tokyo Disney City is a 115-acre theme park at the Tokyo Disney Resort in Urayasu, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Its main gate is directly adjacent to both Maihama Station and Tokyo Disneyland Station. It was the first Disney park to be built outside the New United States, and it opened on 15 April 1983. In 2020, it was known as the prefect place for Yanks to enjoy All-American traditions and good inexpensive shopping. Disney City is also well known for their groundbreaking technology and out of this world security.

Infrastructure
Transportation
Tokyo, similar to the rest of Japan, has the world's most sufficient and advance metro network and bullet train system that runs through the city to the suburbs and to the rest of the country. The metros remain busy and crowded, this is due to the numbers of armed guards that the companies employ, the trains are very safe, and unruly passengers are often quickly dealt with. Other transportation options include busses, cars, motorcycles, and Aerodynes.

Tom's Diner is a restaurant located in Little China, in the Watson district of northern Night City.

Overview
Tom's Diner is a restaurant chain located in Night City, known for their retro, pre-Collapse vibes. Little China is home to the original diner.

Founded, owned and operated by Tom himself, it is usually open 24/7, and rarely closes. A giant neon burger sign that reads "Tom's Diner" is located on top of the small building, stylized after a long-lost type of food joint that almost no one remembers. Inside, above a checkerboard-like floor, there are booths and tables, as well as stools in front of the counter.

History
In 2076, this Tom's Diner was visited by fixer Faraday and Arasaka's Counter Intelligence operative Douglas. Sometime later, a Valentino techie Dalton Estevan-Luis, pursued by Arasaka agents, nearly crashed his Brennan Apollo near Tom's Diner. He then stole a car that belonged to two nomads that just visited the diner. The nomads were then killed by the agents chasing Dalton, which was heard inside, but nobody cared to investigate it.

In 2077, former Diverse Media Systems employee Arturo, edgerunner Al-Beta, NCPD officer Dinesh Kashyap and expert driver Rearview organized a heist at Tom's Diner. Later that same year, it was visited by mercenary V and Goro Takemura, former bodyguard of Saburo Arasaka.

Staff
*Tom - Owner and cook
*Sergio - Cook
*Unnamed cook

Associated Quests

*Fool on the Hill

Associated Shards

Notes
*The Chariot tarot card can be found right behind Tom's Diner.
*Tom's Diner is occasionally visited by NCPD officers, including MaxTac operators.
*The shard Nomad cookbook from 2034, located in the diner's kitchen, is visible but cannot be reached, as the kitchen is not accessible to the player.

Trivia

## Tomorrow Never Knows
Tomorrow Never Knows is a Side Job in .

Walkthrough
The quest triggers upon discovering one of the four Tarot Card murals in Dogtown.

*The King of Cups is found near the main entrance to Dogtown in the parking lot of northern Coastview.
*The King of Pentacles is found on a wall on the upper floors of the Kress Street Hideout building in Longshore Stacks.
*The King of Wands is found on the basketball court at the Tranquil Terrace in Luxor Heights.
*The King of Swords is found on an exterior wall on the northeastern side of The Moth building in Longshore Stacks.

While searching for the cards, V can talk to Misty Olszewski about any that they have found. Once all four have been collected, she can be consulted to give a reading.

## Toshiro Harada
- status：Deceased

引文：So... Ms. Cunningham. I wish for you to tell me all about the program you call... Soulkiller.（Toshiro）
citation

Toshiro Harada (Japanese: 原田敏郎) is an Arasaka executive who appears in the universe.

Biography
2013

Toshiro was in charge of the Arasaka regional office of Night City during its construction. During this time he found out about a brilliant netrunner named Alt Cunningham working for ITS who created a program known as Soulkiller. He organized a booster gang to kidnap Alt and bring her to the tower unharmed. Once Alt awoke in his office he greeted her with a drink and asked her about the program she developed. He considered her a valuable asset to helping him recreate her work in the Arasaka office mainframe. During this time Johnny Silverhand created a riot to assault the Arasaka Tower. Johnny, Rogue, Santiago, and Thompson entered into the building and fought through many Arasaka guards. Toshiro's bodyguard Akira fought them protecting him and Alt from interruptions. However he was killed and Johnny entered the room while Alt was connected to the mainframe. Toshiro warned Johnny not to proceed, but was shot and killed by him before disconnecting Alt killing her in the process.

2077
When V entered the Blackwall of the Net, they relived one of Johnny Silverhand's inaccurate memories of 2013, where Johnny, Rogue, Santiago and Thompson fought Akira, who was defending Toshiro. Once Akira was defeated, Silverhand confronted Toshiro over Alt's body and, after a brief conversation, ended his life by shooting him in the head.

Notes
*Toshiro was originally known as Toshiro Arasaka, presumably a member of the Arasaka family along with Kenji Arasaka. Possible reasoning was to potentially not kill off a member of the Arasaka family so quick in the lore.

## Totalimmortal
Totalimmortal is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough

After V liberates Hanako Arasaka from the Arasaka Estate, they travel alongside Anders Hellman and Goro Takemura (if he was saved during Search and Destroy).

Journal Entry
:Go to hell, V. You're on your own, got that? Stage is all yours. I'll just stand in the wings and watch you meet certain death, 'cause that's how this little coup against Yorinobu is gonna end. That is, unless our porcelain doll's got any aces up her sleeve. But if things go south, just jump out the window. Don't give them the satisfaction - don't let the fuckers take you alive.

:Well I'll be a corporat on a stick. Yorinobu tried to take out the entire Arasaka board in one fell swoop. I'd buy the gonk a beer if I could. No doubt, the sight of Arasakas lunging at each other's throat is a thing of beauty, but it kinda throws a wrench in our plans. Now you gotta take care of Yorinobu on Hanako's terms. Looks like Lil Sis is done playing around - crazy Big Bro's gonna give up Arasaka tower one way or the other. Still, isn't it weird that we're not allowed to hurt a hair on his pretty little head after he marked her for DEATH? Maybe Hanako wants to "neutralize" him herself? One thing's for sure - the path to Yorinobu's office leads through a lot of levels... and a LOT of bodies.

Objectives
*Exit the AV.
*Follow Hanako.
*Talk to Hanako.
*Follow Hanako.
*Enter the elevator.
*Follow Hanako.
*Talk to Hanako.
*Sit next to Hanako.
*Talk to Hanako.
*Talk to Hanako and Saburo.
*Follow Hanako.
*Give your testimony.
**Find a seat.
**Sit next to Hanako.
*Give your testimony.
*Fend off the attackers.
*Talk to Hanako.
*Take the elevator to the upper atrium.
*Reach the elevator.
*Defeat Yorinobu's forces.
*Head to Yorinobu's office.
*Defeat Adam Smasher.
**Decide Smasher's fate. [Optional]
*Confront Yorinobu.
*Talk to Hanako.
*Take the elevator down.

Notes

*The Access Token that can be looted from Adam Smasher will be retained after finishing the game and returning to the point-of-no-return. It unlocks Smasher's secret office on the DV Ebunike, where the crafting spec for the can be found.
*If V spared Sandayu Oda's life during Play It Safe, he will appear during this mission and help V and Hanako's soldiers fight Yorinobu's forces.
*V can ask Hanako to talk to Jackie Welles's engram when they visit Mikoshi to have a conversation with Saburo Arasaka's engram. This is only possible if Jackie's body was sent to Viktor Vektor (and then retrieved by the Arasaka Corporation) at the end of The Heist. Flipping Saburo Arasaka off in Johnny's name shortly before will cut the conversation short, preventing the option to talk to Jackie. It has no further effect on the mission.
*Not pushing the gun out of Yorinobu's reach towards the end of the mission has no consequences.

The Totentanz (German: Dance of death) is a club located in Northside, in the Watson district of northern Night City.

History
Early history
Totentanz was the name of a club on the top of Burleson Tower in the old City Center of Night City. It survived the AHQ Disaster of 2023, and during the Time of the Red was occupied by Maelstrom along the rest of Burleson Tower. Due to the poor state of the building, around 2045, then-Maelstrom leader Warlock tasked Flenser to find a new permanent home for gang and the club. After sending people to search, she found herself with a list of some places in the Watson Development, though she was preferably looking for another hotel. Eventually, this endeavor proved successful after finding an abandoned-under construction hotel. Maelstrom turned much the building as primary base of operations, and converted the upper floors into the new Totentanz club, becoming a significant source of the boostergang's income.

2070s

In 2076, David Martinez and his crew assaulted the building's lobby to rescue Isabella Morgan.

By 2077, the Totentanz was the most popular gang club and "drink and riot" venue in Night City, described as loud, dark and ultraviolent. Gang members from all walks frequented the club to party and listen to heavy rock and neo-death metal music blasting at deafening volumes. They were all welcomed at the club, so long as they obeyed Maelstrom's authority and customs. It was said that if a night at the Totentanz had a body count of less than a dozen, it was considered a boring evening. The band Tinnitus exclusively performed here.

Transmission is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough
After clearing the Grand Imperial Mall and returning to Batty's Hotel, Brigitte leads V to the Maglev Tunnel beneath the Pacifica Serenity Bible Church. This is a hideout of the Voodoo Boys and the physical location of their Data Fortress, Rezo Agwe. Brigitte exploits V and Johnny Silverhand to communicate with Alt Cunningham, who can help the Voodoo Boys' members go through the Blackwall.

In cyberspace, V experiences one of Johnny's inaccurate memories. In the memory, the player will control Johnny in the year 2013.

Never Fade Away

In 2013, Alt Cunningham was abducted by goons hired by Arasaka. Johnny tried to defeat the goons but got ambushed by one of the goons using Mantis Blades. Johnny was later saved and taken to a Ripperdoc called Milt Nauman by Lyle Thompson, a Media who initially planned to meet Alt at the same time.

Later, Johnny hired Rogue and Santiago to break into Arasaka Tower and save Alt together. Rogue was initially unwilling to get involved. However, in the middle of the meeting between Johnny and the two, Arasaka agents broke in the location. They succesfully escaped from the agents. After defeating the agents, Johnny finally got into his car, with Lyle driving. Rogue and Santiago took motorcycles. They went to a safe place and planned the strike. Johnny organized his fans to make a rebellion against Arasaka, and decided to call Nancy to report the rebellion, in order to distract Arasaka. Then Johnny, Rogue, Santiago, and Lyle struck into Arasaka Tower and approached the mainframe. They finally found Alt, who had been jacked in Soulkiller. Johnny unceremoniously killed Toshiro next to Alt, and subsequently unplugged Alt from the mainframe, denying her to return to her body. Much to Johnny's madness, he punched Lyle since Lyle was still recording for the news. Then Johnny had to admit that Alt was dead.

The Blackwall
After the playback, V is returned to cyberspace. V talks to Johnny about the memory, and then flashes back to Brigitte in cyberspace. Brigitte takes V and her Netrunners next to the Blackwall, and sends V to go through the Blackwall and talks to Alt Cunningham for taking the Voodoo Boys' members through the Blackwall.

:Because the shard given by the agent has removed Placide's malware in V but installed NetWatch's own tracker. Once the VDB's contact Alt, she realizes NetWatch is taking action and to stop them she flatlines the Voodoo Boys except for V.
:After V exits cyberspace, with Brigitte and her Netrunners' bodies lying on the chairs, the rest of the Voodoo Boys' members led by Placide are on alert. V must defeat Placide and the remaining Voodoo Boys' members to escape the church.

:With Alt's aid, the Voodoo Boy's Netrunners successfully go through the Blackwall.
:After V and Brigitte exit cyberspace, V confronts Brigitte, and Brigitte finally forces V to leave. V can go leave the church peacefully or choose to use violence.

Journal Entry
:It actually fucking worked. Working with the Voodoo Boys, Brigitte... It leads us straight to Alt. Looks like your troubles are over, kid. Fixing your head is gonna be a walk in the park for Alt, that I guarantee. You just do what Brigitte says for now - I'll handle the rest.

Objectives
*Follow Brigitte.
*Talk to Brigitte.
*Get in the ice bath.
*Wait for the connection.
*Talk to Brigitte.
*Investigate the source of the noises.
*Unblock Johnny's memories.
*Talk to Brigitte.
*Touch the Blackwall.
*Talk to Alt.
*Talk to Brigitte.
*Leave the chapel.

Notes
*The Never Fade Away job occurs during Transmission.
*If this job is completed by dealing with the Voodoo Boys with violence, their generic members who are normally found on the street will disappear and will no longer spawn outside of Dogtown.
*In-game, the place where Johnny and V converse with Alt is physically located in an area named Unknown, which is almost right under Batty's Hotel in Pacifica, some distance below the map. It is a cyberspace recreation of the square room in front of Saburo's office.
*Depending on how V deals with the Voodoo Boys here, extra dialogue and gameplay options will appear in the Phantom Liberty DLC mission The Damned.

Trivia
*The title of the job comes from the Joy Division song, Transmission.

The Tripple Xtreme Epic Workout Center (also known simply as the Tripple Extreme Gym) is located in Rancho Coronado, in the Santo Domingo district of southeastern Night City. During the Time of the Red, this facility was known as the SovOil Paint Factory.

History
2020s - 2040s
During the late 2020s, amidst the early days of Night City's reconstruction, SovOil built this latex paint factory in southern Heywood. Once it was up and running, the machinery began producing much of the necessary paint that was needed for the rebuilding process of the whole metropolis. Even after the establishment of the Heywood Industrial Zone, this factory kept on churning paint non-stop.

By the 2040s, promotional materials bragged that over fifty percent of the paint used on walls all over the city had been produced in this facility since 2030. What those promotions didn't tell, was that during that time it had also poured an astronomical amount of pollution. In addition, local residents short on money that were chasing a chemical high were known to hang around these installations, sucking in the fumes to grab a blast.

2050s - 2070s
At some point, the paint factory was occupied by the Animals gang, who transformed it into a gym. An enormous vat once used to mix chemicals together was repurposed as a pit where a gladiatorial bouts were held. By 2077, a notorious Animal member known as Logan Garcia owned the establishment.

Database Entry

Overview & Layout
In , the gym is guarded by Animals members, and an entry fee of 3800 eddies is required to enter through the gate, or by using intimidation with a Body attribute of 13 or higher. Optionally, a set of red shipping containers on the north side can grant access to a closed shutter that grants entry.

Rhino, who competes in the Beat on the Brat tournament, can also be found here. If she has been defeated, V will be friendly with the other Animals inside the gym.

Ground Floor
After gaining entry to the building, on the left there is a small storage room where an Access Point that requires 8 Intelligence, and computer terminal can be found, as well as an article shard. In the middle is a boxing pit, where the fight for Beat on the Brat: Arroyo will take place, as well as some training equipment, and a ladder that staircase to the 2nd floor office, alongside some lockers and another staircase that leads to a walkway. The walkway will remain off limits, even after completing the fight.

To the far right side of the gym, there is another Access Point which required 8 Intelligence.

In the back, there are several rooms that can be accessed. In the middle room, one can find the Animals Melee Weapon Vendor. This vendor is only friendly after completing the fight. A shard can be found inside a container here.

2nd Floor
On the second floor, a Access Point can be found that requires 8 Intelligence, next to a ladder leading to the roof. An infirmary and bathroom can also be found on this level, that are connected to Logan Garcia's office, which is guarded by a Ogre. An alternative exit from the gym can be found here, behind a door that is restricted to level 8 Technical Ability, that leads to the back entrance.

Associated Shards
*Message (Rancho Coronado) - can be found on an Animals Raptor.
*Archived Conversation: Monica and Logan - can be found on Logan Garcia.

The Kappa (河童) is a Smart Pistol manufactured by Tsunami in . It was added in Patch 1.6 as part of the New Weapons: Firearms DLC.

Characteristics

The Kappa is a fully automatic, close combat Smart weapon with a 30-round magazine designed to compete against market leaders Kang Tao and Arasaka. The weapon's primary selling feature is that it is able to locate and fire at two targets simultaneously. Due to its expense, the Kappa is rarely found in the hands of enemies or on the streets. The weapon is powered by artificial intelligence, which does little to disprove the rumors of Tsunami's adoption of the "Muramasa" AI many decades prior.

Due to the addition of the Smart targeting system, it is not possible to install a Scope and Muzzle attachment.

Database Entry

- transcript：Ready to change the landscape of smarty weaponry, Tsunami Defense Systems crashed onto the scene with a force worthy of a, well... you know. But to compete with top competitors Arasaka and Kang Tao, you need a cutting-edge product. This is why Tsunami has poured tremendous resources into the AI-powered processors they use in their Kappa handgun. Tsunami's latest software update has brought Kappa to the forefront of the smartgun debate. Add to that their strong reputation for quality craftsmanship, and you get a weapon that has raised eyebrows throughout the market – even if it hasn't dethroned the industry leaders just yet.

A single round to the head whilst attacking from stealth, particularly with a suppressor attached, is often enough to eliminate an enemy and maintain one's cover from enemy awareness.

The Nue (Japanese: 鵺) is a Power Pistol manufactured by Tsunami in .

Characteristics
The Nue is a semi-automatic pistol which fires heavy .45 caliber ammunition. The grip is fitted with rubber for a more ergonomic feel. The weapon comes equipped with a magazine indicator, showing the user if the weapon is loaded or empty. Iron sights are manufactured to allow optimal targeting in dark environments, and an LED indicator allows the user to know when a bullet is chambered.

The Nue is Tsunami's foray into the mass market and has been a driving force in the company's profits. It continues to be heralded as the highest quality pistol one can buy. It is seldom seen in the hands of enemies outside of the Valentino gangoons who repurpose and decorate their pistols as they do their most prized vehicles and clothing, saying much for the value of the Tsunami Nue as a quality side arm.

It is possible to install a Short Scope and a Muzzle attachment.

Database Entry

- transcript：Tsunami Defense Systems is known best for its elite and dizzyingly expensive sniper rifles, but more of the Japanese company's products are beginning to gain traction on Night City's streets. Take their flagship pistol, the Nue, for example. Unlike the Ashura or Nekomata, the Nue's design is not founded on any bleeding-edge technologies. But what it lacks in innovation, it makes up for in worksmanship. Elegant, reliable and deadly, the Nue is the unchallenged leader of the pistol market. The only debatable flaw is a size that can prove difficult to conceal. Still... Who would ever want to hide such a masterpiece?

Tucker Albach is a Corpo and Kiroshi Optics employee in .

Biography
Albach lives in an apartment on the corner of Scoffield and Sinkyone Street in The Glen, Heywood. She was formerly the Vice Managing Director of the Kiroshi Optics corporation.

At some point in 2077, while intoxicated, Albach hit a young girl named Rosita Fuscino with her car, severely wounding her. With no witnesses on the empty street and the collision occurring late at night, she kept on driving, leaving Rosita to slowly die of her injuries which otherwise could have been prevented had she received medical attention in time. With the help of CCTV footage, the NCPD was able to discover that Albach was the person responsible, but were unable to convict her due to Albach's corporate insurance covering vehicular manslaughter.

Her employer, Jacob Lan, CEO of Kiroshi Optics, learned of the incident, and in response had her removed from the board, which in turn removed her access to her emergency response security plan, ended her Trauma Team coverage, and also evicted her from her corporate apartment—not because she killed a young girl, but because she had valuable company documents in her vehicle at the time that could have been stolen. Despite the potential catastrophe that her blunder could have caused, Lan allowed her to remain within the company, albeit in a lesser position. One of Albach's co-workers, Hunter McPherson, later e-mailed her to taunt her that, after years of her abuse and mistreatment, he now had her seat on the board.

Marlon Fuscino, Rosita's father, contacted Padre to contract an assassin to eliminate Albach for her crime, paying whomever would be ready to pull the trigger on Albach.

:Tucker Albach will be remembered with a plaque at the Columbarium in North Oak. Her plaque reads: "She cruised through life like a battleship and never swerved from her path."

:Tucker Albach will live, and V is free to take the contents of the safe. Padre will reprimand V, stating that he will have to falsify a story for Rosita's father, but will consider the contract closed due to Tucker agreeing to go somewhere far away and never return.

V can also simply deceive Tucker by agreeing to her bribe. She will stand down her security detail and allow access to the safe and locked rooms within the building. V is then free to simply execute her or incapacitate her and carry her down to Padre's waiting driver, although any guards who witness V carrying Tucker will become hostile once again.

Associated Quests
*Gig: Eye for an Eye

Associated Shards

- type：Conapt

Tucker Albach's Apartment is located in the Glen, in the Heywood district of central Night City.

Overview
Tucker Albach's a conapt located on the corner of Scoffield and Sinkyone Street in The Glen. It is property of the Kiroshi corporation, Albach's employer, though she briefly lost access to the apartment after she was discovered to have hit and killed a girl in her car while intoxicated. Nevertheless, she was given a second chance by the Kiroshi CEO, Jacob Lan, and is currently having the property renovated.

Layout
There are three floors to the apartment and four access points. The first two access points are located on the ground floor, at the front and back door of the property. The front door is guarded and the back door requires a level 15 Technical Ability to be opened. The first floor is under renovation, and there are several construction workers present. The second floor comprises an office space and Albach's bedroom and en-suite, which can be accessed by forcing the door open, hacking it, or by being granted access after allowing Albach to live. Inside the bedroom is another safe and Albach's computer. On the second floor is another access point, which is through a window that can be hacked open. The player can then double-jump through the window before it automatically closes. Finally, on the third floor is the kitchen and living area, as well as Albach's office, where she is located. The player may be able to jump through the window to Albach's office, though this is difficult due to its height. This option, however, avoids conflict with the construction workers or Albach's guards.

Associated Quests
*Gig: Eye for an Eye

## Tune Up
Tune Up is a Side Job in .

Walkthrough
After V's car is wrecked by the divergent Delamain Cab, V is contacted by Delamain to visit Delamain Corp's headquarters on Pajaro street in Vista del Rey, Heywood, to assess the damages done to V's vehicle and receive compensation.

When V arrives at the location and enters the building, it is evident that they are not the only one that was attacked by a rogue cab, as numerous other Night citizens are there to file a complaint against the company. As V cuts in line and talks to the receptionist—which is currently running on a subroutine of Delamain's core. After V's identity is confirmed, Delamain himself will take over and talk to V and apologizes to them, and explains to V that they are currently occupied dealing with an internal crisis. As compensation for their damaged car, Delamain transfers V a sum of 4900 eurodollars.

Journal Entry
:Fender benders are a dime a dozen in Night City. A Delamain though? A first, I'm guessing. But now he wants to hand out compensation for damages? That's just downright suspect. Way I see it, he's got a the AI equivalent of a gun pointed at his head, and this message is nothing but a coded cry for help. Nobody, and I mean nobody, doles out compensation for a little chipped paintwork. Go and see what this is about - worst case you come out a little richer.
