引文：Demand's always high. Was just a matter of tweaking the supply, if you get my drift.（Mr. Hands）

Wade Bleecker, better known as Mr. Hands, is a fixer covering business in the areas of Pacifica in Night City.

Biography
Early life
Wade Bleecker worked as a well-known high ranking corporate at Petrochem. He was very successful in his career until a sudden shake-up in upper management, in which Bleecker was chosen to be sacrificed for the corporation. He managed to survive the assassination attempt, but after a bounty was put on his head, Wade was forced to disappear.

Wade eventually changed his face and name as he became to be known as Mr. Hands, the only prominent fixer in Pacifica. His reputation grew as Night City's most secretive fixer, with no known base of operations or any idea of what he actually looked like; the only image of him people would see were his hands over holocalls. The only way any mercenary could get through to him was over a call, never meeting in person; this is how he preferred to do business, with little interaction with anyone.

2077
In 2077, Mr. Hands temporarily relocated to the Heavy Hearts club in Dogtown.

At some point that same year, Mr. Hands was contacted by a merc named V who had been looking for information on how to meet with the Voodoo Boys. He explained that they'd have to go through Maman Brigitte, however, that it was nearly impossible to meet with them. After a short discussion, Mr. Hands promised he would try to arrange some contacts to get V what they wanted. A few days after, he had some progress with the Voodoo Boys, who could use a merc to infiltrate the Grand Imperial Mall. Hands soon called V to tell them the news and that they'd have to meet with someone first before seeing Maman Brigitte.

Phantom Liberty

Mr. Hands found out about V's infiltration into Dogtown, promptly calling the merc to state his surprise as how they had snuck their way into the combat zone. Considering the new opportunities presented, Hands welcomed V into the district with a few gifts. First, Mr. Hands registered the merc so they could freely access and leave Dogtown at will via the western gate. He also rewarded them with a Makigai Tanishi T400 to travel around the walled-off district, as well as giving them access to a few new gigs. V eventually met the fixer in person, something not many had had the chance to achieve. He opened up about his shadow politics-minded ambitions about Dogtown and the rest of Pacifica.

Mr. Hands attended Kurt Hansen's party at the Black Sapphire.

After Kurt's death, Hands took the opportunity to install an unaware puppet — Chester Bennett — as the new leader of Dogtown. He hired V to make sure this succeeded, and depending on the merc's actions, it could be either dutifully executed or (potentially accidentally) thwarted, with Jago Szabó becoming colonel. If the latter happened, although Mr. Hands was infuriated at first by losing his puppet's position, Jago proved to be a better ally than he initially thought.

引文：And do you know what a fixer does? Allow me to explain. Not only do I finalize transactions. I can accomplish the goddamn impossible. [...] Makin' sure the buyer, supplier, and ever-neglected intermediary not only keep their heads in their games but keep their heads. Period. So don't you ever ask me who, with whom, where, when, why or how.（Wakako Okada to V during Disasterpiece）

Wakako Okada (Japanese: 岡田 和歌子) is the top fixer of the Westbrook district of Night City. She can be found at her own office in Japantown.

Biography
Early life - 2030s
Wakako Okada was born in the Kansai region of Japan. At some point later, she travelled to Night City where she pursued medicine at the Night City University. It was here where she would meet her first husband, Hiroto Miyamoto.

Shortly after graduating, the Fourth Corporate War occurred. Both Hiroto and she survived. Afterwards, Wakako found herself working for Kiroshi as a medtech. Wakako balanced her work with her family life, including helping her husband's childhood friend, Hayato Nakagawa. When the romantic relationship between Ryoko Fujiwara and Hayato was called off by the formers family, Wakako and her husband acted as liaisons for the two lovers.

2040s - 2075
In 2042, after the death of Hayato's adoptive father Shinobu Nakagawa, Hayato, as a high-ranking member of the Tyger Claws, became embroiled in a dispute over his father's inheritance, thus, his enemies saw fit to target his friends. Wakako and Hiroto were attacked, with her being the only one who survived. Afterwards, Hayato Nakagawa became the leader of the Tyger Claws, and began to provide for Wakako in Hiroto's stead, making her a member of the Claws whether she liked it or not. Ever since, Wakako became a confidant and close friend of Ryoko Fujiwara, Hayato's wife and chairwoman of the Nakagawa Foundation.

By 2045, Ryoko wanted Wakako to quit her job at Kiroshi and come work for the Foundation full-time as her right hand, but Wakako always declined her offers.

At an unspecified time, Wakako became a fixer. She rose to become a very well known fixer in Night City, gaining the nickname of "lady of Westbrook estate." Wakako was the one that helped both Pilar and Rebecca get into the mercenary world.

At some point in her life, Wakako lost her grandchild to Arasaka, and has since disdained the corporation.

2076 - 2077
In 2076, Wakako gave a gig to David Martinez and his mercenary crew. The mission was to infiltrate Totentanz and rescue Isabella Morgan from Maelstrom. At her request, a very young merc called Julio joined them. Although the job was a success, Julio got himself killed after activating an explosive trap.

By 2077, Wakako operated out of a pachinko parlor in Jig-Jig Street, Japantown. She had had five husbands over her long life, outliving them all, as well as nine sons who were all high-ranking members of the Tyger Claws, but she kept them strictly in line to ensure that they were never the target of a gig picked up by another fixer. Despite her close ties to the gang, she took a coldly pragmatic view when its members were assassinated by mercenaries, believing that only the stupid and greedy would fall to such an ignominious fate. Wakako was well respected, or feared at the very least, by the community. Her gigs were from all types, including simple robberies or assassinations.

## Wardrobe
The Wardrobe is a gameplay feature in , which was introduced in Patch 1.6 with the Transmog Customization DLC.

Description
:Wardrobe allows you to change the appearance of your outfit without changing your armor stats. You can create up to 6 outfits using the pieces of clothing you own by accessing the wardrobe in any of V's apartments and safehouses and then switch between them in the Inventory panel.

Unlocking Appearances
The Wardrobe will be available as soon as you return to your apartment during The Rescue. New Clothing appearances for the wardrobe are automatically unlocked after obtaining them. The clothing can afterwards safely be sold for eurodollars or dismantled into item components. However, some clothing is excluded from the Wardrobe and cannot be unlocked.

Exclusions
*All special outfits, excluding the Roach Whisperer outfit.
*Clothing obtained during the Epilogues does not carry over to the Point of no Return.

## Washington, D.C.
- motto："Justitia Omnibus"
- aka：DC, Washington, District of Columbia, The Capital
- type：Capital City
- country：USA
- region：Appalachia
- population：702,455
- security_provider：NorthEast Combined Operations Group
- appears_books：

Washington, D.C., is the capital of the New United States.

Overview
Washington, D.C. is a compact city on the Potomac River, bordering the states of Maryland and Virginia. Its architecture is defined by imposing neoclassical monuments and buildings.

While the city controlled the politics of the United States before The Collapse, by 2020 it had become essentially one big military base, with visiting tour groups having to be escorted by armed soldiers. Located within the larger DC Metro Area are the headquarters of the corporate giant Militech as well as the FIA, the successor to the CIA of the 20th century, in Langley, Virginia.

History
In the early 2000s, DC was the site of a series of conflicts between the US Military and the Gang of Four. In 2008, these Gang finally came to an end when the surrounding states blockaded the city and the military finally attacked the Gang directly, but not before a series of states seceded in the chaos, becoming the first of the Free States.

By 2020, the capital city had been totally militarized. The office of the mayor was replaced by a Military Governor, and the Military Police patrol the streets. The city still retained some amount of tourism to the monuments and museums and such, but they were always under the Military Police's watchful eye.

The city continued to be the seat of the Federal Government, but, despite having been rebuilt by the Nomads,, it was a shell of its former self. While it struggled to maintain the current US and attempted to regain the power that it once held, the Free States, and corporate powers at hand, as well a failing country the old government had little success in regaining the power it once held.

By 2077, under the administration of NUSA President Rosalind Myers, a monument under construction to commemorate the tricentennial of the United States in the city was damaged by a freak storm.

Transit
In 2020, DC was served my a fleet of dirigibles, which would fly the wealthy to major cities all across the country.

The city was also the Eastern terminus of the TransCon Maglev, a bullet train that crossed through several major cities before ending out West in Night City. There had been plans for it to be extended further East to Boston and NYC, but the Fourth Corporate War put a stop to that, and for many years ended the Maglev's service.

## Watson (2077)
- type：District
- city：Night City
- appears_books：

引文：Watson used to have it all. Nightclubs, skyscrapers, corporate offices, a top-end med center — but economic disaster put an end to all that. Now, it's known as 'the bad neighborhood of Night City.' The kinda place that suits gangs like Maelstrom and Tyger Claws down to the ground.

Watson is one of the major districts of Night City, located in the northern portion of the metropolis.

Overview

In 2077, Watson is seen as a sad and desperate place. It is well known as one of Night City's poorest districts, with many industrial factories and plants being completely abandoned. Watson is also the battleground in the war between Maelstrom and Tyger Claws gangs. The former reigns over the Northside Industrial District (NID), which consists of derelict factories and working-class apartment blocks. The well-known Totentanz bar is also located here.

Tyger Claws operate from Little China and Kabuki. The former is a high density urban region with skyscrapers, and overpopulated with Asian immigrants. It was once the best place in all of Night City to legally spend some money on body enhancements, but has since been overrun by the Kabuki marketplaces. The old Med Center is located in this area, and so is the notorious Afterlife.

Kabuki is a maze of narrow alleyways located right next to Little China. At night, they turn into a bazaar for implants, organs, steroids, and much more. It is said anything a person could desire can be found in the Kabuki Market. This makes Watson a prime target for Scavs, a ruthless group that kidnaps and harvests peoples' organs and implants for resale on the black market.

The rest of Watson belongs to Arasaka in an area known as the Arasaka Waterfront. This place is completely off-limits to anyone who isn't an employee of the corporation. The NCPD cautions everyone that decides to visit the Watson sub-districts to be cautious.

History
Early history - 2050s
During the Fourth Corporate War, much of the local population of this area fled, leaving it open for the many refuges from the devastated districts of Night City to the south. A conglomerate of Japanese-based corporations known as the Night City Co-Prosperity Sphere (NCCS) helped the communities of the wrecked Japantown and Littla China to move here.

In the following years, the NCCS invested in this area, spending a lot of money in old and new infrastructures, and renaming the growing district as the Watson Development. With the NCCS patronage, the displaced Japanese population settled in a new neighborhood colloquially known as Kabuki. For a period of time, Watson was a thriving district, set to become an extension of the downtown area to the south, as well as the new beating heart of Night City. Thanks to the Co-Prosperity Sphere, the first residential megabuildings begun to be raised here; they were not the first on the list, but thanks to the NCCS money they jumped the queue. People visited Watson for the various bustling nightclubs, skyscrapers, corporate offices, a top-end medical center, and some of the best markets in the whole city. Alongside a renewed industrial sector to the north known as the NID, the NCCS continued to pour in billions of eurodollars with the intent to make it self-sufficient and prosperous, and having a remarkable success in the process. The south, the arrival of more and more immigrants from China and other parts of Asia, alongside the local population that had moved here after the war, made this portion of Watson be known as the new Little China.

By the 2050s, the renewal effort to reclaim the downtown areas to the south finally began to succeed, changing Watson's role from a city nucleus to a supporting periphery once again. Despite this, Watson continued to be notorious.

2060s - 2070s
During the construction boom of the 2060s, other parts of the metropolis like City Center and Westbrook started to become the new hubs of money and power, housing many wealthy and influential residents. As such, the affluent citizens of Watson begun to migrate to the newer and shiner areas of Night City.

Unfortunately for the NCCS, after the Unification War, the Arasaka Corporation returned to Night City in 2070, seeking to cement its influence over the metropolis. In search of a large port access for their company, Arasaka aimed to take control of the Watson waterfront, putting them in odds with the NCCS, who controlled much of the northern district. The conglomerate competed against the giant Japanese megacorporation over Watson, but ultimately Arasaka bled them dry, alongside many of the local corporations, changing the district forever. With the Co-Prosperity Sphere crumbling, its members moved on, and without a stable financial sector, the glory days of Watson ended. Many of the remaining affluent residents moved out, while the NID, once a cutting edge technological park, could no longer provide jobs, leaving people out on the street. Arasaka took advantage of the economic vacuum by taking over the district for its gain, finally getting the port and access to the waterfront that they had always wanted.

Despite this loss of power and influence, Watson managed to find a new purpose. The enterprising and underprivileged flocked in, sweeping aside the dust and transforming the district into a new hive of activity, becoming a very rich yet dangerous environment. Most of the original Japanese population in Kabuki moved to the nearby Japantown, while the neighboring Chinese citizens flocked in. Despite losing all of its original affluence, Kabuki gained new fame by becoming Night City's main black market bazaar (second only to Dogtown), with the Kabuki Market becoming its most notorious feature. On the other hand, Little China became overpopulated by a plethora of different foreign cultures, with most of its threads weaving in from Chinese influence, and having some of the best cuisines in all of Night City. However, the NID never managed to recover, being mostly abandoned by the rest of the city, though a number of factories and other establishments kept functioning. This area also became home to many different types of dangerous gangs and other criminal organizations, with Maelstrom being on top of the chain, reigning from an abandoned hotel which contained the infamous Totentanz club. The Tyger Claws still maintained a notorious presence in the southern and central portions of Watson, though most of their businesses were located in Japantown.

By 2076, Watson was a very diverse district, yet it was considered one of the poorest and dangerous areas of Night City, often looked down upon by the citizens of the wealthiest neighborhoods. Due to a large rat plague in the district, the Night City Environmental Task Force had been using stray cats to address this problem, causing many of these feline animals to populate its streets.

Around April–May of 2077, the whole district was closed-off due to the arrival of Saburo Arasaka, who would soon be murdered in the notorious Konpeki Plaza hotel on the western side of Watson.

Database Entry

Sub-districts

*Arasaka Waterfront
*Kabuki
*Little China
*Northside

Behind the Scenes

引文：Watson was once a thriving part of Night City. It was home to corporate offices, nightclubs, a top-end medcenter, and a prosperous industrial sub-district that provided employment for its residents. Then economic and natural disasters hit, power and wealth moved Downtown and Watson was left to rot on the periphery, a virtual colony of the corporate core of Night City. That tumultuous history has left its visual markers in the styles we see in Watson today. A wall of austere skyscrapers fronts the canal separating Watson from City Center, like a Neomilitarist screen built to block the corporations' view of the grime they left behind. This verticality continues through Little China, then gradually gives way to the low, ramshackle Kitsch of Kabuki, before ending in the sweeping horizontal Entropism of the Northside Industrial District and the austere, fortified Neomilitarism of the Arasaka Waterfront. In the midst of it all, we have Watson's inhabitants, squeezed between the brutality of the corporations on the one hand and of the gangs on the other. For all their impoverished surroundings and bleak lives, they imbue the district with undeniable color and energy.

We Gotta Live Together is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough
The different Aldecaldos V must talk with to complete the optional objective "Talk to the nomads" are:
*Dakota Smith (having a free weapons give-away in the center of the camp)
*Saul Bright (in front of the terminal truck)
*Bob Sagan, Carol Emeka and Teddy Simos (sitting at a table towards the west end of the camp)
**After ending the conversation and getting up, stay and wait for the three to finish talking among them, or it will not be counted towards the objective.
*Cassidy Righter (shooting at empty bottles at the southeast end of the camp)
**V can join Cassidy's target practice; hitting 12 or more bottles prompts him to offer V his revolver, . It is advisable to crouch and aim before Cassidy gives the go.
*If their respective missions were successfully completed, additional characters can be found around the camp and need to be talked to for the optional objective (other than Jake, their respective dialogs are the same as before this mission):
**Jake Scooter from Fortunate Son (playing guitar on a couch by the large camp fire; see also Trivia)
**Benedict McAdams from Gig: MIA (leaning by the stairs up the food truck)
**Bruce Welby from Gig: Goodbye, Night City (sitting on a chair outside the weapon's dealer tent)
**Anna Hamill from Gig: Woman of La Mancha (leaning by the water truck at the western edge of the camp only if V is a Nomad and convinced her to join a clan)
*On top of that, several unnamed Aldecaldos deliver unique wild lines when approached, but do not count towards the mission objective.

Journal Entry
:I was gonna say that this time you'd have to go it alone, but it looks like the Aldecaldos've got some fight in them after all. Wonder what you see in them: a partner? Friend? Family? Something tells me sooner or later you're gonna have to choose one of the above, especially if it's thanks to them you get into Mikoshi.

Objectives
*Follow Mitch
*Talk to Saul
*(Optional) Talk to Mitch
*Talk to Dakota
*Get in the tub
*Talk to Saul
*(Optional) Talk to the nomads
*(Optional) Talk to Mitch
*Talk to Panam
*Join Panam when you're ready

Trivia
*If the mission Fortunate Son was successfully completed, Jake Scooter will sit by the fire. V can ask what Jake is playing, who will then perform a unique acoustic guitar take on the music played during Pyramid Song, the final mission of Judy Álvarez' story arc. That song in turn is a loose play on that mission's namesake, the Radiohead song Pyramid Song. Jake's song cannot be heard anywhere in the game but at this instance. For the lyrics, see Jake Scooter.
*The title of the job comes from the Jimi Hendrix song We Gotta Live Together.

- caption：During the Unification War, Militech soldiers feared little more than the chance their weapons might jam in the heat of battle.

Weapon Glitch is an Control Quickhack in .

Overview
A control quickhack that causes the enemy's weapon to jam, rendering it unusable for 14 seconds.

Weapon Glitch also causes a weapon malfunction, reducing enemy accuracy and disabling Smart-targeting systems and Tech-weapon penetration.

The variant causes locking onto an affected enemy with a Smart weapon to extend Weapon Glitch's duration until the target-lock is released.

The variant replaces the ability to jam an enemy's weapon, but instead detonates their primary weapon, forcing them to switch to their secondary weapon which will be affected by the quickhack's core effects.

The variant grants 6% Crit Chance with Smart Weapons upon successful uploads of Weapon Glitch. This effect can stack up to 5 times for a total bonus of 30% Crit Chance.

The variant doubles the Crit Chance bonus from the variant to 12%, for a total of 60% Crit Chance at 5 stacks.

Acquisition
*All variants can be obtained through Breach Protocol.
*Quickhack and Crafting Spec can be purchased from Netrunners.

## Weapon Vendor (The Glen)
- affiliation：Civilian
- status：Alive
- home：The Glen, Heywood
- gender：Male
- role：Weapon Vendor
- voiced_by：James Goode

Weapon Vendor (The Glen) is a Weapon Vendor in .

Overview
This weapon vendor can be found in the 2nd Amendment at Coyoacan, The Glen, Heywood.

He dislikes being relatively close from the NCPD precinct and City Hall, as there are a lot of squad cars with blaring sirens during the day and during the night they use force to make the homeless go away.

He recommends the DR12 Quasar, an electromagnetic gun, because it's lightweight, compact, quiet and lethal. He also recommends the Crusher for its timeless design and functionality, though it has high recoil. Lastly, he recommends the G-58 Dian for its ease of use as its lock-on system allows the user to fire without having to actively look at their target.

## Welcome Home: Corpo Plaza
Welcome Home: Corpo Plaza is a apartment quest in . It was added in Patch 1.5 as part of the V's New Apartments DLC.

Walkthrough
After talking with Takemura at Tom's Diner on Urmland Street, you receive a text message from El Capitán that his chooms Bob and Emma from EZEstates have some new digs for you to check out on their website.

After checking out the new EZEstates website in your current apartment, you see that there are four new apartments that you are able to rent. For the Corpo Plaza Apartment you just need to put down 110,000 eddies through an online transfer or visit the apartment in person to acquire access.

The apartment can be found in a hotel on Republic Way, next to Empathy in Corpo Plaza, City Center.

Journal Entry
:An exceptionally stylish luxury home nestled in the very heart of Night City. This exclusive suite offers an expansive, breathtaking view and a high-quality neomilitarist interior guaranteed to satisfy even the most demanding tastes.
:Here at EZEstates, we know image is imperative. So make your home here today... and make all your rivals at the corp drop dead! With jealousy!
:Emma, EZEstates

Objectives
*Rent the Corpo Plaza apartment: (€$110,000, one-time fee)
*Go to the Corpo Plaza apartment.

## Weldon Holt
- aka：Rhyne's Bulldog
- status：Alive
- home：Night City

Weldon Holt, nicknamed "Rhyne's Bulldog", is the acting mayor of Night City in .

Biography

Weldon Holt served as Deputy Mayor under Mayor Lucius Rhyne. In 2077 both him and the mayor met with Arasaka representatives at Konpeki Plaza, in which they discussed the lockdown of Watson.

After Lucius Rhyne’s death, Holt took on the role of acting mayor and announced that he would run for the mayor's office against Councilman Jefferson Peralez in Rhyne's stead. Commentators and Holt himself observed that he shared many of Rhyne's corporation-friendly political stances and would be more or less a continuation of Rhyne's administration.

Secretly, Holt was aware of the true nature of Rhyne's death: a virus-spiked braindance had killed the late mayor while he was visiting the invitation-only sex club Red Queen's Race. The staff of the club messaged Holt when they found Rhyne dead in his private room, and Holt sent Detective Harold Han to secure the corpse and cover up the incident to preserve Rhyne's reputation, which would prevent any blowback from affecting Holt's own ambitions. He then hired the Animals to wreck the club, but failed to pay them in a timely fashion, causing them to linger at the club long enough for V, who had been hired by Peralez to look into Rhyne's demise, to arrive and uncover evidence of Holt's involvement in the cover up.

According to media Max Jones, Holt was in Arasaka's pocket. Some of Holt's associates also spoke of him receiving permission for some of his campaign tactics from "those above him." During the campaign, when Holt and Peralez were polling neck and neck, an associate of Holt asked a 6th Street member they knew, Julia Bonet, to approach Ivan Vassiliev, the pro-Peralez president of Rancho Coronado Workers United, in order to destroy his reputation and prevent him from whipping his thousands of union members to vote for Peralez. Holt's dirty tricks did not dampen Peralez's support, and he started trailing in the polls as election day neared.

In the end, Holt lost the election and Peralez became the next mayor of Night City.

## Wellsprings
- type：Sub-district
- city：Night City
- district：Heywood
- gangs：See Gangs
- appears_books：

Wellsprings is one of the sub-districts of Heywood, located in central Night City.

Overview
During the 2070s, Heywood was considered a district of contrasts, and none exemplified this more than Wellsprings, a sub-district occupying Heywood's western neighborhoods. This was a relatively safe area, at least on the sides bordering with City Center. Buildings in the northern parts of the sub-district were newer and modern, erected late in the rebuilding of Night City during the 2060s. These neighborhoods also provided reasonable safe housing for the small middle class of Night City, and were full of working stiffs and underpaid corporate employees. The waterfront (especially the middle and northern parts) was well-adapted for tourists, and boasted a broad variety of shops and other establishments, such as bougie boutiques and seafood restaurants. The Bulwark shopping mall was a popular destination for these reasons. Here there were tasteful apartments offering residents amazing views of Del Coronado Bay, while luxury yachts granted their lucky owners the chance for a more intimate embrace of the sea in the harbors. Due to the large variety of vessels navigating in these waters, this place was a fantastic observation spot for nautical nuts. Residents could also enjoy casual strolls in these low-pressure areas, as well in other secure and beautiful parts of the sub-district.

Further to the south, the structures started to become smaller and older. Apartments here ranged from mid-tier to cheap, though Wellsprings managed to keep an overall aura of class. Most of the buildings here were built in the second phase of reconstruction during the 2040s and early 2050s, with old shabby buildings dating back to when Heywood was still called South Night City. This was a part of the city where the average citizen lived.

Heading inland, the impressionist watercolors of coastal Heywood gave way to a gritter realism brand of beauty. In the eastern parts of Wellsprings, tourists could find service stations on every corner, and were also able to delight in some of the best Mexican cuisines Night City had to offer, including many taco carts. However, the far edges of the district also included shanty houses and similar businesses, evoking memories from the rebuilding period. The Valentinos presence in the eastern and southern parts of Wellsprings was obvious due to the many graffiti and members walking around. Although they were not much of a menace to the locals, as that group usually simply minded its own business. Rumors stated the Valentinos worked on their smuggling operations, but during the day you would never notice it. Other gangs in the southern portions included the Animals and the lone, yet dangerous Scavenger cells. It was advised not to walk these streets at night.

Behind the Scenes

引文：Wellsprings' coastal strip is the safest, densest and loudest part of Heywood. This can be thought of as Night City's Venice Beach, a place to be seen for celebrities and the chance to see them for nobodies, where you can dine on cheap scop hot dogs or ridiculously expensive organic seafood. It is chock-full of Kitsch: oversized mascots, over-the-top slogans, anything that will grab your attention. The architecture is laid back, not so much decaying as casual, with the washed-out vibe of a beach town. At the same time, plenty of wealth is on display, be it in the luxury yachts anchored off the promenade or the spacious condos in its high-rise apartment buildings. Head east and things transition fast. Suddenly, you're surrounded by Night City's rarest creature: the middle class. The apartment buildings are of moderate height and adequately nice. There are movie theaters, gas stations, drive-through espresso joints. If it weren't for the AVs and implants, you'd swear you're in a gentrifying early-twenty-first century American city. Keep going, though, and you'll remember where you really are. Wellsprings' east is as rife with unemployment, shanties and gang activity as any of Night City's other impoverished districts.

## Wellsprings Water Treatment Plant
- caption：2077
- aka：See Notes
- type：Water treatment facility

- district：South Night City (2020)

Wellsprings (2077)
- street：Russell St.
- appears_books：

The Wellsprings Water Treatment Plant is located in Wellsprings, in the Heywood district in central Night City.

History
Early history - 2030s
The Municipal Sewage Treatment Plant of Night City was established on the southwestern coast of the South City District, a facility where most of the metropolis' sewage and waste processing went on. Around 2020, the plant was operated by corrupt city officials through a system of cronyism, and it was well-known for its regular sewage backfills and toxic emergencies.

Shortly after the Fourth Corporate War, nomads from the Thelas Nation took over the maritime operations at the Port of Night City, with none being the wiser as they started to rebuild its facilities and cargo started to flow in once again. During the completion of the port's initial infrastructure, the Thelas discovered that the nearby water reclamation tanks at the treatment plant were on the verge of failing due to damage sustained during the war. This, in turn, was causing the city's sewage system to not properly pour into the tanks half of the times, instead dumping much of the wastewater directly into the sea, not too far away from the port quays. Rather than wasting time trying to convince the Night City Council, the Thelas proceded to rebuild the entire system themselves, without the approval of the authorities. Once finished, the reburnished plant began to properly treat the sewage before returning purified water to the city's supply.

At some point, the local Department of Water moved much of their operations to this facility, starting to closely work with the Thelas at the same time. From here, the city officials maintained the rest of the water infrastructure, as the system elsewhere in the metropolis was particularly vulnerable to the hazards of modern life and was in constant repair.

2040s - 2070s
By the 2040s, the Reclamation Plant was functioning as well as it was possible, with experienced Thelas technicians supervising the workers. These individuals were tasked with filtering solids from the sewage and use chemicals to treat the remainder before pumping the potable water back into Night City's supply system. The solid waste was then processed and sold to other parties, primarily Biotechnica, who likely used it as fertilizer for their reference forests. While the Thelas kept the water clean, the government department frequently sent out trucks with personnel employed in installing and repairing the plumbing and sewer systems across the metropolis.

Early in 2045, the treatment plant was overflowed by a sudden outflow of Continental Brands industrial microbiota, something that eventually pushed out a flow of untreated waste into the city's storm drains. The water department then advised residents to avoid areas of standing, brackish water until the city officials could trace the flow and clean up the residue.

By 2076, the water treatment facility in southwestern Wellsprings was not functioning anymore, though its surroundings were occasionally used as an illicit meeting place. Nevertheless, the infrastructure's exterior remained in good condition, with its sizable parking lot used frequently by the nearby businesses. By 2077, the surrounding space had piles of rubbish and other trash.

Cyberpunk 2077
The parking lot is visited during I Fought the Law in . The lot was also where the Chevillon Thrax 388 Jefferson could originally be purchased once offered for sale by Sebastian Ibarra. The can be found in a shack behind the building, on the shoreline.

Notes
*Other names include the Night City Municipal Sewage Treatment Plant or the Night City Municipal Sewage Plant in 2020, South Night City's Wastewater Treatment Plant or the Reclamation Plant in 2045, and the Wellsprings Water Treatment Facility in 2077.

## West
The West is a region of the USA.

Overview
Formed after The Collapse, the West is made up of the states of Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Kansas, New Mexico, and Oklahoma.

History
The states of The West have not fared very well in the twenty-first century. Already hot and dry, the droughts and global warming of the last thirty years have taken their toll on these hapless places. Nowhere else is the death of small-town America as evident as here. There are few if any small towns left on the map. If any do survive, they're multi, generation homesteads and the like, places where the residents won't leave the generations of family in the local cemetery. No one cares to know whether these towns are still extant or not. While there are still the diehard or desperate few trying to claw a living from the land, don't count on finding one when you're lost and starving in the desert. Even if you do, they're as likely to shoot you and eat you as to lend a helping hand.

Most of the Western states are dominated by deserted highways carving their way between sun-parched dust bowl deserts. With the increased heat and decreased rainfall and trade, most of the ranches and farms, like the plant life, dried up and blew away. People moved to the larger cities, which, with their large utility network, were able to irrigate large 'green belts' beyond the suburbs, where the Western states now produce their food.

Skywalks have become commonplace in the West, as most people will avoid leaving their air-conditioned offices if at all possible. In Tucson, for example, it is possible to walk for eight miles across town without once having to face the heat. This has, of course, added to the complexity of building security, especially when corporate executives demand access to their offices twenty four hours a day. It has also dramatically changed traffic and rush hour patterns.

Economically, the states of the West have no real power. While there are a few excellent companies operating down there (like Phoenix's NetLink Software), the West as a whole does not control a major portion of any industry. There are only two reasons why the United States government pays the West any heed: smuggling and military.

Smuggling is a big problem all along the Mexican border, as private entrepreneurs try to run contraband across the border and major corporations try to avoid high U.S. tariffs. In a partial effort to counteract this, the United States has not maintained any highways except Interstates 10, 25 (in places) and 40, which connect the Californias with the rest of the U.S. This has not slowed down the smugglers much, but, it's as good a reason as any for the federal government to keep the Western states hungry for funds (and therefore loyal to the administration).

The one big asset of the West is their wide open spaces. Miles and miles of empty desert make for excellent training grounds for U.S. pilots and hoverjocks. Military vehicles roam the countryside pretty much at will, because the only people they offend have little or no voice in the state government. As an added bonus, the military presence and free fire laws make smuggling a bit more exciting a profession. But then, if it wasn't exciting, everybody would be doing it, neh?

West Wind Estate is a Combat Zone and one of the sub-districts of Pacifica, located in southern Night City.

Overview
By 2070, around the end of the Unification War, some of the prior investors attempted to restart the Pacifica project. They were not welcomed by the local community, who had taken over the sub-districts and turned them into favelas. Corporate workers tried to clear the construction area of squatters, but were met with great resistance from the Voodoo Boys. Eviction attempts made by the NCPD lead to full-scale riots that lasted weeks. Fearing that clearing the neighborhood would result in a bloodbath, the chief of the NCPD ordered the withdrawal of police units from the area. The City Council shut down all city services in Pacifica to force the Voodoo Boys and locals to leave. From that time onward both the West Wind Estate and Coastview areas slowly turned into a new Combat Zone within Night City.

An underwater tunnel allows travel to and from the Wellsprings sub-district in Heywood.

Neither the NCPD nor the corporations had any power in this area. Gang fights and drug trafficking were part of the daily routine here, but locals had gotten used to it. Outsiders were not welcomed, and in order to get into Pacifica "safely", either the Voodoo Boys or one of the locals had to give their okay.

## Westbrook (2077)
引文：Westbrook is considered by many to be the best place to live and have fun in Night City. If you've got eddies, you come here to spend them. And if you don't? Well, take out a loan and pretend you're on top of the world — even for just one glorious night.

The Westbrook District of Night City is home to many wealthy elites, celebrities, and corporates. It is also home to Japantown, an especially important part of Night City for two reasons. The first being that it's the cultural center for the city's sizable Japanese community. The second is that it is home base for most of the Yakuza families operating throughout Northern California; it's centrally located, has limited police interference, and outsiders tend to stick out like a sore thumb. The Tyger Claws are the dominant gang in the district and are considered its rulers, though only at night, in order to avoid the presence of heavy corporate security.

Overview
Westbrook is considered by many to be the best place to live and have fun in all of Night City. It is home to many wealthy elites, celebrities, corporates, and most influential members of society. This, however, was not always the case. In 2023, after the nuclear bomb set off in the Arasaka Towers, a portion of Westbrook closest to the City Center sustained significant damage, turning skyscrapers into ghostly, crooked skeletons for the next two decades. During the great restoration of Night City, residents saw the many ruins removed and replaced by Asian corporations. The once dangerous Combat Zone, was revived into an exclusive, ultra secure District.

North Oak used to see crime rates that measured higher than any other district, but with the attentive help of mercenaries, order has been well and truly restored. In 2077, North Oak is home to many of Night City's untouchable elite: corporate regional directors, managers, bankers, and executives. Private security forces are present all over, resulting in gangs being non-existent here. Taking a walk through its tree-lined streets at every step, you're met with luxurious cars, private villas, and tennis courts. Nowadays, it is considered the most beautiful neighborhood in all of Night City.

Charter Hill is well-known as the place many aspiring and ambitious corpo that cannot afford to live in North Oak reside. This part of the district is all about mass housing. However living here leads to a lifestyle under constant attack, because of this the wealthy need the work of bodyguards as well as the use of armored vehicles to stay safe. It's the price you need to pay for even just a taste of such luxury.

If you've got the eddies, you come to Japantown. If you don't have enough to spend, well, take out a loan and pretend you're on top of the world. Even if it is just for a short amount of time, it'll be a night you remember. It's chock-full of gaming parlors, street food stands, and capsule hotels. Ain't nowhere quite so enticing. It also lies very close to the City Center.

Database Entry

- transcript：A fair amount of Night Citizens firmly believe that Westbrook is the best district to live in. After all, that's where all the richest and most influential people of Night City live, including the picturesquely situated North Oak - probably the most beautiful neighborhood in the city. Charter Hill has its charm, too - home to ambitious and enterprising corpos who are about halfway up their career ladder. Last but not least, Japantown is widely known as Night City's party district. Yes indeed, Westbrook is where everyone wants to be. But it wasn't always like that. Over fifty years ago, after the nuclear attack on Arasaka in 2023, the part of Westbrook next to City Center sustained serious damage. The bomb's earthquake completely wiped out Japantown's high-rises, leaving behind ghostly, crooked skeletons looming over the district for the next two decades. Charter Hill was inundated with refugees - even North Oak saw ramshackle huts and tents hastily put up on its slopes. Luckily, by the 40s, the great restoration of Night City was already underway - the ruins of megabuildings were removed, replaced by shiny monoliths from predominantly Asian corporations, returning Japantown to its former glory. Charter Hill was also cleaned up and soon saw new homes for corpo employees. The refugee and homeless encampments in North Oak lasted for much longer, remaining a sore sight for the city's authorities. Crime levels there beat the city's records - for a time even soaring above those of the Combat Zone. Eventually the area was brought to order with the help of mercenaries, and shortly after it became the North Oak we know today - the most exclusive and secure area of Night City.

Sub-Districts

*Charter Hill
*Japantown
*North Oak

Behind the Scenes

引文：Westbrook is Night City at its most opulent. Money earned in the city's other districts comes here to be spent. Stylistically, here the Neomilitarism of the City Center gains a veneer of sleek, high-tech Kitsch as it enters Japantown, then is deified into the celestial gardens of the uber-rich atop North Oak. Grime is still present, of course, and gangs and graffiti still abound, but in Westbrook, we catch a glimpse of the carrot dangled in front of the noses of Night City's masses. The message: work hard, and one day, you might own a slice of this—or, as a shortcut, take out a loan and pretend you own it for one glorious night. Never mind that you'll spend the rest of your life paying it off.

## Westbrook Hills
- type：Hills
- region：Badlands
- city：Night City
- appears_books：

Westbrook Hills is an elevated area located on the east-northeastern side of Night City, bordering the surrounding Badlands.

History
Overlooking much of Night City, the scenic Westbrook Hills was where much of the original Westbrook was established. This naturally occurring set of hills gave a great view of Del Coronado Bay area, including both North Oak to the west, and central Night City across the smaller neighboring bay. Since there were many trails and parks around these hills, hiking was a common pass time for visitors. Apex Automated Weaponry Systems kept much of Westbrook Hills protected, assuring people to enjoy nature in a peaceful and safe environment. Other parts of these hills had some hunting grounds, offering plenty of sport for those interested. Around 2020, Biotechnica released their new Mule Deer 2000™ here for that purpose. Some ridges in Westbrook Hills were popular spots for climbing as well.

Following the Fourth Corporate War, the high ground of these hills is what allowed New Westbrook to avoid sliding into as bad state as other outlying parts of Night City, soon becoming a prime location for transmissions, both visual and otherwise. For these reasons, during the Time of the Red, Network 54 and WorldSat established operations up here, vesting an interest in keeping the district at least intact and reasonably quiet.

## Where is My Mind?
Where is My Mind? is a Main Job in . It concludes "The Devil" ending and awards the associated achievement if the requirements are met.

Walkthrough

During the surgery in the Arasaka Tower's Medical Center—to have the Relic prototype with Johnny Silverhand's engram removed—V and Johnny speak with each other one last time in cyberspace before being separated. They reminisce on their time together,

After the surgery, V is transported to the Arasaka Orbital Station, where they wake up in the clinic for the first time since the surgery and start their recovery. After a short conversation with their doctor, Professor Sachiko Kusama, they are escorted to their room, and go to sleep.

During their first night's sleep, V has a nightmare in which they hear still Johnny's voice. The voice draws V to the door, which they open and gaze upon the vast emptiness of space, before leaping into it, causing them to wake up. After waking up, a WNS report on the television reveals that Saburo Arasaka has taken over the body of his son, Yorinobu Arasaka, while they hold a speech on television ensuring that the Arasaka Corporation will go back to its roots and be stronger than ever. As the news broadcast ends, Professor Kusama enters the room to see how V's recovery is going with various tests, such as reading text from a monitor, solving a Rubik's cube, responding, responding to keywords, and motor functions test using treadmill. After the tests, V goes back to sleep, and has another nightmare.

V hears Johnny once more while sleeping, and again drawing them to the door. This time the door opens to the hallway of the station. Upon exploring the hallway, V relives the memory of Jackie's death, with the Relic being inserted again into their neuroport.

V wakes up again, and this day a news report by N54 news is on the television, still reporting on Saburo Arasaka's apparent resurrection and
that numerous Virtu 100 Company CEO's, religious leaders, and human rights groups have signed a letter of protest. Professor Kusama enters V's room again, to subject V to more tests, which after completion allow V to use the communications system.

:V calls Viktor Vektor and he picks up. Viktor tells V that they want them to visit him for a check-up after returning to Earth. Viktor also tells V that Misty Olszewski is visiting family in Warsaw. Unable to provide the right counseling that V requires, they ask that V makes the decision that seems right to them.

:
::V calls Panam Palmer and she picks up. She demands that V returns to Earth immediately and hangs up as Mitch Anderson requires her help with something.

:
::V calls Panam Palmer and she picks up. Panam angrily tells V that they heard about their situation through Viktor, and that they are mad with them for not telling her about it themselves. Panam demands that V returns to Earth before Arasaka is able to hurt them.

:
::V calls Judy Álvarez, but gets played a pre-recorded message, in which she mentions that they may call V back when they are no longer angry with them.

:
::V calls Judy Álvarez and she picks up. Judy is distraught about the fact that they trusted Arasaka, but at the same time she is happy that they were able to remove the Relic. She confesses to V that they would not know what to do if they found out if they were gone, and demands that V returns to Earth in a matter of hours.

:
::V calls River Ward and he picks up, only to tell V that they currently do not have time to talk, and tells V to call back later.

:
::V calls River Ward and he picks up. They talk on the phone while River is also in a conversation with his nephew. River asks V the name of the orbital station, so that he can fly up and bring them home. V is unable to give River the name of the orbital station, as they do not know it, and warn River to not trust Arasaka. The call is ended with River saying that he will find out wherever V is, to bring them home.

:
::V calls Kerry Eurodyne and he picks up. V explains their situation to him, but finds himself unable to place himself in V's shoes, suggesting them to just leave wherever they are, and hangs up so they can continue watching a TV show.

:
::V calls Kerry Eurodyne and he picks up. Kerry is ecstatic when V tells them that Arasaka was able to remove the Relic, and comforts V, promising to watch a reruns of a TV show together. Worried about V being all on their own in the orbital station, Kerry tells V that they are the best thing planet Earth has going for herself and that they should return home. Before ending the call, Kerry tells V that they will make the necessary calls to get them back safely to Night City.

:Hanako Arasaka did not pick up when V called her.

While V is asleep that night, they dream about the tests, eventually breaking open the Rubik's Cube which reveals an image of a Devil. Waking up from the nightmare, a WNS news bulletin about the increasing tension between the Arasaka and Militech corporations is playing, warning of a possible armed conflict.

As the tests go on for the new few weeks, V grows increasingly annoyed at them. Eventually V reaches a breaking point, and becomes aggressive, causing the Professor to hastily leave the room.

The following day, after a recovery period of almost 30 days, V has to make their final decision, as they are informed by Sachiko Kusama that the treatment has been ineffective so far.

:V wakes up to Goro Takemura, who offers V to become a part of the Secure Your Soul program by having their psyche digitalized. In an effort to help V make their choice, Takemura encourages V to go through with the digitization.

:V wakes up to Anders Hellman, who offers V to become a part of the Secure Your Soul program by having their psyche digitalized.

:
::V signs the contract and agrees with being digitized and becoming an engram until Arasaka has found a new body for them.

:
::V refuses to sign the contract to become digitized. V leaves the station to live out the remainder of their life on Earth in realspace, while singing the lyrics of Never Fade Away to themselves.

## Who Wants to Live Forever
Who Wants to Live Forever is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough

As long as you surrendered Songbird to the NUSA during The Killing Moon or Somewhat Damaged, V will have the option of a cure no matter what they say during subsequent quests. You will receive a call/text from Solomon Reed, with the option to decline their help and end the quest; or accept their aid, leading you to the rooftop of Misty's Esoterica. A conversation with Johnny Silverhand will ensue, and afterwards the option to call Solomon will appear. This call option also appears during Nocturne Op55N1.

Journal Entry
:So, here it is, the finale, though grand sure ain't the word for it. Our story ends not with a bang but a scalpel. I die so you can live on.
:To tell ya the truth, V, kinda always suspected it'd turn out like this. I mean, your body, your life is how I've seen it throughout. Now, I can't claim to know what'll happen with you now that I'm gone, but if you don't mind my droppin' one last nugget o' wisdom on you as I go, it's this – no matter what happens, V, no matter how bad the bastards bitch at you, stay fuckin' true to your fuckin' self and no one else.

Objectives
* Wait a day for Reed to contact you.
* Talk to Reed.
* Head to the rooftop above Misty's Esoterica.
* Sit in the chair.
* Talk to Johnny.
* Text your friends (optional).
* Wait for the FIA agents.
* Talk to the FIA agent.
* Get in the AV.

Wilky LaGuerre, better known by his pseudonym Slider, is a Voodoo Boys Netrunner in .

Appearance
Wilky has white eyes due to his blindness. He sits in a chair attached to a machine, which he uses to continue his netrunner work.

He has dark brown locks which fall to his chin. Several scars mark the cyberware on his face.
He wears a sleeveless, striped blazer with a bright orange lapel and black fur tufts at the back, paired with matching slacks. On his feet, he wears sandals. He has noticeable long brown nails, which seem to be painted.

A piece of dark metal cyberware is embedded in his chest, surrounded by numerous scars. Orange wiring runs along his arms, connecting to several ports.

Biography

Wilky was a prominent netrunner affiliated with the Voodoo Boys, a gang known for its expertise in netrunning. Initially, Wilky served as the right hand to Maman Brigitte, the leader of the Voodoo Boys, however, ideological differences arose between them; while Brigitte was intent on breaching the Blackwall, Wilky preferred to stay away from NetWatch agents.

During one of his high-profile heists, Wilky attracted the attention of FIA agents. They subjected him to a targeted netrunner attack that caused severe damage, which resulted in complete blindness. Following this incident, the FIA coerced him into becoming an informant through intimidation and blackmail. Looking to escape their control, Wilky fled Pacifica and joined his fellow Voodoo Boys in Dogtown. Despite his efforts, the FIA's influence reached him there as well.

Ultimately, Wilky met his demise in 2077 at his hideout in the Eventide Resort & Spa in Dogtown.

Will Gunner is the leader of 6th Street, acting as their General. Gunner's gang is on a quest to "bring justice" to Night City.

Biography
Will Gunner only recently came into this position after he betrayed and killed the previous leader, Rick Morton, and his supporters. To legitimise his new position, Gunner falsely stated that Morton had been killed by Pablo Silva and the traitors who sided with the corporations. After taking over, Gunner initiated a large-scale purge of the gang to rid himself of all supporters of the previous leadership. He ordered the deaths of 6th Street gang members who were incarcerated in a Militech prison. Likewise, he ordered his men to hunt down Flavio dos Santos and after the latter was rescued by V, Gunner ordered his men to eliminate the merc.

He also attempted to coerce Tina Agron, a Biotechnica farm worker who was stealing proteins from her workplace and selling them to 6th Street, into entering a partnership with him, but after she demanded a bigger cut of the profits (on par with what she received when working with Morton), Gunner broke negotiations and ordered her death.

As boss, Gunner was largely disinterested in the day-to-day operations of the gang, such as overseeing extortion rackets, but he did occasionally send people out to collect due debts.

His fellow 6th Streeters usually throw parties in Gunner's honor. V can go to one of these parties and participate in a shooting contest.

Phantom Liberty
Gunner provided Solomon Reed and V with equipment and intel to help them assault a MaxTac convoy.

## William Hare
- aka：Corporal Hare
- status：Dependent
- dod：2077
- place_of_death：Kabuki, Watson

- equipment：Carnage
M-10AF Lexington
- affiliation：Militech (formerly)
- role：Ex-soldier

William Hare is a former Militech corporal discharged for showing signs of an incoming cyberpsychosis.

Biography
William Hare signed up to serve with Militech at 17 years old after seeing one of their posters. Witnessing their multi-million eurodollar equipment and armored soldiers, filled him with a sense of adventure and power. He proudly notes being 3rd Light Division, 155th Infantry Regiment, getting everything he wanted with Militech. However, seven years in Brazil turned his dream job into a nightmare. Stuck in the jungle, fighting just to survive, killing and watching his comrades be killed around him left him not just changed, but broken, haunted by nightmares and flashbacks he could not keep away. When he finally returned to Night City, his post traumatic stress disorder was already developing into early signs of cyberpsychosis, which earned him a discharge from Militech. With nobody to blame, he started hyperfixating on politicians currently in charge and their corruption. Hare stopped attending his veteran support group and got involved in plotting an assassination of Weldon Holt, the acting mayor of Night City in 2077. In addition to this, feeling betrayed by the system, he will openly express violent hatred towards anyone in the line of procuring medication, from corporations to ripperdocs.

Hare's final attempt at self-help lead him into stealing a packet of baloperidol from a local ripperdoc. Watson fixer Regina Jones had been contracted to retrieve the items, not knowing much of who stole them or why. Her choice of runner for this job was V, who will be notified of the contract when in the immediate surroundings of Hare's Kabuki apartment.

Hare will not be welcoming, expecting a wide selection of enemies at the door and will greet V with his shotgun. He will however be open to discuss the situation and elaborate his views in a civil manner in case of his order being obeyed. He will explain that the drugs he had stolen in desperate attempt to get better did not work, accusing ripperdocs of being criminals for deceiving people they were supposed to be healing, but will aggressively deny any insinuation that he is actually suffering from cyberpsychosis. His increasing desperation pushed forward by very vivid memories of war caused him to relive all of the events from the most bitter moments of his past as if in a braindance. This followed by knowing how his regiment, those he considered brothers, entirely forgot of him even existing as soon as he had been discharged, adding depression-induced anger to the list of struggles he must suffer.

If V convinces Hare not to go after Holt due to it being just a meaningless act of terrorism leaving a hole another corrupt politician will fill, he will face reality through existential crisis, losing a single motivational drive in life and shoot himself once V leaves his room. Threatening Hare or making any sudden moves while in conversation with him will make him hostile, and they will have to kill or incapacitate him in self-defense.

Database Entry

- transcript：When a 17-year-old William Hare first saw a poster promoting service in Militech's paramilitary forces, he finally understood his purpose in life. As his impressionable eyes scanned the multi-million-dollar equipment and armored soldiers, he felt a brutal power and desire for adventure swell inside him. How could a kid who spent his whole life in the slums of Rancho Coronado resist? The promotional specialists in Militech's recruitment office certainly think so, and they're usually right. Hare enlisted and eventually rose to the rank of Corporal. He got everything he dreamed of plus more - combat military-grade cyberware, a sense of power, camaraderie and adventure. As for the latter, there are some parts he'd rather forget - especially the ones he's forbidden to talk about. After Brazil, everything changed. He lost his good health and came back to Night City a veteran, but with no hope of ever returning to active duty. That's when Hare first asked himself - had Militech taken away more than they gave him?

The Wind Farms are located on the eastern Badlands of Night City.

History
Early history - 2040s
At some point during the Time of the Red, an area of the Badlands to the east of Night City was filled with hundreds of wind turbines, providing a substantial amount of the city's energy needs. To manage and maintain them, the Government of Night City hired the PacCon Electric corporation.

During the 2040s, despite various energy sources providing power to the metropolis, it never seemed to suffice, with blackouts being a common occurrence across Night City.

2060s - 2070s
During the 2070s, this large wind farm occupied much of the plains east of Night City, as well as a portion of Sierra Sonora. Due to the Unification War, the farthest reaches had been dotted with a minefield that denoted the farm's close proximity to the border with Southern California.

Over the years, these old wind turbines had played a major role in generating electricity for Night City, but gradually fell into disrepair. For over fifteen consecutive years, 63% of them had already been shut down by 2077, with only a handful still functioning. Nevertheless, a few operators were occasionally sent to repair some of the damaged turbines.

## With a Little Help from My Friends
With a Little Help from My Friends is a Side Job in .

Walkthrough
Some time after helping Panam Palmer rescue the Aldecaldos's leader, Saul Bright, she contacts V again, this time to ask if they are able to come to the Mobile Camp in Rocky Ridge as soon as possible.

After V arrives at the Mobile Camp, they meet with Panam, Mitch, and Saul in the communications trailer. As V approaches them, Panam receives an earful from Saul Bright for calling them over to the camp, and tells Panam once more that he forbade her from even thinking about the Militech convoy that they heard about. Mitch also joins into the argument, calling Saul a fool for letting a Militech Basilisk slip through their fingers. Saul retorts by mentioning that it could mess up the job they came here to do, which is revealed to be a crop protection contract for Biotechnica, with whom he is meeting later.

Panam reveals that they plan on assaulting a Militech convoy that they have heard about in order to obtain a Basilisk from them, which could prove useful for the Aldecaldos, as it could restore some of their reputation as since taking on the Biotechnica contracts they have been going through a rough time. When V asks how they can help out, Panam suggests that they talk to the others–Bob Sagan, Cassidy Righter, Carol Emeka and Teddy Simos–first and walk over to them near the food truck.

After taking a seat, Panam starts explaining the plan to everyone. Panam explains that the Basilisk will be transported on two trucks on Highway 101, and she plans to block the convoy's path by occupying the railroad intersection that crosses the highway.

:V tells Panam that they don't want to get involved in such a risky job. Despite V declining, the Aldecaldos will continue their plan to try and take over the convoy, and ride off in their vehicles to the train station. Mitch tells V that if they change their mind, they can join them there.

:
::V changed their mind and met up with the Aldecaldos at the train station.

:
::Instead of meeting with the Aldecaldos at the train station, V opted to talk to Saul. V tells them that Panam and co. went on to execute their plan to try and take over the convoy. For their honesty, Saul awards V with 42940 eurodollars.

::A few hours later, V is called by an angry Panam, asking them how they could rat her out to Saul, and breaks off contact with V.

::A few days later, Saul sends V a text message telling them that they did the right thing by informing him about her plan, and that the entire family owes them a huge debt of gratitude. Saul adds that the contract with Biotechnica did not work out and that the Aldecaldos will be moving their camp soon, with Panam, Mitch and the other veterans already having gone ahead of them. As a parting gift, Saul tells V that they left them something at the Sunset Motel.

:V agrees to help Panam and goes to the Corp-Bud Railroad Station.

:
::While driving to the train station with Panam, V talks with her. She notes that Saul probably is in favor of them not being at the Mobile Camp, considering that Biotechnica will be dropping by for a visit. Panam also mentions that Saul is afraid that the Raffen Shiv will attack the Aldecaldos as retaliation for taking the Biotechnica contract from them, and has posted extra security around the camp. When V asks if she misses Night City, she will tell V that she misses the excitement but that she at the same time misses the emptiness of the Badlands. V can understand some of this sentiment and tells Panam about Jackie Welles.

Once the Aldecaldos arrive at the train station and exit their vehicles, they go once more over the plan, and note that all that is necessary to put their plan in motion is to get the old freight train working again. Carol explains that in order to get the train operating, Panam and V will need to override authorization in the control tower.

V helps Panam find the entrance to the control tower, and together they make their way up to the control room.

Once up high in the tower, Carol tells Panam and V that they have to look for a punch card somewhere in the building in order to gain access to the locomotive's control panel. After finding the in a cabinet, V returns to Panam to tell them they have found it, and Carol will instruct them to enter the card into the control panel's reader. After entering the card into the control panel, the locomotive will activate and start moving. Panam will have a heart-to-heart conversation with V, and asks them why they've decided to help her out.

After talking with each other, Panam and V join the other Aldecaldos at the campfire near the junction.  The nomads talk with each other about their current situation and Scorpion, before going to bed.

In the morning, Panam will wake up V and tells them to get in her vehicle, as the Aldecaldos are preparing to start their assault on the Militech convoy. After getting in the vehicle, the Aldecaldos and V ride alongside the locomotive to the railroad crossing on Highway 101 and intercept the convoy. After a firefight, the Aldecaldos manage to secure the Basilisk and escort the trucks back to the camp.

Back in the camp, Panam is welcomed by an infuriated Saul, who give each other an earful. Afterwards, Panam instructs the other nomads to get to work on the Basilisk and talks with V, and tells them she will give them a call when she needs more help from them.

Journal Entry
:The great nomad saga continues: Panam's up to something. That girl just doesn't know when to quit - and my God, I love her for it. You don't seem to know either, considering you wanna go back out there. Maybe you could save us all some time, pitch a tent out in the desert? Think we both know this isn't just about the job anymore.

引文：It took two years to put this Yaiba together. An ultra-rare speed machine that's built for driving only one way: sideways.（ARV-Q340 Semimaru）

This ARV-Q340 Semimaru is a custom vehicle originally manufactured by Yaiba in added in Update 2.3.

History

This Yaiba car was obtained by Mint and Tiff some years prior to the events of , with both splitting ownership of it. They rebuilt the vehicle over the course of two years, replacing many of its pieces with new ones. This process was put on hold for six months after Mint disappeared. In that timespan, the original engine they had ordered arrived, but with no one to retrieve it, it was sent back. Afterwards, Tiff had to ask for a new one. When Mint returned to Night City, she visited Tiff in need of a car after the yellow Mizutani Shion MZ2 she had stolen from Green Dragon had been seized by Gorilla. It was then when they installed the new engine in the Yaiba and finished their project. They had built that car for just one purpose, drifting.

Mint brought the Yaiba to the Serpent in the Badlands for testing, a place her father, Jeremy Taylor, used for practising as well. She intended to beat her father's best time of a consecutive drift, though she didn't manage to do so.

After the retrieval of Kickdown by the NCPD, Mint left the Yaiba behind, which was impounded by the detectives who had worked with her, Ortiz and Jones. Over the following years, both NCPD officers used the Yaiba to run down other criminals and gain the rewards of the gigs they accepted under the disguise of "Mint" while clearing the city of "scumbags." In 2077, however, the Semimaru was stolen by two street racers called Jax Forgrave and Nova MacCaster, who were planning to use the car to win illegal races. Upon successfully stealing the car, Nova fell into cyberpsychosis, running rampant around Night City.

引文：No matter its configuration, a tailor-made Muramasa never fails to deliver the perfect blend of elegance and performance worthy of Yaiba's exclusive clientele.（ASM-R250 Muramasa）

The ASM-R250 Muramasa is a customizable motorcycle manufactured by Yaiba in added in Update 2.3.

Overview
The Murasama was officially designed to be the successor for the Kusanagi as an exclusive, highly customisable, new motorcycle for an elite few who had caught Yaiba's attention. Sold only to those who Yaiba felt as being capable of mastering it, Yaiba partnered with Kiroshi to promote the Muramasa, creating specialised billboards that could only advertise to those chosen as potential Muramasa owners, and an exclusive showroom event was held at Kiroshi's campus in Night City to showcase the Murasama. Unofficially, Yaiba's founder and chief designer Daigo Shinohara after witnessing the events of the Fourth Corporate War came to believe that society was inevitably heading towards a collapse, and that the corporations were destined to fall. Resigned to his belief that Yaiba would fall victim to this collapse as well, he designed the Muramasa as a weapon for those he believed could rise from the ashes of society's collapse as leaders, to ensure that they survived.

Database Entry

Acquisition
*Nitro (Youth Energy) - Purchased for €$95,000.

Modifications
During Nitro (Youth Energy), seven custom configurations for the Murasama can be found in the showroom, while when ordering V can customize theirs by picking from a mix of four parts that can be left off or put onto the Muramasa, allowing any of the seven custom configurations to be replicated. The bike can only be customized once during purchase.

Presets
*Jack of All Trades: "This configuration suits the versatile biker who wants a well-rounded riding experience."
**Parts: wheel covers off, rims without lug holes, branding on, backrest on.
*Fierce: "This configuration is for bikers who want to dominate the road with their bold, aggressive style."
**Parts: wheel covers on, rims with lug holes, branding on, backrest off.
*Designer's Edition: "This configuration is for riders who desire to experience the road as the Murasama's original designer intended."
**Parts: wheel covers on, rims without lug holes, branding on, backrest off.
*Low-Key: "This configuration suits the function-over-frills biker who's actions speak louder than words."
**Parts: wheel covers on, rims without lug holes, branding off, backrest on.
*Show Off: "This configuration is perfect for trendsetters who demand the world's attention. For life on the road, style is everything."
**Parts: wheel covers off. rims with lug holes, branding on, backrest on.
*Minimalist: "This configuration suits riders who desire clean contours and pure speed."
**Parts: wheels covers off, rims without lug holes, branding off, backrest off.
*Yaiba Classic: "This configuration is an homage to die-hard bikers who have stayed true to Yaiba's original spirit."
**Parts: wheel covers on, rims with lug holes, branding on, backrest on.

Parts
*Wheel covers: adds or removes fenders from the Murasama's wheels.
*Rim lug holes: changes the style of rims on the Muramasa to include or exclude visible lug holes.
*Branding: adds or removes a Yaiba name decal from the Murasama's frame.
*Backrest: adds or removes a small backrest from the Muramasa's seat.

Database Entry

- transcript：The Yaiba Kusanagi CT-3X is the fastest, and unsurprsingly, the most expensive motorcycle, originally built in collaboration with the Arasaka Corporation. Its sleek, aerodynamic frame conceals a wickedly powerful engine. Ideally, anyone riding one should be chipped with reflex boosters to avoid flying into a traffic light at 100MPH when making a sharp turn. The Kusanagi is a favorite among gangers, especially the Tyger Claws.

Acquisition
It can be acquired from the AUTOFIXER netpage for €$66,000.

Yaiba Kusanagi CT-3X V Message CP2077.png

Development

The bike made its debut in the E3 2077 gameplay demo. An image and description were later revealed in Famitsu magazine (see Gallery).

The game's official Twitter account also posted an image of the cycle with the caption, "Catching a break with Yaiba Kusanagi..."

Notes
*Despite being called numerous times "the most expensive motorcycle," there are more expensive purchasable motorbikes like the ARCH Nazaré.
*A black Kusanagi appears on the front the Bushidō 5: Body of Law cover.
*During the main job Never Fade Away, a Kusanagi is used by Rogue as a getaway vehicle. Considering it's a flashback of Johnny's engram, and that the bike was made decades later, it should not be considered an accurate memory.
*Prior to Patch 1.5 it cost €$22,000 and reached 189 mph. Before Patch 2.0 it cost €$58,000.
*Prior to the introduction of AUTOFIXER, Wakako Okada sold the bike via a text message: "V. In your line of work, one must be quick and punctual. Since you seem to struggle with both, I figured you could use a motorcycle. If you can have only one, let it be the best - the Yaiba Kusanagi. I happen to have one for sale. Buy it and you will not regret it."

Trivia
*The name "Kusanagi" is a reference to the protagonist of Ghost in the Shell, Major Motoko Kusanagi.
*The Kusanagi bears heavy resemblance to Priscilla Asagiri's motorcycle from Bubblegum Crisis and Shotaro Kaneda's motorcycle from the manga and anime film Akira.
**The pill capsule on the back of Shotaro Kaneda's jacket is visible on the hood of the Yaiba Kusanagi.

Bugs

Yaiba Tower is located in Kabuki, in the Watson district of northern Night City.

Overview
Yaiba Tower is a skyscraper located on Sutter Street in Kabuki. It is surrounded by residential buildings and, most notoriously, Lizzie's Bar. The abandoned edifice has a great view of the bridge to Japantown, as well as the Westbrook skyline.

At some point, this office building was owned by the Yaiba corporation, with some of the floors also also used as a news outlet studio. By 2075, however, no corporations were present here anymore, with the structure abandoned to the locals. A netrunner by the name of Kiwi used one of its top floors for some time.

Around 2077, fixer Regina Jones used one of the tops floors as her base of operations, reserving the whole floor for herself and her partners.

:Max Jones will reluctantly rejoin Regina Jones's team, and take refuge inside one of the skyscraper's rooms.

## Yawen Packard
- gender：Female
- partner：River Ward (ex-boyfriend)
- affiliation：NCPD
- role：Medtech
- voiced_by：Emily Woo Zeller

Yawen Packard is a medical doctor assigned to an NCPD-contracted laboratory in Heywood.

Biography

Yawen Packard is an acclaimed medical professional specializing in neuroscience. She is currently working in the field of pediatric autism, augmenting children's brain waves with braindance technology. Due to the specific nature of accessing thoughts and memories that would otherwise be locked out, the NCPD contracted her lab to help with the investigation of the Peter Pan case, where the suspect suffered a bullet wound and ended up in a coma prior to being able to reveal any information regarding his victims.

Her devotion to the job can easily be noted by her presence in the facility during a complete lab audit - an occurrence which had interrupted an unlawful search of the premises executed by her old boyfriend River Ward and his companion V. Due to previous unpleasant exchanges, she will point out expected disappointment by River's behavior, not reluctantly calling him a bastard, expecting V to agree with her, regardless of knowing near nothing of them. In disagreement, she will simply add how she too thought differently of him in the past. Yawen will be opposed to helping them with finding any more evidence regarding the classified case, especially since she had the knowledge of River's suspension from the department. In absence of time, River will use personal information from her past regarding cheating on medical exams to intimidate her into helping. Yawen will simply get irritated but not succumb until finding out the underlying reason for River's persistence, namely, his own nephew being one of the victims. Despite having theoretical methodology regarding using sensory prompts on patients at her disposal, she remains reluctant to try it on an adult for the sake of provoking dreams. The patient's preferences remain unknown, so until anything he feels strongly about is provided, she will fail at delivering useful results.

When asked about potential knowledge regarding the Relic, she will express confusion with the implication of it being able to overwrite the user's psyche and admit not having nearly enough information to give any certain conclusions on the matter.

Once River and V find enough material for Yawen, she will succeed in triggering dreams in the comatose patient and record three braindances from his past, helping to resolve the case.

Associated Quests
*The Hunt

## Yishen Rhee
- status：Deceased
- dod：August 21, 2023
- home：Night City

Red Willow (formerly)
