Yishen Rhee was a Mercenary in . She made her first appearance in the comic, and appeared during the main job Never Fade Away in .

Biography
Yishen Rhee was a member of the Red Willow Nomads before moving to Night City. Sometime before 2013, Rhee and Johnny Silverhand had a falling out for an unknown reason after an event Silverhand assumed she "didn't like the last time".

In April 2013, Rhee was at the Club Atlantis at the same time as Johnny Silverhand was searching for Rogue Amendiares. Having trouble getting something out of a vending machine, she asked Silverhand to "fix" the machine for her before brushing him off, still angry with him.

August 19–21, 2023
In August 2023, Rhee took on a contract from Prothero, a fixer, to acquire a datashard from the CMO of Zetatech Leo Coghlan for Johnny Silverhand.

After successfully stealing the datashard from his hotel room, Rhee was pursued by two Maelstromers sent by Coghlan. While running from her pursuers, Rhee bumped into Todd, an NCART Techie. She handed him the datashard, and instructed him to sell the shard to her fixer at Monroe Station. She yelled at him to run, while trying to keep the Maelstromers off his back by herself, but was caught by them instead.

Using netrunning skills, the Maelstromers reached out to Todd over his radio, demanding he handed over the datashard, or Rhee would perish. As a response, Todd sent over his bot to deliver the datashard, using the oncoming train as a distraction, Rhee managed to free herself and escaped with Todd. Having made their way outside the metro tunnels, she dismissed Todd to take a cab to the Afterlife.

Having returned to the Afterlife and her fixer Prothero empty-handed, she was attacked by several of his henchmen. However, before they had a chance to harm her, Todd arrived at the Afterlife with a copy of the data she was supposed to steal. The data–a map of the communications network of Zetatech paramilitary bases–could not be retrieved from Todd's implants, forcing Rhee to take him with her on her new gig; assaulting a Zetatech convoy for a friend, with nomads in order to retrieve a case.

The duo headed to the Zetatech Air Base in the Badlands using a Zetatech branded Zeya U420 and stole a Surveyor. Though, shortly after taking off, they were attacked by several Maelstromers hired by Coghlan using a Manticore. Rhee managed to take them out using a well-aimed shot at the AV's pilot, but in the process, they also crashed themselves.

After crash-landing the AV, an injured Rhee and Todd headed to a nearby bar, the Silver Mungo, where she contacted the nomads to meet them at their current location. As the call ended, several Raffen Shiv entered the bar who were familiar with Rhee, and she was with them. The duo engaged in a shootout with the Raffens, where Rhee got shot in the shoulder. Yet, thanks to Todd's chipware, the two emerged victorious just before the nomads arrived.

Alongside them, Rhee and Todd assaulted the Militech convoy and retrieved the case. She contacted Prothero to notify him that they retrieved the goods, and were warned by him that more Zetatech forces were on their way to their location and that Coghlan and Maelstrom were no longer involved. Despite being advised to abandon the contract by the nomads after learning that the fixer would not send help, she disagreed, saying the client was a "friend".

Rhee and Todd took a bus back to Night City to meet Prothero, where Todd agreed to finish the job while the fixer took her to a ripperdoc. That night, a braindance of the events transpiring at the bar and the assault on the convoy would ultimately be uploaded to the Net under the title of "Badlands Raid", after being secretly recorded by Todd's fixer Lexy Hammer. The next morning, Rhee was tracked down and killed by men working for Zetatech due to the release of the braindance while receiving treatment.

The case she retrieved with Todd's help would end up being the nuclear bomb that Militech used to set off the Night City Holocaust.

引文：Fear, ever since I can remember. The one thing I can not deny him - he knew how to cause fear in people. He once told me everything of valve is only a flag blowing in wind. And wind is fear. And then ... he blew in my face. That was the one time he was wrong（Yorinobu）

Yorinobu Arasaka (Japanese: 荒坂 頼宣) is a major character in .

The second son to Saburo Arasaka and first son to Michiko Arasaka, Yorinobu is the rebellious bōsōzoku leader of the Steel Dragons. Although a sworn bōsōzoku leader rockerboy, he eventually became the heir to the Arasaka empire after the death of his elder brother Kei. Yorinobu disagreed with everything his father set out to accomplished and abandoned everything because of it. He is passionate, caring, and determined more than anything else.

Yorinobu is the charismatic counter to Johnny Silverhand in Tokyo (though he does not play in a band). He was known to rally up the Japanese public to rebel against the corporate overlords. Yorinobu still cared for his sister Hanako and would frequently speak with her behind their father's back, swearing one day to save her. In 2077, Yorinobu still rebels against his father, but has not seen him in decades. However, he soon realized that the corporate giant's power was impossible to defeat — at least from the outside.

Biography

引文：Yori-kun, you know about Arasaka Security that made our company famous? Well, that's not the thing that has made the company powerful, what made the company powerful was the Arasaka Bank. I know that with enough extortion and political influence, killing the appropriate people and massacring the workers of the appropriate corp, we can restore the glory of the Empire of the Sun and make Japan the biggest superpower of the world.（Saburo Arasaka）

1995 - 2020
Yorinobu was born in September 8, 1995 to Saburo and Michiko Arasaka in Tokyo, Japan. From a young age he was given the riches and benefits of any Arasaka family member would get, including the best education in the country. Growing up alongside his sister Hanako they were happy being within the Arasaka family compound. Yorinobu was raised with a blissful ignorance towards his fathers corporation. Something Saburo thought was important to keep secret until he was ready.

The day after the 21-year-old Yorinobu graduated from [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Tokyo Todai], Saburo brought him to his private chambers at the compound. His father, proud of his accomplishment, explained to him the true nature of the Arasaka Corporation. Rather than agreeing with his father's vision, as his elder half-brother Kei had, Yorinobu was secretly appalled and chose to stay silent as his father kept speaking. That night, after a celebratory dinner given in his honor, Yorinobu slipped out of the compound and vanished into the Tokyo night. Knowing what went on within the corporation, he hated what his father was trying to accomplish and vowed to stop him, while also wanting to save his sister from being involved.

Four years later, Yorinobu had gathered a cadre of tough Tokyo nomads (Bōsōzoku): 'Kotetsu no Ryu', or Steel Dragons. The bōsōzoku had sworn to expose Arasaka and fight for its demise. At night, they would prowl the canyons of the city, harassing Arasaka employees and unearthing information on Arasaka black operations. Yorinobu's knowledge of Arasaka facilities and corporate procedures gave the Steel Dragons some advantages, but they still lacked the power or information to make serious headway against the corporation. He was, however, able to tread the world of the street and the corporate tower with equal facility. When he wasn't riding with his men, he was travelling the world; meeting with other enemies of Arasaka and looking for funds and equipment. Slowly but surely his operation was growing.

Saburo loved his son, and was greatly saddened by his disloyalty, but acknowledged that Yorinobu needed to be dealt with as he threatened the corporation. Kei, who hated Yorinobu for his defection, had sworn to kill his half-brother. Hanako, on the other hand, still loved her brother. She and Yorinobu had always felt a special bond with each other. Although she was unaware of it at the time, he had sworn to free her from their father's clutches. Once a month, Yorinobu and Hanako secretly communicated through the net, reaffirming their fraternal love for one another.

Yorinobu would visit Night City to gather information from his contacts. During one of Arasaka's sweeps on the city, some of Yorinobu's local contacts were taken prisoner, interrogated, and eventually executed. One of these contacts was Hiraga, who knew the identities of many high-ranking officials and suppliers to the Steel Dragons. The information obtained about the nomad clan was stored at the Arasaka Towers in Night City. Before it could be sent to Kei at the Tokyo Headquarters, Yorinobu had a contact intercept the data. With the data was an order for the assassination of high-ranking Steel Dragon officials. His contact's activity was traced down and they had to commit [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seppuku seppuku] after destroying the data to avoid capture. Unfortunately, the regional security director of Arasaka, Iwasao Koremichi, supposedly had a hard copy with the data.

2021 - 2023
During the Fourth Corporate War, Yorinobu took further action to disrupt Arasaka's operations. Despite attempts from Militech to lure him to their side, he refused to join them. Instead, he played a role in supplying info to the government of Japan that helped their nationalization of Arasaka's assets. However, even after the damage from the war and the terrorist attack on Arasaka Tower in Night City, he saw it still wasn't enough to destroy the corporation. Yorinobu learned that it if Arasaka was to be destroyed, it must be from within.

After the war ended, Yorinobu attended Kei's funeral. It was here he reconciled with his father. With the help of his sister, he was slowly welcomed back into the family.

2045
In 2045, Yorinobu led the Taka (鷹) Faction of the Arasaka Corporation. He made sure that during the War he was impossible to find and tried to reconcile with Saburo after. He still played the renegade game and opposed the other factions. As long as his father stayed in control under the Kiji (雉) Faction, Yorinobu would still be out there trying to bring about the corp's downfall — though this time he had planned to be more subtle than his previous schemes.

2077
Yorinobu was the original heir to the Arasaka Empire before he rebelled and cut ties with his father. For many years he led the Steel Dragons and sought destruction but soon realized that the corporate giant's power was impossible to defeat — at least from the outside. By this point he hasn't spoken to Saburo in decades. In 2077, he was in contact with Ronald Cheever, a NetWatch Operations Manager. The two discussed a cooperation that involved obtaining a sample of the Relic biochip with a valid engram. Yorinobu saw an opportunity and stole a Relic prototype from one of his father's laboratories in Tokyo. He then made sure the engram on the biochip was of Johnny Silverhand. After retreating to Night City, he was warned by Anders Hellman that the biochip was a prototype and was not ready for use in its current state. He eventually spoke with Hellman over the phone. This is when he warned Yorinobu to speak with his father before anything, as he was personally involved with the project.

Saburo arrived in Night City shortly thereafter to retrieve what was stolen and to confront his son alone. In a fit of rage, Yorinobu murdered his father and later covered it up by claiming an assassin had his father poisoned. Yorinobu took full control of the Arasaka Corporation and began to make changes from within. His decisions started to take effect when he started removing facilities in Fukuoka and Kitakyushu in Japan. His plan to sabotage the corporation from within and undo much of what his father built had begun.

Yorinobu participated in the parade to honor Saburo with the approval of Hanako and their niece, Michiko Arasaka. During the parade Hanako was kidnapped and he worked quickly to rescue her with his chief of security, Adam Smasher. After successfully rescuing his sister, Yorinobu made a public statement that anyone who would harm a member of the Arasaka family would be punished.

He decided to order his faction to keep an eye on Hanako and keep her safe in the Arasaka Estate, North Oak. Yorinobu later called an emergency meeting of the Arasaka supervisor board in Night City. Top executives from Tokyo, as well as branch directors from Paris, Shanghai, and Kinshasa all met in the Arasaka Tower of the American Division headquarters. Yorinobu had a plan for a military coup that would give him and those loyal to his faction complete control of Arasaka for his plan of sabotage. Part of his plan also involved his factions in Night City, Kyoto, Dubai, and Paris. The troops loyal to Yorinobu were ordered to destroy all other factions within the corporation as well as to remove the board of directors to gain complete control.

:Yorinobu was successful in his plans of sabotaging the Arasaka Empire, losing much of its political power and control over the world. The Relic project was scrapped as the corporation lost billions. The Arasaka Corporation's future was unclear and would take time for reorganization to bring the megacorp back to stable status. Yorinobu returned to the Tokyo headquarters after he left Night City, grieving his sister, who had become a casualty in the fight.

:Hanako, along with V, stormed the upper echelons of Arasaka tower to dethrone Yorinobu. He explained to V that he tried everything to bring the Arasaka Empire to an end and stop his father from his ideals. He reveals he did not seek power and control, but only to free the people of the tyranny of the Arasaka Corporation and to free them of their fear of Saburo. If V is successful, Yorinobu's suicide attempt will be stopped and Hanako will comfort her grieving brother as he tells her he does not fear the forthcoming consequences, which are later revealed to be his consciousness being overwritten and replaced with Saburo's engram.

2079

:Upon returning to Night City after their coma, V can listen to the radio while in a Delamain Cab. The speaker tells how Yorinobu was considered an inside saboteur of Arasaka and evicted by the company's board. He is said to have fled with nomads afterwards.

Database Entry (2077)

Ambitions
Yorinobu Arasaka — since his father spoke to him about the secrets of his company and his ambitions — has never lost sight of his goal, to bring down Arasaka. As Yorinobu distanced himself from his father he grew to hate him. When Saburo saw someone as a foe he would remove them without mercy and believed the end justified the means, this was a way of living Yorinobu could never abide by. The fear his father brought upon people was his greatest strength and Yorinobu knew this and was one of the few who did not fear him. To put an end to what he believed was Saburo's tyrannical goals he started gangs within Tokyo (Steel Dragons, Iron Lotus), the bōsōzoku gangs' goals were to expose the operations of Arasaka (as well as other megacorps) and destroy the areas that would weaken the megacorp's operations.

However, despite his battle and fighting among the Tokyo streets, Yorinobu was never satisfied with the results until finally the Arasaka Towers in Night City were destroyed by a mini nuke. He finally had realized nothing would be enough to stop Arasaka and his father. He left the Steel Dragons and went back to his family, this time wanting to destroy the megacorp from the inside. Yorinobu's sole purpose in life remained, to remove the fear his father brought onto the world.

Behind the Scenes

引文：Saburo Arasaka's younger son was groomed from birth to one day take the helm of the family corporation. However, the night he graduated from college, he and Saburo got into a heated argument. This father-son spat prompted Yorinobu to turn his back on family and form a gang-Kotetsu no Ryu, the Steel Dragons-hellbent on destroying the Arasaka empire. Unsurprisingly, the gang repeatedly failed to achieve its goal. Eventually, with Hanako's help, Yorinobu eventaully ends his exile and returns to the family and business. Though he is no longer the heir apparent, he nevertheless remains a person of great influence. In appearance, Yorinobu is meant to contrast with his ultra-traditionalist father, a modern American plutocrat rather than devoted caretaker of Japanese culture. His face bears the arrogant smirk characteristic of a high-profile heir who leaves to sow his wild oats before returning home to claim his birthright. His choice clothing likewise conveys the immense wealth and opulence typical of a privileged playboy.

Notes
*His name in the native Kanji appears to be 荒坂 頼宣, according to a post by a Japanese CDPR forum moderator.
**His given name, Yorinobu, is composed of the Nanori readings for "request, rely, depend on" (頼, yori) and "proclaim, announce" (宣, nobu).
**The surname, Arasaka, is comprised of the Kun readings for "desolate, barren" (荒, ara) and "slope, hill" (坂, saka).
*The player can find a picture of the Arasaka family in Yorinobu's personal office but with Saburo's face obscured with a whiskey glass. In Saburo's office, the same picture can be found with Yorinobu's face obscured.
*In the Arasaka ending, V refers to Yorinobu Arasaka as Hanako's baby brother. This is either an oversight or a mistake on V's part, as Hanako is the youngest of Saburo Arasaka's children. Hanako also regularly addresses Yorinobu as her older brother in Japanese (niisan).

The Tavernier Suite, also known as Yorinobu's Penthouse in , is located in Konpeki Plaza at the Arasaka Waterfront, in the Watson district of northern Night City.

Overview
The penthouse can be found on the top floor of the Konpeki Plaza hotel. It is used by Yorinobu Arasaka in 2077, who has made it his home during his stay in Night City.

The penthouse is heavily secured by an array of Arasaka technology, including one Arasaka Shepherd A-T alarm system, two Arasaka Sage VI-C motion sensor cameras and one Arasaka David IIIC automated turret.

After arriving in Night City, Saburo Arasaka payed Yorinobu a visit, and confronted him about his behaviour. Yorinobu, discontent with his father's "old school" practises, had enough and murdered him in the penthouse.

Notes
*Yorinobu keeps a pet iguana inside a terrarium that can be found directly to the left after exiting the elevator. This is not the same iguana that V and Jackie Welles transport across the Border Crossing during the Nomad lifepath prologue, as Jackie points out that the iguana they transported had a saggier neck with more folds.
*With Patch 1.5, V can pick up an Iguana Egg from the terrarium. This egg can be placed inside a bowl and eventually be hatched into a pet iguana in V's Apartment at Megabuilding H10.
*"Tavernier" is a French occupational surname meaning "innkeeper".

## You Know My Name
- type：Main Job
- quest_giver：Solomon Reed
- district：Pacifica
- sub_district：Dogtown

You Know My Name is a Main Job in .

Walkthrough

After acquiring the plans from Mr. Hands, V enters the Black Sapphire via the flooded tunnels that connect to the maintenance area of the hotel. After an underwater section at the tunnels and defeating some enemies at the maintenance zone, they are tasked with helping with making a meet with Solomon Reed.

To unite, a bridge must be drawn and Reed has access to the control panel. V has to take control of a mounted sniper rifle and help gather intel and eliminate targets to securely escort Reed to the panel. Reuniting with Reed, they take the elevator up to the party and infiltrate.

After reaching the floor, they join the party where lots of celebrities or important figures of Night City are. After a while, as she promised, Songbird reaches out to V. Songbird says that Kurt Hansen has the cure, which she is expected to work on with two netrunners who are currently attending the party. She is then whisked away by Hansen and she re-establishes the connection via the Relic.

To attend the upcoming meeting that Hansen, Songbird and the two netrunners are going to have, V needs to impersonate one of the runners. To impersonate them, V needs to have their behavioral imprints scanned. V joins the netrunner siblings playing roulette. To scan their behavior, V asks the siblings questions to provoke emotions from them to get scanned. Just as the roulette game ends, Hansen joins them and says that he knows that V is an NUS agent, threatening V and kicking V and Reed out the hotel. They then leaves the party and then is escorted out of the hotel.

Journal Entry
:Nothing's impossible, huh? Not only you managed to get Mr. Hands to help you, but even got old Solomon Reed to confide in you. You're on a hot streak, V - it seems that even breaking into the best-guarded fortress in Dogtown (maybe even all of Night City) is actually possible. And if you do manage to get Songbird out of there, you should consider buying a bunch of scratch tickets, 'cause Lady Luck is clearly on your side.

## Yugoslavia
language *Croatian *Serbian *German *Russian
ethnic_groups *Croat *Serb *Bosnian *Magyar *Albanian
- population：24 million
- literacy_rate：90%
- military：300,000

Yugoslavia sometimes referred to as The Yugoslavian Splinters is an area in Southern Europe consisting of various countries, and a combined military force. It consists of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia.

History
Yugoslavia has always been mismatched since its founding, and quickly fell into civil war once the global economic situation worsened and it seemed their breadbaskets would abandon them. Eventually, the wars de-escalated and trade opened up between the countries, as well as the setting of rules of war designed to prevent the economy from collapsing.

In 2018, Greece and Albania annexed the former Yugoslavian Macedonia. In retaliation, Serbia allied with Croatia and invaded Albania, annexing the northernmost part of the country by 2019.

By 2077, Yugoslavia faces instability, with Serbian and Albanian rebellions being commonplace, routinely stoked by corporations and criminal elements (such as BARGHEST) having a vested interest in arms sales to and from the fragmented Yugoslavia. Serbia has become a hotbed of separatism, with Netwatch agent Alan Noël describing an illegal arms shipment from Dogtown to Serbian rebels.

The Albanian mafia is mentioned as a criminal network operating across Europe according to a data shard. Corporations such as Digital Dimensions are also covertly stoking rebellions in Albanian-majority areas in Yugoslavia. There remains a political stalemate to this day between Albania/Greece and the Yugoslavian splinters.

Culture
Bosnia-Herzegovina
Various armies have divided Bosnia into various enclaves with their own local lords; arms manufacturers have started giving their prototypes to Bosnian armies for testing. Bosnian citizens live for what they scrounge, which isn’t much.

Serbia
Serbia's black market, backed by the military, is the only place in the country where things like bread and bullets can be purchased. The Serbian army is quick to strip the resources of what little land they manage to conquer for anything they can sell.

Croatia
Croatia is the (relatively) richest country in Yugoslavia as corporations are attempting to rebuild the many coastal hotels on the Adriatic Sea which were abandoned during the war.

Slovenia
Slovenia quickly found western allies to bolster its economy and is fully industrialized, with a decent tourism trade as well.

- transcript：The Bombus was designed as a caretaker drone because, as most would agree, who honestly has the time to raise children? You're back in the office the day after you give birth, working twelve, thirteen, fourteen hours, then another three stuck in traffic. Make dinner? Change a diaper? No chance in hell! Fortunately, the Bombus can fill the role of the dutiful parent: watching over the kids, playing hide-and-seek and popping scop dogs in the microwave. And if your child catches a stray bullet through the window, no problem! The Bombus will even call for an ambulance! Unsurpisingly, with its simple and inexpensive design, the Bombus has found applications in other sectors as well. Courier services use them for deliveries, the NCPD uses them for reconnaissance and gangs duct tape explosives to them to make remote-controlled bombs. Is there no problem a Bombus can't solve?

- type：Combat
- group：Drones
- style：Neomilitarism
- manufacturer：Zetatech
- model：Octant

The Zetatech Octant is a drone manufactured by Zetatech in .

Overview
The Octant is a large drone designed for combat zones. It is powered by four Militech thrusts and several types of weaponry, including defensive flares.

Database Entry

- transcript：Until recently, most considered Zetatech a second-rate company, living in the shadow of giants like Araska and Militech. But today, those same people will now admit Zetatech has proven its mettle in manufacturing products that match the quality of their megacorp rivals and are even sold at a lower price. Take, for example, the Octant. Sure, maybe it lacks the elegance characteristic of Arasaka, maybe its composite materials aren't as high-grade as Militech's, but when it comes down to sheer firepower, the Octant is second to none. This drone series has quickly emerged as a favorite for dictators around the world who aim to pacify mass protests and wipe resistance cells off the map. When Zetatech sold its thousandth Octant, champagne bottles were popped throughout the company's corporate offices. They achieved a sales milestone they could truly be proud of.

Associated Quests
*The Heist - Two can be seen escorting Saburo Arasaka's Rayfield Excalibur, another will pursue V and Jackie as they flee Konpeki Plaza.
*Lightning Breaks - Several will be encountered on the way to the Satwave Power Plant.
*With a Little Help from My Friends - One will be encountered guarding the crashed AV.
*Play It Safe - Several can be encountered as part of parade security detail.
*Forward to Death - Several will be encountered protecting the Maglev Tunnel Construction Site.
* Spider and the Fly - Several will be seen searching for V and Rosalind Myers.

The Surveyor is an aerial vehicle manufactured by Zetatech in .

Overview
Capable of delivering a platoon of troops behind enemy lines. Despite being engineered primarily with personnel transportation in mind, the Surveyor is fitted with smart-missile defense systems powerful enough to fend off enemy attacks. Initially designed and sold for military applications, this enormous AV is now frequently used for civilian purposes.

Organizations like Kang Tao and MaxTac use the Surveyor.

Dogtown Airdrops are delivered by these aerodynes.

## Ziggy Q
- status：Alive
- home：Night City
- gender：Male
- hair_color：Teal (dye)
Brown
- eyes：Blue
- occupation：Talk Show Host
- role：Media
- voiced_by：Ben Cura

Ziggy Q is a Media in .

Biography
Ziggy Q is a famous media personality and the host of his own talk show "Night After Night with Ziggy Q." In his show he interviews many guests, ranging from celebrities, musicians, religious figures, corporate execs, biologist, NCPD officers, politicians, and even other TV show hosts. Ziggy Q is often energetic and charismatic, using sharp movement to entertain the guests. He notably does not care for logical personalities and more often injects his own agenda within his interviews showing a clear bias.

Ziggy occasionally performs acts of philanthropy on his show. One such example is in 2077 when one of his guests, Martin Coleman, told the story of losing his arms when his employer, New American Autoworks, forced him to upgrade to Zetatech cyberarms or he would be fired. Martin was also responsible for paying for the cyberarms from his paycheck and once he couldn't keep up with the payments, the arms were repossessed, leaving Martin with no arms for the next twenty years. After listening to Martin's story, Ziggy gave a pair of Militech Dropner 5X cyberarms.

Ziggy Q can be seen in the Black Sapphire during You Know My Name.

Notes
*Drives a Herrera Outlaw GTS.
*Has an ex-wife.
*Has seven implants.

Zion Wylde is a Cyberpsycho in .

Biography
Zion Wylde was an aging Unification War veteran who worked as a solo in Night City. In 2077, after being hired by the Voodoo Boys for a simple recon gig, he had a religious experience in which he believed he witnessed the Loa, the gods of the Voodoo religion, and was convinced that he could gain entry into their sacred realm by providing sacrifices. It is implied that this experience was the result of the Voodoo Boys hacking him, and the job he was hired to do was only bait. Left with damaged implants, Wylde succumbed to cyberpsychosis and wandered the Badlands to the east of Night City, where he started assassinating members of the Wraiths as tributes for the Loa. The gang took notice of the killings and sent more members to eliminate Wylde, but they were unsuccessful, and rumors of Wylde and his mounting body count eventually reached Regina Jones.

V found Wylde deep in the Badlands, following a trail of Wraith bodies to his hideout, a small trailer camp surrounding a wind farm tower. V can choose to kill or incapacitate him.

Zor is a character in .

Biography
2070
Zor was convinced that his wife and son perished in 2070 when Katsuo ordered the Arasaka fleet to fire upon a northern district of Night City. This resulted in a ceasefire between the corporation and NUSA forces, in which he served. Driven by his thirst for vengeance, he hijacked a military AV and launched six rockets at the nearest warship, effectively sinking it. The AV was shot down by the fleet's anti-aircraft defenses soon after, and Zor was recovered from the wreckage by Militech soldiers. Expecting to be tried for treason, he was instead taken to an undisclosed laboratory, where he had a ripperdoc perform surgery on him. It was the beginning of Zor's seven years in hiding, during which he plotted against Katsuo, desperate to avenge his loved ones.

2077
In fact, Zor's story began shortly before the events of the book. He was an AV pilot for the Trauma Team named Jay. His squad was to rescue Milena from a vast car crash involving multiple vehicles. Jay noticed a boy stuck in one of the wrecks and rushed to free him, disobeying the order to stay put. Unfortunately, he lacked the necessary cyberware as well as equipment to accomplish this. It's unclear what exactly transpired next, though it seems that due to extreme stress, he suffered a cyberpsychotic break, which caused him to shoot the team's commander.

If not for Militech's intervention, Jay would've been executed. He was taken to a laboratory, where Ron replaced part of his brain with ArS-03, a device containing an AI, possibly from beyond the Blackwall. Jay's memory was nearly completely wiped; fake memories were inserted in its place. The bombardment actually never happened; the northern city district never existed, and Katsuo was never in charge of Arasaka's navy. At this point, Zor was created.

Zor worked in pest control, namely for Buyers and Son, a small company that received calls from all over Night City. He tried to lead a perfectly bland life in order not to arouse anyone's suspicion. Zor often stared at ads and read articles regarding seemingly random and unrelated topics, but he couldn't help himself when he happened to come across information about Katsuo, always studying it with great care.

Militech reached out to him, although not directly. The corporation's chief of security, Stanley, utilized his connections to blackmail Zor, among certain other individuals, into carrying out a heist. The heist that also involved Albert, Aya, Borg, Milena, and Ron ended successfully with a mysterious container being stolen from the Militech convoy. They parted ways afterwards, but Zor couldn't get the image of Aya out of his mind. Thinking he would never see her again, he took his co-worker, Morris, for a drink to Marry's Bar to celebrate his birthday. There, he saved a woman who was being harassed by a group of thugs, and she turned out to be Aya. The girl thanked him by taking him out on a date. The same day, Zor was fired from his job as he took the blame for crashing the company's van on himself, when in truth it was Morris' fault.

Ron managed to track Zor down and meet him in person. Both had the feeling of having encountered each other at some point in the past. Ron also made contact with Aya and convinced them to take part in another heist since Zor needed money to live and Aya needed someone to fix her failing cyberware. Ron promised to help her, but only if they stole crates full of Combat SRG-78 implants for military ripperdocs from a Militech warehouse. Then, he got in touch with the rest of the crew from the original heist.

With the goal of obtaining a suitable escape vehicle, Zor and Aya broke into Harry's Garage, a repair shop where Buyers' crashed van was undergoing restoration. Their entry grabbed the attention of the place's sole guard, but Aya managed to calm him down. They got in the van, which recognized Zor as its former user, letting them drive away safely.

Following the heist, as they were heading towards Kabuki with their prize in the rear, Zor needed to halt the van since its engine had overheated. Having sensed an opportunity, several members of Maelstrom emerged from the shadows and demanded everything they had, but ran away when it became apparent that a Militech drone was closing in on their location. ArS-03 communed with it, ordering it to cease action and resume its standard patrol procedure.

Some time later, Zor met with Milena in the Militech Offices, where he asked her to help him kill Katsuo. Afterwards, he and Aya went on another date, during which he told her about his family's demise. They fell in love with each other, but on their way to Zor's apartment, they received a warning against someone hunting them from Albert. Zor noticed that the toothpick he used to lean against the door had been knocked over. He pulled Aya back into the elevator just as somebody fired at them.

Zor carried on with his assassination scheme against Katsuo. Unknown memories suddenly became available to him. He traded the spoils of their previous heist for a sniper rifle and broke into a building in order to get access to the spot where a case of military-grade cyberware had been walled up. Zor took the implants to Ron, aiming to have them installed. He also began preparing for another heist, but his plans were disrupted when he and Aya got arrested by Liam Reed while trying to strike a deal with Animals arms dealers. Due to Stanley's secret intervention, they were released before being properly interrogated. Something led Zor into an abandoned flat, from which there was a clear view of Arasaka Tower. He knew Milena would be meeting Katsuo there. He waited with his sniper rifle, but ultimately resigned from killing him, having realized that if Katsuo died in such a way, he'd never acknowledge his crimes. Instead, Zor snuck into Maelstrom's quarters, where he made an agreement with Dum Dum to release Aya's adoptive daughter, Juliena, in exchange for Militech's container.

The team confronted a fixer known as Renner, and the situation rapidly escalated, turning into a massive shootout between various parties. In the end, his subordinate, Warden, was left in charge of the stolen container. Milena took Zor to meet Katsuo at his house in North Oak. An ambush interrupted the spectacle of Japanese customs as they found themselves surrounded by Arasaka soldiers. Katsuo claimed to be aware of ArS-03 and promised to help Zor, but only if he cooperated. Zor defeated the ambushers with ease but wasn't able to force himself to kill Katsuo. They lingered in a stalemate until a Trauma Team squad arrived. Zor threw a grenade into their AV and was unexpectedly recognized as Jay by one of the surviving pilots. Without giving it much thought, they hijacked the vehicle and headed for Maelstrom's quarters to extract Juliena by force.

Zor collected the container from Warden and managed to pick up Aya along the way. Albert needed lots of computing power for his own personal quest, and thus he tricked Zor into subconsciously giving him access to ArS-03, which he had discovered to be an extremely efficient computer. As the AV was soaring above the Badlands, some memories of his previous life as a Trauma Team pilot recurred to Zor. The vehicle was heavily damaged, and they ended up crashing into the desert sand. In his final moments, Zor opened the container, only to realize it had been empty this whole time. Stanley arrived at the scene with a group of Militech soldiers. Upon seeing Zor, he stated that ArS-03 was a failure and called someone to prepare ArS-04.

Notes

* Apart from having ArS-03 in his head, Zor also utilised an advanced reflex booster, among other cyberware. It was said to be better than the ones used by Arasaka soldiers.
* Since all of Zor's memory has been fabricated, it's impossible to determine any details of his life, save for those explicitly stated in the flashes of his real memories and his story described in the book.
* Very little is known about ArS-03, despite it being an important element in the story. Katsuo believed its presence made Zor a human-AI hybrid capable of serving as a medium between humanity and rogue AIs. How exactly Zor coexisted with ArS-03 is unknown, though it seemed that Militech was able to influence him through it.
* Zor was under constant supervision by three Militech technicians reporting directly to Stanley. They could feed ArS-03 new memories and even command it to self-destruct.

References
References to pages were based on the Polish edition of the book.

## Zuleikha El-Ahmar

Zuleikha El-Ahmar is a character in .

Biography
Zuleikha El-Amar lived with her mother, Gloria El-Ahmar and her brother, Ruben El-Ahmar at their house in Rancho Coronado, Santo Domingo, Night City. Her family are all followers of the Coptic Orthodox Church.

In 2065, Zuleikha's brother Ruben was shot and killed by Joshua Stephenson. Stephenson was arrested and convicted of the murder and sentenced to serve time in Night City Prison, but the El-Ahmar family were left devastated by the loss. Zuleikha, turning to her Reverend Stephanos Nasso for guidance, decided that the best way to heal from the pain of her loss was to extend her love and forgiveness to Stephenson and eventually decided to contact him in prison. Zuleikha and Stephenson began a friendship and regularly communicated over the next ten years, with Stephenson converting to Christianity as a result.

In 2077, Stephenson contacted Zuleikha to inform her that he accepted a deal with Fourth Wall Studios so that he may be released from prison to visit the families of his victims to seek forgiveness. While Zuleikha was pleased with Stephenson's efforts to seek forgiveness, she was appalled at the terms of the deal that included his voluntary death by means of crucifixion. Later, Stephenson visits the home of Zuleikha and her mother with the mercenary, V where they discuss faith and Stephenson's planned death. Zuleikha pleads with Stephenson not to go through with it, but their conversation is cut short by the arrival of Zuleikha's mother returning home. Gloria orders both Stephenson and V to leave her home, offering no forgiveness and begins crying, After their visitors have left, Zuleikha stays behind to comfort her mother.

Associated Quests
*There Is A Light That Never Goes Out
